title: Only drawback is lack warranty but unit is well built
text:
Completed 15 distillations last three weeks-no issues

BASICS:
· I Distill about two gallons monthly
· Appears good quality -item as described. So far- worth money
· No warranty -then again the price is hard to beat.
· Arrived FedEx Ground in five days using their $3 shipping
· No damage to outer package
· Packaging cushion Styrofoam top and bottom - none side
· Contains solid anti-scale compound but no extra filters
· Unit is supplement to eight-year old Kenmore (still operating has loose "ON" button last four years but still operates flawlessly.) -except for cosmetic differences has same dimensions and operation.

ASSEMBLY simple - one minute.

INSTRUCTIONS are brief for a basic unit (bottom reservoir, top head condensor/fan.)
Instructions reminds me of German Chinese with about dozen run-on words; e.g.,
"Thiswillpreventin uriesfromscaldingwaterandprolong." Images on page 4 shows basic assembly.
A bit of overkill is "Rinse and wipe out tank everyday"
The image shows location of filter but not how to replace them. Carefully squeeze the filter holder and rock it out. Reverse once new filter installed. I don't use filters that often.

OPERATION:
· Connect in order listed in instructions.
· I never fill to capacity - usually inch below mark may be reason Kenmore has lasted eight years plus.
· Use hot tap water and distilled water first appears in about 10 minutes.
· Be certain to wipe off any water on white outside immediatety. Only let water touch the inside.
· Slide bottom reservoir outlet nozzle into metal notched cover placed over plastic pitcher.
· Start Button labeled as "ON"
· Keep ON depressed one second and unit starts. Unit hesitates to restart for subsequent operation until it cools
· Be certain fan operating when red light/heating occurs.
· The pitcher is about 1/4 inch short - use cover from dessert whipped topping to elevate then slide into distiller notch.

CLEANING
· To avoid lots of cleaning, observe where on pitcher the water level is when unit shuts off - in future, when level approaches that, pull out power plug. This will leave small amount of water in bottom and not bake residue into reservoir.
· Follow the instruction: "Calcifcationandscalewillbuilduponbottomofthetankandshouldbe" as scale does build up on all these units (including the higher priced ones).
· You don't need to start unit to clean, simply use hot tap water and occasionally swirl the reservoir to remove scale high on inside wall. Wipe with cloth inside.
· I recommend sprinkling a small amount of crystals in couple ounces water after each day's distillation to flake off scale.
· Amazon, Lowe's, HomeDepot stock the descaler.
· Make certain to thoroughly rinse tank -even if some scale remains - to remove trace of corrosive material. Avoid breathing off gases.

title: Good product BUT....
text:
Let me start off by saying that I really wanted to give airfeet better than a three star review. However, there are a few big negatives that just crush the Product overall. Before I get to the good and bad break down, let me say I am a factory worker. I am on my feet for eight to twelve hours a work day. I only use air feet in my work boots. Now on to the bullet points.

- Good
- After you wear them for about a week you will notice a difference and you feet will feel better.
- Works better than any off the shelf product I have tried. (Have tried many)

- Bad
- They just don't last. Three months is the longest a pair has lasted for me. Again, I only wear them at work.
- Lack of durability. When these give out your sock, foot and inner shoe will be coated in a greasy, clear substance. It takes several days to get it out of your shoe.
- Company response to warranty claim. I have mailed back several pairs to the companies P.O. box for warranty replacement only to have the box returned to me after a week because no one picked up the mail at the post office. Then it's on to leaving messages and Twitter. (To be fair, I did get replacement inserts after four months of messages).
- Price. $48+ for a pair of inserts? Not at this quality level.

If air feet sold for $15 or $20 dollars a pair I really wouldn't be as concerned. When your putting down close to $50 a pair and you only get three months use, that's a problem.
Again, when they are new they work great. Does this mean I will stop using them? No. Does this mean I am actively looking for something better? Absolutely.

title: A MUST for your Ipe deck

Even with regular oiling, the natural finish became dull.  Before sanding and starting over, we decided to give Messmer's Combo a shot.  We followed the directions and allowed the cleaner to sit (doing 6 x 12 sections at a time so it wouldn't dry) and then scrubbed it with a scrub brush on a pole.  We then power washed the cleaner off with a wide spray power washer.  Since Ipe is so hard and we kept the power washer moving, we were able to use the power washer without damaging the wood any where.

text: I bought this dental lace to replace plastic packaging and dental floss waste, since I can reuse the bottle, buy refills, and compost the floss. It doesn't pull apart into a bunch of little strands like the plastic stuff does if I have used the same section too much when flossing. And lastly, it doesn't slip off my fingers if it gets wet. It stays put. I read a lot of comments that the floss kept falling back into the container once cut off. I have had ZERO problems with that. title: I was skeptical
text:
After reading an article discussing a cheap stack for healing injuries, I figured for something as cheap as gelatin I'd give it a shot. I was skeptical though, having had a severe meniscus tear in 2012 and a meniscectomy which followed.
I've slowly lost ROM and for the last 7 years I've had varying degrees of knee pain depending on which exercises I did during my workouts. Lately, straight leg calf work has been a killer. It would cause increased pain for days following.
After starting the gelatin 3 weeks ago the constant pain is gone. Pain after calf work is gone. I honestly can't believe it and I have to say I'm very pleased. I mix one scoop as directed in my morning coffee and half a scoop with my peri workout shake. The 1kg tub has 107 scoops which are 9g each, which falls within the parameters of the article. I already started sharing my results with a coworker who also has knee issues. I was the guinea pig. I don't know if gelatin fulfills all the claims being made, but it helped me with my pain. I'm going to keep buying as long as it keeps working.

title: Fully satisfied
text: As an engineer I was careful in selecting this product. After placing my order the scale arrived promptly in good shape and worked fine right out of the box. Now after several weeks of use I am perfectly satisfied with it. It goes on easily by just tapping my foot on the top, the processor inside measures the four sensor outputs and establishes the zero indication within just a couple of seconds. After stepping on the scale the reading is displayed again very rapidly, within another couple of seconds. I like the resolution to within 0.1 lb and the large digits are easy to see. My previous scale had LED readout and was easier to read even in a dimly lit bathroom. But I like the LCD display on this scale and expect to get a much longer life before the battery needs replacement. The design of the scale using a glass top appeals to me and it reflects an elegant design whose assembly lends itself to automated assembly to keep costs low.

title: Perfect for anyone
text: I own several white noise machines because I’m such a light sleeper.  This one incorporates all of the features and functions I love into one machine.  First, it is portable.  You can easily unplug and move it to another room, and you can easily pack it and take it with you when staying with family or at a hotel.  Second, it has many different sound outputs.  Seriously- a ton! If you like a static low white noise, it has that, but it also has many options for example, birds, ocean waves, rain falling, and even the click clack kind of sound you hear when riding on a train! Anyone who’s ever fallen asleep on a train ride or long car ride understands how that can make you sleepy.  I love this machine for all of the options it provides.  Even within just the plain white noise, there are a ton of different tones to choose from.  You can try different sounds and see which one ultimately works best for you.  The best feature is that is has a volume knob.  All of my other white noise machines have just “on” and “off”- but this one has a volume, so if the neighbors are loud, I can turn up the soothing white noise volume & fall asleep easily.  But if I just want it on to ensure a good night’s sleep within no interruptions, I turn the volume to a low/medium range.  This machine also has a low light in various colors you can choose, although I personally like it dark, so I won’t be using that function.  Overall, I love this and would recommend it to anyone.

title: Not your typical Energy Supplement!
text: I competed at a very high level as a powerlifter and was always taking energy supplements that were loaded with caffeine and other stimulants to enhance my performance.  Recently however, I made the decision that powerlifting was not favorably impacting my long term health and I made a major overhaul.  I switched up my training regimen to not just focus on strength, but also muscular endurance, cardiovascular stamina, and flexibility.  I cut out all the "energy supplements" that I realized were draining my adrenal system and were only making me burn out faster in longer workouts.  I started searching on Amazon for a natural supplement that would give me a little bit of a boost for my new routine, and I came across Ultimate Endurance.  I was really impressed with the ingredients, (especially that it is  almost completely caffeine free) and I decided to give it a try. I am now almost done with my first bottle and all I can say is... WOW!  Gone is the roller coaster high and subsequent crash of most workout energy supplements.  Instead, there is a much more subtle but effective maintaining of your energy levels throughout long grueling workouts.  I document all my workouts on paper and the numbers don't lie.  There is much less of a drop off in my strength, speed, and endurance at the end of workouts since I started taking Ultimate Endurance.  There is no magic pill to substitute hard work but for anyone that is looking for a little extra help in pushing themselves this is a MUST BUY.

(you get a better deal on Amazon, as I checked, on Oriental it's $6.25 for a set of 24). But back to the point, I did not want to sell the bracelets with a little sticker on them, so I sat down and removed them from each bracelet (432). It took me upwards of 2 hours, and unfortunately, some of them were so badly damaged from removing the sticker, I couldn't sell them. Most of them left a stretch mark where it was sticking to the bracelet. Some came out fine because the stretch mark was inside where the band sits against your skin, but some of the stickers were sitting right across the lettering. title: both tasty & economical
text:
This is the second stevia product I have ever used. The first brand had a bitter taste, so I used it only in coffee, but never in tea. Also, that other brand clumped horribly in lukewarm or cold beverages. Still, it was the best that I could find, so I continued to use it for about 2 years.

In contrast Stevita Supreme is not bitter, so I can use it in tea. Also, I am also able to use it in cool beverages with almost no clumping, but you do have to remember to stir the liquid just before adding the Stevia, rather than just pouring it in any which way. Don't put the Stevia in the glass and then pour the liquid in on top, or it will clump a bit (although nowhere near as horribly as the last brand I bought).

It does have an aftertaste in the same way that Equal or other non-sugar sweeteners do. If you are annoyed by those types of non-sugar tastes, you will be annoyed by this too. That said, it does not have a taste WORSE than (or stronger than) Equal or other such sweeteners. Just different.

In any event, I am trying to keep my glycemic index/load down, so any aftertaste is something I am willing to live with, rather than forgo sweetness entirely. Bottom line is, if you want the taste of sugar, you'll need to buy sugar. If you have reasons for avoiding sugar, as I do, I think you will find this to be a very welcome replacement.

Incidentally, one packet is exceptionally sweet-- much sweeter than an equivalent-sized packet of Equal. (The product description says 1 packet is equal to 2-3 teaspoons of sugar, which seems accurate.) As a result I seem to have bought too much-- I'll need only half the volume of sweetener packs that I thought. This makes it a great bargain, but do remember to factor this in before you buy.

For me, now about 75 packs into a 2,000 pack box and 1,925 to go, the issue has been how to keep the extra packs away from humidity. I finally put them in some extra-large air-tight Mason-type home-canning jars. Hopefully this will do the trick.

[Edit to add: 1) I bought these in January 2010. Now, almost 2 full years later (late October 2011), they have stayed impressively un-clumped, and that is true for both the ones I kept in the large mason jars and some others I simply stuffed into a gallon-sized Ziploc bag and kept in the closet. Tokyo is extremely humid so I have to say they stood up extremely well. 2) I totally overbought for the volume I actually use, so I ended up giving a large amount to a local elderly care home. If you're tempted by the price-per-pack but aren't sure if you'll really use ALL of them, one option is to donate any leftovers to your local elderly care home/PTA/church/etc.]

title: BEST.AMAZON.PURCHASE.EVER
text:
This is the BEST thing I have ever bought off of Amazon. My husband and I both like to sleep with a fan, but during the winter that gets cold. Enter the Dohm!

It takes a couple nights to get used to because it doesn't sound EXACTLY like a regular fan, but it is worth its weight in gold. It is small and actually has a little fan inside. It is not a "noise machine" that plays a recorded fan sound, but an actual fan. The fan noise can be adjusted by turning the top. It's just preference how much you open the vent. When I turn it on I immediately feel relaxed and ready to sleep. I considered the newer model with different speeds, but read that the most open setting on this model is the "high" setting on the more expensive model. I'm really glad that I went with this one.

Keep in mind that it doesn't block out all noise. I can still hear my dog bark to go out in the morning and would be aware if someone broke into my house, but it's great for those of us who need white noise to go to sleep.

title: The search is over, this one does it all
text:
I have tried many different wax products, and this is by far the best. First off, let me explain what my criteria is. My car's paint is aging, so it's getting harder to wax. I wanted something easy to apply, has a good shine, and doesn't turn plastic, and seams white. This one does it all. I didn't test the protection claims, because I just don't drive or park under rough conditions. I'm sure it performs well above my needs from other reviews I've read.

This is so easy to apply. To give you a comparison, Tech Wax, or Nano Wax takes about 3 to 4 hours to apply, becuase it streaks, and I need to apply 2 coats in some areas. Walk on wipe away (WOWA) products like Opti-seal takes about 2 hours to apply because I need to add a coat of wax on weathered surfaces. It just doesn't shine like wax. Armor All only takes 1 hour, because it's so easy to use, and doesn't need an extra coat.

When you apply it, it goes on like liquid, and seems to absorb into the paint. That's something wax doesn't do. When you wipe off the excess, it doesn't streak like wax or WOWA. If you have an older car with a dark color, you know what I'm talking about. Carnuba wax just streaks everywhere. With this, you don't need any elbow grease at all when applying or wiping, amazing! Tip: make sure you have extra micro fiber cloths on hand, because a dry cloth makes it easier to wipe off. When you're done, it has a slick feeling similar to wax. WOWA doesn't have that feel.

Another advantage is that it won't leave a white residue in the the seams, or on plastic parts. I have a louvered engine cover, which I never waxed because the residue made it look awful. Now, I can give it a coat, and the streaks are unnoticeable. The same with all the logos on the car.

It costs more than most waxes, but with the amount of time you'll save, it's definitely worth it. After years of searching for a wax that can do it all, the search is over.

title: Good value and comfortable
text:
After a skip and fall, two weeks in hospital with a fractured pelvis and a week of rehab, I was told to buy a walker to use for the next three months. A walker is a very slow and uncomfortable way to get around; speaking to a physio in Vancouver she recommended that I try Canadian Crutches or Forearm Crutches.

The Medline crutches are very comfortable and I can move around at least twice as fast as I could with the walker. The only issue I have had with them is the alarming speed at which the rubber on the legs is wearing down - I might need to buy some new ones but where from?

Aside from that they are good value for money and have transformed my ability to get around for the 3 or 4 months when I can use just one leg.

text: Got the Aria a few days ago and it works great.  I got the white version and it has a very nice clean sleek look.  Setup was extremely easy.  I set it up using my macbook pro over wifi in the living room on a hardwood floor.  Downloaded the setup app, put the scale into setup mode and followed the instructions.  The app asked permission to use the wifi password associated with my login so I didn't even have to have my passcode for Wifi with me.  Quickly linked it to my fitbit account.  Sent my wife an invite to use the scale through fitibit.com and she linked her fitbit account to it.  I don't have a basis to compare the body fat % in order to verify accuracy but it has been consistent. BMI is not shown on the scale but instead is calculated and shown on your fitibit account.  Scale and fitbit data will be very helpful with my overall health and fitness program.  My only slight issue is that its pricey for a scale but i guess you're paying for the wifi and instant linking to fitbit.

title: Could not connect to network - tried two different scales and had the same problem.  Third was the Charm - see Follow-up.
text:
Received the FitBit scale and wanted to use it with the now recalled FitBit Force (that I Love.) Could not get the scale to connect to the wireless network despite using 3 wireless computers, 2 networks and an iPhone.. Quickly sent it back and asked for a replacement. Amazon Prime was great with the replacement, New one came in and it had the same problem. Could not connect again using any of the networks or iPhone. Tech Support offered standard support (10 feet from the router, etc.) but nothing worked. I uploaded 2 setup logs which showed the installation errors to their Help Support line but they never replied. I am going to move the scale to a different building using a different ISP and try it there, if that doesn't work then I will return this unit also.

Follow-up. The third Scale came in today. I tried to connect and had the same problem. Called support and they walked me through a smart phone setup different from the one on their website. Let me share it - from the iPhone, start Safari and go to [...] - follow the instructions, personalize the scale,but when it calls for the battery to be pulled, pull all four batteries not just one. Wait 30 seconds and then put the batteries in different order. Connect to the FitBit wireless and follow the rest of the instructions. That made it work for me - hopefully this helps the next person.

title: Long Ice Pack, Perfect for neck or lower back
text:
I get frequent muscle spasms, usually in my neck. I have much better luck with ice for long-term relief than a heating pad. So, I have tried many different types of ice packs, from cheap drug store varieties, to the expensive ones my physical therapist's office sells. These are pretty in-line with the nicer ones from my PT's office, at a much better price.

They are a little thinner, which didn't impact their use at all. They are also a little stiffer than some, but they soften up within a few minutes, to conform to the neck. They stay cold more than long enough to do the cold therapy (recommended time is 20 mins, but I typically forget and go over a bit).

I have not tried these hot, but I have heard from others that ice packs typically don't last as long if you rotate it back and forth from hot and cold, they are better for one or the other. If I want heat, I typically use a heating pad. My only issue with this 6X20 is that to fit it in my freezer I have to fold it, but it doesn't seem to be making it break any faster.

The colors are fun too. I went with blue, but I love that you could potentially color code for specific purposes if you wanted.

I received this product at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. However, all opinions are my own.

Typically I feel nauseous within a few blocks/ miles, but today I tried these out for a 6 hour road trip through some residential and some highway sequences. I managed to read. I didn’t know how they’d fare at night when the liquid wasn’t visible but I read on my kindle with absolutely no issue. Before, I could read a sentence on my phone and I’d instantly feel sick. I spent the entire ride reading or on my phone. Yes, I looked ridiculous in them, but I’d rather look a little odd for 6 hours instead of having long-lasting nausea and drugging myself with Dramamine to pass out instead. title: Icy-Hot on a pad!
text:
I saw a great review, and the woman claimed it felt like a cool breeze on her undies. I liked the idea of natural plant based pads, as the synthetic ones cause irritation and chafing. So I was very excited to try these out.

When I first tried them on, it did have a slight cooling sensation. Then within 5 minutes after sitting down, it felt like someone had pranked my pad and put icy-hot on it. It felt like I was sitting on hot coals on a cold day. Thankfully I was driving to the store, and once I was walking around with some space between me and the pad things started to return to normal.

The ride home was not quite as intense, but I would not say it was in any way comfortable. Just to give it a fair assessment, I attempted to continue wearing it a while longer. 1 hour in and it felt like I had chafing, but once I switched back to my regular pad, it didn’t take long for things to return to normal again.

I did give it four stars for adhesion because it did not shift, bunch, or lift in any areas while I was squirming from the discomfort.

For a tougher woman, it may be a breeze, but if you have sensitive skin- STAY AWAY!

title: Used to be the best, now Chinese junk!
text:
I've used Trim brand fingernail clippers for over 30 years. They used to be the only brand worth buying: very inexpensive and excellent quality.
Clippers mysteriously disappear over time (kids borrowing them, falling out of my pocket when I pull my keys out, etc) so I needed to buy some new ones recently. I had to buy over 10 sets before I found one that worked correctly. Most of them had mismatched "teeth", so you couldn't get a clean cut. After finally finding a few passable sets, I had accumulated around 20 sets that were junk. I boxed them up and sent them back to the manufacturer.

I finally found an old set and then the difference was clear...these used to be made in Korea, now they are made in China. Unfortunately, Trim has lost a lifelong customer until and unless they start making a quality product again.

Don't waste your money on this product!

title: great straightening brush and all you need to straighten your hair quickly and easily
text:
I have very thick hair. It has some wave to it and It is sometimes frizzy. The Apalus Hair Straightening Brush made straightening it quick and easy. I absolutely love using this brush!

It has a nice long cord so I don't feel like I'm tied to the wall when I'm using it. A push of the power button and it powers on and quickly starts heating up. The buttons lock after 5 seconds, so if you miss setting your temperature at first, you can either hold down the power button to shut it off and restart it, or double press it to unclock the keys and adjust the temperature from there. It goes up to 450 degrees and only takes 3 minutes to get to that temperature. I set mine to 400 and it took around 2 minutes to get there. If you prefer to view centigrade temperatures, you can press both temperature control buttons "+" and "-" at the same time.

The brush also came with a couple of plastic to help separate your hair. I also really appreciate that it came with a glove as well to help you from getting burned which gave me peace of mind while I was using the brush knowing that I didn't have to focus on not getting my fingers too close to the bristles, but instead just getting my hair right. There are a good amount of bristles and they are spread over the brush in a manner that is helpful to really get into my hair, but also not put too much tension on my hair and the bristles don't snag my hair.

I like that it is offered in 2 color choices, I chose the black and blue one, but appreciate that others may prefer pink. The LCD screen displays the temperature. The handle stays cool to the touch. If for some reason, you forgot to turn off the brush, it should auto-shutoff after 1 hour. Although, I always unplug mine and let it cool off after I am done using it.

Included in my picture, the left side gives you an idea of what my hair looked like before using this brush, and on the right side is after using it.

I think this brush is a great value and I would highly recommend it to anyone who would use a straightener!!!

text:
I just ordered my 3rd and 4th tube of this stuff. It's great and helps me get over the fear of choking on my medicine. I have used this product very casually -- just an occasional tablet on crave-heavy days. I felt unconcerned because it didn't contain ephedra. This week, I happened to go to the doctor on a day that I had taken a Dexatrim. I was totally confused when, after taking my blood pressure, the nurse became instantly alarmed and went to get the doctor. I generally run about 135-140 / 65-70, but that day, it was horrific -- 180/90. Something was terribly wrong, and I hadn't been climbing stairs, or anything like that.

The scary thing was, I really didn't feel much different than usual. I felt perhaps the tiniest bit shaky, but not enough to have concerned me at all. I have to go back in two days to make sure my blood pressure has gone down. Be very, very careful with any type of stimulant drug. I was shocked to learn what I was doing to my body, without even knowing it. I'm playing it safe -- I threw out my remaining tablets.

title: A Product That Works
text:
I've been shaving my legs for a long time, and razor burn has been the bane of my existence from the start. No matter if the effort was with disposable razors or electric - or different shave creams - the end result was always the same - angry, rashy skin.

Nothing worked consistently until Coochy Shave.

The good stuff: I bought the large 16 oz Pearberry (it's lasted quite a while), which has a pleasant, 'hair conditioner' smell. Note that it does NOT foam up like shave cream out of a can, so if that's what you're after, keep looking. Instead it remains in that hair conditioner-like state which allows razor glide, since the hair is well coated. It makes your legs (etc.) very soft and smooth; there is almost no need to use lotion after a shower with this product. In fact, they recommend it as a hair conditioner also, but I've not experimented with it in my hair. I don't notice that it makes my leg hair softer, but to me that's neither here nor there.

The bad stuff: It's a bit pricey, but worth it. I wonder if one could use cheap drugstore hair conditioner instead with the same good results...

title: Perfect for the guy or gal who wants a consistent, clean smoke.
text: Ok. So here is what i've gathered after 3-4 bottles of rez block (I have been consistently using it for give or take a year) : It gives your water a light pink hue, and does not give off much smell nor change the taste of your smoke drastically (I say it like this because I always notice an underlying sweeter flavor than just water by itself when doing some air hits to disperse the rez block through my piece before seshing). I also believe that rez block will cultivate mold (This make sense in my mind because it is a fruit extract) in your piece of left in the same water for a day or two because after this time period is when I would notice little white particles floating around inside of my water pipe (please correct me if i'm wrong, this is ultimately why I am apprehensive on this purchase). LAST but definitely NOT LEAST the FUNCTIONALITY of this stuff is amazing I have a tall long tube style water pipe with a short recycler going from bottom to top chamber, a honeycomb barrel percolator, that goes up into a tornado drain, but the tube it travels up in from the percolator also has a glass ball in it for diffusion that gets very dirty very fast and actually loses its functionality within a week of daily smoking without rez block. with rez block it doesnt even get a spec of resin on it until maybe like a month and a half in. Would highly recommend maybe even say its a necessity for a lazier smoker who doesnt like to clean their piece twice a week. definitely a necessity for anyone with an intricate water pipe that relies on small pieces ie: glass balls, and little recycler tubes. HOPE MY REVIEW WASNT TOO LONG. I am a huge fan of the stuff and I think the pros outweigh the cons here. Just be proactive about the mold lol

title: surprisingly good experience
text:
**Update: Added two stars since my weight on a digital fitness scale in a medical facility and my weight at home were the same within a .25 of a pound.**

After reading the reviews I was expecting a lot of problems but there really were none. I'm giving 3 stars because I have only had the scale for 3 days. We all know electronics can work for the first week/month/year and then freak out.

Setting it up was much easier than the reviews lead me to believe. Before starting set up I changed my generic WiFi network names so they didn't have any dashes since reviewers said that was a problem. I set my 2.4 GHz network to b/g/n since Aria only works with b, which is so silly because b is ancient. I did the set-up over my iPad and there were 0 problems. It didn't stall, there was no need to reset anything or remove batteries, I proceeded from step to step until the scale was ready to go. The whole process took about 2-4 minutes.

I put the scale on the linoleum by my front door since I live in a tiny apartment that doesn't have hardwood or tile. I did a few trials and the weight/BF readings seemed both accurate and consistent. There was a little variance (+/- 2 lbs) when I moved the scale to the kitchen, so I decided to leave it by the door and not move it.

I've been trying to lose weight for 2-2.5 weeks and my weight was about 7 pounds less than my previous recorded weight in a medical facility. The real test of the scale is when I'll be weighed again this week. If I show a 5-7 lb weight loss there I will add stars. If I don't show that range of weight loss I will buy a piece of heavy tile to put the scale on to see if I can get a better reading.

I accidentally discovered a way to get my weight down by 20 lbs by repositioning my feet towards the outer edge of the scale. So I make sure to stand with my feet mostly together, toes near the dial, when weighing myself. From what I understand the Aria goes for accuracy above consistency (ie it's not programmed to show you your last recorded weight if your new weight is within a certain range) so it may be more sensitive to positioning.

Since I'm trying to see drops by 5-10-20 lbs, 1-2 lb variance is not that important to me. If it's important to you buy a physician's balance beam scale that uses counterweight. They are only $20-50 more than this scale here on Amazon. I didn't get one because I don't have room to keep it. Counterweight scales are usually found in gyms as well so if your weight seems wrong pop into your gym and weigh yourself to check. These are the scales people usually say are "heavy" which is a dysphemism for "more accurate than my electronic scale at home."

Of course half the fun is that it works with my Zip and the FitBit dashboard so I can use it to set goals and monitor my progress. I've had no problem with my data syncing. Adding multiple users takes a few minutes and you can do it from the app or the Dashboard.

title: New to toners
text: I'm 21 years old, and I've had a rough past with bad acne. After going to three different dermatologists and being put on 3 different skin regimens, it wasn't till my third try that my acne finally started to clear up. After my acne started to calm down, but I was left with noticeable acne scaring. I decided it was time to start a more healthy skin regimen to prevent any future breakouts, and hopefully my scars would be reduced in the process over time. I chose to buy Prep Skin refresher as the toner I would use because it promotes getting rid of dead skin cells, as well as promoting new cell growth, which I thought would help with my scarring. I bought a Neutrogena liquid cleanser for my oily skin that I use once in the morning and once at night, I follow the cleanser with this Prep Skin Refresher every night. I then use 100% Argan oil for a moisturizer (bought on amazon) after using Prep skin refresher. This product gives a slight burn the few times you use it, but nothing that is unbearable and only lasts a minute or two. The first time I used it, I noticed it mostly around sensitive areas of my face, I think I may have gotten a more intense feeling because my skin was very try at the time and this could have dried it out even more. I believe there is some alcohol in it. I've been using it for about 3-4 weeks now, and I can honestly say I've had less breakouts and the scarring left from my past acne has gone down significantly. The price may be a little high, but considering, it isn't too bad. I use just enough to saturate a cotton pad and it goes a long way. I've been using it every night for 3-4 weeks, and I haven't missed a day yet. I still have more than half of the bottle left. They include a sample of one of their other products they offer which I thought was cool. Great company, great product!

I weigh about 178 lbs and the chair just tilts and becomes unstable. I thought it was just me because of my gait with the shoulder sling but my wife tried it out and she had the same issue.

I take about 1 tsp and add water to it and chug it down like a shot. The taste is not very pleasant, but the benefits of this product are well worth it.
If you can't tolerate the taste, try putting a drop or two of a high quality, food grade essential oil in it, like a mint or citrus flavor. I put a couple drops of grapefruit essential oil in it and it is fine.
Also, using room temperature water can help keep the taste at bay. Cold water livens up the camphor.
This is a great product and always on my shelf! I won't be without it.

text:
I purchased these not long ago for my 5-year old son who had a severe cold. The pharmacist encouraged me to try them and let him know what I thought- he assured me they were safe for my son.

I had a touch of a cold as well and happily volunteered to sit in the bathroom while my son was in the shower so he wouldn't try to play with the tablet. Within minutes our bathroom was engulfed in a thick, menthol haze. My eyes were beginning to water, my son complained that his eyes burned. I turned the exhaust fan on and opened the door but the smell was still too overwhelming for us. I stopped the shower not long after it started and, in spite of the fumes, my poor kiddo showed no relief with his congestion. Neither did I. The remaining tablets were thrown away, unopened.

This may be the type of thing that works for some people and not others but I would definitely think twice before using it for a child do to the overwhelming smell.

title: Ok For The Price - A Little Rickety, Knee Pad Leaves Painful Marks
text:
This is a decent knee cart. Wheels are for indoor only, little too bumpy/hard to steer on the road or driveway. I'm in pretty good shape and found this cart to be a somewhat wobbly and feels a tad bit unsafe (It may not be, but when it's jiggling you feel uneasy until you get used to it). Would not recommend for someone who is heavy or in a weakened state.

The cushion has deep grooves or channels in it - these leave deep, long lasting impressions in your knee and made the skin on my knee hurt to the point I didn't want to get on the thing or could stay on it for very long. A folded towel on top of the pad alleviates the problem, but I don't understand the purpose of the grooves in the pad. All they do is cause pain. The manufacturer should ditch these grooves and just make the pad smooth. In the picture, the impressions on my knee are only after about 5 minutes on the cart.

Brakes work well, basket is definitely handy to have, and construction is o.k. All in all, not a bad cart, but not the best either.

title: Compare 2x/day vs. 4x/day
text:
[[VIDEOID:85e6f611432e4ff4eb89fbd331997dd7]] I have two pill organizers from BUG HULL - The 2 times a day Upgrade Version (UPC 631514679828) and 4 times a day (UPC 632202555882). This review compares the two products. View my video for details.
2X/DAY
- Very easy to open/close
- I like having the sides facing each other (as opposed to the previous version)
- Night and day sections can be removed from base to be used in two locations (separates by week)
- Cannot adjust start of the week (start day is Sunday)
- Not very portable
- Not practical to lift the entire item to pour out pills; makes more sense to pick pills out of container with fingers which might be a challenge for some
4X/DAY
- Not as easy to open/close; might be a challenge for someone with arthritis or other hand/finger issues
- Compartment lids get in the way when you’re trying to fill with all open
- Very portable
- Can easily arrange to start on preferred day
- Separates by day (each day can be removed)
- Easy to remove pills from compartment (just open the lid and flip over)
Both appear to be high quality, and I anticipate they will last quite a while. I found the Bug Hull customer service to be excellent. I prefer the various symbols used to delineate each pill time rather than more specific times like on other products (more versatile). If you think you will have trouble opening the 4x/day and you don’t need to worry about portability, I recommend the 2x/day for its easy opening/closing mechanism. You can always get 2 of these if you need 4x/day. However, if you need something that is portable, the 4x/day is perfect. Both of these have “large” compartments, which appear to hold 8 to 9 large capsules or a similar mix of large and small. I only fill about 1/3 of a compartment with my 3 capsules and 4 medium to small pills.

title: If they lie about being vegan...
text:
If they're lying about being vegan, as Vitamin D3 (Cholecalciferol) is animal sourced (D2 or ergocalciferol is plant sourced), then what else are they lying about? I almost bought this before I noticed the vegan sourced claim. So, I asked in the customer question section how could this be vegan if it's D3 or cholecalciferol, which the animal sourced form of vitamin D. No one ever answered me. So now I'm writing a review.

I didn't buy this product, but that's why. I prefer the D3 or cholecalciferol form because it is less toxic to the human body than the D2 or ergocalciferol form. But the fact they claim it's vegan gave me pause, as I began to wonder what else they were lying about if they were willing to blatantly lie about this product being vegan. Either it's vegan and D2 (ergocalciferol) or it's not vegan, animal sourced, and D3. It can't be both.

I bought this scooter to get around due to impairment of my right leg as a result of back injury. It is very easy to get on and to learn to drive but a few things need to be adjusted first. The emergency brake is difficult to use but I finally got mine to work properly. You need this to work as there is no park feature as you find on other chairs

I also had to adjust the toe in to get it to drive safely. Before it was very difficult to drive as it darted uncontrollably as I picked up speed. Be sure to inflate all 4 tires as well, I set mine to the max of 40psi as there is no recommended tire pressure. All 4 tires were way off when I got it which contributed to the poor drivability.

The frame and body panels are well done and solid, I have most of the unit apart to inspect and to add a trailer hitch. They have attachment points both font and back which I assume are there for attaching accessories such as a Custom hitch or bumpers.

I love mine as it has 4 speeds, slow + 1-2-3, slow is about the same as walking speed, 3 gets you up to 24 kmph or about 15 mph. I drive mine on the road (keeping right) to go for coffee in town, it has a full automotive lighting pkg including signals. It is an attention getter, lol.

title: Front wheel drive scooter has to go up ramps in reverse.
text:
We bought this scooter to take on trips and particularly on airplanes. It works fairly well around the house and outside on level surfaces. However we have experienced a problem on slopes. The scooter is front wheel drive. When we sit on the scooter nearly all the weight is on the rear wheels with little weight on the front drive wheel. Thus we cannot drive the scooter up ADA ramps in our house. We have to back up these ramps because only then is adequate weight on the drive wheel.

One other issue is that the handle is rather close to the seat even in the roomiest positions. As we are near the weight limit of the scooter, we could use a bit more room.

And finally, a 3-wheel scooter is not as stable as a 4-wheel. This scooter tips over rather easily and in fact more easily than the other 3-wheel scooters we have, I think it is because the wheelbase is short,

title: Really more of a professional tool
text:
This is a quality tool. It's well made, and does its job very well, but it definitely takes a little getting used to. There are several features that may be different from cuticle nippers you've used before.

First, the cutting edges are curved so that the nipper closes and forms a very sharp point. This allows you to cut more accurately and deeply than with normal nippers. Second, you might notice the two handles are not identical. The handle on the right is shaped so that your hand won't slip when you are holding it in your right hand. (It should be noted that this makes it a little difficult to use while holding it in your left hand, which is why I say it's more of a professional tool. It seems like it's designed to use on someone else.) Third, this cutting edges are extremely SHARP. It cuts cuticles and thick skin quite easily, which is what it is meant to do, and ultimately one of the main reasons I feel this tool deserves 5 stars.

title: Heavy but effective
text:
I have a bad back and use this every time I go to a restaurant or other public event, as it guarantees I will not be sitting on a hard surface. The cushioning is VERY high quality gel and adjusts to my sitting position. However, it is a surprisingly heavy item, so if you have a bad back, the weight is something to consider if you are going to be toting it around.

In order to be sure I don't leave this expensive cushion in a restaurant or lose it, I took some precautions. First, I left it in the decent-quality plastic carrying case which came the cusion (makes for easy cleaning). I put my name/phone/e-mail on a piece of paper and put it inside the clear plastic cover. If I leave it some place, the finder can reach me.

In order to ensure I don't leave the cusion behind in a restaurant/theater, etc., I created a way to clip it to my belt loop when I sit down. Here's how:

Get a 2' length of bungie cord from Orchard Supply Hardware (about 1/3 as thick as regular bungie cord - no hooks on ends). Attach it to the carrying cord of the plastic cushion-cover with a key ring by doing the following:

Attach the bungie cord to the key ring by leading the bungie cord through the "whole" in the key ring and doubling it back. Then attach the doubled-back part (about 1") to the rest of the 2' length bungie cord using a zip-tie. Singe the ends to prevent running.

Next, secure a D-ring (spring-loaded clip) on the other end of the 2' cord the same way (lead cord through ring, double back and secure with zip-tie).

So now you have a 2' bungie cord with a key ring on one end and a D-ring on the other.

Attach the key ring to the plastic cushion-cover by threading the key ring onto the carrying handle of the plastic cover (like putting a key on the ring). The other end of the bungie cord still has the D-ring attached.

When I go to a restaurant/movie/ball game, etc., I just clip the D-ring to the belt loop on my pants when I sit down (the other end is attached to the cusion's carrying cord). If I try to leave w/o the cushion, the cord attached to my belt loop will remind me to grab it.

I know it sounds goofy, but it has saved me many times from forgetting the cushion at a restaurant or at other event.

Hope this helps!

title: I don't want ever to use generic rechargeable batteries again
text:
I've had different branded batteries from less known companies (Mox, Multilaser and such) and while they did the job (power a device and receive a new charge), they usually lost charge too fast outside devices and the actual capacity of some of them area a bit fishy.

Since I had the opportunity to grab some Sanyo Eneloops, I did and was surprised that the actual capacity of 2000mAH seems to surpass all my previous ones, all of them claiming a higher capacity, ranging from 2100mAH to 2500mAH.
And they hold the charge way better when left unattended, inside a turned off device or a low power device (remotes, corded phones with caller id etc). I can charge them as soon as they're drained from use and left sitting somewhere until I need them.

Just a warning for those who may think the slow discharge is linear, it is not. They will lose a lot more of charge in the first few weeks than in the following months. Neverthless, they will still have a decent ammount of charge even after a year left unattended.

The 8 AA case is also nice, a pity one of the two came broken.

title: Nice lamp, hard to adjust
text: I'm pleased with the construction quality, light level and color temperature of this light, but the adjustability needs some work.  The cord that goes from the head down the tube and to the outlet is very heavy ... a good thing, from a durability standpoint... but it makes height adjustment nearly impossible.  You are supposed to be able to loosen the knurled lock ring and just raise or lower the upper arm, but it doesn't work out that way.  You can raise it fine (with some effort, since the cord inside the tube provides a lot of resistance), but getting it down again is impossible. There are only two ways I've found to do it... first way is to stand on the cord with one foot and push the base away with the other foot as you lower the arm... this will pull the cord out as the arm lowers.  Second way is to lay the lamp down on it's side on the floor and tug on the cord as you slide the upper arm back into the tube.  Either way, advertising this lamp as "height adjustable" is a bit of a stretch... it's more like a "set it once then leave it alone" type of thing.

text: I took Bergamot after reading numerous reviews about how it had helped bring down some users' cholesterol readings, but for me it did exactly the opposite. Even though I improved my diet (gave up red meat and started eating lots more vegetables) and exercise habits (started exercising for a least one hour every single day, up from 3 or 4 times a week) my cholesterol got markedly worse! I had a fasting blood test done just before I went on the supplement and again three months later and I was in total shock to learn that my total cholesterol went from 178 to 202, my HDL went from 45 down to 40 and my ratio went from 2.6 to 3.3. So I stopped taking it immediately. If you do decide to give it a try, please do yourself a favor and get your blood drawn two or three months later so that you don't take something which is actually making your health worse for too long.

title: Possible alternative part for 1/2 price
text:
These are fine as belt replacements.
Looking at my original belt, it states "Pioneer 61 MXL"
This is a 6.1" belt with 76 teeth at an MXL-sized tooth pitch (per Google search)
You can find an equivalent from Gates, directly from Amazon: search 61MXL012
This is a 1/8" width belt (same as here) with the same gear tooth pitch for half the price (<$5), with free shipping if you meet Amazon minimum order amounts.
("MXL" defines the spacing on the belt 'teeth')

While I have NOT purchased one myself, this is what I'll buy when I have an SV780 needed a new belt (we have two of these vacs at home)
I will also look up/measure the gears inside when I get the chance and can provide info on those as well; you'd need a micro hex key most likely to secure it onto the motor (if an equivalent size is available)

Also, on one of my older vacs, the belt would slip off the main teeth on the motor gear and lose traction, so the brush would no longer spin. I fixed this with a couple rubber washers (about 1/2" dia, ~1/8th and 3/16ths hole sizes. They easily pop on over the gear end, and keep the belt running straight over the gears.

title: This stuff is poison - do not use it on anything you might want to touch. Or anywhere you breathe.
text:
It's extraordinary that this can legally be sold as a shoe deodorizer as per the labeling. Actually, it almost certainly is not legal to do so. More importantly, selling this as a product to put on your shoes is crazy irresponsible. The warnings on the can speak for themselves:

* ”For use on precleaned, nonporous surfaces; not for use on humans or animals."
* "This product contains a chemical(s) known to the state of California to cause cancer."
* "Causes substantial but temporary eye injury."
* “HARMFUL IF ABSORBED THROUGH THE SKIN.” (Ah, like from a sweaty foot in a shoe?)
* “DO NOT GET IN EYES OR ON SKIN OR ON CLOTHING.” (Clothing, like shoes?)
* “Wear long-sleeved shirt and long pants, protective eyewear (safety glasses), shoes and socks, and chemical resistant gloves (such as or made out of any water proof material).
* “Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before eating, drinking, chewing gum, using tobacco, or using the toilet.”

It doesn’t say anything about sexual intimacy after use of the product, so I assume that’s OK.

I’m afraid of this little poison bomb. I’d return it, but according to Amazon: “This item can’t be returned since it requires special transportation and handling which we can’t provide.” Right, because it’s an explosive poison — makes sense. Can’t throw it away, because that’s dangerous, too. Now I get to call a company that deals with the disposal of hazardous chemical waste and arrange delivering this carcinogenic care package to them — a fine venture for a Wednesday afternoon. Where's Erin Brockovich when we need her? Where are the ethical marketing police?

Cancer sucks. Here's to your health, with the greatest hope that you don't buy this product.

title: LOVE IT!
text:
My son is over 4 months old and started outgrowing his original newborn tub until he was super smushed in it. I looked at a lot of different bathtub replacements and liked the look of this one the best and decided to give it a shot. I love it!! It's like a water boppie pillow, lol. Ok, the details.

Good: It dries just fine in our closet, the rubber backing keeps it from going crazy in the tub. It's soft and comfy, but he gets to stretch out in the tub. The water gets through it so he is surrounded by water. He's not really sitting up on his own yet, so this is perfect. I put him belly down the other night, and although I kept a hand under his chest (better safe than sorry!) he absolutely LOVED seeing the water up close.

Bad: It doesn't fit him perfectly, but what would? So he slides down a bit and if he's off the cushion part too much it floats a bit, so I do have to keep moving him up and down on it - but he'd rather be down a bit so he can kick and splash in the water than up on it and out of the water too much. Also, I think the directions are right on - you MUST hang it in an open area (not a closed up bathroom) so it can dry out fully. We haven't had much of a problem with it drying out because we followed this direction. But I did see some reviews of it getting moldy and I can see it getting moldy if you ignore those directions.

That's all I've got!

title: I recommend
text:
Saving your child from the pain and complications of a sunburn is usually on parent minds during the summer time. But, did you know that kids and adults can get a sun burn during the winter months also? You absolutely can! The sun can actually be more dangerous in the winter than in the summer. Many people don't know that the sun's rays aren't as direct in the winter as in the summer. Higher altitudes mean more intense UV ray exposure. Snow is the perfect sun reluctant. If you go skiing in the winter most of those hills are at higher altitudes. Protecting your child's skin is most important.

UV rays that are reflected can be just as damaging as direct exposure
Finding that perfect sun tan lotion or spray is the most important thing. My husband who has psoriasis has to purchase lotions that are high in oil. Especially when we are talking about swimming in chlorine. He dries out so bad that it actually hurts. But for children it is imperative. Their skin is so new to all the rays that they burn so easy.

text:
Likes:
-Long Battery only charged it once or twice in months

-Battery Indicator (Green for good battery/Red for battery dying)
-LEDs for each setting so you can clearly see which setting it is on
-Carrying case and extra brush heads are useful

Dislikes:
-Brush heads hard to get on and off
-Settings leave more to be desired
-Charging door is hard to open
-Not a Micro-USB port (would have been better in case of missing charging cable)

The tooth brush is decent for the price, but the brush heads outlasted the tooth brush itself lol. The tooth brush lasted me 7 months with two brushes per day, which isn't too bad if you factor the price compared to other tooth brushes, but others would probably last longer so you get what you pay for. title: Overall I'm very pleased 😀
text:
[[VIDEOID:afe1165b3118188e821d9011b79892e0]] Just received it today. This is my first electric toothbrush. Cons then Pros.

I'm a little bit disappointed because there are a few markings on it with possible spot of glue on it.[I didn't take photos of that.] Some of the metal is scratched up a tad, too. It leads me to believe that these are new toothbrushes and because of the markings, they're being sold at a cheaper price. Just a theory here. Another thing that bothers me is that the lube they use for the rubber cap was smeared a bit on the brush and seems like it leaked onto the charging port (which I hope you can see in the photo). Instructions are kinda strange and lack some info. Like some stuff seems as though it "got-lost-in-translation". It mentions about removing sexual tooth stains...???... Super mode only states that it's a very interesting and practical pattern. So, it's just for fun? I was hoping for more info.

It came fully charged straight from the box! Feels very smooth like a very soft suede. The toothbrush head has bristles that are soft and have those bumps on the back to use on your tongue. I decided on using the white setting because I smoke cigarettes and drink a lot of coffee. Brushing my teeth was an interesting experience. I was trying to hold in the giggles because of it tickling my gums and the roof of my mouth. I'm amazed of how the brush feels like it "hugs" my teeth nor did it hurt my sensitive gums at all even at the highest setting! Very happy that it got plaque off my gum line and can reach the back without awkwardness. While I wasn't expecting miracles, it did a nice job lifting off some stains.

title: Not Impressed
text:
I also bought this product from "Best in Market" and was immediately skeptical when I noticed the 09-11-05 date stamped on the bottom of the jar. After looking at BOM's website I read where they said that's how Asian countries list their manufacture date, meaning the first two digits signify the year. Prevera states it can offer their product at a "low price" by "cutting out the middle man" thereby having it manufactured by Experimental Nutrition Research (ENR). I don't know...is ENR an Asian company?

At any rate, Prevera has not hurt my skin or caused me to have a bad reaction. It simply hasn't caused me to have a reaction at all, good or bad. I've been using it for two weeks and see absolutely no difference in the appearance of my skin. It doesn't look older, it doesn't look younger, it doesn't look...different. I'll continue to use for a couple more weeks just in case something magical happens to kick in any second now. But at this point I can say 100% I would never order Prevera again. I'd rather keep my $30 for nothin.

title: Effective and Durable
text:
These things make washing your hair (or your dog's fur/skin!) so easy. I'll use these forever. They detangle gently when properly used, relieve scalp itchiness or head pressure, and speed up the lather process of washing ones hair.

As a per brush, it pulls a lot of shedding fur out and makes scrubbing your dog easy. The rubber spikes massage and pull undercoat out gently when your dog's fur is wet.

They do eventually tend to get water inside and mold as the pressure from scrubbing your scalp with it pulls the rubber from the plastic and creates a crack for water to seep into the handle, but by then, it's normally time for a new one anyway, as the spikes become less firm (like a toothbrush almost) and even discolor over time due to effectivness of scrubbing the scalp.

I will say that because of the eventual moisture-inside-the-handle issue, the transparent scrub brushes are the ideal choice. With the opaque ones, you won't necessarily be able to see when water is inside.

Plastic use could also be reduced... it feels wasteful to get these every 6 months to a year.

title: Terrible Customer Support
text:
I recently bought a Purple Double Seat Cushion and Back Cushion. There were problems from the start. First, they only sent one cushion. I had to contact the company multiple times before they finally sent the other cushion. it was 3 weeks late.

I found the Back Cushion extremely uncomfortable, so I tried to return it. I had to wait several days for them to issue a Returned Merchandise Authorization. By then, the RMA form said that it was too late to return the cushion. The form actually showed a made-up delivery date (I have no idea where they got it from). I had show them the Fedex tracking with the actual delivery date. Then, they decided to not refund the full amount for the cushion. I’ve had to contest the charge with my credit card company because they refuse to explain why.

Clearly, Purple isn’t concerned about providing any kind of customer support after the sale. I’ve probably spent 2-3 hours emailing and texting with them about all of the problems. I wish I had never heard of Purple because their customer support is simply atrocious.

I first heard of Purple when we were mattress shopping a number of years ago. We looked at Intellibed and Purple. They originally used the same gel technology, but there was a lawsuit (which Purple lost). Comparing the two mattresses side-by-side, the Purple mattress was much lower quality. The Intellibed cost more, but you definitely get what you pay for when it comes to mattresses.

We’re still very happy with our Intellibed mattress. Since it had been several years, I decided to give Purple another try. I thought, “How can you go wrong with a seat cushion? If I don’t like it, I can return it.” What a mistake! You should learn from my mistake :)

title: Plastic Pump for 16 oz Jar, also works with 19 oz CeraVe Cream Jar
text:
Update: June 7, 2015

Unfortunately I had to revise my review of this pump. It broke after 10 days of use. The pump separated from the lid, rendering it useless. It was only used twice a day and should have lasted a lot longer because I consider that "normal" use and not heavy duty use. It may be fine for thin, watery lotions, but it will only last a short time for thicker creams and lotions. I'll be looking for a replacement.

Original review: May 28, 2015
I bought this pump for use in a 19 oz size jar of CeraVe Moisturizing Cream purchased at Costco. The Costco size is slightly larger (19 oz vs 16 oz) than what I usually find in my local stores. I was worried that this pump would be too short to reach the bottom of the jar because some reviews indicated that might be the case.

However, the pump I received was actually too long. After a quick trim with a pair of scissors, the pump was a perfect fit. The first few pumps (to "prime" it) were a little hard to pump. Now it works great - but remember if you are using this with the CeraVe Cream - it is a CREAM not a lotion. The CeraVe Cream is thicker (in a good way) and therefor the "pumping" will always need more pressure than pumping a thin lotion.

I really like this pump and will keep to use in my next jar of CeraVe Cream.

title: An awesome impromptu jump bag!
text:
I am an EMT. When I am working at the fire department, I have a spacious, generously-garnished jump bag supplied to me by the station. Off duty, however, I am left to my own devices. This bag is perfect to keep in my car, take with me when staying with friends and family, and of course, when my younger and more reckless friends invite me to their college parties.

Most reviews complain of how small the bag is. However, it is exactly the size listed in the product description. In case you have trouble reading the product description, it is a little less than a foot wide. It has an adjustable divider in the center compartment (attached via velcro) to better accommodate each individual's organization methods.

To give you an accurate gauge of its spaciousness, I'll list everything that comfortably fits in my bag.

Left side compartment:
-a copious supply of nitrile gloves

Right side compartment:
-trauma shears
-mini note pad + pen for impromptu patient assessment, notes, and Hx
-pen light
-aspirin
-small bottle of hydrogen peroxide
-several packets of ketchup (great substitute for oral glucose in a pinch for someone with low blood sugar!)

Center compartment:
-alcohol pads x 6
-antiseptic wipes x 5
-lidocaine insect sting wipes x 3
-burn cream
-antibiotic ointment
-cotton swabs and cotton balls
-4x4 gauze pads x 2
-2x2 gauze pads x 5
-3-inch rolled gauze x 2
-eye pads x 2
-many assorted bandages
-1-inch tape
-2-inch self-adhesive bandage wrap (honestly my favorite stuff in my bag)
-instant cold compress
-tongue depressors
-adult CPR pocket mask
-pediatric CPR pocket mask
-6 different-sized oropharyngeal airway adjuncts

Perhaps an exhausting list to read through, but I hope that gives a future potential buyer a good depiction of this bag's storage abilities. I grew up playing Tetris, so I've more or less mastered the art of optimally fitting as many things as possible into a small space.

The only downside I have found is that I really would have liked to see a shoulder strap. It's not a big deal though, seeing as I have many extra straps from old computer bags.

Including this bag, my entire emergency kit has cost me only around 60 dollars. I am seriously considering buying another to stock up and keep as a backup. Great product!

title: It is really easy to using the pumping handle to take out the ...
text:
I bought this Cupping Therapy Set for my mom. We already had one that she bought from our local Chinatown, but we didn't have enough cups to do her entire back in one sessions which is why I decided to buy more.

Pros: It is really easy to using the pumping handle to take out the air from the cups. Most of the time, I use 2-3 pumps and it's sticking on my mom's back, and it will stay on the entire 15 minute session. On the originally cupping set, there were times I had to pump 8-10 times, even when it was new. The largest cups are huge. Bigger than my other cupping set so it covers more area. I usually use this for the lower back/hip area.

Cons: I mainly use cupping therapy on my mom's entire back so the smaller cups are not very useful for us. I think there's way more smaller cups than needed. This cupping set has twice as much as my old one. However, maybe others will disagree because of their own needs. Also, all the cups and handles are laid out on styrofoam so every time I had to take something out, it will make that horrible screeching sound. For those of you, who uses this for work, it might be easy for you to carry around if you have to walk around. My old set had a handle and you can carry it around like a briefcase but this one is just a box.

As a disclaimer, I did not try using the pump handle with the long tube. I am unsure how much it can help out in hard to reach places. I did test put a cup on my back by myself. Let me tell you, that's not going to work. First of all, not going to be long enough to reach the lower back, only upper back. Second of all, it's hard to keep it flat on your back unless someone does it for you so that defeats the purpose. Maybe it can be used on the shoulders.

Warnings: I normally perform the cupping therapy on my mom for 10 minutes. However, I read the instruction manual and it says it's possible to go up to 15 minutes. We did that, and my mom had a whole bunch of blisters on her back. I know this can happen if the skin is thin or the cupping therapy last too long. Therefore, be careful on the time especially if your patient is more sensitive to this. I know now to just keep the sessions to 10 minutes.

title: Your toothbrush will get a new life
text:
The battery arrived completely depleted, but it took a charge (installed in the brush) and so far, is holding it.

Installation is a bit finicky, but with a simple hack, becomes much easier.

I was not able to completely remove the old solder from where the battery pins go through the board. As a result, every time I tried to push the pins of the new battery through, they would just crumple, and I was afraid they'd break if I kept trying.

I ended up running a short length of wire from the board to the battery compartment. I removed a little bit of plastic to fit the wire inside the housing. This did the trick, and will make future battery changes so much easier!

title: Doesn’t stay mixed
text:
Flavor is ok, but very strong. If I were to purchase again, I’d order direct from them where I can customize it. It is very filling and I like the benefits of it, but it seems to take some learning in how best to prepare it.
My main problem is that I cannot get it to stay mixed. I’m used to mixing a large protein shake and sipping it throughout the day. However, with this kind, it starts to separate after a few minutes. The first time i used it, I mixed it in a ninja blender with ice, water and instant fruit drink mix. I ended up with a layer of watery juice, layer of mixed fruit/vanilla milkiness and a layer of thick vanilla protein floating on top. Id used a clear tumbler and could see the different layers as it separated.
Second time i used it, I mixed it ice, water and a scoop of a coffee flavored whey protein that I’ve used everyday for years... It drank fine at first. Then about 20 minutes later it felt like it was getting oddly thick. It started to feel almost like drinking bubble tea. I poured it into another cup so I could see what was going on - I had normal shake consistency, but at the bottom of the cup was a gelatinous goo. It had the consistency of congealed pan-drippings. Eww!
I do actually like it, but it’s going to take a bit of trial and error to find the right stuff to mix it with so it doesn’t separate.

title: EXCELLENT CHOICE!!!!!!
text:
I have a chronic pain condition & Parkinson's. Because of these medical problems & side effects of medication, mainly dizziness, there are times that it is not safe to shower. The portable bidet seemed to be an inexpensive and effective choice for the solution to this little problem.

The Palm arrived today and the directions could be a little more detailed (especially for those who are direction challanged - like me). After figuring it out (didn't take long) I did a test run. It was easy to use and now I feel that I can always be clean and fresh. This definitely gives me peace of mind. It will be much better than the "sponge bath" at the sink. Instead of trying to rinse with a wet washcloth, the Palm gives you a nice stream of fresh clean water. The water pressure is good - on a scale of 1 to 10, I would give it a 7.5. For a portable device, I think the pressure is really good. Just make sure that the nozzle is pointed in the right direction or you might be cleaning the wall or floor tile. I tried it at the sink first and almost sprayed it in my face.

The Palm is small which makes it easy to take it with you when traveling - it would fit easily into a large purse or carried discreetly in the travel pouch provided. You might have to refill it once to clean front & tushie but that's a small price to pay for cleanliness.

It's battery operated and does make some noise. If you're using it in a public restroom, someone might wonder what type of device you are using - maybe a vibrator rather than a portable bidet. Who cares, it's better to be clean than worry what someone else might be thinking. Just smile at the person if they're at the sink next to you when you're washing your hands. Thinking about using it in a public restroom, you should probably take a few paper towels into the stall with you so you can dry the small drops of water on the outside of the bidet.

I deliberated for a while trying to decide which portable bidet to purchase as I looked at the array offered on Amazon. It is well made and worth the price. I think I made an excellent choice.

I used it again and it I am impressed with the quality of the Bio-Bidet and I don't get impressed easily! I highly recommend this product!!!!!

title: A decent bag for a small kit
text:
Ordered this bag because as an EMT/FF who is also a county inspector for road/bridge projects, I wanted to put together a small kit of various bandages, tape, tourniquets, etc. to keep in my work truck, without constantly switching my large first aid kit from my personal truck all the time - and most of the pre-filled first aid kits "feature" items you never actually need in an emergency situation - or are completely useless (for example, a snake bite kit when the nearest venomous snake is 200+ miles away).

The overall size of this bag is exactly what I wanted - has plenty of room for a half dozen pairs of nitrile gloves, some coban, ace wraps, various gauze pad/rolls, SAM splints, tourniquets, etc. without being so bulky as to take up extra space in my truck, which is already crowded with survey equipment and coats/jackets for various working conditions. The two outside pockets will work well for the frequently used/quick access items (gloves, shears).

The inner liner/divider...is a joke. The liner is not attached to the bag in any way, shape, or form, and is too small for a snug fit - it is a good 1" shorter than the bag itself, so unless you always carry and store the bag flat, smaller items WILL end up underneath the liner. With the liner installed, there is a 1/4"-1/2" gap all the way around between it and the bag. Not ideal for a fully stocked kit riding in the truck. The divider not easy at all to get positioned -- I suspect it is meant to be attached with the velcro at the sides and bottom 'bent' to match the sides, but it's really too stiff for that, and the velcro has a VERY strong grip - great once you have it where you want it, but makes positioning difficult. My camera bag (with a similar divider type) has sewn in 'hinge' points to make installation of the divider easy. No such deal with this.

I will have to see once I get the bag fully stocked with the items I want to carry - maybe the liner will have enough rigidity to work; if so, I will be able to keep some 6x6 pads under it and out of the way. If not, I will probably get some heavy cardboard or a thin sheet of plastic and glue the liner to it to form a hard bottom. Just realize that in the product picture, for as 'floppy' as the inner liner looks, it's not nearly that strong in real life.

I’m amazed that people who claim to have “no clue” about what to expect or were angry because you can’t ingest this gave very bad reviews for this German chamomile. If you want a mild chamomile that smells pretty like the tea you drink, you want Roman chamomile. It’s relaxing - aroma therapeutic. If you want a powerful Medicinal Grade oil for wound healing, minor burns, immune system booster, and an anti-inflammatory, you want this German chamomile. I am never without “German” chamomile in my home apothecary. It should have STRONG smell and dark green color. If it does not, you have a diluted product. This is an excellent quality. If you’re new to ess. oils, there are three that work well together synergistically (or on their own): German chamomile, tea tree, and lavender. But each one has it own benefits, so read up. And do NOT ingest them. They’re for EXTERNAL use. I used this blend all the years my son was growing up instead of antibiotics for colds and skin abrasions and other things. title: Perfect for short 4b/c hair
text: So far so good but I just received it and immediately put it to use. I have short-ish 4c/very strong coiled hair and I just wanted something to stretch it out not necessarily straighten it. It was very hard to achieve what I wanted with just my blow dryer and come so I ordered this comb/brush So I plugged it in, turned it on to the first setting and waited--- when I went back to look at it, it had turned off. So I turned it on again and tried it on the second setting-- again after waiting 5-10 minutes it turned off again.  So I tried it a third time on the second setting and waited about 3-5 min.It warmed up to the temp and I proceeded to do my hair. I was SOOOOOO easy it was unbelievable. Again I just wanted it to lengthen not straighten, It did just that and it was so easy. I was similar to brushing my hair but because of how tight it was I did separate my hair and straightened that way. I'm sure on the higher setting it might have straightened it more but that wasn't what I wanted but it seems capable with more time and heat. So in about ten minutes I did my whole head and got the look I wanted-- I looked to turn it off and It had already turned off. I'm not sure if this is an automatic sensor that turns off after a certain time-- but sometimes it takes 20-30 minutes for some ladies to get the straightness and length they want, that can be annoying if you have to continuously look to see if it turned off and then wait for it to heat up again. I will update if anything changes or if I notice anything and will try to post a picture of before and after so you can better understand.

At first I was skeptical if this vacuum bag would even be able to contain the extremely fine dust that we make (sometimes sanding out to 220 grit). The results were incredible! The vacuum has more suction power and the bag contains all the dust. It even gets used on installs and tear outs, easily picking up nails, wood bits and other debris, all without rupturing the bag. I have been so impressed that I ordered a second vacuum bag for the back up 16 gal ridged shop vac.

title: Best. Massager Thingy. Ever.
text: This is by FAR the best back massager I've ever used (full disclosure - I've never had one of those crazy expensive massage chair things from Brookstone). I got one as a gift last Christmas, and liked it enough to get one for someone else this year. Everyone at Christmas was stealing it, so I know what gifts to get next year! I injured my back (not seriously) a couple years ago, and every once in awhile I get a nasty twinge just under my shoulder blade. title: Not for overweight people, warm environments and/or sitting long hours
text:
I weigh 240 lbs. and sit in a warm environment sometimes reaching 80 degrees. This cushion flattens out on me in temperatures over 65 degrees or when sitting for long hours. It's definitely not a cooling cushion and it causes my butt to sweat after a couple of hours. I moved it into my car for the winter and it supports me fine in relatively short trips under 20 miles, but as soon as it gets above 65 it flattens, so it's only good for short trips in the winter for me. It feels slightly lumpy (due to the wide columns) and moving around on it is uncomfortable because it conforms to your shape and locks in to it. So when you move, it feels like you're sitting on a hard, two-level surface. It only goes back to its original shape if you lift it up and shake it out or leave it alone for about an hour or so. I have to shake it at least 10 times a day. No joke. Also the cover isn't non-slip. I constantly have to push it back into position. Occasionally it slips right off the front of the chair!

I've been using it for 11 months and it hasn't permanently deformed yet and it shows no sigh of ever doing so. Oh, and the smell is a bit strong, but dissipates after a couple of weeks.
