title: We love this thing!!!!!
text:
First of all- my husband is a dentist and has chronic neck and back pain. He’s always wanted a massage chair, but the prices always seemed too high. We took a chance on this chair as a Christmas gift, and months later he still thanks me for making the purchase. He sits in it daily and has had a tremendous amount of relief as a result.

PROS:
-Works extremely well for back, legs, feet, and forearms.

-Comparable to more expensive chairs we’ve tried at Brookstone.

-Allows for custom settings to either provide full or concentrated spot massaging focus with kneading, shiatsu, or simple vibration.

-Customizable in how far back you can recline.

-The benefits of the legs and feet massagers were a huge added bonus, and helped some pain that my husband didn’t realize he had.

-Rollers are strong and can be adjusted for narrow or wide reach.

-Setup was easy and took 15 minutes or so.

-The seller and delivery folks were wonderful. They actually called to notify us that our original chair had been damaged in transit. Instead of giving us the damaged chair, they ordered and delivered a new one so we wouldn’t have to deal with setting up and then returning a faulty chair. Their customer service, honesty, and integrity was very much appreciated.

NEUTRAL:
- the heat works but not well enough to really comment on it being a PRO. We didn’t purchase this chair for that reason, however.

CONS:
- Like many chairs, this isn’t the best for neck. It’ll reach your neck and provide some comfort, but some of the other neck specific massagers do a better job.

-The remote beep is loud when you’re moving the manual settings to spot adjust or decline the chair. We haven’t found a way to lower the volume, but it’s only a minor nuisance until you reach your desired spot.

-The massagers get louder if you use the chair for extended periods of time (1+ hour). This isn’t an issue necessarily, but we were worried we had damaged the chair. That wasn’t case, however. It’s still working perfectly. Just be aware that it may happen.

OVERALL:

We felt like we were taking a gamble on this chair, given that we hadn’t tried it, and we were nervous about such an expensive purchase. But nearly two months later, we absolutely love this chair, and our family may actually be purchasing another one.

Highly recommend this for anyone looking for a comparable chair at an affordable price!

Happy Flossing!

title: It's a Tea Tree Product
text:
This is a good quality topical salve. It is very soothing and healing to the skin and the 2 ounce jar actually turns out to be quite a bit of product.
The smell is not anything stinky like a neem product per say, but it simply has the antiseptic scent that comes with any Melaleuca plant extract, especially tea tree. But that is a small price to pay to have the healing and antiseptic properties of this sought after plant.
I actually had a friend who stole my first jar because it was helping heal some of her foot sores much faster than they were without it (and she is not a fan of tea tree usually...)

They do not put a bunch of extra fillers and unnecessary junk in it, just 5 quality healing ingredients: Organic Calendula flowers in a base of organic unrefined olive oil, beeswax, tea tree oil, grapefruit seed extract.

The Calendula turns the salve orange but it does not leave your skin orange. The medicinal scent of the tea tree takes away any aroma from the Calendula flowers but that does weaken once it has soaked into your skin. It does seem to melt into the skin easily (a testament that they have not overprocessed or obilterated the natural ingredients) and it is gentle enough to use directly on the delicate skin of the face as well.
We use it just like we would Neosporin, over cuts, bites, small wounds, etc. Overall a great product and you can't beat the price.
If looking for a salve that is a natural healing alternative to neosporin but with a less medicinal scent than check out some Moon Valley Organic's healing salves.

title: Save Time and Money Cleaning Contacts
text:
Originally, I used to use multi-all purpose solution for cleaning my contacts, but a friend recommended using this because it was overall better at cleaning contacts with less effort. I've been using this brand contact solution for about three years now, and it is definitely worth purchasing.

First off, you save time cleaning your contacts at the end of the day or after wear. You don't necessarily have to pre-rinse your contacts or rub the contacts with cleaning solution. You simply take out the contacts, place them in the container, fill with fluid, and let the solution do all the work. The formula/ingredients hasn't given my eyes any issues as long as the instructions are followed.

Not only does this save you time, but I've noticed my contacts lasted longer because I didn't have to rub the contacts myself to clean them (my guess is that it doesn't introduce micro-tears into the lenses from rubbing with the finger, thus the lenses last longer over time).

If you value time and money, it's definitely worth the purchase!

text:
I have used this type of system for years. Usually the Walgreens knockoff brand (which I will probably go back to) This package is for 2 12 oz bottles and one case. The one case you get does not last for 2 bottles, barely even one bottle.

When I purchased this I had to use up my flex spending money so I bought 8 packs, thinking that would last me for a long time. I have almost gone though all the cases and still have 8 bottles left. Once my eyes start to burn I change a case and that is usually after 1 bottle, sometimes it doesn't even make it through one bottle.

I have contacted Alcon, they asked me all kinds of questions and insisted that the case should last for 2 12 oz. bottles worth of use and couldn’t even fathom that it wasn't working for me. They were not remotely helpful.

Well my eyes don't lie, they start to burn after one bottle (sometimes about 3/4 of the way through one bottle). After going back and forth with Alcon about getting some extra cases, (which they repeatedly said they cannot send) they did eventually send me a few travel size packs with an 8 oz. bottle that have a case so I now have some extra cases. Though I will still be short on cases for the amount of bottles I currently have.

Now I have a bunch of travel size bottles to go with my collection of 12 oz bottles.

What I have started doing is dumping out the clear care and filling the case with saline solution in the morning, and letting the lenses soak in there for 10 minutes or so. That keeps the burning away. I am not sure if they are getting clean.

I will probably go back to buying the knockoff brand. I don't know who makes it, but I know I never had this issue until I started using Alcon. Use at your own risk is all I can say.

title: I really like this product
text:
I really like this product! Whenever I apply these on my contacts, they feel like they become a new pair. It completely rejuvinates your contacts which is awesome because contacts are already expensive. Thus ill buy anything that will extend their use time. This is a deep cleaner so I use it once a week or more depending on how dirty they become. This especially great in ALLERGY season as they wipe all the pollen out. Some people use it everyday like a regular contact solution but I think thats overkill. This deep cleaner is good on a weekly basis. It comes with a vial that you can use to clean the contacts. Be careful because when you fill the vial, it will overflow if the surface is uneven. The peroxide will breakdown to saline and this reaction causes bubbles that will spill out if you pour more peroxide than the marked line in the vial. The vial itself has two "arms" that you place you contacts in. One of the "arms" are marked with a small "R". This is where you put your right contact. The other one does not have a letter and thats where you put the left contact in.
Keep in mind that it takes 7 hours for the peroxide to breakdown to saline. If you wear them before the 7 hours, then it will burn your eyes because the solution has not broken down to saline. This is not fault in this specific product, its just peroxide cleaners in general. Also dont be decieved by the bottle size. It goes by fairly fast because you have to use a decent amount for every cleanse. Overall, I really like this product

title: Clear Care. Must Buy.
text:
This amazing product is what I’ve been missing for the last 5 to 10 years! If only I’d discovered it sooner. Make sure you read the directions before using it though. I didn’t and almost blinded myself. Lesson learned.

I purchased it from a local box store, hoping it would do a better job of cleaning my contacts. I routinely feel eye fatigue and was throwing away perfectly good contacts prematurely because they weren’t getting clean enough using (only) my normal contact solution. Because of this, I recently switched to using two sets of contact lenses, which I’d hoped would allow the contacts to soak longer, and get cleaner, after wearing.

Ultimately, the missing solution was Clear Care. I now use this once every 2 to 4 weeks to give my lenses that deep clean they’ve been missing. It’s eliminated the tired eyes feeling I usually get after 15 to 20 days of use, and they feel new and cleaner than ever.

I let my lenses soak for the recommended time of 6 hours, if not longer, then clean, rinse and soak them (overnight), using my normal contact solution. I wear them the following day while putting the other set of contacts through the same steps. If you wear contacts, using Clear Care will extend the life of your contacts, whether daily, weekly, monthly, etc. For me, Clear Care has been a life and money saver.

title: Mixed review
text:
When this product works, it does a very good job of cleaning. For better results, I have taken to cleaning my lenses with another solution (Renu) and then soak them in Clear Care. Without rubbing the lenses in the other solution, there is some debris that can irritate the eye. Unfortunately the solution is too harsh to handle directly on the skin on a regular basis.

The problem with this product is that every so often, the solution fails to neutralize completely and you are left with an eye burn. The problem must be with the case, because usually for me it is just one of the eyes. It is a real nuisance when it happens, because it really stings and the lens would be unwearable for the day if you didn't have a backup solution. (Usually, I rinse it in the Renu and put it in and take it out multiple times with rewetting drops to try to dilute the Clear Care. It still stings but goes away after awhile -- there is a lingering worry that it might cause lasting damage.)

Another problem is that sometimes the solution bubbles out so much from the top hole that there isn't enough to cover the lenses, so the top edges dry out by the morning. If closed very tightly, it helps a bit, but the case should be placed in a dish or cup to avoid the solution spilling onto surfaces and damaging them.

title: Product needs a clearer warning
text:
While the product itself does a very good job of cleaning, the manufacturer should be on notice that it needs to do a better job of distinguishing its product from the typical all-in-one lens cleaners and warning newcomers to its product of the potential dangers of assuming it is the same, unless it is fine with injuring new customers.

For a start, the bottle and box it comes in should be a different size and shape, just to get the message across, this is a DIFFERENT product that yoru typical lens cleaner and the instructions MUST be followed or severe eye injury may occur. If packaged the same as the others, the manufacturer can assume that the customer will not read the instructions, because who knows, the person using the product might be extremely exhausted or drunk or whatever, and not think twice about popping the lenses with this solution in the old case. For myself, I had originally opted to use my old case, because the case that came with it requires much more solution, and it seemed like a such a waste. When I took out the second lens, I must have had a tiny bit of solution on my fingers because it burned -- I instantly knew it wasn't the same product, thankfully without causing damage. I then read up on the product online, and about cases of new users who didn't read the label and ended up hurt.

The first sentence on the label warns not to put it directly in your eye, or burning will occur; a similar sentence appears on the ordinary, much milder solution. While the warning is in red, it would do nothing for those with red-green colorblindness -- additional signals are required. The second sentence warns to use the product only with the special case provided. That really should be the very first sentence and in huge, capital letters, explaining why this step is absolutely necessary. The idea that the solution needs to be neutralized,and that the case must interact with the solution to neutralize it would be counter-intuitive to most new customers. The majority of new users switching to this product from Complete or Renu, etc. will automatically assume that it can used the same way.

While this product works very well, I am giving it one star to signal to the manufacturer that they need to do a much better job of warning new users and distinguishing their product. The potential for injury for those who aren't vigilant is too great.

UPDATE: This morning, the hydrogen peroxide on the right contact lens did not neutralize properly, and it hurt badly. I'm wearing glasses today as a precaution. Usually when I open the case, the lens is on the convex bit of the case -- but this morning it was lodged on the concave portion. Don't know if that makes a difference, but perhaps it was situatied in a way that made it less accessible to getting neutralized. Guess that must have been it since the left lens was fine.

The new cases (with blue tops) only work for about 5 days.  On the 6th day, when I put my contacts in, I feel a burning sensation.  This has happened to me 3 times.  There's only one new case per dual pack so I've gone through 3 packs now.  I called Alcon after the first occurrence, they were very nice asked me to return the solution and case with a return shipping label they would send in the mail.  They also said they would send me replacement products.  I have returned all the products to them and received zero replacement products.  I'm happily using the generic drugstore hydrogen peroxide product now.  If I ever get the replacement products, I'll give them a try and post another review.

They should really design their product so that the liquid itself is of different color, which would make a mistake immediately obvious. As of now, it's too easy damage the eye and screw up the day.

title: Sorely disappointed with the product -- Not working as advertised
text:
Sorely disappointed with the product -- definitely not consistent with some of the higher rated reviews on here. Perhaps I got a defective model?

At the very least, the scale only changes by increments of 0.8 (not 0.2 as advertised), and the scale readings are completely inconsistent for my weight. Sometimes it'll record a weight differential of up to 3 pounds in a span of 30 seconds!

I have even tested the accuracy of the weights by standing on the scale, recording it, and then measuring myself again holding a 15 pound dumbbell and checking if the displayed weight would increase by around 15 pounds. Instead, I've been getting huge fluctuations with this test. Sometimes my weight increases by around 12 pounds... sometimes it'll change by up to 19 pounds. It's not like my dumbbell is changing weight spontaneously.

I bodybuild and carefully track my weight, so I have no use for a scale that reads +/- 4-5 pounds on a given reading.

Again, I could just have a defective copy, but either way, I'll probably by a different scale from another vendor. Is there a way to refund this?

title: The only thing that's really preventing me from giving this five stars is the fact that it's a good idea to be careful getting o
text: I got this to help me keep track of a new fitness program I'm trying, and it works! Simple, seems durable (Having gotten used to older scales, I was a bit nervous about the tempered glass—but I shouldn't have been!), with a clear display that's quick about taking each reading. It even does this neat thing where it flashes to let you know it's "captured" your weight—as in, no fluctuations while you're standing on it! The only thing that's really preventing me from giving this five stars is the fact that it's a good idea to be careful getting on. The scale is supported by three feet towards the center of the underside, so there are edges that aren't really supported. For most people, you'd probably get on towards the center of the scale, so you'll probably be fine. But for the hilariously clumsy (like me) or people with balance issues, tipping the scale over by stepping on the edge instead of the middle might be an issue. (I miiiiiiight have already done so once.) Still, that might even be just user error; otherwise, this was a great buy.

title: False Precision, But Basically Works
text:
I am not in the habit of writing reviews, but buyers should be aware of a few things. First, it is a piece of glass resting on top of four circular pads, so you will not be under illusions about why it is so cheap. Second, it is not obvious how to turn it on, the directions are incoherent. There is a battery compartment on the back with a tiny unlabeled switch inside of it. Left is Kg, right is Lbs.

I'm fairly indifferent to these aesthetic details. However, the display implies it has a precision to one decimal place, but it is not actually that precise. When I got back home from work I was exactly two pounds lighter. I picked up a textbook and was exactly three pounds heavier. Testing it again, it was bouncing back and forth by 1.2 pounds, sometimes giving one or the other answer.

I have not tested other scales yet to check for accuracy (if it is consistently biased by some number from actual weight), but it is the weight differences that really matter, so I do not hugely care and will just adjust it in my head. There is no way to reset the tare weight. It will still roughly do what I need to police myself in a downward or stationary trend. If you expect the scale to reveal some infallible, metaphysical truth about yourself, you should probably buy a more expensive one.

title: Cheap bathroom scale. It works, but not exactly quality.
text:
Cheap bathroom scale. Looks cheap, feels cheap, is cheap. It does seem to provide weight consistently, but also very clearly, price is the strongest selling point. The glass just feels a bit...cheap, as does the plastic on the bottom. If you're in America and are using the English weight system, note that although the weight is given to the tenth of a pound, the scale doesn't actually measure weight in pounds. Instead, it appears to weigh in kilograms, then does a conversion to pounds (which means that you'll always see the weight go up and down in increments of 0.6 lbs.)

I am probably going to keep it until it breaks, but I wouldn't buy it again -- I don't want to bother with the effort of returning it because it does actually work, and seems to be consistent. It is just obviously a cheap product made in China.

title: Inconsistent and innaccurate. Or, on the bright side, great for those who want to be in denial about weight fluctuations
text:
As pretty and compact as this very nice-looking bathroom scale is, it has real problems with consistency and accuracy. Its fluid relationship with the truth is like being lied to by a cheating boyfriend about your weight every day. I ask it, "is my booty getting big?" and step on like a fool so it can tell me, "No, honey. You're as thin and beautiful as you were yesterday. And the day before. And the day before. And the day before that. No really. Exactly as thin and beautiful. Exactly. Exactly the same weight. To the ounce. You're holding a bowling ball now? Well, then that must mean that you're *losing* weight! Congratulations! Now go make me a sandwich."

Sadly, I have found this scale to be incapable of registering more than one reading per rough pound of body mass. If you're 102 lbs, give or take, it will tell you you're 102.4 until you edge up another half a pound or so, and then you'll jump up to register as 103.6. Never 103.2, 103.4, 103.8, it only knows 103.6. Adjust your footing and you're mysteriously and miraculously at exactly the same 102.4 from the day prior. Take off shoes or heavy clothing or put down your gargantuan smartphone whose manufacturer specs clock at half a pound in its kevlar advanced bomb suit case and see no change on the display. Not even a fraction of a pound. Pick up your purse and discover that it will cycle through the single weight it knows for each one-pound increment until it settles on its half-hearted guess. Put your purse back down and it refunds all that weight to you, save for one pound that is maybe some sort of rounding error or restocking fee, I'm not sure. Step off and back on and you're at your "original" weight, presumably having burned off that pesky pound doing step aerobics on your scale in search of an accurate reading.

Losing some weight? No you're not. Or maybe you are. It's a mystery. That 195.6 lb reading gotten by the second party tester you brought in to see if the scale would be more cooperative with another user will suddenly drop to 192.4, where it will stay until another pound or more is shed, and it will tell you then that he may or may not have moved into the next one-pound weight class. Or wait until he has a tantrum and shifts his left foot, at which point it will show another lost pound while mocking you under its breath.

I know that accuracy isn't that big a deal or terribly reliable with home bathroom scales, but this one truly seems like it's not even trying and is outright incapable of registering anything but preprogrammed weights, one per pound. I have no idea what I weigh right this second, but I know my doctor's office and gym scales agree that this one is playing head games with me. Either that, or I am gaining and losing brain mass trying to compute mathematical and histographical averages all the time in an attempt to divine my true weight from the scale that lives in my bathroom.

I gave it 2 stars because it looks nice and I suppose if you are just looking for a rough order of magnitude estimate of your weight, it will do the job.

title: Fantastic scale!
text:
A few days ago, my wife and I purchased the Fitbit Aria as a tool to track our weight loss and to maintain our weight once we achieved our goals. We were on the fence about whether to purchase the Withings or the Aria. After a bit or research, we decided on the Aria for 2 reasons: first, the Aria was $30 cheaper and secondly, many of the reviews comparing the 2 scales preferred the Aria. The scale is fantastic. It integrates very well with the fitbit web site (setting up an account is free), it looks good, and it is pretty accurate (with 10 weigh-ins on both the Aria and the scale that I was using at the gym, the Aria is consistently less than a ½ pound off of the gym scale). The scale also determines your percent body fat as well as your BMI (once you create an account on the website, you enter age, height, etc.). I can't speak to the accuracy of the body fat calculation because I have never had that calculated. It does fluctuate from time to time even though my weight may not (after doing a little research, I found that your percent body fat can change depending on how much water you have been drinking).

I want to address an issue that I saw brought up in a few consumer reviews (an issue that I was worried about initially because I found the reviews after I had ordered the scale). A few of the reviews that I read mentioned that the set up of the scale was difficult. One of the reviews was written by an "IT guy" and he mentioned that the software set up for the scale was not written correctly (not quite sure how he knew that!). Anyway, I am pretty computer illiterate and I found the setup to be about as simple as it could be. The only issue that I had (and I probably should not call it an issue) was the initial linking of the scale to my wireless network. I had the scale in the same room as my computer and router and it would not link. I assumed that would have been close enough! After 2 unsuccessful attempts, I look at the instructions again and saw that the scale needed to be placed on a flat surface next to router. I placed the scale on the table right next to the router and it synced the next attempt. Once we synced the scale, we moved it into the bathroom and have had no issues.

Setting up additional users is also a breeze by simply sending them an invite to the scale via their fitbit account email address. The information between multiple users can either be private or shared, depending on how that fitbit account is configured.

I don't usually write product reviews unless I find the product exceptional, and I found the Aria to be exceptional! Although the price point is a bit high, I would recommend this product to anyone who was on a weight loss journey or just wanted to maintain a healthy lifestyle!

text: I'm a podiatrist and I recommend these all of the time to patients. They are second only to a great custom orthotic. These are generally ideal for people with a mildly flat foot to high arch that need a little extra support. They work best in an athletic shoe with a removable insole. I wear them in my shoes and boots that I get very dirty so that I don't ruin my custom orthotics (which I still prefer personally). I do have some patients that prefer these over their custom orthotics. You can't beat the price. Expect them to last 6-12 months depending upon how much you wear them and in what conditions. Now I just step on the scale and it gives me my weight and body fat and then a check mark to let me know it has been uploaded to the FitBit site. The scale looks very durable with the glass top and is definitely not an eyesore (I have the black version). If you have a FitBit Ultra Tracker this scale is a MUST...it automatically uploads your weight and body fat to the FitBit site and helps you track your goals easily. title: Battery Life Sucks
text:
The pros of this chair is that it is light, foldable, relatively cheap and small. I can use it to go up small hills, get on buses and do most of my business.

The Cons are 1) irrational battery life and 2)instability in turning- it tips over a lot if you go too fast. You have to go very slowly around turns.

I've had this chair for about three years. When the batteries are fresh they will work for anywhere from 3 to 9 months. Then, after that period, depending on how much you pay for the batteries, it will go to about half power after about 20-30 minutes. When this happens the scooter goes very slowly and won't take most small hills, even 2" sidewalk lip.

I bought batteries on Ebay for about $60 each and they worked for about three months and then conked-out after twenty minutes. Then I went to a store locally and paid $100 for each and they lasted about 11 months before they went to half power after twenty minutes. I don't know why this happens. I have had this chair checked for defects three times, each time paying an extra $75-100 a pop and each time they said there is nothing wrong with the chair. Yet I know there IS something wrong with the chair because no batteries function to specifications. This is for both the 12 mile or 18 mile version, the result is the same. They go about 3 miles before the batteries go to half power. I think there are a lot of crooked dealers there; however this chair is ALSO a POS. Its cheap but its not a bargain. You can't take it anywhere heavy-duty or you're putting your life in your hands. Don't rely on it. I've had to ask bystanders for help lots of times to get myself out of jams. This shouldn't happen. It should go 12-18 miles. It doesn't.

None of the hairs have come off during lathering or shaving. The black handle is plastic and feels light in my hand. I wish it had a nicer heft, but I'm not deducting any stars for that since it's part of the reason this brush has a nice price point. There are plenty of brushes out there wish silver handles if you want to splurge, but this brush is an excellent choice for those on a budget.

title: A good buy
text:
I purchased this dryer in November, 2014 and wanted to use it at least a few months before reviewing. During my research, I found a lot of reviews that indicated stand dryers tend to be top heavy and unstable. When I first set it up (by myself, if I may add) it was indeed tilting and I was afraid it would fall so I leaned it against a chair for stability. Later when my guy friend took a look at it, he tightened the bolts and wallah - it was stable and sturdy. I have not had to lean it against anything and have no fear that it will fall and shatter. I am now very comfortable with the stability.

This unit has a nice window and flips up and down for ease of getting under the dryer. The dyer is quite loud, so having a conversation is difficult while using the dryer.

I have natural hair and I have sat under this dryer - which is my least favorite thing to do, but now I can do it in my home :-)... anyway, back to the heat settings ..... I find that I need to be under the dryer for just about 60 minutes to get my hair dried. I don't use the very hot setting so this may be the reason it takes a bit longer to dry my hair.

OH - the instructions ...uhm...forget about it. Did the manufacturer think the assembly was intuitive....whatever! I did find a youtube video and I was able to follow that to get mine set up.

Overall, I do enjoy having and using this dryer and it allows me more flexibility with different hair styles that require the use of a dryer. Now if I only had more time...

title: Fantastic device for less stress, improved mood, and better sleep!
text: I love my Cove! In a nutshell, it's relaxing... and if you're someone who suffers from stress or depression (like I do), healthy relaxation is truly priceless. I have tried all variety of ways to improve my energy and mood, ranging from prescription medication to vitamins to Accupuncture and yoga. And I've also tried ways that are less healthy, like drinking alcohol... but if you're a fellow stress-case, you know how frustrating the wellness journey can be. What's awesome about Cove is that it's 100% healthy, easy to use (and re-use), and it makes me feel more "zen" in the space of ten minutes or less. I use it at least twice a day because it's easy to put on when I'm working at my desk, watching TV, or cooking, etc. I've also worn it while doing gentle yoga and that was really beneficial... which is to say, it works any time but even better when combined with a mindfulness practice. Initially, it takes a little experimentation to fit it to your head and adjust the intensity settings to optimize the "good vibe" feeling that it gives you... but that's about it in terms of a learning curve. I sometimes use it without the app, but I do prefer using the app to track how often I use it and what times of day seem to work best. For example, I have found that multiple daytime sessions are more beneficial for my sleep than a session right before bed (probably because it keeps my overall stress levels from building up over the course of the day..?) Whatever the reason, I'm super-grateful to have discovered a tool that helps me feel better. I really hate taking medication for sleep and/or depression and Cove gives me hope that I can stay on track without pills that affect my brain chemistry. Thanks, Cove!

I think this is a great product for children learning how to swallow, for those with sensitive gag reflexes and those chronically ill.

title: It's Far From Perfect
text:
The Deluxe Pedal Exerciser from Isokinetics Inc. Isn't a perfect piece of exercise equipment, but works well enough to at least keep you active during the work day. If you're like me, you work anywhere from eight to ten hours a day, and exercise is definitely a necessity, but not necessarily something you have the time or desire to do once you get home at night. This machine helps me keep active by allowing me to peddle here and there throughout the day, and keep my metabolism moving and calories burning.

Now, with that said, this is not the kind of "bike" I would recommend for someone who is looking for a fast paced, heart rate raising workout. It's a light weight piece of equipment, so it probably wouldn't hold up to that kind of routine, nor does it function well when used as such. I find it's perfect for a nice paced rotation of the pedals, and it keeps me from being sedentary all day. The end result is that hopefully I'll drop a few pounds here and there as my metabolism speeds up, but I'm not necessarily banking on that.

It's important to note that your weight could be a key factor in how well the machine operates - if at all. I'm roughly 260 pounds, and I was able to keep the pedals rotating fairly fluent without the machine moving or shifting. Someone else in my office who was roughly 120 pounds couldn't even get the thing to work. It wobbled, and slid on her. Admittedly the pedals are a little stiff regardless of whether you get it working right or not, but I'm hoping with use that this will ease up over time.

For now I give it three stars. As long as it holds up to the use, and keeps me mobile throughout the day then I'll be getting what I expected for my purchase.

title: Does excacty what it promises
text:
A few years ago, I used this culture to make a batch of cultured vegetables; kimchi. It worked exactly like it was supposed to and I didn't have to overload on the salt. Kim simply means "vegetable" in Korean, or so I understand. Besides the usual cabbage, I've seen Korean kimchi made from daikon and cucumber.

For cultured vegetables, it's best to use vegetables with a fairly low water content, since a high water vegetable, like celery, will disintegrate in mater of three or so days. I've made cultured vegetable mixes with carrots, daikon, beets and crushed red pepper flakes for a little heat. Since I'd chopped the veggies into small enough pieces, my former half-Korean neigbor said he would use it as salsa and that it had a nice heat. I hadn't thought of it, but that's a good use for cultured vegetables.

text:
Unlike all the other reviewers, I did NOT receive this product at a discount, unfortunately. It was definitely worth it though. My five year old daughter was having accidents every night even after going a few weeks with none. We were expecting a baby and wanted to get her bedwetting under control. I believed she was sleeping too deeply to realize she needed to go during the night so that's what prompted me to buy this. LO and behold, 3 days of using it and the problem was fixed, with the exception of one accident about a week and a half in.

It took a minute to figure out good placement so that it didn't give a false alarm, we found it worked best when clipped on two layers, so I just folded her underwear in the spot I wanted and then clipped it on, also worked well on the side, where the seam is.

Also, after wearing for 3 weeks straight, the wires started popping out in a few places, thus was the only major issue, but it didn't effect it's function at all.

Bottom line: I tried everything under the sun to try and stop her bedwetting which was happening every night for months, and this alarm worked. Took 3 days, and she has been accident free for over 2 months now. It was easy to use and definitely worth it in our case.

title: Like and dislike
text: I love that these have so much room for pills.  You can see by the pic that I can fit 6 capsule size (including Vit D which is huge) and three other pills.  I like that they have labels for the days of the week and that it has an outer case to keep them all together.  I love that I can take out one day and carry it with me because it is so small.  I am using it as a month long med container.  I take pills twice a day but hate filling my med container so I put them all in the same slot and take the am leaving the pm for that night.  I dislike that they are rounded at the top as it makes it really hard to get out the individual day compartment.  I hate that on Sunday's day the 3 slot down doesn't close at all.  It came that way.  I contacted the seller within two days of receiving the product.  It has been one week and I have heard nothing from them.  I had already filled the entire month of meds and when closing the container realized the one out of 28 slots didn't close or otherwise I would have returned it right away.  So note to anyone who buys check each compartment before filling so if it is broke it can be returned.  I ordered two of these and the other came fine.  The second pic shows a size comparison.  The container in the top right is the one I bought.  The one on the left is a 3 a day med container that holds even more than this container and the one on the bottom is a 4 a day that we use as a monthly one for a kid who takes less meds.

title: Warning: it can change your granite stone color
text:
I purchased cleaner, sealer, and polisher and was excited to use because of good reviews. Unfortunately, I used in incorrect order of polish then sealer (I am unsure last sealer use). The stone color changed, more like all the black streaks that I didn't notice as much popped out as black as can be as well as some pinkish spots in yellow brown granite. With added new shine, the black streaks looked terrible. I contacted the seller, she said this can happen when granite cleaned and polished. And she gets this kind of complaints from panicked customers all the time (even with correct order of use). And some people don't like their new look. She recommended to reseal again. I am afraid to use their products again. I highly recommend to try on small area first before applying whole area. Because you might end up with totally different new look that you might not like.

P.s. according to granite expert guy I spoke to, he said it can happen with certain products with oil containing and recommended PH neutral gentle cleaner. He said overtime the darkened color might lighten up.

title: Perfect for Chocolate Cravings
text:
Are you in need of a chocolate fixation but stuck on the keto diet? Look no further as this cocoa MCT powder is perfect for those cravings. One container yields 30 scoops which should last up to almost a month if you use once a day. I have been using this powder for a month and haven't stepped out of ketosis once! The chocolate overwhelms the coffee taste, but you can add more cold coffee if you want to balance the chocolate and coffee taste. You can also use this product in the form of hot chocolate which tastes really good when you add SweetLeaf stevia to it. I haven't tried it yet, but I can bet money that you can use this as a chocolate flavor for a keto dessert such as cheesecake if you were ever to try to make one.

I want to point out for anyone cautious of carbs to take note that one serving does contain 3g of carbs, so don't overdo it. Overall, I highly recommend this product if you have a hankering for chocolate.

title: Proven product
text: I purchased Dr. Mercola Culture starter kit to make sure my sauerkraut got a good start with the right probiotics to ferment. I have used organic cabbage and carrots previously thinking the starter kit was an unnecessary cost. After 2 weeks my kraut did ferment and had a taste of having the fermentation I needed. After using this culture kit and only @ 1 week the fermenting had a very different taste and more what I was looking for.The taste was tart/salty/crunchy and much better tasting than anything I have previously purchased from the store. In my recipe there is an added ground up apple(without core or skin) to feed the bacteria...does not make it sweet. When eating the finished product I recommend small amounts at first until your gut gets used to the new addition to the bacteria already there(can make you gassy at first). I have made several batches with this Culture kit so far and have enjoyed every jar so far with no throw aways. I use the pickle pip fermentation lids http://www.amazon.com/Pickle-Pipe-One-Piece-Waterless-Fermentation/dp/B01726CJ9Y and quart jars to make my Kraut and find that it works out nicely. With many other Culture kits one the market I decided on Dr. Mercola brand because of his trusted name and I am glad I did.Would highly recommend this product to anyone starting fermentation to get the best results right away. Thank you Dr. Mercola.

I had received this ionizer at a discounted price during a promotional offer in exchange for an honest review, I love it and I love the company stands behind their product offer a full one year warranty! I posted the warranty below, that is awesome! This would make a great gift for any smokers or people with seasonal allergies too!

"We stand by our product and offer a money back guarantee if not satisfied with a full ONE YEAR warranty. Pure Ionics is dedicated to making our customers happy and we will go to every length to ensure you are happy with your purchase."

title: Great Knee Sleeves made by Copper Care
text: I received the Copper Knee Sleeves at a discounted price to provide a honest review of this product.  I have seen these in stores and have stopped and read the package a couple of times but have always put them back thinking that they would not help with my condition. I have nerve damage and Fibromyalgia and walking up and down steps can be extremely painful for me, but at a discounted price I though what the heck, so I bought them and gave them a try and they are great.  When I received the product I was not convinced that they would so anything for me as they are just a little thicker than what a pair of pantyhose are and I thought no way will they give me enough support.  Although it is still extremely painful to climb up and down the stairs; I had more range in motion wearing these.  I have currently wore these for almost a week and even my sister stated to me that I was doing better on the stairs and I told her it was because of the knee sleeves that I was testing.  The only thing that I would say negative is they run small or I needed an extra large set.

title: Made by an MLM company but still a great product.
text:
I first heard about this product like 5 years ago from the alex jones show. Dude's hilarious and I bought this product out of curiosity. I bought from some of his advertisers over the years and have been pleasantly surprised each time. This product was no exception.

It's basically a multivitamin you can mix in a water bottle, shake it up, and have a juicy tasting beverage that gives you energy. I usually end up taking it twice, breakfast and some time after lunch. Tastes good and really made me feel energized. It definitely quenches that sugar / fructose craving I get in the mid day. It also makes me feel pretty good throughout the day.

This stuff could also be useful for hikers and outdoorsmen who need these vitamins for sustained energy. Put it in a little container and mix it with your water.

There are some cons to this product you should be aware of, though.

1. It's expensive. You can get stuff 75% cheaper as chewies and pills.

2. Youngevity MLM sellers advertise and spam on health forums and sometimes claim their products can cure and prevent diseases. That doesn't make the product *bad* however. Most MLM's try to recruit everyone they come in contact with and this one doesn't do that. It's actually one of the better companies out there.

Overall I highly suggest this product to all my friends and I'm not even a partner. I just love this product. There is nothing else like it.

title: Maybe the best of its type, but definitely cannot be considered high fidelity
text:
Although these were supposedly designed for loud music, and promise to "not deform the sound" , they definitely do not attenuate the entire audible band equally. I tried them with headphones on and found that the higher frequencies are attenuated much more than the lower frequencies. Unlike "dumb" fiber or foam earplugs, these do let some of the highs through, but the overwhelming passage of the bass frequencies eliminate any possibility of hearing a reasonably flat/balanced sound through them.

To their credit, these sound no worse than any other brands of passive high fidelity ear protection I've tried. They just aren't much better either.

Oh, one more quibble: these will not fit if you have relatively small ear canals. I struggled for 10 minutes each to get them in.

title: Good product and excellent customer service
text:
I ordered this for my brother who was badly debilitated by COVID. He is 6'2" and about 260 pounds. This rollator fits him pretty well considering how tall he is. His forearms rest on the pads and he has to lean forward a little bit.

He lost most of his hand and wrist function due to COVID so the upright position of the brakes is in the perfect place for him. The brakes have just enough resistance that he can safely operate them. They are secure and can lock when needed.

He used it pretty extensively for about 5 months when we noticed one of the forearm pads had cracked and the assembly for collapsing it had broken from so much use. I wrote to the company and explained how beneficial their product was and asked if there was a warranty or if there were replacement parts. They were very prompt and extremely accommodating and sent an entirely new device! My brother has now used that one for just over 2 months with no issues. He currently has 3 different walker styles and this is his favorite. He never uses it for seating so I cannot speak to that.

Pros:
Easy to assemble
Lightweight
Fairly sturdy at full extension even when used by a large man
Maneuvers extremely well
Upright hand brakes are easy to use and work well
Excellent customer service

Cons:
The trick to collapsing it is to reach underneath and release the clips. They are also attached to a handle in the seat (it lies flat so no worries when you sit down) but repeated pulling will stretch the metal clips and prevent them from working correctly.
Once fully extended (for my brother's height) the arms do not easily retract for loading into a car. I could have tried something like silicone spray and that probably would have fixed it, but I have a small SUV so it didn't matter.

Over all he is thoroughly happy with this item and the customer service. Of all the pictures I have of him, I don't have a good one of him using the rollator!

title: If you get muscle cramps it's most likely due to low Magnesium levels
text: Magnesium is one of the underrated minerals and is often overlooked by medical professionals because there is very little of it in serum so blood tests can't determine if you are getting an adequate amount of it. Magnesium resides inside all of our cells and its function is to calm muscles (including the heart), nerves and the brain. If you stress these systems with intense exercise, sleep deprivation or not enough fuel (food) muscle cramps can be the result. Meat and dark leafy greens are naturally high in Magnesium but as you cook these foods the magnesium is stripped out of the food. Avoid boiling vegetables and opt to steam them instead. When cooking meat capture the drippings and add it back as sauce or gravy. I am a mountain climber and ultra runner with a heavy training schedule. Since it is difficult to acquire the magnesium I need to fuel my activity level through food I add in a magnesium chloride supplement every fourth month. I take 3 capsules for 20 days as recommended by Dr. Volek in his book "The Art and Science of Low Carbohydrate Performance". There are many different types of magnesium supplements out there but NOT all are created equal! Avoid magnesium oxide as this causes diarrhea and only a small amount is absorbed by the body because it passes right through you. Magnesium gluconate is made up of mostly 'gluconate' which is a form of sugar so these pills do not actually contain as much magnesium as they do carbohydrate. Magnesium chloride (found in this supplement) is the form you want because it is a slow release capsule increasing the amount of absorption of the supplement by your body. title: Defective out of the box, Returned and will NOT re-order
text:
[[VIDEOID:187157bb478d88678cfebe2fd954a3a8]] [[ASIN:B0015TGAMW Life/Form CPR Prompt BLUE Single Infant Manikin w/10 Lung Bags & Tool - LF06002U by Life/Form]]

I purchased 4 of these infant manikins to help with teacher CPR. I saw the price was quite a bit less than the others so I went with it knowing going the look and feel of them which are less quality.

It's weird, but I was actually excited opening up the boxes. I read the instructions and looked over all the items included. I placed a lung in the manikin which is kind of cumbersome compared to other manikins I've used but that's okay. As mentioned in another review, being able to see the chest rise can be difficult sometimes and requires a little practice which is fine.

Then I noticed by accident that when I picked up one belly facing the ground, the head came forward and popped off also taking the chest piece off. I put it back together as instructed using the bottom and top tabs of the chest, making sure the head was in correctly and the neck piece was in correctly. I lightly tapped it on the back and pop goes the head and chest again.

Thinking that this was just one defective manikin I opened up the other ones as they were indiviually boxed (packaged quite well actually) and tried the other ones. All of them have their head and chest pop off with very little effort. I tried to take a video showing how little force it actually takes. I know for certain my students whether they are adult or teens would easily and often pop these things apart which would make me look like a cheap instructor.

I called Nasco customer support as listed on the enclosed papers. The lady wasn't even sure what item I was talking about and then she finally figured it out and seemed confused. (I don't think they know their products very well). All she said is, "uh, I don't think they're supposed to do that" which I won't write what my reply was in my head. She suggested I return them to Amazon which is what I am doing. Thankfully Amazon has really good customer service.

I will be ordering different manikins and not only will I not order these again, I will be very vocal with anyone I know in my CPR circle that they should stay far, far away from these.

You get what you pay for I guess applies here. Buyer Beware.

title: A good starter first-aid kit
text:
I purchased this mainly to have on hand when target shooting on BLM land in the SoCal desert. For the price, this is a good starter purchase depending on what your application for it will be. I truly believe a better allotment of space could have gone to including a Quikclot bandage, or even a single packet of BleedStop, but that's just my opinion. I also understand that those items have expiration dates while everything that is included in this kit does not, so it could just be a storage and logistics things.

On the one I purchased, the retention strap was only held on by a single thread which broke off the first time I tried unhooking it to pull the kit off the back of my vest in a controlled environment. This can always be sewn back on.

In short, provided you are willing to piece together and source extra components for a triage MOLLE bag, this can be a decent starter kit to build off of.

title: So glad to have an alternative
text: My cat constantly chews holes in my CPAP hoses. I've been taping them back together, but finally gave up and went to a local CPAP store for a replacement. They don't sell the tubing separate from the mask/frame, so that cost $99. I couldn't find a hose cover that was the right length to cover the short tube to the mask, so the cat chewed a hole again within 2 days. I tried this replacement tubing, figuring it was worth a shot, for the cost. I was very happy with the results. Just know that it doesn't connect like the original ResMed short tube. There is a ring that goes inside the N20 nasal mask and then the short tube has two clips that latch on to the ring in the mask. The short tube is also a bit longer that the original, which is nice, because I think it will fit my longer hose cover. It took the cat almost two weeks to bite a hole in this tube. I think it's a little thicker than the original. I'm going to try it with a longer cover and see if that protects me from attempted murder by my feline.

title: Pretty good for the price...
text:
Distillers of this design do not come with an On/Off switch, which is confusing to some consumers. The "On" button is actually a reset button for the internal thermal circuit breaker. [Note that many power strips also have a circuit breaker reset "switch" instead of a real On/Off switch.] When the water is boiled down close to dry, the thermal breaker activates, cutting off the power. In other words, it knows when to turn itself off. If you want to shut it off mid-cycle, you need to pull the plug. The On reset switch is easily bumped when handling the distiller, resetting it. So when you go to plug it in, you may mistakenly think that it is "always on" and somehow defective.

In use, it is preferable to boil water in a teakettle, and fill the distiller with the hot water, as it will save time and probably be more cost effective if you have a gas stove and gas costs less than electricity where you are. Then put the cover on and plug the wires in. And press the On reset button if it is not already reset. The bottom section boils the water, and the cover has a fan which pulls air from the sides, over heat dissipating fins that cool a section of coiled stainless steel tubing, and through the top, causing the steam in the tubing to condense and drip out the end. There is a small "cup" containing a small charcoal sachet that the distilled water drips through. That's the part in the photo that pokes out the side of the cover. The stainless steel cup is supposed to be removable for cleaning or changing the charcoal sachet, but it is quite difficult to do, because it fits very tightly. The distilled water drips into a plastic bottle that is included. The bottle is designed with the proper height to accept the drops, and it would be difficult to locate your own pitcher or other substitute container that would fit and hold the volume of water needed. The downside is that the container is plastic, which purists would find objectionable. The bottle is welded from two halves, with a prominent vertical seam. The threads at the bottle top are not completely formed, so water will leak if the full bottle is tilted even with the cap screwed on.

After the initial use, I found that there was some leftover polishing or buffing compound on the internal shiny stainless steel surfaces. They had to be cleaned off with soapy water, alcohol, & detergent in succession. (Incidentally, I have found that new stainless teakettles sold at Macys may also have the same "feature" of not having been thoroughly cleaned of polishing compounds on the internal surfaces, either.) At the end of each cycle, unplug the cords, and remove the cover. But don't do this immediately after the unit shuts off, or you will be burned by escaping steam. You will be surprised by the dirty residue at the bottom of the boiling vessel. That's the stuff you were drinking all those years! Pour about a quarter inch of vinegar on it, and let it sit awhile. For my first gallon of vinegar, the residue came off and dissolved in the vinegar easily. For my second gallon of vinegar, additional brushing was needed; I suspect that the vinegar being sold today is weaker (the first bottle was an old one, the second one newly bought).

Overall, the unit is built to do its job pretty well, but the cosmetics leave room for improvement. The electricals are very good quality, but the product was not assembled in a clean room and the workers didn't wear gloves. But the design is robust and the seal between the cover and boiling vessel is quite good, and they didn't skimp on the stainless steel.

Plus, it has this delicate medicinal scent that instantly transports you to the sterile halls of a hospital—oh, the nostalgia!

Now, let's get to the real magic—how quickly this wonder balm works its wonders! Seriously, it's like a magician pulling a rabbit out of a hat. One moment you have a painful, red gash, and the next, it's like the wound fairies came in and kissed it all better. Neosporin works its healing mojo, leaving behind only a distant memory of the injury. It's like a superhero swooping in to save the day, leaving you in awe of its powers.

But wait, there's more! Neosporin doesn't just heal wounds; it also possesses the uncanny ability to make you feel invincible. Slap a bit of this miracle ointment on your scrape, and suddenly you're ready to conquer the world. You'll be doing backflips, climbing mountains, and maybe even running a marathon—all thanks to the healing powers of Neosporin. Who needs a cape when you have this little tube of magic?

title: I have A LOT of baby fine hair. It's also what I call "strangely wavy
text: I have A LOT of baby fine hair. It's also what I call "strangely wavy," meaning that it tries to curl and wave but each section goes in a different direction and not very well. So I have to either fully curl (which doesn't hold) or straighten my hair to look nice. I don't love flat irons because of the damage and the smell of my hair burning. I bought this brush after a beauty blog recommended it as it's top pick. I love it. I can separate my hair into two sections (top and bottom) and run it through (from underneath, you can't really use this like a normal hair brush) and be done in a few minutes (on a fairly high setting) or just flip my whole head upside down and straighten the middle-to-end and be done faster! My hair looks great, I have more volume (especially if I do it upside down) and there's no nasty smell! The handle and head of the brush don't get hot and the little balls on the brush itself do a great job of protecting from burning. I just don't suggest running this down your head like a regular brush, the little balls rub my scalp and kinda hurt.

title: Great for the price but could be better.
text:
Bought this as a general use desk lamp as well as a better light source and magnifier for soldering surface mount components ( ~2mm items) on a budget.

PROS:
I like the adjustable brightness and light color for the kind of work I do and the light is somewhat focused (which could be a drawback but in my case it is helpful) so overall it is good. The range of travel of the arm itself is decent and the lamp head is big so it casts a good amount of light where it is pointed. The head of the light itself feels like it is good quality.

CONS:
My only complaints are that the arm on this lamp feels cheap so it doesn't provide a very rigid support for the lamp and the head of the lamp doesn't have as much dimensional positioning as I'd like for really fine tuning what I am looking at through the magnifying glass. The metal part of the clamp is also kind of cheap and I'll probably rig it with more durable hardware since I've already bent the bar to tighten it. Also the plug for this lamp doesn't have a ground pin which is mostly just a pet peeve of mine. Finally, the plastic peg that attaches the arm of the lamp to the clamp bracket feels sloppy and weak-- I'm concerned that it may break at some point in the future.

If I were to go back, I would have purchased something with 4x or higher magnification since I have to get this lamp super close to my circuit board in order to really get a good view of what I am working on. The problem with that is that I can't use my soldering iron when the lamp is so close. However this is a mistake on my part so it doesn't affect my rating.

In the end, I like the lamp and for any other task I would purchase it again mainly due to the quality for the price point.

title: Fast and easy hair straightener!
text:
Let me start by saying that I'm not a hair and makeup person. I like to wash and go. I probably blow dry my hair twice a year. My hair isn't quite straight, and the slight wave is exacerbated when it dries while tucked behind my ears. I hate how it flips out, but I don't have the time/ability to straighten it with a flat iron. I also don't want a pin-straight look. When I saw this hair straightener brush, I decided to give it a try.

I'm pretty impressed! While the ionic function didn't seem to help with friz or flyaways, the straightener function was exactly what I was looking for. I started with hair that was washed that morning, and it air dried while tucked behind my ears. After brushing my hair with the ionic function, I only had to wait a few minutes for the straightener to heat up. I used the default 190 degree setting and separated my hair into upper and lower sections. I spent about 5-7 minutes to get the results shown in the pictures, and part of that is simply my ineptness at using styling tools. I'm sure it will get better with more practice! I didn't have any problems with burning my fingers, and I used the brush both facing in and facing out.

I was surprised that my hair was still relatively straight when I woke up the next morning. It's always somewhat humid where we live (OR), and it was a little warm that day, too. The brush comes in a nice velvet bag, and the purple color is more of a dark magenta. All in all, I'm very pleased with this purchase and would recommend it!

title: Pretty good after all!
text: My hair is curly and I love making it straight.  My Chi Air flat iron is wonderful, but takes quite a bit of time to straighten my hair.  So I thought that having a straightening brush would help touching up my straightened hair in the mornings or after having it in a pony tail.  The summer is especially testy as I can't stand to put all of the time into straightening and then get in the pool or walk out in the humidity. My niece, who is also my stylist, said that they had used one in her salon and no one was very pleased with it, but she knew that I was interested in trying one and encouraged me to do so.  So after researching and reading reviews, I came across the RoseMyst brush.  At first I tried just blowing my hair dry and then tried to straighten it with the brush.  That didn't work very well, because it didn't get the kinks out at the root and didn't produce the smooth look that the Chi does.  But I kept experimenting and realized that it really worked well if I just let my hair dry naturally without any hair product and then straighten it using the brush.  And...it works quite well to touch up once my hair has been straightened by the Chi.  My hair has a more course feel to it using the brush, but it also doesn't tend to curl or frizz once it's done.  So...I am very pleased with my purchase now that I have figured out how to get around the limitations and work with my own hair type and convenience.

title: Godsend After Developing Allergy to Alcon
text:
For over 10 years I used Alcon Opti-free in several varieties. It was a great product, especially the No-Rub Opti-free Express. However, I eventually developed an allergy which got so bad that I couldn't wear contacts for more than two hours without severe redness and discomfort. I had to stop wearing contacts altogether. Getting frustrated with my glasses, I eventually decided to give Clear Care a try as a desperate attempt to make contacts work again for me. The result was incredible. No allergy problems. My contacts were comfortable and clean. I could wear them all day without irritation or dryness. It made daily contact use possible again.

The drawback, of course, is the volume of product that you need. The storage tank requires more solution than the usual two-chamber contacts case, so you run through the stuff much more quickly. I could get three or four months out of my Alcon stuff but the same size bottle only lasts a month with Clear Care. But for me it's worth it.

The other drawback is the 6-hour minimum soak time. I sometimes work very, very long hours and can only catch 3 or 4 hours of sleep a night before trudging back to the office. When those late-night/early morning times hit, I have to wear the specs because the peroxide hasn't finished neutralizing. Thankfully that's relatively rare, so not a huge concern.

Overall, a terrific product that I can't recommend highly enough.

title: Low mAh readings from my eneloop's
text:
Update 2 on 1/4/12
I am putting the update at the top to cut to the chase. I have broken into the second set of 16 batteries and they are are testing at 1900-2000mAh, just as they should. I seems as if I have one four pack that is bad with less then 50% of what they should be after 4 charges. Sanyo tech support thinks so anyway and I agree. I recommend a good charger and testing all batteries to catch any bad batteries. I am thinking this isn't the norm after testing the rest. I have 8 more to test but am thinking they will test good also. They will replace the 4 bad ones I have. updating my ratings by 1 star but because of the time and effort I can't give a perfect 5 stars. I can say it looks like 28 of the 32 will be perfect and I just got one bad pack. Stuff Happens. Side note the second set didn't come with battery holders as advertised but will request them from Amazon.

Update 1 on 1/1/12
The second set of four all read in the 1900mAh range so I now know that the battery charger isn't having an issue with under charging the batteries. So now I am marking the good batteries with a permanent marker and will keep those. I will continue to test and will request replacements for the ones that are way down on mAh readings (below 1000mAh). I am feeling a bit better as I believe I can identify and hopefully at some point will end up with 16 batteries that in are in the 1800mAh range.

Original post.
I am new to rechargeable battery technology and don't claim to be an expert by any means so take this for what it's worth. I ordered this new eneloop 16 pack (4x4) 2000mAh after reading the mostly perfect reviews. In fact, I was so excited and have enough equipment (weather stations, multiple high powered flashlights, remotes, etc.) that use AA's, I ordered a second 16 pack while the first was in transit. I also ordered the La Cross3 BC-700 charger which also had great reviews. Here is my experience and feedback so far;

1 of the plastic battery holders was broken in two pieces. 3 out of 4 aren't bad and I will see if Amazon will replace it. Not a big deal but wanted to report it. Stuff happens, I understand that. The batteries are stamped 1900mAh on the batteries themselves so I don't understand why they are packaged and sold as 2000mAh batteries. I am not too worried about the 100mAh discrepancy to tell you the truth. I put my first pack of 4 on the BC-700 charger and put them into the test mode. That's the only way you can test the capacity (mAh) as it completely charges, then discharges and once again charges the batteries. Upon completion you get a mAh reading for each battery. Slot 1 was 822mAh, slot 2 was 799mAh, slot 3 was 1267mAh and slot 4 was 921mAh. I called a battery shop in town and they suggested it might take 5 or so full cycles to get the full capacity of the batteries. I have run the same test cycle multiple times on these same four batteries and the mAh readings change a bit but they aren't getting any better. I guess I was hoping to see readings closer to 1500-1800mAh and 3 out of 4 of them are in the high 700's up to the low 900's. The last averages around 1200mAh. I will note they seem to be working good in my Fenix TK41 flashlight which wants a lot of power to run in turbo mode at 800 lumens. I am thinking it would work better if I can find a rechargeable that is closer to 2000mAh. I have emailed eneloop and am awaiting their thoughts. Because I don't know any better I think I will buy a 4 pack of a another brand to simply to see if I can get to the 1500+mAh I think I should be seeing. I will not go as far as saying anything negative, just that I don't understand the apparent low readings. Again they are marketed at 2000mAh batteries but I am seeing most around 900mAh. I will update this when I can test the remaining 12 and another brand. Maybe I just don't understand but hope to soon.

If anyone would like to help me understand what I am seeing please leave a comment.

Thank you!

Update 1
The second set of four all read in the 1900mAh range so I now know that the battery charger isn't having an issue with under charging the batteries. So now I am marking the good batteries with a permanent marker and will keep those. I will continue to test and will request replacements for the ones that are way down on mAh readings (below 1000mAh). I am feeling a bit better as I believe I can identify and hopefully at some point will end up with 16 batteries that in are in the 1800mAh range.

title: Aria WiFi setup details
text:
We purchased the Aria scale in December, 2013, from Amazon. Prior to the purchase, from reading the reviews, it seems that some users had Wi-Fi setup problems. In trying to find out more from Fitbit's general Aria product page, there was very little other than stating that it is "easy" to setup. Out of the box, there is very little information about the setup other than to go to the Fitbit's web site. We did not have a setup problem, but I thought Fitbit's web site was very poor at explaining the setup requirement and process other than saying it is easy (which is probably true for most but not all users). So here are some info to help others understand the setup process and decide if this is the right scale for them.

WiFi setup requirement:
1 - your home Wi-Fi must support 802.11b (it is a much older version of WiFi protocol); most new WiFi router setup commonly will default to be backward compatible with 802.11b/g/n; but if you had changed it to g or n only, then this won't work.
2 - Initial setup will require a device on the same home WiFi network. For many users, this will be your laptop or smart phone. If you use your PC, it must have the same WiFi access and its Ethernet cable (if connected) will need to be disconnected.
3 - make sure you already have a FitBit.com account so it can store your WiFi setup information later

WiFi general setup process:
1 - put the scale into its setup mode (by removing the battery for at least 10 sec, or insert a pin via the scale's bottom hole); this setup mode allows the scale to broadcast its own WiFi network so your computing device can connect to the scale and send your home WiFi information to it.
2 - use your computing device and go to Fitbit's website to download a setup application
3 - the application will detect the current home WiFi network name and ask you for its password
4 - the WiFi information is then sent to your FitBit.com account
5 - the same WiFi setup information is also sent to the scale (via the scale's internally broadcasted WiFi network); you'll need to make sure your computing device is near the scale so as to reach the scale's WiFi network.
6 - once the scale receive the setup information, it will then switch its WiFi mode so as to connect to your home WiFi network (instead of broadcasting its own network).

To support multiple weighing users:
- each user will initially show up as a Guest in your FitBit account's weight measurement
- if the user wants to track his/her weight, a FitBit account will be required
- you can send the user an invite
- once the user accepts the invite, you can then link up the newly measured Guest weight to the invited accounts. You only need to do this once for each new user. After that, the weight will be automatically linked to the proper user based upon previous weights and %body fat.

Weight measuring process: the LCD will display the weight, followed by body fat %, your recognized account name abbreviation (or Guest, if not recognized), and then the upload process to sync with Fitbit. If synchronized successfully to Fitbit, it will display a check mark.

My setup information:
- scale is on the 2nd floor master bath room
- home WiFi is located on the first floor towards the ceiling approximately 25 feet away from the scale
- WiFi router used is a D-Link DIR 655 (purchased in 5/2010) configured to run 802.11b/g/n
- the computing device used during the setup is an Asus laptop running Windows 7 Professional and Internet Explorer 11
- the initial setup was done in the Kitchen where both the laptop and the scale are within 15 feet of the WiFi access point
- after the initial setup, the scale was then moved to the 2nd floor master bathroom

Overall, the device is working well. I had a lot of uncertainty going into the setup due to the lack of Fitbit's documentation. Some of that information is available on their website's support page, but you'll need to dig deep to find them. For this reason, I've downgraded the rating to 4 stars (instead of 5).

title: Interesting but not life-changing
text:
I wanted to share some specifics I was hoping to see when I was deciding whether to buy this.
As others mentioned, it's super easy - comb through hair and collect enough strands, place in the bag and stick in the mailbox. Results were very quick once they received it (I mailed it in before the holiday weekend so understandably that added a few days). The report is also easy to understand - items are characterized as red (severe), yellow or green. Also, there's a "nutritional imbalances" category but I didn't have anything listed there (guess that's good news).
If you read the description, you will understand this is different from allergies and I don't have any known allergens/ haven't had any other similar tests done. So I have no way to speak to the accuracy of this BUT here are a few examples.
There were 13 severe items on my report and the majority are things I don't consume regularly anyway. That was disappointing because I definitely experience upset stomach regularly but have had trouble figuring out what foods might be causing that. This didn't get me much closer to understanding that. Several of mine were chemical type ingredients often found in processed foods.
Also some interesting nuances here...
-"cola" = severe but "cherry cola" is normal. I don't drink either, but that seems odd.
-red lentils = severe; all other color lentils = normal (no details given on why)
-granulated sugar = severe but cane sugar is normal. I didn't even know the difference between these so had to look that up. Am I going to ask my local donut shop if they use granulated sugar or cane sugar?
My moderate / yellow category included around 100 items. Some are things I eat regularly (avocado) and some are not. It recommends eating these items in moderation, which I think most of us do anyway? Unless it's something you are consistently having every single day, not sure I would change my behavior on the yellow category.
This kit is reasonably priced, so I think it's worth trying if you're ok with maybe learning something helpful, maybe not. I wouldn't go into it expecting life-changing type results.

The first time I used it I had been fishing for nearly half an hour with limited strikes but no fish on the bank. I decided to put a little on my plastic worm. title: Setting up Aria
text:
It wasn't as diificult as others had posted. Maybe FitBit improved this process?

These are the steps followed using a wifi enabled laptop. Just followed the posted steps.

1) pointed IE browse to [...] (as indicated on the attached paper applied to the top of the Aria)
2) pressed "GET STARTED" button below the Aria device icon
3) clicked on "web based set up" link below the Download button (didn't want to load another app onto work laptop)
4) the following screen summarizes the next steps:
- Personalize Scale with your Info
- Put Scale in Setup mode
- Connect to the Scale's wifi (NOTE: the Aria uses its own wifi hotspot "access point" for configuring, which I think stumps most people)
- Reconnect to your Home network
5) press the two "Get Started" buttons, enter your Scale Personalization info then press Continue button
6) remove and re-insert battery,then press Continue

title: Hyperacusis
text:
I have hyperacusis. I find myself wanting to get away from my children or hoping my wife doesn't laugh too loud. I try to find quiet places in the house or avoiding lunch with co-workers. I position myself in a conference room so the phone isn't too close. I bought these hoping for some relief as some reviews say that they don't block voices at concerts. The filters are solid and the plugs really seal up the ear canal. For me, this just makes it so I can hear the muscles in my face.
I took a 5/64th drill bit and drilled out the middle of the filter. I realize this make the attenuation less than 18 dB, but I didn't want the pressure of a solid ear plug. It wasn't enough to keep from feeling the pressure and hearing my face. I pull out the plug far enough to keep it from sealing up my ear and in far enough that it doesn't fall out. It does help some, but I'm going to keep looking for another solution.
The quality is good and the case is easy to carry around. They are comfortable enough to wear all the time. Nobody realized I had this in my ear. I didn't feel it would get lost in my ear. I usually wear the middle size ear buds for listening to music. The size that normally come from the manufacturer.
I contacted support and asked if the had another filter that would help me and my situation with maybe only 3 or 6 dB filters, but they couldn't help me.
