title: There are few products that are TRULY AMAZING: This is one of them.
text:
Let me preface this my saying this is how my concert experience usually ends up: We arrive early so my wife can be right up front so she can be there when the main act comes on stage (rock/metal concerts). By the time the opening act is done everything sounds sort of muffled, almost has a digital feel to it.. By the time the final band is playing it's all just a mess of sounds and muffled everything. Once we leave the venue is when I can hear the truly bad tinnitus and the ride home consist of having to turn the radio up to double volume and even then I can barely hear the treble or anything but a ringing and the bass of the music. This tinnitus and muffled hearing will make sleeping that night nearly impossible and will stay with me for at LEAST 2 years.

Finally being tired of this and knowing one day my hearing may never come back, I read the reviews and gave these DownBeats a chance and I am blown away. Normally I can not stand stand earbuds that go into the ear so I was worried about earplugs in general. Surprisingly, I had no issues with these earplugs; they didn't feel unnatural and didn't annoy me when they were in. What really got me with these was how I kept feeling like I didn't have them in properly as I could still hear everything around me, converse normally with my wife between acts, and the music seemed as loud as it normally does but that's where they're magnificent. The ONLY way I knew these were in was when i spoke, I sounded much louder than I normally would to myself. I also loved how they're practically invisible unless you know to look for them. Another thing that steered me away from the standard "orange foam" earplugs was how dorky some people look with them in. I was much less self-conscious with these things in.

Many aspects of the concert still seemed rather loud to the point where I kept checking to make sure these were inserted properly and they always were. There were even parts of the concert that were still overwhelmingly loud. By the time the final act came on I could hear perfectly fine; no discernible ringing, no muffled sounds, and no "digitizing" of background noises. It wasn't until we left the venue, got in the car, and I removed the earplugs that I was truly amazed: I had minimal to no tinnitus. The radio was at the normal volume it always is and I almost couldn't believe I just went through a concert that felt as "loud as normal" with no perceivable side effects.

How these things manage to keep volume levels at perceptibly normal levels and yet still protect your hearing is truly a marvel. I chuckled when the instructions said "it's science!" but it's true; these things are nothing short of miraculous and I deeply thank whatever scientist(s) made it their life's work to create these things.I no longer have to worry about going deaf before I hit 35.

title: Great value and reliable
text:
I've tried the amazon tourniquets and they have snapped on my during demonstrations. These rhino ones have held tight. Did some research on them and for the price, these are great not to mention that these can actually save a life.

Most people will keep the tourniquet in its factory configuration. For legal reasons I'll tell you what I do but I'll neither confirm nor deny that this is the way a tourniquets should be set.

Let's get started. If you follow my pictures this will be much easier for both of us. Pull out the strap until it is completely out of the buckle. After that, take just the tab and place it back through the buckle and secure the end to the velcro. Only 2 to 3 inches of the tab and strap should be going through the buckle. Next from the opposite end, fold the strap onto itself so that the fold reaches the buckle. Continue to fold the strap on itself until the end of the buckle were the tab is folded is the same length as the folded strap. Finally, to secure all of it, take the retaining velcro strap that says "Time:" on it and wrap the folded straps. Secure the end of the retaining velcro to the plastic lever arm retainer via the velcro. And there you go, that tourniquet can now be put on and off with just one hand. Practice with it so that putting on the tourniquet will become second nature. I'd you can put it on yourself then you can save someone else.

title: Poor choice for those that want to exchange health data with apps and platforms
text:
We bought the Aria scale a month ago and have been reasonably happy with its performance. It was easy to setup on a wireless network (especially from a tablet or smartphone). It has occasionally confused my weight with my wife's (I am 70 pounds heavier than she is). Each time this has occurred it has been possible to correct using the Fitbit app. It is a bit of a pain and I accidentally deleted a couple of accurate weigh-ins. The weights that were incorrectly assigned to my wife could not be reassigned to my account and the data was lost.

Fitbit is at war with Apple and is refusing to integrate with HealthKit. This means that my data is trapped and cannot be shared with the Health App. There are over 70 pages of customer requests for this integration on the Fitbit web site with only weak responses from Fitbit. Fitbit is putting their interests in front of their customers. I would recommend the Withings scale ahead of the Aria.

text: I have been using the Cove device on and off for a little over a month. It is lightweight and easy to wear around the house, which makes it pretty easy to use every day. I prefer to use it at night when I am relaxing as I feel the effects more than when I am running around getting stuff done. I feel like it can either work to amplify the effects of meditation or act as a more attainable form of it (for instance, you can just wear this while you sit and watch TV with your fam). text:
I got the two-pack of these glasses to go along with the 51-LED light I bought to hunt down pet urine. Contrary to what some of the one-star reviews claim these DO seem to block a substantial amount of ultraviolet light, as I found out by placing them between my new UV flashlight and my UV-reactive driver's license.

These glasses make all the difference when I'm using said flashlight, by the way. Like most cheap UV LEDs there's a lot of bleed-through into the purple visible-light spectrum meaning that the visible light it emits may be enough to wash out the dimmer florescence of the organic stains you're looking for. The glasses seem to filter out the near-UV purple light just as well as it does UV which increases the contrast significantly. What look like faint stains become vivid and what was completely washed out by the visible light becomes noticeable.

title: The semi-hard case is perfect for a first aid kit
text:
After arriving exactly when it was supposed to, I opened the box and was pleasantly surprised. The semi-hard case is perfect for a first aid kit. Cloths ones are too flimsy and plastic ones can break or crack. It seems made to be very sturdy. (Including top handle and strap.) It was nice to get an instant ice pack in there that doesn't expire until 2019. I haven't had a need for a bandage yet, so I don't know the quality of those, but there are quite a few.

Now for the few things I'm not so excited about... 1. The tweezers. They're a thick, aqua-ish (new word) plastic and I'm not so certain that they'd really be of any use. 2. The razor blade. Why put a razor blade in there and not a small pair of scissors? I know it probably costs a little more, but I'd rather accidentally run my hand over scissors than a razor blade. 3. The design of the middle compartment. I was happy to see there were plenty little storage spots, but they don't close. Also, getting the middle compartment-storage-thing back in was confusing to me. There is velcro on both sides, so does that mean they're both supposed to be affixed Addy the same time?

All-in-all, however, I think it's a cool little kit. I've been needing one. I will put a few more things it. I was in the medical field and my whole life I've always been the family's "nurse". I would recommend getting one.

title: Some items are different than pictured and the instructions are not too clear.
text:
A pain to put together, seems the manufacturer has changed some items, possibly because of earlier reviews.
First. The bars don't fit one inside the other, instead there is a metal bar connector that slides inside both bars. Short bar has 2 square holes and long bar has only 1 hole. The "connector" has only 2 holes so you have to put 1 bar in the rubber bracket and line up the holes with your finger till you can secure it through both the rubber bracket & the bar. Then you can insert the other side of the bar. Once I figured that out (due to the still cryptic picture only instructions), I was able to assemble pretty quickly. However, the bolts are carriage bolts so they keep the bolts from turning once tightened. Yeah, the heads of the bolts are almost bigger than the holes in the top of rubber bracket so in order to get them through the top of the rubber so they seat in the square holes, you have to wrangle with them a bit. The screws to attach the brackets to the bars are longer than notes in previous reviews, almost too long so when tightening the middle screws for attaching to the roof rack (i did this to make sure the carriage bolts seated), I kept scraping my knuckles on them. The middle belt for attaching to the roof rack is quite long and is actually a separate nut with a plastic piece that slides over the bolt and the nut seats inside it. But in previous photos, it is no longer a daisy shape but only has 3 points. I'm not sure if that's for being able to get a better grip when securing to the roof rack or if the piece is just cheaper.
So assembly made a nice Friday night project.
I have not mounted or used them yet because it's cold today and, to be honest, I just don't feel like it. :-)
I will post again with mounting and transport. But for the price, I'm hoping to be able to say they were worth the $ and the "learning experience" of assembly.

A double-blind placebo- controlled study was conducted at Osaka City University to evaluate the effmts of oral administration of supplements containing rice ceramides in 33 patients with a habitual tendency toward dry, rough skin. The 33 patients were comprised of 6 men and 27 women, and the study was performed in keeping with the tenets of the Helsinki Accord, with written Informed Consent forms. This study was performed as a double-blind trial involving 6-week oral administration of “functional supplements” containing rice-derived Ceramides or a placebo.

The test supplement was given in the form of soft capsules provided by Oryza Oil & Fat Chemical Co., Ltd., with a daily consumption of rice-derived Oryza Ceramide, 40 mg/day, containing rice-derived sphingolipids of 1.2mg/day. Placebo capsules were administered that were identical in appearanceand smell, but containing 0 mg/day of rice-derived Oryza Cerarnide and 0 mg/day of rice-derived sphingolipids. After the 6-week trial period, no subjects had dropped out and no adverse events were reported. Other evidence of the safety of ingested Ceramides is also presented in this study:

Experiments have shown that after oral administration plant-based ceramides are absorbed unchanged in the small intestine or are broken down into sphingosine and fatty acids for absorption and are then reconfigured as ceramides. The substance is then transported by the capillaries into the horny layer and the keratin intercellular spaces. The supplements containing rice ceramides as used in this study, in contrast to the ceramide substances distributed in animal brains, provide superior supplementation that can be exnected to be both safe and effective for oral administration.

Confirming this assessment is Lati, who as early as 1995 wrote about the use of ceramides in functional foods:

Ceramide has been highly appraised in the field of functional foods because of its hydration characteristics and vectorization of vitamins (vitamin C and E). Presently phyto-ceramides by INOCOSM [Laboratories] are used as ingredients for various functional and cosmeceutical foods. Because of its hydration characteristics, ceramide is most extensively used in this field, and it is generally used together with vitamins. Ceramide has shown numerous benefits as a food additive because of its very unique characteristics, and it is effective not only for the tissues but also for the stabilization of foods in some cases. If a certain amount of phyto-ceramide is ingested every day, the following benefits could be attained:

title: Great taste but DECEPTIVE STATISTICS (calorie and protein gram ratio)
text:
I have tried the variety pack and really enjoyed most all of the flavors. They are pretty spot-on and realistic to the stated flavors. Just be aware, that they are a little cheeky in the way they represent calorie and protein gram figures! At first sight, you think you are getting 23 grams of protein per serving... and that each serving is only 25 calories. Beware, that they minimized the calories and maximized the protein in the larger print. Upon closer scrutiny, you find that one serving is only a tiny 1/4th OF A SCOOP!! 25 calories, but just under 6 grams of protein! So...you will be ingesting 100 calories (in a normal full scoop) to get that 23 grams of protein you wanted. Still, great flavors and I would order again; just wish they were more transparent (like the Designer Whey that I also bought and love). Never helps to try to fool customers! Would have given it 5 stars if it hadn't been for the fuzzy math.

UPDATE ON FLAVOR: If you are looking for a flavor that is not too sweet, this is likely not quite for you. At the same time that I discovered Syntrax, I also tried Betty Lou's Low Glycemic Vanilla powder. As I have been trying to get away from things too sweet, I now find my Syntrax way over the top - at least the vanilla. It has what I call the Stevia Sting--that too-sweet taste for those who don't have a sweet-tooth. I have tried to add unsweetened protein powder just to finish this current order so as not to waste it...not working very well...

title: Good stuff but doesn't have as many nutrients as a prenatal vitamin.
text:
I used this to up my levels of B vitamins after a severe antibiotic poisoning i didn't trust doctors to treat me with. The amount of thiamin, folate, folic acid and enzymes really helped me recover from POTS (dysautonaumia where blood doesn't circulate back up from your legs) that I got from severe thiamin and folic acid deficiency due to bactrim. They really should ban bactrim. Anyway, this gave me so much energy throughout the day!
What I do miss out of it though is a few of the non-essential nutrients like molybdenum. It also has low Iron in it and zinc. No manganese?
It tastes "okay" especially if you mix it into gatorade but it is a struggle for me to take it every day because the taste is kind of crap. I'd rather just take a prenatal supplement that I know has everything. And is cheaper and has extra good stuff in it.
I know this is vegan, non-gmo etc etc which is good. But it just doesn't contain everything that your body needs or wants to function at it's best.

I do like how there's a crap ton of B vitamins in it though. That's what gives you the energy when you take this supplement and I'm sure that it is sourced from excellent sources. But I personally think prenatal vitamins work better and are cheaper. Don't cheap out on prenatal vitamins though, get the rainbow type or whatever that has legit everything from adam to eve.

this stuff is really great, it helped me combat POTS which caused lots of fatigue and nervous system damage, etc. But I can't justify $50 for 1-2 months worth of a drink that not only doesn't taste great, is overhyped by vegans and it doesn't even contain every nutrient that your body needs to function at it's best. Dr. Wallach or whoever promotes this is on the right track to promoting high vitamin and mineral intake as proper nutrition but his products don't exactly reflect that. Don't get me wrong, there are a lot of great and beneficial nutrients in this powder, but for $50 I would expect to have EVERYTHING in there.

title: They're long-lasting and usable. The case is built like a tank.
text:
Disclaimer, I have bought no other musician's earplugs, so I don't have a point of comparison for my "sound quality/noise cancellation/value" ratings. I just think these earplugs work well enough for my situation, and considering that it's probably the cheapest option on Amazon, I would recommend it.

I work at a restaurant and use these every day to protect my hearing from clanking plates, metal pans and breaking glass.

Clarity of sound is not perfect, higher end gets muted or even nearly unnoticable. With these on, I can't hear my car's right/left blinker unless I really concentrate. But the high end muting has its advantages, like for example, the loudest thing at my workplace by far is a recycle bin full of ~20lbs glass, being emptied into a chest-height container. The glass breaking noise is all high end. So these earplugs are perfect for me!

If you're using this for playing music, a word to violinists, a lot of sound travels from the chinrest of the violin through your jaw, completely bypassing these earplugs. So if you're in an orchestra playing violin like I was, the sounds of your own playing will drown out every other sound, making playing in the ensemble more difficult. Literally an unsolvable problem though, not a problem with this product.

As for verbal communication, I'm hearing just about as well as everyone without earplugs. Loud environments aren't great for verbal communication in the first place, literally everyone is mishearing things just as you are.

After about a year of use, my earplugs turned a pretty gross yellow color, but they're still perfectly usable, and these earplugs are so unnoticable that no one notices until you point them out. I bought a second pair recently however, to be prepared for the day when I lose this first pair or if they somehow become unusable.

Speaking of losing these though, they might be easy to lose. if you casually screw the case too loose, the case slowly unscrews in your pocket and you've got a pair of earplugs in your pocket ready to fall out. Miraculously even after maybe 10 times of the screw becoming undone in my pocket over the course of a year, I have not lost this pair yet. So maybe this worry is unwarranted. It's not at all a problem with case build quality though, the case's build quality is excellent and the screw-on lid to the case has stayed strong even after a year.

What didn't last for me though, is the little keychain at the top that attaches to your keychain. Mine broke after about 3 months of use, after a violent incident of accidentally kneeing my key ring into my car. As seen in my picture, it's been long replaced with a spare key ring. It was a HELLISH time trying to put that key ring on, as the top of the carrying case's lid is very thick and not very suited for threaded inside a key ring.

title: Does as reported on websites regarding h.pylori
text:
I bought mastic gum to try to treat symptoms of what I believe is H.Pylori. It was recommended by several websites etc. I've taken it for about 6 weeks (no faithfully) The symptoms have changed, though I don't think I've managed to figure out exactly what's going on. I'm not a doctor and this is not medical advice. My wife and I have roughly the same symptoms, in our 40s, and self diagnosis indicated H.Pylori - subsequent testing on my wife by a doctor says H.Pylori is not a factor for her. Final notes on mastic gum are yet to come.

The Swanson product is what you would expect of quality products, shipped quickly, and is priced reasonably. This is not what you find in other such products. Over all experience with Swanson Mastic Gum via Amazon is 100% satisfaction with regard to buying a product. The jury is still out on whether the product does what others claim it will do. It's sort of like buying Vitamin C... does it do what's others claim it does? I have had no bad effects from this product, and the changes to my symptoms are positive. I've not had an upset stomach since starting this product.

If you think that mastic gum can help your symptoms, I recommend Swanson mastic gum from Amazon. It seems effective and is priced nicely. Shipping and quality are 5star.

title: Hidden charm
text:
Since I run a Go club, I am always in the market for Go equipment bargains and interesting items. The price was the first thing that attracted me to these stones, and the glowy color in the pictures was also attractive.

When I first received the stones, I was disappointed in the darker, duller coloring than what appeared in the photo, but that disappointment vanished the first time I played with them. In a brightly lit room, both the white and the black stones cast a subtle green shadow, especially noticeable on a light-colored board. The effect is beautiful and enchanting. (I actually sort of wished the board was white to enhance the effect.) The black stones seem more translucent than usual, at least compared to my old Yunzi set

All stones arrived intact, in sturdy cardboard boxes suitable to be used as containers while playing. Yunzi stones are a glass product, but are combined with melted rock and other ingredients to make them less fragile and heavier than regular glass. Yunzi stones must be washed and oiled to appear at their best. One slight disadvantage of the cardboard boxes is that they now have slight oil-stain markings. I'd say the only way I would like this product more was if it came with some suitable wooden bowls. But then, they would hardly be selling them for such a sweet price.

title: Does NOT work outside
text:
I bought this for indoor use, as the BBC recommended regular oximeter readings as a way to catch Covid early. It arrived at my doorstep 5 days ago and the packaging made this look like a very sharp, neat, and professional product.

Immediately upon opening the package and observing the device, I noticed that the plastic was severely scuffed on one side, as if someone had dropped it with some significant momentum onto concrete or asphalt. This has lead me to strongly believe that this is NOT a condition-new oximeter. Further review of the product's page here on Amazon shows that there is no guarantee that the product bought would be new. So, I am 99.9% certain that I received a refurbished (and still slightly albeit cosmetically damaged) unit. Either that, or their Quality Control simply doesn't care about superficial damage. Regardless, I am deducting 1 start from my review for this alone.

The other two stars are deducted for a pretty significant issue with the device's function. It straight up does not work outside under moderately-bright sunshine. For the past 5 days, I've been using it indoors with no problem. In fact, when it works, it's great! There's a visual graph showing your pulse along with all the numbers that you would expect from a pulse-oximeter. However, on two separate occasions today (separated by a couple of hours), this device proved to simply not work when exposed to sunlight. I live on the coast of California and it has been somewhat overcast/foggy all day. I tried using it in my local supermarket's parking lot, and the device simply refused to acknowledge that there was even a finger in it, displaying flatline metrics and quickly returning to its powered-down state. Worked fine inside the store. Later, while out for a walk, I tried it again outside and again it failed to register the presence of my finger. And again, after returning home and trying it inside, the thing works fine.
So... if you're looking for a pulse-oximeter for your indoor activities (at home, inside a gym, etc), I'd say that this is a pretty good product. If you're looking for something you expect to use outside, however, this is NOT FOR YOU.

Finally, this product is made in China, which is something I didn't consider when I hit that "Buy Now" button. This alone would have been enough to keep me from buying it if I had realized beforehand. No use crying over spilt milk now; but if you are conscious about that sort of thing, consider seeking out a different brand.

title: Not all omegas are created equal
text:
DHA was recommended by my daughter's nutritionist to help reduce inflammation caused by her inherited health condition. We tried all kinds, and she liked this one the best - still using it, years later, although she can (and does) swallow pills of any size. It's true that they are gel capsules, not chewables - she sucks on them, like candy.

Watch out for so-called DHA supplements that contain both omega-6 and omega-3. Omega-6 isn't bad, but American diets contain way too much of it already. The point of an all omega-3 supplement, like this one, is to balance out the large quantities of omega-6 that we're already eating. And the point of a supplement that has both omega-3s and omega-6s is... um... to sell supplements, I guess. Also, switch to canola oil wherever you're currently using corn oil, or you're trying to empty the ocean with a bucket, as far as getting a healthy balance of omega-3 and omega-6 is concerned.

Now for the bad news… supposedly it is not harmful and you can’t burn yourself. I absolutely say that is false. I was using the product On the lowest setting and I felt like I could burn myself if I stayed too close to the lash line for long. Then I bumped it up to the medium setting- where I proceeded to burn my eyelids at the lash line multiple times! I guess if you get to close to the skin it burns. title: The Perfect Item for My Baby
text:
I know what you're thinking. I know EXACTLY what you're thinking. I thought the same thing when my husband told me about this "awesome thing he saw somewhere" that allows you to suck the snot out of your baby's nose with your mouth. Ummm, excuse me? No. Well, it finally happened: my husband was right, and I was wrong.

1 or 2 little "baby colds" later, half a dozen restless if not completely sleepless nights later, I sent him out to purchase this miracle tube. And miracle it is, my friends.

First of all, it's not as disgusting as I first thought. It's not like siphoning gas - the snot isn't going to fly up into your mouth. Check out the picture. The snot is collected into a tube at the baby's nose, and then you blow it back out into a nearby tissue or wipe. And unlike the infamous "bulb syringe", this works.

Picture this: You're up in the middle of the night because baby is snoring and grunting. He can't breathe. Again. You lay him down on the changing table and grab the bulb syringe and depress it, and stick it into his nose. It slooooowly regains its shape and sucks out a bit of snot. You depress it again. By this time your baby is screaming like he's being squashed by an elephant. The problem with the bulb thingy is that it doesn't always "suck" fast enough, leaving you with a screaming baby. You grab it and place the end of the tube into the baby's nose. You suck quickly. BAM! You can see what's coming out. You see your progress. Within 5 seconds, your baby's airway is clear and you pick him up to comfort him.

It's easy to clean. It's transportable. It's ready whenever you need it. It's fast-acting. This thing ROCKS.

Oh, and don't act like you're grossed out by this review.. If you already have a baby, no doubt you have seen and read things much, much grosser. And if you don't have one yet, well, let's just say that your conversation topics and amazon searches will become totally shameless, and snot is the least disgusting thing you will experience and talk about.

To address other reviewers' germ concerns: I'm just cracking up at the number of 1-star reviews saying, "I GOT THE EXACT SAME COLD AS MY BABY OMG!!" Don't let being afraid of breathing your baby's exhalations that you don't order this. You're going to be all around his sicky germs regardless of what aspirator you use.

title: Great sunscreen for children with delicate skin
text:
Kids love spending time outside no matter if it is summer or winter, hot or cold weather. Their energy can be envious but safety is our first priority. While the shiny sun brings lots of excitement, the sun exposure can be dangerous and harmful to our skin if do not take proper ways to protect it. When it comes to baby and child skin, using a sun screen is a must especially when children are exposed to the sun during vacation time, travelling or playing outside. Even during winter months our skin is sensitive to sun and has to be protected. There are lots of varieties of sunscreen products on the market and recently we were offered to try Sun'n'Fun Broad Spectrum SPF30 Sunscreen for Kids.

First, what we liked about this product and always consider when buying skincare for kids is that Sun'n'Fun Broad Spectrum SPF30 Sunscreen for Kids is natural, toxin-free & paraben-free sunscreen and contains organic ingredients like marshmallow, grapeseed and raspberry rich with vitamin C. Second, it is chemical-free mineral based with hydrating and moisturizing features providing UVA & UVB protection. We also like that Sun'n'Fun Broad Spectrum SPF30 is anti-irritant and anti-inflammatory thanks to green tea and tamanu oil which is perfect for kid’s sensitive skin. Third, the sunscreen has soothing and moisturizing features to protect and nourish delicate kids’ skin to avoid dryness and eczema. And finally, that amazing chocolate smell our kid loves it so much, the smell when you enter a chocolate store.

In winter our boy does not need much sunscreen to apply, mostly for face when playing outside or go skiing, just a few drops are enough. Sun'n'Fun Broad Spectrum SPF30 Sunscreen for Kids protects and moisturizes kid’s skin very well.

The size 100ml is perfect to take with you when travelling or going on vacation to a sunny destination.

title: NEED ANOTHER PERSON TO APPLY CUPS
text:
Inside the box there is an instruction book(English). I did not read the instruction book, but did my own internet research on where to put the cups to treat different problems. I heard from a friend who grow up with cupping therapy suggest put the cups (the big ones) on the back is the safest place, and put them on the place where there are ""meat"", not bones. I did this for my son (9 year old) who has asthma to clear up debris on the back by putting 6 cups (3 each side) near chest area.

The suction guns are powerful, and just two pumps I see the skin raised almost to the silver point inside the cup. Two pumps are usually enough to get results. I used this for my son who got sick often and even after getting well he would continue to have dry cough that usually drag for weeks. I used the cups 10 min each time before bed time on the back when he was at the dry cough stage. I did my own research what meridian points on the back I should place the cups. The first time I did this I saw good results. He started to cough out phlem instead of dry cough, and after one week he totally stopped coughing and there was no more restriction in breathing. You may see the skin turned red or purple (like a pepperoni) and I read that was normal. That color change was due to ""debris"" and the cups cleaned them out. From my experience, the peppeoni went away in a few days. I used the cups for 7 days and my son's cough was less and less. After 10 days I no longer need the cups. I am sure I will use it again next time he get sick.

The cups does not suck well on elbow joints, knee joints, legs, or ankles. And I do not find much use of the small size cups yet. I read that they are for face, or for babies, and I have been using the big and medium size cups. So far I only use them on the back and only need 5-6 cups, and got good results, and I am happy with them. Also after applying the cup, don't move, or they will fall out. My experience is that you definite need a second person to hold the cup and angle the gun right on top of the cup to suck. After you remove the cup, the skin may feel itchy so have some cream, lotion, or massage oil ready to rub a little bit to make you feel more comfortable.

I dropped the cups a few times on hardwood floor from about 2-3 feet high and luckily they did not break. But it is hard plastic so there is a chance it will break if you drop it on very hard surfaces.

title: Have to use it right
text:
I have been using the Sacro Wedgy for about two weeks now. I have been experiencing sacral/hip problems for about two years. I have worked with yoga, other stretching, consulted a chiropractor and other doctors, and bought an inversion table. All provided relief to some degree, but for some reason never could alleviate the problem, yet x-rays and examinations were not showing any significant problems (welcome to the msyteries of back/hip pain).

Within two days of using this simple device, I was able to isolate the cause of my back problem. I sat on the sacro wedgy for a day in my office chair and felt everything in my pelvis/hip relax, the pain disappeared. I was very happy...then I got in my car to go visit some clients and run some errands. It felt like someboy stuck a hot knife into my lower back and twisted it by the end of the day. Bingo! When I was in my 20's I had an old pickup truck that caused sciatica, which vanished within a week of my replacing that vehicle. However, this wasn't sciatica, and the link was immediately apparent and the car is only 2 years old...the pieces started to fall together.

It was my car seat that was causing my problem. My car is a small compact car, and I never noticed any overt discomfort from it, but I made some adjustments to it, and used the sacro wedgy until I started feeling relief. For the first time in two years, I am 95% pain free and improving.

My recommendation to people looking at this product is to read the instructions very carefully and really feel with your body where it should be placed. It takes a little experimentation to get it right, and I am sure it changes for each person in question. I have found it more effective to actually sit on it on my sofa, office chair, and elsewhere than the the lying down application, although that helps too.

Next, check all your regular seating against the results. If you are experiencing symptoms consistent with tight psoas and iliacus and/or sacral tenderness (do a search on these), then this thing will help you, but what I found most amazing is how quickly it helped me identify the culprit (car seat) and how subtle that problem was. Yet, it was able to put a severe kink in my life for quite some time.

I have a lot of experience with martial arts, body work, etc., and had tried several paths to relief, I am very aware of my body. So, you might want to speak with a good specialist who can help you with the use of this if you don't have a good sense for your own body. If you use it wrong, it will hurt and could make things worse. However, with proper use it could really help.

I don't think this device will help people too much with middle and upper spine issues, but I could be wrong, the back is a complex and wonderful thing. So, good luck, I hope this review helps people with the sacro wedgy and possibly opens up some ideas for people to find relief.

title: You Might Want To Keep Shopping
text:
The hand tightening nuts were all threaded incorrectly and will not thread onto the carriage bolts supplied. (They're suppose to be 8mm 1.25 to match the bolt, but they are not) Upon test fitting with other nuts in place of the hand tightening ones, I discovered these will not work with aero type load bars- Thule, Rocky Mounts, Yakima- as the shape of the mounting surface is a poor match and the carriage bolts are too short. The mounting surfaces of these are painted steel offering no protection to the load bars or provide any grip to keep them from rotating. Additionally, as others have mentioned, the instructions are rubbish.

If you have round or square load bars, don't mind the eventual damage these may cause or the potential for them moving when loaded, want to purchase a tap and tap handle to rethread the hand tightening nuts, along with possibly longer bolts, and assemble things from a vague and poor quality image, these may be just the thing for you.

title: Well worth the price
text: I bought this set through subscription when first announced and suffered through the torment of the initial publisher going belly up. The Heinlein Trust stepped in and completed the project in a viable form, including reprinting the first six volumes which had been previously published by the other company. This was a limited edition, numbered as such (mine is 97 I think). You will NEVER see this set as such in paperback. The Main reason being that except for the collected letters, the screenplays, and a (very) few odd nonfiction shorts, EVERYTHING Heinlein ever wrote is still available in print. He is one of a very few authors whose work has never yet gone out of print. If you look you should be able to find all his fiction and most nonfiction in paperback editions at retail prices. The first Heinlein I read was Red Planet. I was seven years old, by the time I was seventeen I was buying every new Heinlein in Hardcover as they came out. I still pick up used copies as I find them to give to friends, grandkids and others to introduce them to Heinlein. The website for the Virginia edition is still viable and a few copies of the original 2000 are still available. I think the set is worth it. If you don't ...as I said they books are all in print and you should be able to find them here on Amazon.

title: Love Vital Proteins But Don't Like This
text: I pre-ordered this product direct from the Vital Proteins website (not from Amazon) when they first announced it was coming out and received it just as soon as the first batch was ready to ship.  I am a big fan of Vital Proteins AND Sarah Ballantyne.  I regularly make smoothies with fresh greens (like kale or collards) plus berries, protein and fat.  I use two cups greens to half or one cup berries (blueberries + raspberries) and don't need to add any sweetener because the berries add plenty of sweetness.  There is no undesirable taste of the fresh greens in my smoothies.  Due to my particular dietary restrictions, I have to be careful about the amount of sugar I consume, including from higher sugar fruits, which is why I stick to berries (no bananas for me).  I was excited about this product because I thought it would be an easy way to add more veggies to my smoothies, or use it in place of fresh greens when I'm running short on time.  However, to me, the taste is very unpleasant and requires that I either use no more than half a scoop OR cover up the taste with plenty of stevia, some vanilla, and cinnamon or cardamom.  Even then, the strong, unpleasant taste still comes through.  I agree that if you are looking for something more on the line of a V8 juice, this will definitely fit the bill.  If you want more of a fruit taste in your smoothie, this won't work unless you use only half a scoop along with your other ingredients, in my experience.  I won't be purchasing this again.

title: It really works! I'm so thankful for this product.
text: My son is 7 and has been struggling with bedwetting.  After seeing his doctor, she recommended a bed wetting alarm.  I found this one online and based on the reviews decided to try it.  It was affordable and had very good reviews.  It comes with all the instructions you need.  The armband comfortable adjusts to my son's arm and the sensor clips on this under garments. When the sensor feels moisture the alarm will flash a light, vibrate and make a noise.  My son has been using this alarm since Oct 5th and it is working. The first week took some getting use to but STICK WITH IT!  Just like any treatment plan, it takes time.  My son is a very deep sleeper. We had a few dry nights here and there. We also had a few nights where he had multiple accidents. It took time to get his body adjusted but I can see how this alarm is re-training him to wake up when he needs to potty. Our routine included taking him to potty at 11:30 every night and we wake him up once in the night to potty.  Of course the alarm wakes him up if there is an accident . This is the 3rd week using the alarm and I can proudly say my son has had no accidents in 5 nights in a row.  He even wakes up and goes to the bathroom now which he has never done before.  We are continuing to use this a few more nights to be sure.  This is a GREAT system if your child has bedwetting issues. Keep in mind this is an aid in a treatment process and not an overnight fix.  .

title: Simple Straight Hair!
text:
I received this straightening brush for free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

This brush is a life saver for my hair! I can never get my hair to go completely straight when I just brush and blow dry my hair. I always have to use a straightener and that just does more damage to my already damaged hair.

With this brush, I don't have to worry about frying my hair. All I have to do is make sure my hair is dry and tangle free, then brush my hair with the straightening brush like I would with a normal brush. It's amazing how well this brush works!
I was very skeptical about using this. I thought, "There is no way this is going to actually work." I was quickly proven wrong! My hair felt so soft and I didn't even have to use a heat protectant spray. I do recommend using one just to be safe though.

The brush comes with two clips to section hair for easier straightening, a plush velvet carrying bag, and a heat protecting glove to prevent burning your fingers.

The brush's temperature comes formatted in °C but can easily be switched to °F by pressing the + and - buttons on the side of the handle at the same time. It heats up very quickly. It takes 1 minute heat up to 80℃ (180℉) and 3 minutes heat up to the max 230℃ (450℉). When you first cut on the brush, the power and UP/DOWN buttons are locked for 5 seconds to provide accurate heating. You can unlock the buttons by double clicking the power button.

The brush also has a built in safety feature. It will cut off after 60 minutes of no usage, to prevent heat damage or risk of fire. This is great of you are a very forgetful person like me. The cord to the brush is designed to swivel to prevent cord damage and tangles.

title: I really wanted to love this watch.
text:
I bought this watch for myself and really wanted to love it. My old talking watch died on me and I needed a quick, economical replacement for it. This one seemed to meet those criteria. Sadly, it didn't live up to my expectations. After less than 2 months, it just plain quit working right.

There ARE good points about this watch. There are 4 diferent alarms to set for time reminders. I loved that. It woke me up, alerted me to it being time to get the kids off to school, told me when they would be home soon and let me know when it was time to start getting them ready for bed. I loved the stopwatch feature. I was really in love with the date function. In so many ways, it was everything I wanted. And then there were flaws...

I loathed the watch band. Looking at the picture, it appeared to be your typical rubbery plastic sport-type band. But it wasn't. It's a stiff plastic that really made it a pain in the backside to buckle on my wrist. And then there's the fact that it's lasted me a mere 6 weeks before dying on me. I turned off the hourly report feature one nite. 45 minutes later, when I went to check the time, it didn't respond. It was totally blank. Ticked off, I set it aside and looked at it the next morning. It was once again showing time (the incorrect time), but the buttons wouldn't do anything. No talking. No resetting the time. Nothing. I've never gotten it wet. It's been taken care of. And it just died.

Now, perhaps I got a bad one. One of the parts in it just fizzled out. But when you're visually impaired and your watch dies, you're kinda up the creek without a paddle, so to speak. If I were you, I would buy a totally different watch. If you want something cheap? Independent Living Aids sells a REALLY cheap talking watch for around $7. It's ugly to look at, but will do the job if you need that. Or you can spend around double and buy something that looks a whole lite nicer and much better quality to last a lot longer.

title: Genie XL (WHPH) Pack vs. the FlexiKold Gel Pack
text:
I researched many cold packs to use after my knee surgery (ACL) in order to avoid paying $200 for the PolarCare Cold Therapy unit that my doctor had recommended. I needed something large enough to cover my whole knee, so I bought this Genie XL (WHPH) Pack along with the FlexiKold Gel Cold Pack (10.5" x 14.5" size) so I could compare and switch between them when one got warm.

First, I put both of them in the Freezer for several hours and did a head-to-head test with a thermometer to see which one stayed cold the longest. This Genie XL Pack definitely stayed cold much longer than the FlexiKold Pack. After 30min, the Genie was about 10deg colder than the FlexiKold, and the difference grew to ~20deg after about 2 hours. The Genie definitely won this test and was able to stay very cold for several hours, while the FlexiKold was too warm to use after about an hour.

The main downside to the Genie is that it came out of the freezer very stiff and difficult to wrap around the knee. If you knead the gel material for a minute, then it softens up enough to wrap, but it doesn't really conform to the knee until it warms up after a several minutes, meaning you have to keep repositioning the straps and pulling it tighter to keep it on securely (no elastic to keep it tight). Also, there is NO GEL along any of the long strips of velcro, so you lose a great deal of cooling area at those key locations (just above and just below the knee) where the swelling is the worst. The one way to get around this is to take the upper and lower edges that contain gel and fold them underneath so they are tucked under the velcro sections that do not contain gel. This allows for more uniform coverage, but also effectively reduces the size of the wrap.

Unlike the Genie XL Pack, the FlexiKold Pack was very pliable straight out of the freezer and could easily conform to the knee with larger overall coverage. It was also very easy to push extra gel into specific locations with the most swelling that needed more cooling. The main issue with the FlexiKold Pack was that it has no straps, so it doesn't allow for much movement, and I also found that I needed to wrap it with something in order to keep it pressed against my leg. With that and the fact that I had to change it more often because it didn't stay as cold, I ended up slightly preferring the Genie XL Pack over the FlexiKold Pack, until...

After using it for about 3 weeks, the Genie XL Pack STARTED LEAKING GEL, so I had to return it (barely inside Amazon's 30-day return window). Upon close inspection, I could see that the edges of it were poorly made and not sewn or reinforced in any way. Now I am left with the FlexiKold, which is much more durable, with higher quality stitching around the edges for reinforcement. It still lasts long enough for me at this stage (about an hour), and the fact that I have to wrap something around it (since it doesn't have straps) is actually no more annoying then the extra steps I had to do for the Genie XL (kneading, then folding in the edges, and constantly readjusting it as the gel warms).

Even though it has some major design flaws, I still gave this Genie XL Pack 3 stars because it stays very cold for a long time, and also comes with straps for moving around that some of the better gel packs don't have.

title: Yes, it is that good. No, it's not a miracle.
text: It is easily the longest-lasting, most chemical-resistant paint protection product short of a ceramic coating. Will it last a full year? Not for a daily driver parked outside 24/7 in the Pacific Northwest. But it will last well for 7-8 months under those conditions, enough for the rainy season. Nothing else will short of a coating—not Collinite 476, not Sonax PNS, not any of the "ceramic" spray coatings (except maybe Griots 3-in-1). So it will last 1/2–2/3 as long as a coating-lite such as Gyeon Can Coat or Carpro Lite, but it is several times cheaper per application (a tin is 2/3 the price and is good for 15-20 applications) and it does not require being protected from water for 12-24 hours like the coatings. (Do not apply any coating unless you can keep the vehicle inside for 12-24 hours. I don't have a garage, so I can't use a coating. Plus, it is much less prone to water spotting than coatings. It takes a bit longer to a)pply than the coating-lites, but not much, and there is no cure time. It is not difficult as long as  you apply it very thinly. Do wear gloves and a mask, and store it in an air-tight container or outside your living area.

In fact, I never had to buy another pair until I moved to Tennessee and the Bluettes didn't make it with me. I found Bluettes through Amazon.

I would never buy any other household gloves.

title: Incredible Game-Changing Head/Face Shaver
text:
My bald friend once asked me the question, “How do you shave your head?” I often wondered how others do as well. Some people use razor blades and shaving cream for the closest and smoothest shave possible. I unfortunately can/should not use a blade so electric was the right thing for me. I struggled with bald clippers for a year or two that hurt and cut my head if nicked at the wrong angle. It was never a close shave either. I tried using my face shaver on my head and that got a close shave and was convenient with cleanup but it burned my head BAD leaving burn streaks and giving me the worst pain with taking a shower right after. My head would be burning and itching for days leaving me with an awful and uncomfortable feeling.

(Head) So I did some research and voila! I stumbled upon The Bald Eagle! I read a bunch of reviews and had to go for it. After the first use my mouth dropped. This thing is INCREDIBLE. It is a nice smooth, close shave that does not hurt, does not burn and incredibly, does not leave hair clippings anywhere on your head or body. You can shave your head and not even have to hop in the shower to clean up! After using it for a month, the shave gets better and closer as I use it.

(Face & Neck) Since I was a teenager, I’m 30 now, I’ve struggled with Pseudofolliculitis Barbae which consists of hair being shaved on my neck, causing the sensitive skin to be irritated which results in hairs curling into my neck creating bumps. I’ve used blades with sensitive gel recommended by doctors but that did nothing and still had this problem. I used my face shaver which, once again, burned and irritated my neck. I've struggled with this for years. Since trying The Bald Eagle on my face and neck, it has been a dream come true. My neck does not hurt or burn and I have very minimal bumps a couple of days after use. Such an incredible device that has changed my life forever.

To clean it is simple by putting it into a warm bowl of water right after use and turning it on for 5 seconds. All of the hair clipping are released and your shaver is clean. Amazing. Nice comfortable design with an incredibly long battery life! I now enjoy shaving my head knowing that it will be a close shave and it will not hurt upon completion.

I just wanted those who struggle with finding the best and quickest way to shave their head that there is an incredible device out there that smokes the competition.

title: Same old low quality
text:
I have replaced the shaving head many times. They all fail in the same way: the center two cutters break free and fall out. This latest is the worst yet in terms of life. It was placed in service on 9-13-2020, and it failed on 10-29-2020, for a total of 47 days of use. You would think that that I would be mad a Braun, but I am really mad at myself for being stupid enough to continue buying these things. One of the definitions of insanity is repeating the same action and expecting a different result, so I guess there is some insanity involved.
Like many who have experienced these Braun shaver head failures, I justified the replacement by telling myself that the razor was so expensive, I could not give up on it. This last failure is the last straw. I give up, time to try a Panasonic. For anyone experiencing the same failure, my advice is give it up and move on.
I am sure that a Braun rep will read this and reply with the same old canned response about calling them. I am done with Braun forever. They got a reputation for quality shavers years ago with their simple design. The later ones are poorly designed and overly complicated.

title: it feels damn good. It also does a good enough job shaping ...
text: My beard is wiry. I had been using my one of my girlfriend's stiff hairbrushes to straighten it out, until she caught me. So, I had to get my own. The bristles on this brush are *very* soft compared to the one I'd been using. In fact, it pampers your face. The first time I used it, it made me giggle. This won't grab your beard and straighten it out. But, it feels damn good. It also does a good enough job shaping the beard if you use some product. I use both a beard balm and a little bit of oil to groom my beard. This brush comes in a tin. I put a tiny bit of oil in the tin so it gets on the bristles, and use that to brush my beard after using the balm. I use the balm mostly for the skin under the beard, and because it does a better job in helping the beard hold its shape. With that combination, this brush works to keep my beard in order. I really don't think it would work very well if you didn't use an oil or a balm with it. If you're looking for something stiff that will pull your beard straight, this isn't it. But if you've never tried soft bristles and want to give it a shot, this is a great brush and I'm very satisfied. I can't say I ever really looked forward to brushing my beard until I got this thing, that's how good it feels. Is it worth the money? To me, yes, I'm happy I bought it. But I didn't try anything cheaper, so I can't really compare. I can't think of anything I'd change about it, other than I would like a handle on the top of the brush so it'd be easier to remove from the tin, and easier to hold on to while brushing.

title: Drastic reduction of students getting out of their chairs!
text:
I teach 9th grade English. I purchased these the first time in the middle of the 2021-2022 school year because I had a few students who could not stay seated. They were good kids with great attitudes. However, they kept disrupting the class to throw something away, or to go sharpen their pencils, or one of a million other piddly little things that could and should wait.

I asked one of the students with the worst ADHD if he would help me with an experiment. I did not tell him what experiment was. I also asked a few other students in the class, both with and without ADHD to join in so that he wouldn't feel singled out. At the end of the class, I asked him what he noticed about the band during class. On a normal day, this kid would get out of his seat 10 times. He could get in trouble, see a principle, have his parent speak to him, then two seconds later get up out of his chair again SMH. He could not control the behavior. Back to his response about the band. He said, "Mr. *****, I didn't feel a need to get out of my chair."

HALLELUJAH! The heavens opened up! A light shone down upon my classroom. Doves fluttered above our heads. Angelic voices sang school hymns. Bacon mana strips fell from the skies and sizzled to a perfect crispness, even though cool enough to hold, as they hit our outstretched hands....

The bands, of course, are not a cure. The students will still act out. Just because it helps with their focus does not mean the bands cure ADHD. They do help the kids focus, though. Some days will be better than others. Some, not so much. As all educators know, every little bit helps. The kid did continue to get out of his chair over the course of the year, but instead of 10 times a day, he would only leave his seat 5 or 6 times.

I found two downsides. A few students will kick the bands loudly and make noise. I make sure those students do NOT have a band. Plus, by end of the year, they are caked with whatever was on the bottom of the students' shoes. Use gloves to remove them from the feet of the chair. Since they are rubber, they are easily cleaned.

text:
Pro:
- It does one thing reasonably well: turns a light on slowly at a specified time

Con:
- It does a bunch of other stuff poorly

I had one of these for about 8 years until a power surge killed it. I won't be buying a replacement. It did the one thing I wanted, but outside of the sunrise light, it just has...quirks:
- It either loses or gains time, I think based on ambient temperature
- Occasionally, it just reverts to a 30 minute wake up sequence instead of the 15 I set it to
- The white noise has patterns in it that you'll eventually hear and fixate on, rendering it useless
- The white noise also has no volume control, I had to put it on a sweater to make it quieter
- It takes 10-20 button presses to change the alarm time from 7 am to 7:30, and that's not counting the button presses to change the minutes

You get all of this for about $115, way too expensive for what it actually does.

text:
I purchased the Glowa Sonic facial cleansing brush ten days ago to replace a Clarisonic that I loved (because Clarisonic is no longer made). I guess I should have read all of the questions before purchasing, not just the reviews. After trying 6 other brushes, I finally found one that I liked! This is the best option to replace the Clarisonic that I've found. I like it enough that I wanted to buy replacement brush heads to let my son try it so I could order another for him if he likes it. When I went to Amazon to order the replacement brush heads, I found there are no replacement brush heads available even though they've been promised for months!!

Are they going to have replacement brush heads? If so, what type? Will there be one that is a little firmer than the ones that come with the brush (they're a little too soft for my liking)? How much will they cost? Very disappointed that they released a product that requires regular replacement of a part without having the replacement part available!

If they don't have replacement brush heads available before my return deadline I'll be returning the one I purchased rather than buying another. I'll update this post if I find that they are available before my return deadline.

I ended up returning it and purchased another one on Amazon that only supported cold water.

TLDR: The bidet does not heat the water so you need a hot water access point near by. The bidet stopped working while I was installing it and customer service email on the instructions was no help because they have stopped supporting this product.

title: Completes the Fitbit Experience
text:
I started using the Fitbit Ultra in January, and have dropped 19 pounds. Wearing the pedometer/altimeter/calorie counter, and syncing with the apps on my computer and iPhone have helped me triple the number of steps and stairs climbed every day. I use the LoseIt app, which integrates with the Fitbit site, to count calories. And now the Aria scale completes the array.

No more playing games with when and how I weigh, All are recorded, and a clear record is there to see, in numbers and graphically. I had been planning to buy the scale, but was thrilled when my daughters gave it to me as a birthday gift. My husband has also been using Fitbit and has dropped 14 pounds since June-he loves to weigh himself many times a day and watch his weight fluctuate.

My first Fitbit started to "peel" last month, and I had a new replacement within days. I think this is such a terrific product that I have bought 5 of them now (two for husband whio lost first one, ond for daughter, one for friend). The scale only adds to my satisfaction.

title: The stem came detached from the plug on both pairs and one stem remained lodged in my ear canal.
text: This is the third pair of these ear plugs I have purchased.  My husband and I had no issues with the other 2 pairs but I was wearing the third pair for the first time last night while working at a large NYE music festival and both malfunctioned.  The stem came detached from the plug on both pairs and one stem remained lodged in my ear canal.  I could not get it out with my fingers and trying to get it out only pushed it further and further into my ear and caused pain and discomfort.  Unfortunately I was at a paid photography gig and could not miss my assigned acts and I had to stand directly in front of numerous giant speakers with no ear protection for an extended time due to this.  At a break I had to go to a medical tent to have the stem removed.  Fortunately they gave me a different pair of plugs to wear for the rest of the concert.  It has not been 30 days since I bought these, but I cannot easily find a way to contact the seller about these issues via my orders in Amazon.  Now I am also scared to use any of the three pairs and risk this happening again.  It is the next day after the concert and my left ear is still sore and tender from this.  I feel I was close to damaging my ear drum and that is scary.  It was very uncomfortable to have the medical staff digging around in my ear with the tweezers to remove the stem as it was quite deep in my ear canal.

title: Worthy replacement to the ER20s
text:
Got this to replace my [[ASIN:B0044DEESS Etymotic Research ER20 ETY-Plugs Hearing Protection Earplugs, Standard Fit, Clear Stem with Blue Tip (Light Blue)]] (lost them at a concert). After going through reviews all the similar products sold, ultimately chose this for what other reviews seem to indicate: more comfort / smaller form factor (ER20 standard was comfortable enough for my ear size but personally feel the stem gets in the way) and comparable dB reduction.

Fits about the same as the ER20 Standard Fit but feels like it went in deeper (probably due to lack of long stem) and dB reduction feels comparable. Tubular keychain carrying case is a plus. They are definitely more comfortable than the ER20s for my ear. I have left it on for 6+ hours and also slept with it without any problems or discomfort.

In shows I have brought these to (rock & electronic shows mostly), the decibel reduction were pretty level, softening sharp highs (crash, high frequency noises) without muddying vocals. As I no longer have the ER20s to compare side-by-side with, I cannot comment on the difference of audio quality between the two.

Overall, definitely happy with the purchase!

text:
I very rarely write reviews for anything so the fact that I'm writing this should probably tell you something. I bought these ear plugs for a concert at a very small, loud venue. I was able to hear everything--the band and my friends standing next to me. I totally felt like I got the full concert experience. Several people in my group noted how obscenely loud the concert was so when I pointed out that I was wearing earplugs (they couldn't see them in my ears!) I looked like a genius. But the real test of these ear plugs was that I had absolutely no ringing in my ears when I left the club. Nothing. Nada.

Some people have made comments about the size of the ear plugs in their reviews. I have fairly small ear canals so I actually thought they were pretty big. I also didn't have any problems getting them out, but if you have large ears I suppose you might.

In sum, I loved these and thought that the price was reasonable (especially if you have Prime). Keep in mind, though, I don't have anything to compare them to...other than not having them and that's not an option anymore. I will take these with me to every concert I attend from now on!

title: Awesome Ear Plugs
text:
I have tried a vast array of different earplugs over the years, spanning from inexpensive single-use foam plugs to some of the higher-end silicone models (though I've never sprung for custom fits from an audiologist).

I play music in a couple of bands, and go to shows relatively frequently, so I try to find plugs that meet a few requirements: (1) they form a good seal, (2) they're comfortable enough to be worn for hours on end, and (3) they don't completely inhibit conversation or awareness of the environment. I also prefer to find plugs that are (4) relatively flat in frequency response and (5) have minimal profiles when inserted to avoid unwanted jostling, though these are preferences, not hard requirements.

Simply put, these plugs are hands-down the best in categories 2-3 and 5 I've ever tried. The double-flange silicone forms a comfortable seal, and the plugs themselves aren't easily jostled or start to come loose if I sweat or move around. For category 1, the plugs don't beat out the one-time foam, or other heavier re-usable products like Hearos Skull Screws, but they actually come quite close to that level of sound rejection, while also far and away more comfortable and much flatter in frequency response. These are real winners in my book, I recommend them to my musician friends all the time.

My one complaint is that the key chain case is a little awkward to open/close. Unlike the more common squeeze case you see with Etymotic or similar designs, these cases require two hands to open/close. The trade-off is that while it's more difficult to operate (and I personally cannot do it one-handed like the squeeze cases), the case provides a better seal to protect from outside dirt and moisture (I believe the case is even water-tight). So that makes this a relatively small inconvenience, and the case does perform the tasks it's designed to do.

title: The show was fantastic and all of the bands were amazing
text: I don't write many reviews. As a matter of fact, I think this may be my second, but I feel compelled to do so after testing these out. A few weeks ago, I went to see Doyle (formerly of the Misfits) along with the Bloodline, Pain, and Sixteen Cylinder at a small club in Maryland. I wore a cheap pair of foam ear plugs to the show. The show was fantastic and all of the bands were amazing. However, my ear plugs blocked out much of the sound. So much so that I kept one out at all times and rotated between my left and right ear just so I could hear the bands. After a few songs, this no longer worked either because I had to squash the plugs to get them in my ear. This would work for a few minutes and then the plug would return to its natural form and I would have to put it back in. Eventually this got annoying, so I gave up entirely on the plugs and enjoyed the music. For the next week, my ears rang and I was concerned that I may have permanently damaged my hearing. Thankfully I have recovered since. This leads me to these plugs by DownBeats. I had the pleasure of seeing Coal Chamber, Filter, Combichrist, and Saint Ridley the other night. title: DownBeats compared to ER-20
text:
I'm a long-time user of the [[ASIN:B0044DEESS Etymotic ER20 attenuators]]. I have both sizes of Etys, and I just bought some of these DownBeats.

Here's my comparison.

The DownBeats come in a robust aluminum case. They don't rattle inside (there's a plastic liner), and the base doesn't unscrew and fall off the lid. It does clank on my keys, so I wrapped it in tape. It's easy to get the plugs out of the case.

The Etys come in a rubbery plastic squeeze-case. Also fine on a keychain, but a little more bulky, lighter, and a lot less noisy. The rubbery case gets dirty and beat up over time. It can be difficult to get the plugs out.

The DownBeats are shorter -- only two flanges against the Etys three, and a stubby stem. That makes them smaller and less noticeable from the front -- the stem doesn't poke out from your ears. But the stems of the Etys are clear, while the DBs are white; from the side the Etys are less noticeable for that reason.

The shortness is an advantage under a helmet, hat, or laying against a pillow, but it slightly works against the DBs when inserting and removing. Only slightly, though.

Now, on to comfort and fit.

The flanges on the DBs are as fat as the large Etys. If you have small-to-medium ears, that might affect how well they fit.

To me, with mid-to-large ears, both the white (large) Etys and the DBs are noticeable in the ear -- there's a constant gentle feeling of pressure when inserted. It's not bothersome, but you do notice it when compared to the smaller Etys.

The Etys go deeper into the ear, and have a longer stem. That makes them less comfortable than the DBs. The comfort distinction is exaggerated if you're moving your ears or wearing something on your head -- the stem moves and applies pressure inside the ear canal.

By contrast, the smaller blue Etys are slightly more comfortable than the DBs, but only if you stay still and don't move your face!

Sound-wise: all three are good, and to most ears there won't be a difference in attenuation or sound quality. Fit is the most important factor to how these perform for you.

Comparing back-to-back with good over-the-ear headphones is too close to call regarding quality: it would be dishonest to make a judgment. The DBs seem to attenuate slightly more than the blue Etys, which makes sense -- the blue Etys are probably a tiny bit too small for my ears. The DBs seem to have a more even attenuation curve, blocking heavy basslines a little better than the Etys.

In conclusion: I'm carrying and wearing the DBs. I find them more comfortable, I prefer the way they sound, and I value the small improvement in attenuation.

If you have small ears, have trouble inserting or removing earplugs, or want a soft case, you might prefer the Etymotic ER20s. If you find deep earplugs uncomfortable, need a lower-profile appearance, or want a hard case, go for the DBs. If you're stuck between the two, the DownBeats are a good choice.

title: Accurate but painful for small arms
text:
I've been using this cuff for a few months now. It appears quite accurate, but it is often very uncomfortable to use. I have used it a couple dozen times, and I would say 75% of those times, the cuff squeezed to the point that my arm lost circulation and I started to get that 'pins and needles' feeling. Sometimes, the cuff takes a long time to measure on top of that. For instance, it typically inflates up to about 160, and then slowly counts down while barely deflating. Today, it counted all the way down to 20 before finally releasing the pressure on my arm. A few times (not often), it did this and then said error, so I had to repeat the process.

It is worth noting that I have fairly low blood pressure (~100/65 or so) and a small arm. My husband has higher blood pressure (~130/75) and a bigger arm, and he has had a fairly normal experience with the cuff; it doesn't cut off his circulation and usually reads his blood pressure quicker.

title: This Is Authentic Wild Harvested Sea Moss
text:
This is the real deal. Authentic wild harvested sea moss as described by Dr Sebi. It is golden in color (not pale), the stems were thin (not thick), it smelled like the ocean (not chlorine), had no salt on them was completely dry (not moist) when received, and was crunchy but not brittle when squeezed and stretched.

I used the soaked method to keep it raw as I’m not a fan of the boil method. Heating sea moss unless adding it to meals is counter productive to me. It started coming right back to life during the first rinse. After you’ve rinsed the sea moss in running water, soak it in spring/distilled water this rinse it in running water again, soak it in spring/distilled water for 24-72 hrs in covered glass bowl or jar. Blend it in the same water it soaked in for the 24+ hrs to maintain the minerals released into the water by the sea moss. It gels great.

The 16oz bag yields four to five batches that went into 9x9 glass baking container with a top. I cut it into 16 pieces with one piece as one serving. It lasts my family a week and is a great deal for $35 every 5weeks. It delivers fast. The ad for the 8oz says it comes from St Lucia but the 16oz bag says it comes from Jamaica. Both locations are great to harvest sea moss.

Please keep this great quality Red Kitchen Sink and you will always have a customer in us.

I bought another brand called Mr Seamoss, in case Red’s Kitchen Sink wasn’t the real deal, and it was horrible. First it comes from Vietnam and not the Caribbean, even though he says he’s from Trinidad. It yields no way near as much a Red’s Kitchen Sink as comes moist (not dry), full of sand, salt and debris. The debris was pieces of plastic and a long strand of hair. It looks like it’s starting to mold with very dark soft spots akin to mold. He has no social media that I could find to comment directly on his product which is suspicious too. We will use it as a topical only since he charges $15 in shipping we won’t get back plus we’d have to pay to return it to him. I’m not trying to down the brother but his business is not up to par and should not be supported until it meets the quality standards set by Dr Sebi and the rest of the sea moss community.

title: Effective BCAA Product!
text:
If you’ve done any amount of research on BCAAs, then you know they are great for increasing your fitness level whether you are wanting to build muscle, cut fat and/or increase endurance. BCAA stands for Branch Chain Amino Acids are known throughout the fitness world as the “building blocks” of the body.

BCAAs can be beneficial to any fitness program. They make up a large portion of muscle mass and are important to any supplement program. Basically, there are 8 amino acids that are considered essential, meaning your body cannot manufacture them and you must get them in your diet. The rest of the amino acids are non-essential, meaning that your body can make them with proper diet.

This particular product has Leucine 3,000mg, Isoleucine 1500mg and Valine 1500mg in each scoop. This is the recommended 2:1:1 ratio of BCAAS. The bottle provides 40 of these servings. One thing about powder amino acids is they don’t taste very good but you can always mix it with something if you don’t like the taste. I’ve taken the pill form of BCAAs for years and it’s quite a bit of pills to take. For example, you would have to take roughly 2 servings of the pill form to equal one scoop of NutraFx BCAAs which makes this a very good product for those who don’t like to take pills.

This product also came with an awesome shaker cup! It’s probably the best one I’ve ever had. It has a cone inside to help break up the protein and a container that screws into the bottom where you can store an extra serving of protein or to put extra supplements in. Pretty sturdy build also.

There are a lot of different ways to take BCAAs, but the preferred method for powders are during a workout. My supplement stack consists of a pre-workout consisting of Creatine, an energy blend that has caffeine, a “pump” blend that has various versions of L-Arginine and vitamins. During workout, I take BCAAs and if I’m using a powder, I sip it during the workout. Post workout is always followed by a protein shake of at least 25 grams of protein with 3-5 more grams of Creatine. I always try to eat a high protein snack within an hour or so of training.

Add a good BCAA product like this one to your supplements and you will be able to do more work in the gym and build muscle faster than ever. I received a reduced price for this product in exchange for an honest review. As always, if you have any questions about this product or training in general feel free to ask!

title: Impressive craving control
text:
I'm not a huge eater, but I'm about 30lb overweight 190/160. I suffer from problematic sinus and asthma issues that keep me from being able to do any kind of extreme training regimens. In addition to that I'm genetically engineered to have random cravings for tacobell and candy or other nonsense despite being a bit of a healthnut. I just can't control myself. I workout in the mornings with light weightlifting, pullups, squats, situps and then run about 2 to 5 miles in the evenings.
I decided to give this a shot on a whim, because I didn't want to load up on something dangerous or fancy. I'm on my fourth day of it and I'm impressed. I still have cravings from time to time but its much more under control. Before work I drink this mixed with milk and a glass of naked or bolthouse Banana/berry mix juice. The milk helps thin it out and make it less of a smoothy. This ends up being surprisingly tasty though you need to mix it well. I noticed immediately the sugar cravings are gone. I have one those of workplaces where people are in your face with the donuts constantly and I'm able to stay away easily and I'm in no hurry for lunch and no real craving even at dinner.
I think if you are really struggling with food and want a magic cure this is not for you, but if you're actively fighting the good fight and could use a little help this at least for me seems well worth it. My advice is to not bother with fancy diets. Figure out a way to eat healthier but still enjoy yourself. Otherwise it's hard not to bounce back to bad habits after punishing yourself with an awful boxed probar atkins clone diet or whatevers hip this week.
I will update after I run through this container.

title: Wonderful product!
text: I used the first edition of this book 2 1/2 years ago when my son was born.  I was a first time mother and had ZERO experience with child care.  Needless to say, my learning curve was very steep.  This book was my bible.  I used it myself for the first four months, documenting when and how much my son ate, how many diapers he went through, his sleep schedule, and most importantly, the immunizations.  When it was time for me to go back to work, my nanny used it as well.  It was a great tool to keep us both on the same page.  When I came home, I didn't have to ask her a million questions about how he slept, what he ate, how many diapers he went through, etc.  It was all there in the book.  It also came in handy when grandma watched him or daddy was home alone with him.  It was the perfect way to document the first year and keep everyone in the loop.  I intend to use it again for my second child when he or she is born in a couple months.  I will reference my son's book with regards to his sleep schedule for my new baby.  That part was my favorite.  The first month or so was very sporadic with regards to his sleep pattern, but after some time, a pattern emerged.  It was nice knowing why he was crying.  Just a quick glance allowed me to see that it was time for him to go to sleep or needed to be fed.  It's also a nice keepsake in addition to his primary baby book.  I highly recommend this book for all mothers.  Lack of sleep and "baby brain" makes it hard for the first few months to keep everything straight, and when there are other caregivers involved, it's a must.

Bought this because I am pregnant with twins...my midwife recommended it and I finally gave in when I learned I was measuring 41 weeks pregnant at 33 weeks. It has been a lifesaver, especially since I have three other (kiddos ages 6, 3, and 2) to keep up with!
