I also have enough high-necked shirts in my wardrobe to be able to wear this without the "x" showing--again, were I feeling a bit more energetic it would be simple to unpick the stitching and make the "x" join up lower down, or else to sew on some pretty fabric or lace to disguise it...but at this point in my pregnancy I simply do not care that much. :)

This belly-cradle helps keep away the awfulness of round ligament pain and let me move around much more naturally and freely during the day. I don't wear it at night since I already have a bit of trouble breathing and I don't like the restrictive feeling of the band when I'm lying down. I would highly recommend this to anyone who is pregnant with twins or who just wants a bit of extra support for the final months of pregnancy.

title: Do Your Research! Not the Best Model!!
text:
I rarely take time to write reviews but I have a $1300 invested in this product and want to help other consumers to NOT make the same mistake I did. Please read reviews beyond those here on Amazon and do plenty of research before you invest in a robotic cleaner. I should have listened to the reviewer that warned the machine ejected debris that ultimately settles back into your pool so it is an endless cycle. My pool will look clean but after a few hours or the next morning after all the fine stuff has settled again, there are all sorts of little piles and the corners of the deep end are dirty again. As soon as I realized I reached out to the company that sold it to me since o am a Prime member and I was told it is a type of merchandise that is excluded from being returnable. The merchant told me to contact the manufacturer because it must be defective. I did that immediately. The manufacturer told me it must me my basket is not the right size and I must need the fine or ultra fine basket “which don’t normally come with the machine but we will send sue to your inconvenience.” I responded i was looking forward to receiving both. Today i heard from the agent she was sending me just the fine basket which I had realized over the weekend is what I have been using. I just sent her that information with photos of the results. It is not successful!! I am really curious why a company would sell a machine without the basket that is going to catch all of the stuff that is inevitably going to be in a pool? It is preposterous to me quite frankly. At this point, I am not confident that ultra fine basket is going to make the difference.

The machine itself is easy to clean and study. The cord is a hood length and doesn’t twist too much.

But at the end of the day I would not recommend this machine to anyone who doesn’t have $1300 to throw away.

title: It's good for a year?
text:
I purchased this scale in 2013 and for the most part it worked well - recently I had to change the batteries and afterwards I started to get an error. After researching the error, I was informed by the Fitbit Community that this was a known error and to contact Fitbit Support and they would replace. After exchanging several emails with FItbit Support and trying different remedies, to no avail, I was informed that because my scale was over 365 days old, there was nothing they could do. See below:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Hello Michael,

Thank you for getting back in touch with us.

We can imagine how disappointed you may feel at this moment. Our limited warranty provides replacements for scales deemed to have a manufacturer's defect within 365 days of purchase and we stand behind the products are within this time frame. Because your scale didn't meet these warranty conditions, we are unable to provide a complimentary replacement.

We strive for excellent customer service and though customer satisfaction remains our number one goal, the demands of running a global business require that we enforce our warranty consistently.

Thank you for being a Fitbit customer.

Sincerely,

Adriana A and the Fitbit Team
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

I suggested a new slogan for Fitbit "Hopefully our products last longer than 365 days - because after that, we're off the hook!"

title: Lemonine, Ethanol and Ozone Combined. Neuralized cat urine odor.
text:
Some mad genius combined lemonine, ethanol and ozone. Please don't blow yourself up trying to mix that stuff at home, I'm only mentioning the ingredients to give a reasonably intelligent person an idea of how this product works.

Was skeptical of this stuff at first. It isn't exactly cheap. As far as I know, Volcom only occasionally makes shoes and I wanted to be able to wear my Volcoms again. Wore them with no socks one summer and they've been not so fresh ever since. Sprayed them with this stuff and they are odor-free. Didn't go all nutcase crazy and empty a can, just a few seconds of spray while trying to lightly soak the thin canvas. I expected the sweat odor to return after a wear or two but that wasn't the case. This spray actually neutralizes odor. I was able to revamp some of my old Chucks, too. Stuff works on canvas, leather, every material I've tried it on.

Ok, so here's the interesting part:

It also works on carpet.
Have a female cat missing a back leg. She can't help but drag urine on the carpet after she uses the box. As much as I love my kitty friend, that is something I can't tolerate. It's been an issue since I can recall. Tried everything. Tried laundry detergent. Soaked carpet in vinegar, baking soda and a mix of the two. Shampooed and steamed the carpet a dozen times but the pheromones in cat urine are impossible to get rid of. So I tried this spray. Actually alleviated the smell! I can't believe it! I don't mind the faint citrus scent, and it's so much better than cat urine. Worth mentioning that the citrus scent does not seem to fade. It isn't overbearing.

On carpet I sprayed more liberally. I assumed the carpet and the pad were too thick and dense but this stuff is tenacious.

I cannot recommend this spray enough. 100 out of 5 stars.

text: This unit makes a pleasant background noise, similar to the "whoosh" of a well-made fan.  It has two speeds, high and low. It isn't loud enough to fill the entire room, so you might consider purchasing two of these if you are serious about screening out sounds from the outside world.  You'll want to place each one between where you work/sleep/read/whatever and the door or window that is letting noise into your room.  It does seem to work better if you elevate it off of the floor by placing it on a table, stand, or chair.  I find that it compliments my portable fan nicely.  With the two of them placed strategically in my living room, I can work or read without being disturbed by common street noises or the conversations of my neighbors.

Look both ways before crossing, and compare prices before buying.

title: The best product I’ve purchased for tonsil stones
text:
I don’t often write reviews but this product 100% warranted it. I’ve unfortunately been plagued with tonsil stones and purchased many devices ranging from water flosses to long plastic sticks with syringes to dislodge the stones. As time progressed I tried to devise my own solutions using the tools I’ve bought with one being to use the syringe to suck up the stone instead of dislodging them. Thankfully I happened upon this product and it’s been the best purchase I’ve ever made.
The success I’ve had with it is based on placing the suction device directly over the stone on high setting, creating a secure fit around the hole. By applying small back and forth movements, all the stones quickly and more or less painlessly get dislodged. No gagging, no bleeding, no discomfort, and no more wasted time.
This product is a game changer and would 1000% recommend to anyone. Only issue that would be mentioned is the light. If you are able to use the off hand to light up the area and place the suction device over the stone then it will work flawlessly. Otherwise it becomes a bit challenging because there needs to be a secure fit for it to work properly. Even with the illumination issue I still believe this to be the best product sold for tonsil stones.

title: My Experience with this pump...
text:
My Experience with this pump (as a first time mom)...
1. The noise level is actually pretty good compared to other pumps, a few people I pumped around were surprised to know that I was pumping under my cover instead of breastfeeding.

2. Its not the most friendly to clean either. it has too many pieces and I almost lost a some a few times but the plus side to this is that it has the silicone breast pieces which feel a lot better than most other pumps, especially if you have sensitive breasts.

3. But the part that is the worst about this pump (in my experience) is its lifespan. the suction on the pump was great at first but I discovered quickly (less than 2 months of owning it) that it started to lose pressure fast. one side almost lost its suction altogether. not sure if it is just the pump i got. I also had a theory that that is was you get when you buy a pump that doesn't plug into the wall but charges - they are bound to lose pressure/suction over time. As a first time mom, this frustrated me because I thought I wasn't producing enough for my baby.

Overall, I'm giving it more than one star because it did have nice features about it (easy to take places/pump anywhere) but if I could do it over from the beginning, I wouldn't have even put it on my registry.

title: Tangled, indeed....
text:
The major complication here is that you have to be able to FIT all your hair in the center, then manage to roll the darned thing up and snap it shut. If you can. And good luck with that.

I was truly excited when I got mine - 2 weeks later than what they initially said, but hey, it's coming from China, I'm not going to fuss - and got it out of the package. The first thing I thought was, "WOW, this thing is small." But I'll give anything a chance once, so I brushed my hair out and got all the tangles out, then worked to lace my hair through the central hole.

Here is where I met my first challenge. First, the darned hair wouldn't stay in the piece - likely my problem. It's finicky. I have thick, long, deeply wavy/curly hair (curly when it's freshly washed and left to air dry) and it's a monster. I've had it thinned, which is really the only was to tame my beast. So I fought it and fought it, kept having to fight, then finally gave up for a while.

Long and short of it (no pun intended), this thing doesn't work for me.

title: Is Lady-Comp Right for You? (Summary & User Tips about a fantastic device)
text:
This device makes natural birth control about as simple and hassle-free as it can possibly be. I have been using my Lady-Comp successfully for over 3 years and absolutely love it. I have been so impressed with the constant accuracy of the device, despite my somewhat irregular cycles. It gives me reliable and quick information about the status of my cycle and the amount of risk involved in having sex on any given day. This device collects, tracks, and calculates a significant amount of data to determine its daily red/green light displays and cycle information; so, please do not be mistaken that this is just a fancy thermometer or a form of the rhythm-method. The device is MUCH more than that.

The Lady-Comp has provided me with very accurate cycle tracking and ovulation signaling displays. Please note that this accuracy is dependent upon the user being very consistent in taking their daily morning temperature upon waking and faithfully abiding by the red, yellow, and green light signals (which indicate "safe" and "unsafe" days.)

How do I know it is accurately calculating my fertile days? I have been using 3 cross-check measures: I have been using separate fertility tracking software on my computer to cross-check the information my Lady-Comp provides me. I also intermittently do saliva testing with a small microscope kit to test for impending ovulation (the "saliva ferning" method can indicate rising levels of estrogen which triggers ovulation.) I periodically check the position of my cervix, which is an indicator of where a woman is in her cycle. The Lady-Comp's red/green light information coincides with all of these cross-measures every time. And when it comes to alerting me which day my period will start, its accuracy is always spot-on... pun intended. :)

I WOULD HIGHLY RECOMMEND THE LADY-COMP IF YOU...

1) are wishing to avoid or achieve pregnancy naturally, but are daunted by the tediousness of doing your own charting.

2) are interested in tracking the patterns and changes in your cycles so that you can better understand your own body.

3) want a device to remind you when your period will start. (This feature is seldom discussed, but I find it to be one of my favorite features!)

I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THE DEVICE IF...

1) you are certain that you cannot be consistent in using it each morning upon waking up. (This is much easier than it might seem, however. It quickly becomes routine, especially when using the pleasant sounding wake-up alarm. Using the Lady-Comp takes less than one minute each morning with its speedy thermometer. To me, remembering to do this seems no different than remembering to take a pill each day.)

2) you are not ready to stop using hormonal birth control such as the pill, Nuvaring, IUD, hormonal injections, etc. The Lady-Comp cannot be accurate if you are still using hormonal birth control, since these hormonal methods are intended to interfere with ovulation/implantation. (Personally, I find the natural method SO much better for many reasons. The most significant reason is no longer having the terrible side-effects I experienced with hormonal birth control.)

SUMMARY:
If you are considering natural birth control, would like to achieve pregnancy, or are simply wanting to be better informed about your body, I feel this device is WELL worth the money. The device will last you a very long time; so when you consider comparing its cost to the monthly cost of birth control pills over a few years, the Lady-Comp is a very wise investment!

Does idea of completely relying on a computerized device for birth control still seem a bit nerve-wracking to you? If so, I would suggest learning to check your other fertility signals to use in combination with the Lady-Comp. (See the recommended book in following paragraph.) You can also use a barrier method along with the Lady-Comp for awhile, until you gain full confidence in the Lady-Comp's accuracy. Even if you decide to continue using a barrier device along with the Lady-Comp, the information and knowledge it provides you ALONE makes it worth every dollar, in my opinion.

Like other reviewers, I highly recommend the book "Taking Charge of Your Fertility" by Toni Weschler as a companion to using this device. It will provide you with wonderful information that will compliment your use of the Lady-Comp and help you understand your cycles and your body. It even comes with a free trial version of fertility tracking software. I saw a copy at my public library, so check your library if you would like to glance through it first. (I would recommend eventually obtaining your own personal copy, however, as I find myself going back to mine for reference quite frequently.)

I wish I had known about this device years ago. I write this review in hopes of encouraging other women that there ARE effective alternatives to hormonal birth control, and the Lady-Comp is one that makes natural birth control very easy.

USER TIPS:

* Remember, a red light means you ARE highly likely to get pregnant if you have unprotected sex. If you choose to use barrier protection during those red light days instead of abstaining, keep this in mind: IF the barrier fails or is not used correctly, there is a very high probability of pregnancy on any red light days! If it is very important that you not get pregnant, then it would be advisable to abstain from intimate contact during those red-light days! The great thing about this device is that it can provide quick information about the status of your cycle and the amount of risk involved in having sex on any given day. It is then up to the user to decide what to do with that knowledge. You can decide how careful you need to be and how much risk you are willing to assume on those days.

* Although the device stores and gives you access to cycle information (such as recorded temps) for up to 6 months of prior use, I recommend periodically going back through the info on the display and writing your daily temps down on a calendar. (You can access these by pushing a few buttons on the device.) Enter these temps into separate fertility tracking software to see an actual chart of your cycle. The device itself will not give you a chart that you can see or print. A printed chart of past cycles can be helpful to give to your doctor, especially when you are trying to achieve pregnancy or if you are having cycle irregularity problems.

* Be prepared that it will take several months for the device to become familiar with your cycles. Green light = a safe day. Red light = an unsafe day. Yellow light = the device is not sure or is "learning." You will probably get quite a few yellow lights the first month or two, so you will want to plan to use barrier protection if you don't plan on abstaining on those yellow days. This is especially true if you are just coming off the pill or other hormonal method, as your cycles may be irregular at first. (The device comes with specific instructions for users who have just finished taking the pill or other hormonal method; so make sure you read those first.) Be patient for the first few months; because, soon, you should get very few yellow lights unless you miss taking your temp for several days. My device gave me no yellow lights by the third month.

title: Disappointing
text:
I had high expectations after reading all the other rave reviews for this 8-disc set. After listening to "Nutrition" and "Common Concerns" I was slightly underwhelmed but still wanted to give the "All About Labor" a chance to redeem itself... no such luck.

This is my first pregnancy and I don't think I've done tons of reading or research on the labor & delivery process, but the whole time I was watching the DVD I kept thinking "even I could have put together this powerpoint presentation!" The photos were nice the first few mintues, but seeing still-photos and words on the screen the whole time did NOT make me feel prepared or educated.

The other night I attempted to try another of the audio discs and was again disappointed. Just *skimming* through The Birth Partner or the Bradley Method gives me a much better sense of preparedness, and neither of them cost as much as this disc set. Hopefully, MyBirthClass will stand behind their 60-day money back guarantee.

=============UPDATE=================
MyBirthClass was very good about providing a refund. They informed me that they've created a "Gold Edition" disc set. In the Gold Edition there are only 6 discs total. The "Labor&Delivery" DVD is *much* more informative and includes interviews with Drs., couples, and is hosted by Becky herself! I love the part where she demonstrates effacement with a knitted uterus & softball; she explains lots of options and its obvious she's tried several of them in her own pregnancies/deliveries.

If you buy the Perfectly Prepared Birth Class In a Box, be sure you get the GOLD EDITION... much better than the original!

text:
I purchased the RiteLite with the intention of using it in a show booth to illuminate my photographs. I was attracted to the product because it ran on batteries instead of AC power. LED's gave it had a long battery life. I confirmed this by leaving it on for over 5 straight hours. It can definitely be left on for much longer without changing batteries.

The gooseneck and tilting light head are great features but inadequate. The gooseneck is too short and/or the head does not tilt enough. With the light on, you can see the lit LED's because there is no front shield. This shouldn't be the case with a true picture light as it distracts from the image. At least the beam is somewhat focused so light didn't spill too much towards the viewer. A front shield/reflector would make this a better product because, despite 6 LED's, the light could not cover a 16x24 area.

In end I didn't use this light and wouldn't recommend it for artwork much larger than an 8x10 (not including the frame).

title: Proved to be ineffective at managing Lyme
text: I had high hopes for this product after a year and a half of encapsulating my own whole herb capsules for a year and a half. This product, as a combination of herbal extracts targeted at Lyme, promises greater convenience for people like me who managed Lyme with whole herbs. Over the course of two months use of this product, my condition gradually deteriorated. While I was managing my Lyme effectively previously and was without symptoms, I gradually developed sleep disturbances and fatigue while using this - though at the time, I didn't attribute those symptoms to Lyme. However, this product was out of stock recently, and I had no other option but to return to my previous herb treatment protocol. Like every other time I have "herxed" before (Herheimer reaction - exaggerated symptoms caused by rapid die-off of the pathogen), 24 hours after taking my herb combination caused a serious reaction. It is evident that if this product was effective at managing Lyme, there would be no reason for me to "herx" when switching products. I will not use this product again.

title: Great product, questionable company
text:
I've been buying this product direct from ProHealth for quite a few years. It works exactly as advertised, and is well-priced compared to Mucinex. However, I see that I can now purchase 400 mg guaifenesin much more cheaply under the Kirkland & Maker's Mark brands, and will cease purchasing from ProHealth immediately. Why? First, they have yet to send a "your order has been shipped" message that includes the name of the product shipped. Since I receive several different products from them, I never can tell what they've shipped until it arrives. When I commented about this to them, they said they had been unable to figure out how to get their email to include the product name. Until a few months ago, their emails didn't even include a subject heading. It's unbelievable that they can't get their email system to work properly. It just isn't that hard. Second, as noted by another reviewer, their packaging leaves something to be desired. Everything is shipped in bubble-lined mailers. This is not a good way to protect a non-flat shipment. Third, while they sell a certain number of good and useful products, their primary sales pitch is woo. Homeopathy, idiocy about "natural" products, conflicting health recommendations (people with fibromyalgia should avoid aspirin because it contains salicylates, but should take willow bark extract, which is merely a salicyclate with an uncontrolled amount of active ingredient, but hey, it's natural), proprietary combinations of supplements pushed by the doctors who developed them (beware doctors who make money off of selling you proprietary supplements--they have every incentive not to be impartial when creating a treatment plan). Their website is a masterpiece of nonsense, lumping valid study results with conjectures from the journal Medical Hypotheses (as the name suggests, this is a journal in which people publish suggestions for possible future studies, not actual scientific findings) and anecdotal tales from consumers.

So, 5 stars for the product, 0 for the company, averaging out to 3. Buy guaifenesin 400 mg because it works, but not from ProHealth.

title: Nice Shine
text: I have a new Toyota Tundra TRD, that I purchased in May, 2021. It is now August. I have been taking it to a state-of-the art touchless car wash to be sure that I don't get swirl marks from dirty cloth car washes. I just used the product the day before yesterday. The directions state that I don't need to wash the vehicle. I trust only in my own judgement on that one. I don't want to grind in road debris with my towel. I went to the car wash, sprayed tar and bug remover on the front of the vehicle as always, pulled in, had the pre rinse, then had the foam soak, power wash and rinse, let their power drier blow it off, drove home and began applying the wax. My garage is a side facing garage, that I make a 90 degree turn into. I parked in the morning shade of it, while the temperature was cool. I sprayed Fukken wax on, one panel at a time. I lightly spread it around with the nappy side of the cloth then let it dry to a haze. I went on to the next panel and repeated those two steps as the first panel was drying. I flipped my cloth over to the micro fiber side and polished the first panel. I had a nice shine. Then I polished the second panel with the micro fiber side. When I completed the vehicle, there was still a bit of tar and bug type debris stuck to the front area of the truck. This was expected because the truck had never been waxed. I sprayed more wax on and lightly spread it around. I let it soak for three minutes. Then I polished it off, using a bit of elbow grease with the micro fiber side. It removed most of the persistent debris. I used the side of the cloth that was soaked with the wax and gave it more elbow grease. The debris came off. I let it dry to a haze. I polished it with the micro fiber side of the towel. I let everything stand for about fifteen minutes. Then I pulled out a clean towel and buffed the entire truck to a brilliant shine. I followed up and did the windows. This product works by following the directions, regarding application, and following up with a final buffing with a clean towel, using the micro fiber side. Remember, when you first spray it on, shake it up and just lightly spread it around so that it can soak in and lift remaining dirt or grime. Then let it dry to a haze. Then polish with the clean side of your towel or with a fresh micro fiber towel. Let it stand for a while. Then polish the whole vehicle with a clean micro fiber towel. You will be pleased with the results. I have never used Fukken wax before and it works very well.

title: My Favorite Plant-Based Protein Powder
text: I'm about ready to order my third container of Sunwarrior's Classic Plus Protein Powder as I absolutely love it! I always order the Natural flavor (no added flavors or stevia) and place one scoop of the protein powder and approximately 10 oz. nondairy milk (soy, almond, or both), 1/2 tbsp. cacao powder, 1 tsp. maca powder, 1/2 tbsp. maple syrup, and a splash of vanilla extract into a blender bottle and shake. Sometimes I put together the shake the night before, keep it in the fridge overnight, and drink it after my morning workout (the shake tends to thicken a little after being refrigerated overnight). To me, the taste and texture are better than others I've tried - Garden of Life and Vega Sport - but I'm not that picky. This protein powder also mixes well, does not have a grainy or chalky texture, and has a relatively neutral flavor (protein powders are what they are - don't expect it to taste like anything other than a protein powder, however). I have tried Sunwarrior's Warrior Blend (Natural) before, but the two taste fairly similar to me; after finishing the Warrior Blend container, I chose to order the Classic Plus version because it contains a slightly higher content of each amino acid and therefore has a slightly better amino acid profile.

I did end up going back to my old crappy straightener because It worked better than this one and I was just tired of the frizz it created and the frustration of it always turning off on me.

title: Love brush/straightener! This product took about a week and ...
text: Love brush/straightener! This product took about a week and a half to arrive. As you see in the picture, it comes with a little user manual, brush/straightener, and mini bottle. On the brush side, there are many bristles, the red plates are the ones that heat up. The metal circle area towards the top is where the mist comes out. It's gives off a really fine mist while combing/straightening your hair. The outer top part of the brush has an area to add water with use of the mini plastic bottle that comes in the box. There is a mist button on the outer side off the brush, press once to turn on and once to turn off. The highest heat setting I can wind up to is 446F. It is adjustable with the +/- buttons. You turn it on by pressing the ON/OFF button and to turn it off you press the ON/OFF button for a few seconds. You can also change it to Celcius by double clicking the ON/OFF button. I would like to give this 5/5 stars but when I got the product, it already had scuff marks as you can see on the outer area off the brush. Overall, it does straighten my hair (best used when completely dry). It may not be as straight as when I use my hair straightener, but it does get pretty straight.

Only minor gripe is the tacky rubber on the forearm hoops isn’t very comfortable, as I expected. Grabbed a set of forearm pads in the same order. You should do that too.

Hope you’re off these thing quickly, and can put these in a deep, dark corner of the garage & never use them again. But if something does happen, at least you’ll be ahead of the game.

title: Covers EVERYTHING!
text:
Pros: Covers thinning areas well, takes less spray than most to do the trick, blends in well with my natural hair while it makes hair look fuller too, not to bad on the pocket book.
Cons: Not only does it cover the thin spots, the over-spray covers the entire room...be prepared for plenty of clean up. It also has a bad(odd smell)when you spray it on, but it seems to fade out immediately afterward as it dries. They claim it washes out with shampoo, but they forgot to tell you it "also" rubs off dry as well...pillow cases, hands, hats, etc. It also creates a mess in the shower and will leave a colored residue on the fiberglass. The best and only thing I found to clean it off with was lighter fluid...yes, lighter fluid! (obviously use common sense and caution while doing so if you choose this method!!!)I used it on a rag then cleaned my tub again thoroughly afterwards with a household bathroom cleaner to get rid of the lighter fluid smell as well. I'm not sure what happens when your hair or scalp gets wet from the rain, swimming and so forth as this is my first can I've used and I'm yet to experience that scenario; although I'm not feeling confident that it won't run down my head and face or fog up the pool. It also leaves a dull look and dry feel to your hair as well.
Synopsis: Great for work or a short term fix...I wouldn't recommend it on a hot date or pool party. I originally tried this product because of the claims it made, the price and the fact the can cover looked very similar to one I've previously used for years that "DID NOT" rub off and the over spray was much less intense and messy.(I thought they may have bought out this company?)I just hate when you find something that works and they stop making it...why? I also wrote this review because I understand how hard it is to deal with thinning hair, especially as a woman. I can only hope the company reads these reviews as well to perfect their products and make them more user friendly with a few more trials and tweaks!!

title: Great with water!
text:
I'll be up front: I never heard of this stuff before stumbling on it while browsing Amazon. I was intrigued, and decided to give it a shot as I own a large...."water pipe" (16" tall beaker style with an ice catcher).
So after almost a month, here are my thoughts.
1)These beads expand A LOT once they absorb the water! The package I received was enough to fill two 1 liter bottles once they achieved full size, so unless you have a lot of glassware to fill, hydrate a pinch of the beads.
2)Despite what people say, DO NOT FREEZE these beads! Freezing the beads will destroy them, so keep that in mind. You can throw them in the freezer for a few minutes to chill them, but don't forget them. I would suggest storing them in the fridge if you want to keep cold ones handy.
3)These are NOT a replacement for water, they simply can't filter the way water does. They do diffuse the smoke, but the point of water is a smoother hit through filtration, not diffusion. Diffusion helps filtration, however.
4)When used WITH water, these beads are great! These beads are noticeably cooler than room temp, and when in water, they will actually chill the water! It's not ice cold by any means, but it definitely makes a difference! They also help diffuse the smoke in the water so you get a smother draw!
5)They DO help keep the glass clean. My glass is used heavily, and gets a large buildup of resin (and ash) at the water line. It has to be cleaned every few weeks to get rid of the buildup before it becomes too much. These beads have prevented that buildup, instead I can just change the water and rinse one a week! They don't CLEAN the "pipe", but they do prevent the buildup.
6)They look cool! I wish I could find some in a deep colors, rather than the pastels I see from everyone, but even so it adds some color to my clear glass!
7) I have reused the beads several times just by rinsing and replacing the water. You can dehydrate them after use and rehydrate when you need again, also.
TL;DR- Cool beads get huge, great with water, makes the glass look cool and clean(er)!

title: Not a strong battery life
text:
I first want to mention that this device is very small. It can fit in your hand. It's not necessarily a bad thing because it packed a good punch for being so small. In fact, the sounds seemed to be very good quality and the melodies that played were very soothing and calming. All of my kids really enjoyed them. Here are the problems with this device:
1. You have to charge the unit to 100% once it dies and CANNOT use it while it is plugged in. So you use it until it dies and then it needs to charge to 100%. It doesn't take too long to charge. Maybe 3 hours or so. I tried unplugging it before it had charged to 100% and it didn't want to work.

2. There is no indicator of the battery life on the device. You don't really know when it is dying or almost done charging. So you can either choose to charge it every day before you use it or take a chance and use it until it dies. At first it lasted us almost 5 full nights (around 50 hours of use in total). We use it as a sound machine at night for our kids. After a month of use, it started holding less and less of a charge. We finally returned it after about 5 weeks because it wouldn't even last 2 full nights (or 20 hours).

3. The "night light" isn't really a night light. So the light on the device can either be set to "on" (which is VERY bright), "off", or "blinking" which is just simply distracting.

If all of these things were resolved I would purchase several more because this machine was really convenient and the sounds were of good quality and not annoying or scratchy.

*** A few things to note, we never used the night light so that was not the reason for our battery usage. Also, I did notice that the melodies used up more battery life than the simple sounds did so if you are wanting to use it for a business with the melodies you will not be able to use it for more than 8 hours or so before needing to charge it again.

title: Great help & good design
text:
My dad has used this for the last couple of years with great success. It has been instrumental in allowing him -- and caregivers -- to sleep well and stay in bed through the night. Now he has declined to the point where we have transitioned to condom catheters because he is no longer able to hold the urinal and position it correctly.

I would give it 4.5 stars if I could, because there's a slight improvement I'd like to see in the design. We have used the same urinal for a couple of years, but we have changed the collection bag several times (which cost only a few dollars each). The urinal drain tube is the same diameter as the collection bag tubing, and there's a stretchy thin rubber sleeve (the green section you can see in the photos) that goes on the outside of both pieces to hold them together and seal the joint. To change the bag, we
• Remove the hard plastic barb fitting at the upper end of the bag tube, as it is not used
• Roll back (condom style) the stretchy sleeve to release the old bag tube
• While holding the sleeve in a rolled position, butt the new bag tube against the urinal drain tube
• Release the sleeve and unroll it over the new bag tubing
This is easier said than done. The sleeve is hard to roll up far enough, then hard to hold in place. while positioning the new tune. If the new tube and the urinal drain tube are not butted closely together, the gap can allow the sleeve to twist and seal off the drain. And if you let the sleeve slip in the process, it is very difficult to get the new tube in place without the sleeve rolled up.

So the design improvement I would suggest is to change the joint at the urinal drain tube to allow easy usage with standard drain bag barb fittings.

I suggest buying two of these. We disinfect my dad's after each night with bleach water, but periodically, it's good to immerse the urinal itself in bleach water and soak it. Having two of them makes this easier to do.

title: Use the real thing
text:
I have suffered from lower back and leg pain due to vertebral disc problems for many years. Having a desk job exacerbated the discomfort.
I purchased the [[ASIN:B000LBGO1M Obus Forme High-back Backrest, Black]] and another "back saver" type seat cushion about six (6) years ago. When the other cushion no longer served its purpose, I purchased the [[ASIN:B000FJS6KC Obus Forme Ergonomic Seat, Black]]. The Obus Forme Ergonomic Seat simply connects to the Obus Forme High Backrest Support with two hook and eye extentions. The Obus Forme Ergonomic "set" allows me to sit for 1 - 2 hours with greater comfort, i.e., the numbness and pain in my lower back, buttocks and legs is minimized. The Obus Forme Ergonomic Seat is padded and reinforced. The segmented seat adjusts to support unique gluteus. Since the Obus Forme High Backrest Support has been very durable, I expect similar substance from the Obus Forme Ergonomic Seat.
If you suffer from chronic back pain and/or sciatica, help minimize your distress: purchase the Obus Forme Ergonomic Seat. (Consider the Obus Forme High Backrest Support, too).

My wife has been snoring lately, and my custom earplugs disintegrated from use. I have really small ear canals, and that's why I ordered these. My wife's snoring has been waking me up several times a night. I basically had to poke her so that she would change sleeping positions. Neither of us was getting the rest that we needed.

The first night I tried these it was pure bliss! It canceled out her snoring completely. It's been a week now, and I'm pretty happy with these earplugs. The only issue that I've found is that they tend to go further into my ear canal depending on where I place the "tail". I found the location of the tail where it doesn't get pushed further into the ear canal and that has made a difference.

There were a couple nights where it went into the ear canal too far, which was painful. I don't think there's any way to engineer these better. It does a really good job already. As I wrote earlier above, you just have to find where in the ear you want the tail to stick out, so that they don't get pushed in further than needed.

I bought a couple more kits as I tend to lose small things. No way I want to be caught sleeping without these anymore!

I purchased the hybrid solar charger hoping to use it on a camping trip, but in testing prior to the trip I discovered it's not even worth taking. Prior to purchase I knew of some product flaws like there being no off switch and needing to remove the batteries when not charging, but the flaws are worse than I imagined.

Initially I tried to leave the charger in my sun room which receives a good amount of sunlight, but the charging light didn't even come on during the course of a few hours. It needs really strong sunlight to "turn it on." After which I could bring it back inside to the sun room and it would continue charging with the light on. I tried this over the course a few weekends and only once did the batteries actually charge. Every other time one of the batteries completely discharged. At first I thought I had a bad battery so I tried multiple batteries with no luck. The batteries were Energizer NiMH and they have performed well in my Xbox 360 controller.

I knew the charging speed would strongly depend on the brightness of the sunlight, but I didn't expect that more often than not charging in the sun would drain the batteries rather than charging them.

The reason I chose this model of solar charger was it's support for AA batteries because I figured I could always bring extras and use them to charge my camera at night. This didn't work out so well either. Numerous times I tried charging my cell phone as a test case and not only did my cell phone not charge, but it seemed to lose charge at a faster rate than it would have if the charger wasn't plugged into it.

I'm not sure if I've waited too long to return this thing, but hopefully I can at least discourage others from buying it.

title: Beware of Arsenic Poisoning in Rice Products
text:
I bought this product and I have been using for a while. Rice Bran is a true nutrition powerhouse. It is made from the hull and germ of rice; this is the part that is shaved off to yield white rice. Taking out this nutrient dense part of course gives white rice a long shelf life but also makes it lacking in essential nutrients. Two servings of most rice bran products will give you loads of B vitamins, vitamin E and almost your recommended daily allowance of Magnesium and Phosphorus. In addition it has an immune booster called Inositol hexaphosphate. I prefer getting my essential nutrients from food sources and not from pills if possible.
My experience with this product (the tub is almost finished) is that it mixes very well with my morning smoothie and actually gives it a sweet taste (not overpowering), it does have a mild energizing effect. So why have I given this product 1 star? I will actually five it zero star if possible.
I did some research recently showing that since rice is planted in water logged land, it is more susceptible to arsenic toxicity. The water enhances the absorption of the arsenic and other toxins. More arsenic has been found in the hull and germ of brown rice compared to white rice. Also, rice grown in the Southern U.S. is commonly exposed to inorganic arsenic which is still found in the soils there from past use of inorganic arsenic based pesticides. Places like California never used inorganic arsenic based pesticides therefore the arsenic taken up by the rice grown in California is naturally occurring.
I had bought Nutra Bio Stabilized Bran, Bob's Red Mill, Stabilized Rice Bran, Natural Traditions Rice Bran & Germ Powder at some point or another (all at different stages of being finished). I was also considering buying Sunfood Tocotrienols/Rice Bran Solubles. So based on my research on potential arsenic toxicity, I decided to write to all the companies to confirm the source of their rice bran and if they did any third party lab testing. I sent my enquiry more than two weeks ago, up till now, I haven’t received any response from Bob's Red Mill and Natural traditions. Nutra Bio responded saying “we are unsure as to what part of the country that the Stabilized Rice Bran comes from. We are also unsure as to what the international safe levels for arsenic are”. I was aghast! Arsenic is probably the number one carcinogenic toxin. The only third party testing that Nutra Bio sent to me was a 2014 test and their customer service said additionally about the 2014 tests that “the tests that we have are the most up-to-date tests that we have. Until they are out of date, we are still authorized by the FDA to use those tests”. Sunfood response says their rice bran is sourced from California, but the third party tests sent did not show the level of ‘inorganic arsenic’ which is the real culprit.
These are the probably the top brands of rice bran in the market, and in my own assessment they fall short by their response or lack of it. If you take a rice product, be aware of arsenic poisoning. Unfortunately the supplement is not strictly regulated and these manufacturers, just like ‘Big Pharma’ are out to get your hard earned money, they really don’t care about your health and that of your family. Please do your research. title: The "Rain-X" for paint
text: I got this on sale at the a local store. I was skeptical about the ambitious claims and paid reviews spammed all over the internets. Because clear coats have come such a long way, wax is pretty much obsolete. They don't really improve shine or protect, in fact I only stuff I use is cleaner waxes to get residue off these days. I got my car washed up and put it on. It's been a week and here's the general consensus so far: Dust is still highly attracted to the paint and generally it's hard to see a difference between other waxes when the suns out. Things change after clouds move in and rain falls. Just like Rain-X the water beads up and runs off like it's on wax. I also noticed that the thick layer of dust my brother added to my car (due to a lawnmower drive-by) was taken away. Even bird plop was mostly washed away. Needless to say I'm pretty impressed with the performance so far and even if it lasts only a few months, its easy to throw on. In less than an hour I had my car done. For the average person this is a great way to add a few more days on from the local car wash.

title: Hate 15 Minute Auto Shut Off - Massager Needs Remote
text:
Massager is fine for what it is (I’ve had better like this one) but the 15 minute auto shut off is horrible and is the real issue.

For someone taking care of an elderly parent who has limited mobility and uses this for back pain relief it is totally obnoxious to have to constantly go and restart this device so frequently. I can maybe understand a 30 minute shut off but 15 minutes is unacceptable for the almost $50 price tag.

When the device is behind you and the start button is tiny and the exact same shape as multiple other buttons on the device it’s very difficult to turn on again even for a normal healthy person without back pain and other mobility issues. For a 75 year old in chronic pain it’s impossible.

If you have any pain or mobility problems you typically have to pull it out again from behind your back to restart then reposition behind you. This totally defeats the relaxation and pain relief properties you’re hoping this device will offer. 15 minutes is just not long enough for someone with real pain issues to find relief from.

This needs a remote control so that someone with such issues can easily use this otherwise it’s nice for someone who is healthy and just needs some relaxation etc but if you’re thinking about this for yourself or anyone who has real pain and mobility problems I would hard pass until some kind of remote control is added.

Also you can get a deeper massage from the ones with the arm straps - this is the third one like this with the rotating balls and this one gives the least deep massage.

title: Not bad when mixed with milk, coming from a meatatarian
text:
First off I'm not vegan, vegetarian, or even close to it. I heard about Vega products on someone's blog who I think highly of and thought I'd try it because my diet is awful. I picked up this exact almond smoothie package at a local Whole Foods.
The instructions say to mix with water, but seriously... NO! That was not tasty at all, and I love almonds! Drink this mixed with some kind of milk. Rice milk, almond milk, soy milk, whatever. I've tried it now with a rice milk and a vanilla almond milk and it's good when mixed with those. The instructions also say to mix with 8 ounces of water, I mix with about 16 ounces of milk and it's better that way IMO.
Mix in a blenderball and sip on the drive in to work. It's not bad, I try to chug it. The rice milk isn't as thick and I shake it more but with the almond milk I see the little specs floating and don't shake as much.

Yes it has a greenish tinge but I'm guessing that's what veggies look like (j/k). It has a ton of good stuff in it, so if you want some nutrition, drink some of this as a breakfast or afternoon snack. But definitely use milk

Updated 5/30/12: I updated this from 4 stars to 5 stars after tasting the other Vega products. This is the tastiest Vega health smoothie I'd had, the least gritty, and best blending. The packaging has changed, I'll upload a picture of the old vs new packaging.

title: Used for PPE Goggles
text:
Just wanted to place a review so it may benefit others who may need readers while using PPE's for whatever reason. I bought a pair of DeWalt antifog goggles to use while working in the hospital. The reason being we are seeing more and more people with respiratory issues and we are implementing stricter precautions. Prior to this I use using simple reader bifocal safety glasses which would fog up when using an N95 or simple mask. As an RN i chart a lot on a computer, which is a light prescription then my reading glasses, so I came up with the idea of making a tri-focal goggle to be able to use during my ling shifts. I trimmed my computer prescription down placed those just below eye level and then placed my reading prescription under that. I used a dry-erase marker to look in the mirror and centered it on my pupil at the 2 different angles I would be using when using a computer and when I would be reading close up. It took a little tweaking here and there but I am very happy with the results. The cost is a little more then I would like to pay, but it is a lot cheaper then custom goggles from an optometrist and a lot faster. To me the prescriptions seem about 0.25 off. If I had to do it over again I would get 0.25 stronger then my normal prescriptions. I have worn them around the house for about 3 hours and so far so good. when walking around the top is clear and I don't get any blurriness from the computer lens, this is due to my placement, you will have to experiment to get it just right. The cool thing is when the lens is wet and being placed it stays in place, but can be moved easily until it dries. Also the lenses can be removed and cleaned and replaced on another set of glasses or goggles.The inside of my goggles should stay clean so I don't plan on cleaning the inside that often. If I have to take the lenses off and clean the inside I will have to re-measure with the dry erase marker method to place them back in the right place.
I will update this review once I have worn them for a few full shifts. I hope this helps anyone out there who uses reader glasses and is in either Healthcare or any work environment where you need to wear eye protection.

text:
I post reviews only when I'm moved to do so. Either the book's too good not to sing praises about or the product's way too bad to not warn others! This is my first herbal supplement review as I've never come across anything quite like it.

My package of vitamins and supplements arrived yesterday at about 11am (sometimes I order via Amazon, this time I ordered directly from Swansons). I had a Rhodiola extract tab before lunch. About an hour later, half way through my work, I felt something was different - then it struck me that I did feel pepped up and my mood had improved! The effect lasted pretty much through the afternoon into the evening.

This morning I took another tablet after breakfast and it happened again, so - for me at least - yesterday wasn't a fluke.

I've tried lots of supplements and about 90 percent of what I've tried don't do anything for me. This one definitely produces a positive, tangible cranking up of energy and mood.

Google 'Rhodiola rosea' and see what it's supposed to do for you. If you think you'd like to try it, I'd recommend you try this extract as it's worked for me.

Cas, author of [[ASIN:9810844891 Cassius Cheong's Positively Quit Manual: The Thinking Person's Guide to Stop Smoking]]

Under the heading of "First aid".
"IF ON SKIN OR CLOTHING: Take off contaminated clothing, Rinse skin immediately with plenty of water for 15-20 minutes. Call a poison Control Center or doctor for treatment advice."
"IF IN EYES: Hold eye open and rinse slowly and gently with water for 15-20 minutes. Remove contact lenses, if present, after the first 5 minutes, then continue rinsing. Call a poison Control Center or doctor for treatment advice."

Under the heading of "PRECAUTIONARY STATEMENTS - HAZARDS TO HUMANS AND DOMESTIC ANIMALS" "WARNING: Causes substantial but temporary eye injury. Harmful if absorbed through skin. Do not get in eyes or on skin or clothing. Wear long-sleeved shirt and long pants, protective eyewear (safety glasses), shoes and socks, and chemical resistant gloves (such as or made out of any water proof material). Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before eating, drinking, chewing gum, using tobacco or using the toilet. Remove contaminated clothing and wash clothing.

And last but not least; "WARNING: This product contains a chemical(s) known to the State of California to cause cancer."

While I appreciate the manufacturer's disclosure of the dangers of this product I deduct all stars for making me buy a can before warning me. I simply can't use this on my or my children's shoes.

title: Good for long haul flights
text:
Flights longer than about 3hrs are *extremely* painful for my rear end. After a bunch of research, I decided to buy the Purple Simply Seat Cushion for a trip to Asia this past summer (including a 7hr, 12hr, 15hr!, and several 2-4hr flights). The cushion fit all the various airlines seats just fine and wasn't too bulky or heavy to fit in my "personal item" (stored under the seat in front of me). I also bought a Therm-a-rest trail seat inflatable cushion to compare / combine.

By themselves, neither cushion was enough, so I ended up typically using both cushions together, which basically eliminated my discomfort! I was even able to sleep on some of the flights, which is unheard of for me.

Even though it wasn't enough by itself, I give the purple a full 5 stars because their website advertises the "Simply Purple" cushion as good for a "Medium (4-8hr)" sit time and my long flights exceeded that. I didn't want to go up to the thicker (and much heavier) Double or Ultimate cushions as I expect those would be too inconvenient to travel with. It might be possible to swap the "Simply" for the lighter "Everywhere" cushion and still be ok.

I feel like I've cracked the code for long flights and this cushion will be along for the ride going forward!

title: A must-have safety essential
text:
Flashlights are the kind of thing you never think about until you REALLY need one. A crank flashlight like this one is perfect because you don't have to worry about making sure the batteries are charged!

I keep one of these in my car, and a couple throughout the house. The light is plenty bright enough for emergency use -- it goes without saying that it's a heck of a lot better than nothing! :)

It's decently made, despite the bargain bin price. The surface is slightly rubberized, and it's a good size for my hand: not too small, but easily fits into a pocket, drawer, or glovebox. The crank feels solid enough that I don't worry about breaking it, and it's placed in a way that makes it easy enough to wind.

If I had to find things to nitpick, the strap isn't really all that great, and the on/off switch is a bit awkward to use. Hardly worth complaining about, especially for the price.

title: 90% of a high end massage chair, 20% of the cost
text:
After testing out several massage chairs at Brookstone, I found it very difficult to justify $3-4K on a chair. I took a calculated gamble by buying this chair and was really interested in trying the "Long Rail" feature.

I have been extremely impressed with the quality of the massage. The "Long Rail" basically takes the kneading, thumping and shiatsu all the way too your BUTT and it feels really good to me. The only areas where the balloon cushions are utilized are the feet, calf and arms. The balloon pressure is strong, the way I like it. The rollers on the bottom of the feet are like icing on the cake for me. I am 5'6" and the chair fits me perfectly. It is possible someone with longer legs may not get their entire calf into the seat. I would estimate 5'9" would be the maximum height before the experience starts to degrade for a user.

The four automatic programs are remarkably similar. They could have just labeled the programs along the lines of strong, medium, weak. There is a nice sleeve pocket on the left hand inner side of the massage chair to hold the remote which is a nice feature some users may not have noticed.

A few cons: There were a few loose screws under the foot rest that came off probably during shipment. Not a big deal for me to install back on. Keep in mind these products come from oversea, China. Also, the manual is written in Chenglish (Chinese English) so average Americans will find the manual difficult to read. Another downside is there is no vibration feature.

The few cons have in no way soured my experience so far with this chair. If the chair can last at least 2 years I will feel very happy with this product. In fact, if after 1 year there are no issues, I may buy another one. Highly recommended so far.

title: amazing supplement
text:
As pointed out by other reviewers, the Longvida brand of curcumin is THE best. If you want a detailed look at the evidence, check out this video:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UdpU9BSi2Zc
Basically, Longvida maximizes bioavailability of FREE curcumin, (as opposed to glucuronidated curcumin). Free curcumin is the only form that can cross the blood brain barrier and exert effects on the brain. Other brands fail to increase levels of free curcumin at all really. So the difference is VERY IMPORTANT.

That's the science, but everyone likes anecdotes better, right? So I just want to say that this supplement, along with a few other things, has had a major, huge, enormous impact on my mood, clarity of thought, and anxiety. Before I started, I was a wreck. I couldn't read a book or watch an episode of tv---"normal" people's methods of relaxation---without becoming anxious. I was trying out SSRI's, but they were proving to be useless. After starting this, along with a few other things, I'm 90% better.

What about the "few other things"? Well, they include pregnenolone, NAC, probiotics, and a fluctuating roster of other herbs, and they're helping a lot too...but I estimate that curcumin is doing ~50% of the heavy lifting. When I ran out of this stuff, my OCD returned with a vengenace, my mood plummeted; I was better as soon as I resumed taking it.

So check this stuff out, and don't think of it as a purely "anti-aging" supplement. That's what it's marketed as, but it's a powerful anti-inflammatory, and everyone in any kind of disease-state is likely to have inflammation going on.

title: Cannot recommend this product and company enough!
text:
In a wacky kind of way, after working with Schneider Labs I wish that I needed to do lead tests more often. If all companies were run like and did customer support like Schneider labs, the world would be all that much more amazing.

These guys are awesome. I bought this test thinking that it would just be an automated thing that I sent in and got the results for a few days later. But when I read the instructions for conducting the test, which were incredibly clear and easy to understand, I saw that I needed to send all 10 samples in together. I think the listing on Amazon says this, but I must have missed it. My intention was to use 1/2 the samples at one time and 1/2 the samples at another time. So I called their customer service and they were extremely friendly and willing to accommodate my request. They also were more than happy to let me pay the difference in price between the 5 business day sample and 1 business day sample to speed up the test results.

Their website is really easy to use when you're gathering your test samples. You just need to mark each sample with a unique name, then log on to the website and add that name along with the time tested and then ship your samples in a provided prepaid envelope along with a unique PIN that they prepare for you on the website. The turnaround time for my 1 business day tests was less than 24 hours after they received the samples.

As for the testing, I'm not a chemist or inspector, but the results were fairly consistent with other facts that I happen to know about what's going on in the locations that I tested.

I cannot recommend these guys enough. You won't regret buying this test kit. The only thing I caution is that you should buy the kit for the number of samples you wish to collect as they prefer that you send them all in at once. They also offer 5 sample kits and 1 sample kits I believe.

text: I tried this product because I have some food allergies and intolerances and decided to try a diet that removed all dairy and vegan protein products from my regimen. The diet is based on the book It Starts With Food, by Dallas and Melissa Hartwig, and is basically clean meat, fish, eggs, vegetables and fruits. It works very well for my inflammatory and autoimmune issues and for my quality of life in general. The main glitch is that I don't have the appetite to easily consume enough protein to maintain muscle mass without the clean vegetarian sources I was using before. I'm a 51 yo fit male, very active. I walk about 15 miles a week on average and lift kettlebells 3-5x per week as a baseline, so I need a good amount of protein ie.150-200 gms p/d. This product really helps me to build muscle faster to stave off the impending sarcopenia for as long as humanly possible. It seems reasonably clean, mixes fine in either a blender or shaker jar, and I like that it doesn't have any antibiotics or hormones in it. I also like the price compared to bone broth protein, which might be my only other option. I will continue to buy this beef protein isolate. As with any new protein product, there is a bit of a learning curve. The longer you leave it in the blender, the more foamy it gets, but if you just pulse it a few times it will blend right in.

title: Sturdy and Reliable - even in Zion and Yosemite
text: These are basic crutches that do the job well and are ROBUST. I am 6'1" tall and 165lbs/75kg and they are great. I ordered these along with a set of top of the line $220 Ergobaum 7G crutches for comparison. The more expensive ones were more comfortable (they had soft hand grips and suspension) but I kept these ones and sent back the more expensive ones simply because these looked more robust. I was not wrong. I am not the heaviest guy out there but I put the crutches through their paces hiking up Angel's Landing in Zion and Half Dome in Yosemite and used them to support my entire weight on long climbs and descents. The tips gripped well in dry and wet conditions. I have also used them to hike up streams with the tips completely submerged in water with no problems. On all occasions the crutches were great and the tips have lasted well - they got me to the very top of Angels Landing and Half Dome and they still have life in them (yup, I even got them up the chains and the cables, if you know those hikes...just don't tell my physiotherapist). Sure, they don't look as stylish as some crutches out there but the more expensive ones I bought and immediately returned only looked great because many of the components were made of plastic. I was worried they would eventually snap. These are mainly made of metal and have lasted well. I did get blisters on my hands on long hikes but gloves fixed this problem. An aftermarket handle grip pad would add more comfort. I am 6'1" tall and I bought the regular adult length and I do not have them on the tallest setting. Everyone is different but they are plenty long enough for me. For reference I used them whilst recovering from minor knee surgery. Hope this info helps.

text:
Because of various injuries over the years, I've had quite a bit of experience with both forearm are armpit crutches. If you've never used crutches before and now need them, I highly recommend you go with forearm crutches. While a bit more difficult to get used to initially, they are more maneuverable, more comfortable and don't create as much clutter in your personal space.

These Medline crutches have solid engineering and bomb-proof construction. There are three adjustments to make on these: crutch height, hand drip to forearm grip height and forearm grip size. The crutches excel on the first two adjustments but completely fail on the last. The forearm grips ARE NOT adjustable and have a HUGE opening. I was able to make an adjustment by using Coban wrap and soft padding. This is actually a very important adjustment. It enables you to remove your hand from the hand grip to pick up things while letting the crutch hang from your forearm.

title: Helpful for the reader and for the eyes
text:
When my 6 year old son suddenly had a vision change from 15/20 to 60/20 within 5 months, I started doing extensive research on eye issues in growing children. The rate of change in the eyes of a developing child before the age of 15 is very dramatic. After 15 year of age, the eyes' rate of change slow down. That means a child subjecting his/her eyes to accommodation (i.e. reading at close range or proximity) will develop myopia faster at 6 years of age than at 15 years of age.

Within the 5 months time in which my son's eyes changed from 15/20 to 60/20, he had read approximately 250 books. His eye exam with an opthamologist showed that he had myopia with no other eye problems or issues. The opthamologist prescribed glasses for him to see things in the distance. I, however, did not want him to have glasses yet. I reasoned that if the eyes can change so drastically for the worse in such a short period of time, the eyes can also improve (as long as accommodation - changes in the eyes for close range work - had not yet become permanent.)

I began to change the way my son read and did close range work. Following any prolong close range work, my son would take 10 - 15 minutes breaks where he read small letters from across the room. I bought the Ott-Lite bookstand where my son would read books from 1.5 arm lengths away. I bought the Ott-Lite bookstand because it had an adjustable back which could be changed to accommodate my son's height. This was very useful since different chair and table heights often placed my son's vision at different angles (with respect to the book)which could then be easily corrected by tilting the bookstand backward or forward to varying degrees. The Ott-Lite also had built in lights which helped to illuminate the book he was reading in areas where lighting was poor. My son was also able to double the bookstand as a writing table at times. And I liked the fact that one can increase the width of the bookstand by pulling out the sides. To fit taller books, we just moved the light fixture back. It is true that sometiems the bottom lines of a book are blocked because the book sits deeply into the bookstand. However, my son easily solved the problem by placing two jenga blocks where the book sits in the bookstand to move the bottom page higher up for viewing. In addition, we like thattThe bookstand is made of strong plastic and does not feel flimsy. It can withstand the abuse and use by a 6 year old.

It has been about three months since my son has been diagnosed with myopia which requires glasses. We recently took him to see the same opthamologist for his follow-up eye exam. My son's vision is now at 40/20 in one eye and 30/20 in the other eye. The opthamologist said, "At this point, I would not prescribed glasses for him. It seems his eyes have improved."

We plan on continuing our son with proper reading posture and using the Ott-Lite bookstand to obtain our goals.

title: Works best in open floor plan
text:
I have never owned a robotic vacuum, so I can only compare this to my experience with what I own which are traditional vacuums.

Pros:

-Set it and forget it. Regulate it through the app on your phone (this wasn't super easy at first) and it can run when you are out. Why is this important? Because it's not silent (con). It bangs into furniture and moves around on a battery operated motor. It makes noise.

-doesn't require batteries. Recharges in its own station, which in theory it finds on its own when it needs to (con- can't seem to get that function to work).

-seems to clean up well. The side brush is key.

-automatically stops before falling downstairs. Shuts itself off when it falls more than a few inches.

In general I had trouble having it fit with my older home. It has multiple levels on the main floor and lots of furniture. I think what it all boils down to though is that this is the type of vacuum that works great with open floor plan homes, and all on one level with either hardwood or short pile carpets. I personally find it irritating to be around it when it's on, and I find the small collection container underneath to be too small for pet hair collection. This would be great for a small apartment - with no cats to be annoyed while you ran it while you are at work. Definitely run it while you are out.

title: konjac sponge is the most natural and gentle exfoliant
text:
Konjac sponges are made out of konjac root, a porous root vegetable that grows in Asia. They work great to exfoliate the skin gently. When soaked in water, the konjac sponge becomes incredibly soft and almost feels slimy. Because of its texture, you can exfoliate every day. I have used konjac sponges for my babies too. These are six sponges in different colors, all infused with other ingredients:

White - Pure konjac powder,
Black - Bamboo activated charcoal,
Yellow - Turmeric,
Dark pink - Red clay,
Green - Aloe vera,
Pink - Sakura (Cherry Blossom)

Each sponge has a little string, which is very helpful to hang it dry. Out of the bag, these sponges are hard as a rock and need to be submerged in water for a couple of minutes. My other konjac sponge came with the instructions to microwave on high for 2 minutes to sanitize, but this brand doesn’t ask for that. After use, it’s important to rinse, squeeze out the water; your sponge will last longer and be cleaner. That should be routine with any washcloth, though, so this may be an unnecessary comment.

These are great, I scrub my face EVERY DAY with my Red Clay konjac sponge, and my skin does not get irritated. They are recommended to change every two months, but I first have to see if they can live for two months.

title: Not exactly 13Gallons and not too durable BUT will biodegrade in 45 DAYS!
text:
Looking at these trash bags I have a hard time believing they’re made out of cornstarch. They appear durable and the texture is soft and smooth to the touch, it doesn’t feel like plastic bag.

The bag doesn’t come with the string. If you try to force trash in the bag it will stretch and it will start separating and eventually will puncture. I don’t think this bag can take too much beating but it can definitely take some. I would definitely not try to overload and force things in. The capacity is up to 13Gallons but when compared to Kirkland 13Gallons bag it is noticeably smaller so I don’t believe this bag can take 13gallons. See the pictures. For the fact these bags are environmentally friendly I totally love them and support the cause. I also don’t mind going through a little hassle if I can help preserve Earth for my kids and grandkids. According to manufacturer these bags will completely biodegrade within 45 days! I wish there was a string because with no string you have to tie bag ends to close it which then further reduces the capacity. But overall excited with this mission!

title: I still have sensation in my hands! Great gloves with grippy surface

I hope this makes sense. However, these gloves are not one of those thick rubbery gloves that numb your sensation for touch. They are still thick and durable but feel more like a silicone then rubber and allow my hands and fingers to have a good sensation to touch. I have medium sized hands and M fits me well with a little extra room too. The fingers are not too long and the overall fit is very good. They are even decorated and have a little trim design around the hand opening. They are not too deep, see photo. They come about half way to my elbows. The palms and fingers are textured in a cute way and this allows for a better grip when holding something in a soapy water. I received 2 pairs, white with blue fingers and plain purple and both colors are cute if that matters.

Bottom line, I always hated rubber gloves but I use these without dreading it, it’s a first. Good pair of gloves.

title: Convenient effective anti-snoring device!
text:
I have used Smart Nora for about 6 months now and it definitely does reduce my snoring quite a bit. My wife is pretty pleased that she is able to rest much better. I feel like I even sleep better with Smart Nora... or as I sometimes call it "SNora"...
I had one issue when the air bladder developed a leak, the unit could no longer adjust my head position and be effective. The manufacturer sent me another bladder after I sent a picture of the bladder with the leak. It was covered by warranty.
I will say that you need to pay attention to where the bladder assembly is positioned under your pillow. I find that if it is to high (close to the wall and away from where the pillow touches my shoulders), the pillow will go up and down but my head position is not affected and I don't stop snoring.
I have used Nora with and without my white noise fan and it seems to be effective in both situations.
If you snore and don't want to wear a chin strap and a binkie (if that even works) then this is worth a try. I snore loudly and all night long... It has worked for me...

title: Suggestions for outdoor use of retainers
text: I've had fairly good luck with this sort of eyeglass retainer--make sure that the little metal rings holding the rubber earpiece connectors are fully closed--if the split ring accidently opens too much with prolonged use, the strap may slide out of ring. I replaced the rings with fully closed, wrap-around types (or the strap end openings could be tied directly to the rubber pieces with loops of sturdy thread). Out in the field one day, my eyeglass cord came loose this way while removing my glasses, but the problem can be remedied as described above if one wants to go to the trouble.  Otherwise, these retainer cords are thin, durable, and comfortable, and the end pieces are flexible and secure. After that minor repair (perhaps the company should replace the split rings with something more reliable), this kind of retainer design works very well for me. As another option, Chums makes retainers with straps directly fused to the rubber end pieces, although the cords are a little thicker, and that design is also comfortable and secure.

title: Great Price, Much Better than Foam Earplugs
text:
This is actually the second pair of these that I've bought (lost the first pair a while ago). These are great for concert going. I have very sensitive hearing, but I love going to concerts. I tried standard foam earplugs for a while, but they left everything sounding muddy. These don't have any of that problem in my opinion.

On their website, they claim these earplugs reduce noise levels by about 18 decibels. That's a bit less than typical foam earplugs (which seem to be around 25-30 decibels, from what I've read), but they still provide enough protection to keep you from ending up with ringing ears the next day.

Compared to typical foam earplugs, the sound is quite a bit clearer. The details of the music still make it through, and you can still hear your friends when they try to talk/yell at you.

I keep mine in their little carrying tube in my glove compartment, and they've held up just fine to the summer heat.

While I'm sure there are more expensive earplugs out there might provide better protection and clarity, these are still a great investment for the price, and they're so much better than the typical foam earplugs you'd buy at a store.

text:
I’ve been searching for a protein to add to my diet for so so long- I’m always trying to find something low in sugar and high in protein. There are plenty out there, but up until I discovered Soylent every single one was artificially sweetened and flavored with lots of additives I didn’t need or want.
I had settled on using a protein nut based milk in my coffee and while it did add some protein it left me unsatisfied and I always needed to supplement it with something else. Now, I use about two scoops of Soylent with less than the recommended water because I like it to be a bit thicker and a small amount of brewed coffee. The Soylent adds a nice neutralized flavor to my coffee and keeps me going through breakfast until lunch.

My days are long and I always find myself overeating, but with Soylent in my coffee I can last considerably longer before needing a meal and still feel satisfied. If you prefer flavored protein mixes, I’d say this isn’t for you, but if you're anything like me and have been searching for the perfect unsweetened protein- look no further!

title: Mr. Misty is an okay buy.
text: I bought the Mr. Misty mainly for its thermometer capabilities, as I suspected that my landlord was cheating my apartment building on heat.  That part of it seems to work well.  However, I'm not as convinced by the humidity function.  I started using that function because I have horrible allergies and my doctor suggested raising the humidity level indoors to help alieviate my symptoms.  I use the Mr. Misty in conjunction with the Air-O-Swiss Ultrasonic humidifier and the read-out on the humidifier is consistently lower than the Mr. Misty.  Sometimes the two read-outs are the same, but after the humidity reaches about 45%, the Mr. Misty seems to sky-rocket up and stay far above the other read-out.  So my suggestion would be to use the Mr. Misty for temperature and not for humidity (unless you plan on keeping your humidity level below 45%).
