title: Works well with the Somnodent
text: I ordered this denture bath with basket as a replacement for my Somnodent case. (I don't have dentures but I do have sleep apnea!) The Somnodent case was the basic plastic hinged lid style and two of the three hinges broke after 3 years of use. The denture bath has no hinge to break which is great. It is plenty big enough to hold my Somnodent (enough water to cover it only fills it to 2/3 full.) Having read reviews stating the lid only sets on the bottom without a positive connection, I decided to order anyways. Indeed the lid sets very loosely on the bottom but knowing this in advance, I can work around it by making sure I keep my thumb on top if I carry it with water in it. That should keep spilling to a minimum. All in all, I'm very pleased with this denture bath. Anyone looking for a replacement for a broken Somnodent case should consider this product.

title: Good Bulbs
text:
There are a lot of different LED bulbs out there and the differences are not captured well by comparing lumens and color temperatures. The key attribute to these is they are a little short and their light comes from a half sphere at the top. This dome is evenly lit but bright enough you still don't want to look at it directly. Relatively little light goes down toward the base while much more goes up. This orientation makes it nice for a fixture pointed at the ceiling as more light spreads through the room and less gets caught up in the lamp shade. Other bulbs send more light to the sides.

These bulbs do not dim but are slightly more power efficient than bulbs that do. LED efficiencies are high enough this difference is more a matter of how hot they become than how much money you spend. All are expensive to buy and cheap to power while these are just a bit cooler.

I like the 3000 color temperature. To my eye the tungsten 2700 is a bit long on yellow, 5000 daylight is harsh, 3000 just right. Still, there isn't an awful lot of difference between 2700 and 3000. I remain puzzled by my own reaction to 5000 bulbs despite having confirmed their color balance is indeed similar to natural light coming in a window. I like the natural light and dislike the daylight bulbs, not clear why.

Pick these if you want the light in an even top dome of 180 degrees and don't need dimming.

title: Dr. Duck's = Outstanding!
text:
Cleans and lubricates anything on a guitar/bass. Not greasy, oily or waxy it leaves no residue once you buff it sufficiently.
Purchased to treat several very dry rosewood fingerboards it is the best I have ever tried and is the only fingerboard treatment that seems to last. Use only a small amount and rub it in thoroughly, then wait 5 - 10 minutes and buff off any excess with a clean, soft, dry cloth. It will clean a moderately dirty fingerboard, but if yours is really gunky you should probably clean it first with a suitable gentle cleaner, then treat it with Dr. Duck's Ax Wax.
After I rejuvenated my fingerboards I decided to try it on other parts. A natural finish on a Peavey Grind 5-string had become uneven and splotchy-looking so I tested a tiny bit of Dr. Duck's on it and was amazed to see that it restored even, rich coloring and gave it an even, subtle sheen over the entire body, neck and headstock. It looked far better than it did the day I purchased it.
Inspired by it's performance I then attacked an older very used and worn Ibanez that has a battered black poly finish. A lot of hard use has left it with loads of spider-web like scratches and a dull haze of fingerprints and dirt and who knows what had accumulated. It was a beater that I didn't spend any time maintaining. Once again Dr. Duck's was amazing. It cleaned the finish without having to use any polish or other compounds. I loved the way it made the instrument look because it left the signs of use yet it gave a deep rich look to the finish and it now resists fingerprints much better. The rosewood fingerboard on this Ibanez now looks beautiful. It looks so good now that I am considering upgrading the pickups and tuners on it!

title: Nice design, but the body fat readings differ significantly from Tanita
text: I have owned a Tanita body fat scale for years and asked for the Aria for Christmas because I use a Fitbit one and liked the idea of wifi readings going directly to the fitbit app.  I have an athletic build and work out about 5 times per week.  Using the athlete setting on the Tanita, my body fat reading has been hovering around 21-22% for the past month, so I was shocked that, even using the lean setting on the fitbit site, I measured 24.8% the first day.  The second day, the reading was over 26%, the third day, it was 29%, and the fourth day, it was over 30%.  Today, the reading was 30.1%, and the Tanita said 21.8%. One would think that biometric scales would use similar technology and get similar readings.  I have no idea which scale is correct, but since my habits haven't changed much, and the inconsistency appears to be with the Aria, I am inclined to think something is wrong with the calibration of the body fat scale.  The weight is within .2 pounds of the reading on the Tanita.

title: Don’t mistake these for your diva cups.
text:
I will review the use of the larger cups since that is what I mainly use (for my cheeks/chin/forehead):

The plastic material of the cups was nicer then I thought it would be. Another review mentioned that the plastic is thick, but that’s not a bad thing since that is needed in order to provide suction power and durability when squeezed.
The plastic also feels soft to the touch and the rounded opening is gentle on your face and makes it easier to glide across your face when suctioned on (use an oil or serum when sliding the cups). The cups are also easy to clean since it is so streamlined compared to other brands which have ridges.

The cups are only meant to be used on the face. I tried on my lower back and neck but there just isn’t enough air in the large cups to provide enough suction power. The silver lining to that is that it lessens the chance of facial bruising if used as intended.

Overall, I like the build and quality of the cups but the silicone brush is kinda a throwaway that they just added to up the price. Also, I only use one cup at a time so the other cup is just a back up, I guess.

title: this works pretty well. Water never spills out of it
text:
I bought this because I was tired of using my ghetto tupperware foot soaker which was always cold and too small. I have a slight toe issue, some missing cartilage on my large toe which causes it to swell whenever I walk for a long time (2+ hours), run, or play tennis. I needed a warm tub that keeps water warm and where I can salt a foot bath. For the price, this works pretty well. Water never spills out of it. There is an easy hole in the top front to be able to easily pour out water. It feels solidly made and like it will last a long time, so far I have had it a few months and am happy with it. I would not say it is the best footbath, but for a middle price, you should be pretty happy with how it works. The Brookstone version of a foot salon is higher quality, but double the price, and this one is just fine. The biggest difference between the Brookstone one and this one is that the Brookstone one heats up a lot faster and better. However.. workarounds to save you about $50...

If the water is already hot, it will keep it warm for you. So just start out with hot water and you're golden. Water is still hot after an hour of use as long as heat setting is put on as soon as you put the hot water in.

If the water is cold and you are heating it.. it will take 40-50 mins to heat it up. Probably don't reuse the water and just start with hot, or if you really want to reuse then take some boiling water and carefully mix it into the cold water first to get it started.

Weird thing-- can't heat it without the bubbles or the vibrating setting (one or both have to be on). Also, the 3 little attachments cause SUCH a rattle. If you just take those out, use vibration with heat mode, you're golden and you can barely hear it. You marginally may need to turn up the sound of a TV or game but not by much. I don't know why they made a place to hold the 3 attachment pieces if it was going to make it absurdly annoyingly loud.

I am not sure if the little spiky roller are any good, they don't really help me at all. Can't say those are massagers, just spiky things. If I could change something, I would ask for the heat setting to be better and for the heat to be able to be on without the bubbles or vibration mode. All I really wanted was the heat setting. All in all, it does everything I need and is a great price so I say 5 stars.

title: Works quite well for me
text: I have very thick, naturally curly hair, so I was a bit doubtful about how well this straightener brush would work.  After using it about 5 times, I'm liking it more and more.  One pro is that it really cuts down on the time it takes me to do my hair.  This morning it took me less than 5 minutes to get presentable once my hair was dry, and that's a record!  I have noticed that the humidity makes a difference in the performance of the straightener.  When the humidity is high, it doesn't work quite as well for me, but remember that my hair is thick and curly.  Today, though, it worked very well.  It's great to use when I just want to quickly straighten and go, but I will still use my flat iron for the front & sides when I'm needing more of a finished look.  One con is the design -- the temperature control is on the handle and it's easy to accidentally change the setting.  However, I love that there's a display so I can readily see the temperature.  I had borrowed another brand from a friend to see if a brush would work on my hair, and it did not have a display.  In fact, I couldn't even see if the brush was on.  This Magnifeko brand, however, is great because of the display.

title: One of the best things I've ever done for my health
text: I've been drinking barley powder for about 5 years now, nothing but great things to say about it and I've told many people about it who also love it.  I used to use "Just Barley" brand but discovered this one a little while back which is a much better value.  With either brand, barley powder gives me more energy, clearer thinking, and one of the biggest wins is overall digestive health, to name a few benefits.  Within a couple weeks or so of starting the regimen of a tbsp. in the morning and a tbsp. just before bed (start off with less than a tbsp for beginners) you will notice "a cleaning sensation" of your digestive tract, believe me, you will feel great after about a month of this, if you're overweight the results should be even better!!  I typically do this for two months then go back to just once a day for a few months then back to twice a day to get a good clean in.  I will likely continue to use barley powder the rest of my life.  It's easier than growing my own wheatgrass or barley and juicing it, plus its likely cheaper in the end, not to mention the time.  I know fresh is better but this is certainly a great shortcut to growing your own.  As for the mixing of it, I used to use a shaker bottle but have been using a nutribullet for the last year, it foams on the top for a few minutes but it certainly integrates the powder the best in liquids.  There's plenty of documented benefits of chlorophyll and greens in general so get yourself a bottle and enjoy!!

title: Tried lots of good recipes but still have many more to try
text:
I would definitely recommend this book if you like keto baking. I got this book because I've really only found about 5 or 6 keto recipes that are desserts or baked items that I like, and three of them are Carolyn's. They are her garlic bread sticks from her soup cookbook, her almond crusted butter cake (blog), and her scotcheroos (blog). They are all amazing! I have tried several things from this book, but still have many more to try. There are several that I haven't liked and several that I have liked. I will go over what I have tried.

I started out with the rum cake because it was around Christmas. It was pretty good but not good enough to finish the whole cake because I love rum cake and it just wasn't the same. I've learned that with keto treats it's usually better for me not to try to replicate things that I love in the non-keto version because they rarely compare. Having said that, I tried the banana bread and it was amazing! It was so much like real banana bread that I couldn't believe it! The chia seed trick really made a difference! I would buy this book just for that recipe!

In general, I hate keto cookies! I love real cookies and the texture of keto cookies is always awful. I love gooey, chewy cookies and most keto cookies taste like cake. And not very good cake either. I've tried at least 10 keto cookies and ended up throwing them out, so I didn't make any of her normal cookies. They sounded the same as the many I had tried. But, I did try some of the cookies that were supposed to be crispy because I thought I might like the texture. I had the oatmeal lace cookies and the cowboy cookies and both were great! The only thing I didn't like was that you had to use erythritol sweetener (not allulose which I prefer the taste of) or they wouldn't be crispy. I thought they had an extreme "cool" taste, which I didn't like. That's more the fault of the sweetener than the recipe.

I tried the vanilla ice cream which I didn't like at all. It had a whipped cream texture which I hate in ice cream. I also tried the caramel sauce to use in one of her online recipes. It tasted okay but it was for Carmelito's and it doesn't get chewy like normal caramel, so it was disappointing.

Then I tried some of the savory items. The rosemary olive oil bread had good flavor but a weird texture that I didn't like. It was better if I buttered a slice and put it under the broiler. I made the cloverleaf dinner rolls and they were okay. I much prefer Carolyn's garlic bread sticks in her soup cookbook. They are amazing! I made the bagels and they were just okay. I wouldn't make them again. I made the cream cheese biscuits and the cheddar drop biscuits, and they were both pretty good. But I think my very favorite thing, in addition to the banana bread, are the fresh herb and ricotta scones. I love those! I've made them a bunch and even for company. They are delicious!

That's about all I've tried so far. But I still have a ton to try and I'm really looking forward to it! I think the cookbook is definitely worth getting for the things I have liked because it's so hard to find good tasting keto items that are baked or sweet. That has nothing to do with the author, it's just the way it is. If I can find a few that I actually want to make more than once and wouldn't mind serving to non-keto company, then it's worth it!

title: Long Lasting Moisturizer
text:
Not a miracle product, but deffinitely keeps dryness and itchiness at bay for longer than anything else I've tried. Consistency is pasty and greasy. But unlike some heavy duty moisturizers, it does not rub off on clothes or hair too badly. I would only recommend this particular cream for severely dry skin as the packaging indicates.
During pregnancy I began having really dry, itchy, red skin on my hands and face. My skin, normally moderately-sensitive, became super-sensitive and I had to discontinue use of all products I had been using on my face, since they all made my face burn and itch. I went to see a dermatologist who told me to discontinue all products except for vaseline and Cetaphil Cleanser and also prescribed a steroid ointment. Eventually had to change my shampoo and conditioner as well since they were also irritating. Anyhow that combo did help, but even the Vaseline was not keeping the dry skin at bay. I had to reapply several times a day. After sleeping I always woke up with dry flaky patches. I was desperate to find something more long lasting.
I searched the national eczema foundation website and found that Theraplex Emollient had 5 out of 5 on their rating system so I ordered it to give it a try. Initially I got the smaller tub since I wanted to waste s little money as possible if it didn't work. When I started using it I immediately noticed a difference. For me this will last through all day without reapplication, so I only have to use it morning and night, instead of every few hours like other creams I've tried. Like I said it isn't a miracle cure, but it has definitely helped make me more comfortable.

title: These are awesome! Recently
text: These are awesome! Recently, we found out that my 4 year old boy cannot see much of anything and ended up with a pretty powerful prescription which make his lenses thick and heavy. This is his first pair of glasses and I wanted to get him something that would keep them on his face without making him self conscious  or make him frustrated with putting them on. After a ton of browsing and reading reviews, I settled on these. I did NOT put the strap that comes in the set on his glasses because the little hooks are enough on their own. He is a typical boy... runs, jumps, climbs, wrestles, ect. and these little silicone hooks do even better than I hoped keeping his glasses secure on his face. These little hooks are very soft and pliable, easy to put on and easy for my son to adjust behind his own ears when he takes his glasses on and off. He has only had his glasses and these little hooks for about 2 weeks now and he is a pro at putting them on and adjusting them. I ask him periodically if his glasses are comfortable and he says they are very comfortable. NOTE: when I got these in the mail I took them with me to the optometrist to pick up his glasses so I could ensure my sons glasses were adjusted appropriately so the silicone didn't add extra pressure to his head and end up making him sore after prolonged use. Some other reviews said it caused the glasses to be too tight and bother the child so, I wanted to try and lessen this possible issue. Even the eye doctor was impressed by the little hooks and asked when I got them.

A friend recommended this product and I figured it was worth a shot. I'm blown away by the difference! Mind you, it did take a few practice shots to figure out the best technique (put the pill dispenser at the back of their throat and be quick to release; the more time you spend aiming, the fussier your cat will get). It's easy and you will get better with practice! Also, if the pills are small you can fit a couple in there and give at the same time. Now the process is quick and my cats don't have much time to react or get fussy. I make sure to give them treats afterwards to create a more positive medicine experience. Overall, I'm very happy I got this product!

title: VERY difficult to use
text:
These rollers come in this weird design that doesn't wrap fully around the roller in one rectangular piece - it's like a streamer is wrapped around the roller in a twisting fashion (if that makes sense). This makes it VERY difficult to peel off half or more of the time (you have to dig your finger in to a corner and hope you can get a tiny section to peel AND that section will bring the rest of it with it), and if you don't peel it all off, some of the top layer remains, and that's even harder to remove.

On top of that, the extra rolls they give you do not lock into the roller, so as you use them, they slide off the roller and you lose control. While cheap, this option is NOT suggested for the reasons above - it's worth saving yourself the headache and spending an extra dollar or so to get logically designed and functional products.

title: Completely ineffective.
text:
I used to leave my car parked in an unshaded lot for my ten-hour shifts, from seven in the morning to five in the evening. I had breaks around 9, 12:20, and 3, plenty of opportunities to see first-hand how cool the car would be after letting this fan run during different times of the day. No matter how I tried (with the weather stripping, without, installed on either side of the car, front, back window, etc.), my car was always a stuffy oven.
The first problem is that the solar cell doesn't have power most of the day. It's too weak to pull much energy unless the sun is almost directly perpendicular to the cell. Even the black vent duct shades the cell once the sun moves far enough overhead.
The second is that the fan simply does not move enough air, even when the motor is spinning at full blast. I don't know if the fan blades are just poorly made or if the motor doesn't have the power, but the result is the same.

As an experiment I made sure to visit my car when the fan was operational. You can hear the fan running (though it is quiet), and you can feel warm air coming out. But it's simply not enough, not while the fan is running and certainly not when it's idle (which is most of the time)

My advice? Skip this gimmick. Buy a cheap shade for your windshield and leave your windows on each side open by about half an inch. You will get FAR better results.

title: Essential Addition to Medical Response Kits, especially outdoor recreation, use with caution
text:
Seems like something everyone should have close by, just in case of emergencies. Hopefully I will never have to use it on myself or anyone else. If this stuff is used, make sure to show the EMTs or medical staff that treat the wound afterwards, once medical help become available. I think this newer stuff isn't supposed to burn, but I haven't tested out that theory. Sometimes applying this stuff can make a wound worse. Sometimes this stuff can mean the difference between life and death. Consult a medical professional because I am NOT one. To me this stuff is essential medical first aid kit content for the backpacker, cyclist, rock-climber, skateboarder, responder, etc. Or just get some gauze or a Z-Pak. Bandages are available with this stuff worked into the gauze. These types of medical supplies should only be applied when needed, sometimes only as a last-ditch effort. Please receive as much training as possible.

Lightweight and doesn't take up much space. Easy to take on a hike or camping trip without sacrificing weight or space. If someone had a puncture wound with severe bleeding that could not be stopped with a tourniquet, this stuff might be an option, along with bandages and a plan to get medical treatment ASAP.

Again, I have not used this stuff, and I am not a medical professional. Hopefully I will never have to use Celox, and if a treating a wound does not require it, I wouldn't apply it. I only know what I have learned myself or been told by others with medical training. Great addition to First Aid Kit, use with caution, hopefully you wont have to either. It's one of those things you have "just-in-case"

Does have a shelf life.

title: First thing to actually work
text:
I have had a real issue with smelly shoes. It wasn't just bad when I took them off but I was announcing myself with them on. I have tried everything with no luck. (Oder-Eaters, Dr' Scholls Oder Eaters, Lysol, baking powder). The only option I had was buying sneakers every two months. I saw this last month and was willing to try anything.
This stuff really works! Shoes that really were smelling bad, I took out the insoles and sprayed the shoes and insoles and let them sit 24 hours. WOW what a difference.

For anyone who has it really bad as I do, here are a few other thing I have started which seems to be working.

1) buy two pairs of sneakers and each night take soles out and let sit 24 hours while the next day I wear the other pair.
2) bought SweatBlock Antiperspirant towelettes - One once a week before bed
3) Soapy Soles Foot Scrubber - for shower
4) PediFix Fungasoap Liquid, use with Foot Scrubber
5) Spray Right Guard Antiperspirant Spray, Which I spray my feet each morning, before I put on my socks
6) remove shoes once I get home to allow them to air as much as possible

title: Godsent during pregnancy!!!
text:
So grateful for this adjustable cradle. When I wear this brace my belly and legs don't ache, and my feet don't swell. I'm able to walk more and further. I'm 35 weeks pregnant with my second and I worn this cradle for both pregnancies. I recommend this cradle to everyone in the birthing industry- my midwife, chiropractor, doula, etc. My hope is pregnant mamas everywhere discover it and alleviate unnecessary pain.

Note on sizing. Order based on current weight not pre-pregnancy weight.
First pregnancy I started off at 123 lbs and delivered at 150 lbs. The small cradle worked great.
Second pregnancy I started off at 123 lbs but by 28 weeks was already 152 lbs. I ordered a medium and was grateful I did. It initally fit on smallest hook and still left room for my growing belly. Highly suggest this cradle for later in pregnancy over other types that don't adjust or don't cross over the shoulder. I tried both and they weren't nearly as effective.

I suggest adding hooks in between the hooks provided to add more adjustability. The hooks provided are about 4 inches apart. Adding hooks enables you to adjust every two inches. That said, the band stretches so if you aren't able to add hooks the cradle still works well.

The cradle shoulder straps do show on many outfits--but the benefit of the cradle far outweigh this flaw in appearance.

Best wishes for a healthy and pain free pregnancy. This cradle certainly can help!

title: This product was recommended for my Dad by his regular physician
text: This product was recommended for my Dad by his regular physician.  She felt that at his age (86) his body was not absorbing the vitamin tablets he was taking, and she wanted him to try this.  She sells this as part of her weight loss clinic, and I bought the first canister from her.  I followed her directions to give him 1 scoop once a day mixed with about 1/2 cup water or juice, and I noticed a slight positive improvement in his physical and mental abilities.  When that canister was empty, I went back to her office to get some more; they were out.  They were out for the next 3 weeks, and my dad's health, physical and mental, was declining rapidly.  So I ordered it from Amazon using the Prime shipping option on a Friday, and received it 2 days later, on Sunday.  I mixed it according to the canister directions, which is 2 scoops once a day mixed with about 1/2 cup water or juice, and gave him a dose Sunday night, and another mid-day on Monday.  His mental and physical health bounced back dramatically by Tuesday.  So I continued to give him the 2 scoops dosage.  This product has probiotics in it and that has helped with his elderly digestive issues that had developed.  I quickly found out that since it is a powder, it does not mix well when stirred, but does mix very well when put into a jar with a lid and is shaken.  It is like any dry powder:  it takes a bit of time to absorb the liquid.  The product is a red powder, and mixes up to look like an opaque red kids' drink.  It tastes like a mix of red kids' drink and grapefruit juice; it has a strong citrus flavor.  I take this as well now, and I personally like it better mixed as directed then put into a larger cup and topped up with orange juice.  I also prefer it chilled, so will add a cube of ice just before serving.  Every other vitamin powder I have ever tried looks and tastes like pond water with algae in it; this does not!  It is very pricey, but if you or someone you know is having some issues, physical or mental, try it; it might help.

text: Overall I found the 27 watt bulb in this lamp somewhat dim for most tasks, especially compared to the 42 watt full spectrum bulb used in similar lamps, such as the Bluemax. Moreover, my Verilux lamp failed after only 200 hours of use, but because my lamp was out of warranty, the company was unwilling to replace the lamp (although I was offered a 25% discount on a new lamp). The failure was probably due to a failed or defective ballast, which in this older model is not replaceable. Interestingly, the new models do have a replaceable ballast, which suggests that lots of other ballasts failed in this older model. Verilux's handling of my failed lamp, and probably of many other similar failures, reminds me of car manufacturers, who refuse to issue needed recalls, calculating that their cumulative legal costs will be less that total recall costs. However, Verilux, like VW and Toyota, will probably learn learn that a diminished brand name is far costlier than the handling of any defects in fair and honest manner.

The way I learned that you apply it is is by not coving all the lashes with it completely but mostly by the root. I left that on for about 13 min and then wiped it off with a Cotton swap from root to top. When I did that for each eye I got a clean cotton swap dipped it in jar c and wiped each eye from root to top. After I got jar B and applied it the same way as jar A on both eyes I let it sit for about 10 min and after 10 min i removed it from both eyes with clean cotton swabs from root to top
Then again with a new cotton swap I dipped in jar C and when went over them again from root to top. Once that was done I got a new cotton swap and
Dipped into jar D and proceeded
To removed the eyelashes from silicone pads by rubbing the cotton swap gently side to side until they lift. I used that same cotton swap to remove the actual silicone pad from the skin. When both pads are removed you will find that your lashes and eyelid have glue on them. I used coconut oil to remove the excess glue and one of the black mascara brush provided In the kit to brush the eyelashes out. The eyelashes may look partially clumped together but this is normal but make sure not to wet them within the first 24 hours but once you do wet them after that time the eyelashes will separate. As far as clean up I used the coconut oil

title: Amazing results
text:
I would have given 4 stars due to lack of instructions, but the final result is so amazing it made up for it! I watched a lot of tutorials on youtube, and there's some mixed info regarding how much product to use, how long to leave it on, in what order, and if it's okay to wet them or use mascara in the first 24 hours. This is the method that worked for me:
1) Start with clean & dry lashes. Mine are very long but straight, so it really helped to use an eyelash curler before staring everything. If I didn't have good vision, I would have had a hard time doing his on my own without help (since you have to look in a mirror up close during the process).
2) Select a rod size or pink silicone size relative to your lash length. The sticky white rods were too small for me, and a pain to use. I used the size L pink silicone (you will receive size S, M & L).
**Do one eye at a time**
3) Put lash glue on your eyelid and on the smooth/flat part of the silicone rod that will go against your skin. Wait about 1 or 2 minutes before pressing onto your lid, that way the glue is a bit tacky and it will stick. When it's freshly wet, it won't stick too good. I learned this the hard way. Press the pad gently on your lid for a few minutes. If there are gaps at the edges & you can't seem to get it to stay, don't worry, once you get glue on the lashes it'll pull it down against your skin. Just to make use of more tools in the kit, I used the pink round air pump thingy to shoot air onto the silicone pad with glue, so that the glue would dry faster. I think that helped a bit.
4) Work in little sections! Put lash glue on a few lashes, and use the white thin tool (the thin edge, but on its side) to slide & press your lashes upwards and onto the pink silicone pad. Keep doing this until they stick. Add a little more glue if you have to. When the glue starts to dry, lashes stick a little easier. Once the lash section is stuck on the silicone pad, use the pointed white part of the tool to separate lashes that clump together on the silicone. Repeat this in tiny sections until you finish your whole eye.This step is what takes the longest.
5) Use one of the little green sticks with small round felt tip, dip it in jar A, and work in sections layering it on your lashes (you'll have to dip for more product). I did not put a big glob of product. I went over all my lashes about twice with it, dipping it a few times in the jar, but being careful not to overdo it and get it in my eye. I left this on 12 minutes.
6) With clean q-tips, wipe product from jar A off. I went from root to tip, rotating the q-tip, and I used several. Then, I dipped another q-tip in warm water and went over my lashes again. I was afraid the little bit of water would mess up the process, but it didn't.
7) Rinse and pat dry the little green stick, dip it in jar B, and repeat the process above. This product gave me a tiny slight tingle in my eye, about halfway through, but I had no redness and no irritation. I was extra careful when I did my second eye, and it happened again. Not sure why. I left the product from jar B for 10 minutes.
8) Repeat the q-tip cleaning process.
9) Now for the other two jars...this is where I had no idea what I was doing, but I got great results regardless :) I dipped a q-tip in jar C and wiped my lashes with it. Then I did the same with a fresh q-tip in jar D. The q-tip combined with jar D seemed to loosen my lashes from the silicone, but I still needed extra help with get the glue off.
10) The lash glue was a mess. It was everywhere & not really coming off. I used neutrogena oil free eye makeup remover with a cotton ball on entire eye/lid, as if I was removing makeup, and it came off right away! For my second eye, I dipped Q-tips in the neutrogena eye makeup remover and wiped my lashes on the silicone with it & they came off easily. Then I began wedging a q-tip with makeup remover behind the silicone pad against my eyelid to gently unstick the silicone pad from my skin. I still had to wipe my entire eye with a cotton ball & eye makeup remover at the end to get every trace of glue off.

-I put a teeny bit of the mascara that came in the bag, and snapped the pictures. I don't know how this isn't the most popular beauty trend ever. It's incredible how amazing my lashes look!

Step 1: Make sure eyes are clean and dry. Prepare your tools even the ones that aren't included. Q-tips, warm water and any type of make-up remover.
Step 2: Use the Sticky Perm Rod or Silicone Pad S,M,L. I used the Large Silicone Pad, then applied glue to the smooth side to stick to my eyelid, make sure it's as close to your lash line as possible. The glue can get a bit tricky but just be patient, once the Silicone Pad is secure apply glue on to the other side and begin the lifting motions in section with either the long white tool or the little black brush. Brush, apply more glue, repeat that till your lash are fully glued to the Pad and notice the glue is starting to build up. Then begin to separate clumped sections with the white tool.
Step 3: After you secure all your lashes on the Pad or Rod take Formula A. Apply evenly with the green felt tool and let it sit for 12-10 minutes. Make sure you have the under eye Cotton Pad applied while using the Formulas because they do sting a bit.
Step 4: Once the time is up take the warm water and Q-Tips and begin removing slowly Formula A, in upward motions starting from the roots to the tip of your lashes. Just make sure you don't complete remove the glue though.
Step 5: Now apply Formula B evenly with a new green felt tool and let it sit for 10 minutes. And repeat the product removal step once the time is up. After every Formula removal make sure you just have glue remaining, no extra product, you don't want to mix them.
Step 6: Formula C! It's has a consistency of an oil so you can apply it with the black brush, apply small doses because it does help separate and move lashes a little easier. Let this sit for 5 minutes and repeat the removal process.
Step 7: Just like Formula C, Formula D has the same oil base consistency, apply this one for 5 minutes.
Step 8: OPTIONAL: apply Growth Mascara for 5 minutes.
Step 9: It's time for cleaning up finally. Water will not change lashes so you'll be fine. I lifted my Silicone Pad and slowing became cleaning my eye with warm water and Coconut Oil, I use that as a make up remover. It will lift the glue instantly and nourish your lashes. I did my first eye with a benefit make up remover and it took longer to remove, the Coconut Oil was most effective!

After you have one eye down repeat these steps!

title: Product works great. 1
text:
Had an issue with the pack, the seller fixed it promptly. Product works great.

1. decide if you'd rather use the white rods or pink gel things. The rods seemed a bit too little for longer eyelashes and I went with the reusable pink gel pad thing. There's also packets of lower eyelash protective pads-not a must, just your preference. You'll need the eyelash glue (white bottle, blue lid), the white bent tool, and a LOT of patience for the first part
2. Line the pink gel thing on the bottom, about 1cm wide, with eyelash glue. Wait about 30 seconds for it to get a tad bit tacky and then place it as close as possible to the eyelid/eyelash hairline and hold for 40 seconds. Do both eyes to save time. The less you blink, the better it will stay.
3. Ok, this is tedious, but, the most important part. Use small amounts of the eyelash glue on the pink gel where it's riveted. Use the white bent tool to slowly plaster each hair into a slot. The smaller amount of glue the better, but be sure the hair is firmly on the pink gel thing. Note: if you get impatient and plaster a bunch of eyelashes crooked and not straight, you'll get that as your final look, take your time and do 1-2 hairs at a time if you can. You will also need to wait till the glue is a bit tacky to work. So tiny dab of glue, let it get tacky, and slowly plaster up. You'll want to press and pull the hairs to toward the brow line.
4. Ok, so you've been plastering for what seems an eternity. Now, get bottle A and a green wired q-tip thing and generously cake a layer onto the eyelashes. This stuff is mildly irritating in your eyes so be mindful close to where the eye lid meets the lashes. Now, wait, as long as you possibly can. I waited 30 minutes on one eye and 10 on the other...the 30 minutes is where it's at. Then, wipe off gently with a paper towel or something with not a lot of lint.
5. Repeat with B and a new q-tip. I left this on for about 10-20 min. Then wipe off.
6. Bottle C starts to take the eyelash glue off. Go slow and try to work off as much glue as you can. Then use the q-tip to slowly slide under the pink gel that's touching your eyelid. Slow and steady so you don't pull any eyelashes off. Lots of re-dipping the q-tip.
7. Bottle D is like a conditioner, so you can hold the pink gel there to paint it on.
8. I'd treat it like a hair perm and not get it wet for the night if you can stand the extra eyelash glue feeling. Then a hot shower to get that annoying crap off.
9. And viola, you have gorgeous eyelashes all.the.time. I looked up how much it costs to get it done at a salon, and it's about $150! Should last 4-6 weeks. If you mess up, and make one side different, you can fix it by redoing the process.

title: Great tool
text:
I was desperately looking for a drill bit to drill two-inch holes in hard ground. Not for planting bulbs, but for putting down 2x2 stakes for sign posts. I wasn't even sure such a product existed. I looked at all the hardware stores, and most didn't have a clue what I was talking about. Finally, one guy said, yeah, it's called a "bulb auger", but we don't carry it. So then I called around to the lawn and garden stores, and none of them had it either. In desperation, I checked on Amazon, and there it was! And at a decent price, too. I must have drilled 200 holes in hard-packed dirt with it over the first week I had it, and it performed amazingly. The cutting edge was dulled and worn down after all this drilling, but no more than I would expect after the workout I put it through. But it still drills great.

If you do buy this, take my advice on how to use it. This bit just cuts through the dirt, in a spiral pattern, and the dirt between the spirals remains undisturbed. So, every 3-4 inches, you need to pull up on the bit, while continuing to drill, to loosen and remove the dirt you've already drilled through. If you don't, you won't have a whole at all, but an 18-inch-deep spiral cut in the ground. And if the ground is hard enough, then eventually the blade will stop cutting, and the chuck will keep turning, but instead of the bit turning, the drill will twist around, and might break your wrist, or the handle might hit you in a place you don't want to be hit. So drill a few inches, then pull up, then repeat until the desired depth is achieved.

Also, be careful if drilling in an area with a lot of roots. It WILL drill through roots, not like dirt, but it will go through them. If you hit one, just keep applying light pressure, and the blade will whittle away at the wood of the root until you're through it. Be extra careful of the blade getting stuck on roots. And note that this really dulls the cutting edge, as do rocks. But even when it's dull, this tool easily chops through the hardest of ground.

the battery would not charge to full with the GEL profile at 14.2v. I used the SLA profile on my solar charger which has 14.4v, still under the 14.5 - 14.9v asked for but will charge to full.
higher voltage will decrease charge time but will shorten battery life. The digital voltmeter built into the top is a good addition to the battery.

So they have the best of both worlds. GEL temp stability, GEL high cycle count, AGM amp output, AGM faster charging, makes for good battery specs.

So you get the best of GEL tech and the best of AGM tech.

will be ordering more if they hold up. MightyMax has my attention.

It does produce some ozone that I can smell even though the specs say it produces within FDA guidelines. There are many types of air filters on the market and I prefer ionizers because replacement filters are a pain and I can tell the ionizers work. The best way to keep a home's air clean is to have good air flow and open your windows. When you can't do that or outdoor air is compromised then these units come in handy. I would suggest one for each room of your house. They will be much more effective this way than one expensive unit. You do need to clean them about once a week or every two weeks. The cleaning is not very easy and that is a drawback. I like the fact if I want to I can take it in my car and will work better than any car type air cleaner. I would highly recommend these but I would suggest buying from Heaven fresh at the retail price because they offer a 3 year warranty. You will be lucky to get three years out of these due to the design. Nothing wrong with the design it is just an inherit problem that over time the metal plates and pins wear out. title: Crazy, but it's healing my injury!
text:
These insoles are a miracle! I think they are HEALING my feet. I thought I'd take up the hobby of jogging 8 months ago. I've always been active but more with body weight exercises, dance, pi-yo, and lifting. I was stride fit on a treadmill for Asics shoes for slight pronation at a reputable running store. I easily jogged 1 mile in my new shoes to break them in. Instead, I was limping the next morning. Then every pair of shoes hurt. It didn't get better after 3 months. The first few steps in the morning were especially excruciating, and I have a very high pain tolerance. I was diagnosed with plantar fasciitis. I did everything I was told. 600 mg ibuprofen, stretches, yoga, physical therapy. It helped somewhat. Nikes helped some more, but I still had to tie ice packs to my feet literally all night if I was on my feet for several hours just to be lucky to limp the next day. I have kids... I needed to keep up! This is the FIRST thing that helps. I tested the insoles out with normal errands on the first day. All good. I did 50 minutes inclined walk on the treadmill the next day. I finished feeling well and cried happy tears at the gym in front of everyone. Exercise has always been part of my life but it's tough when even standing hurts. I admit my feet were sore the next morning after the treadmill but the soreness went away as the day passed. So I did 100 floors on the stair climber. I had no pain that evening or the next morning. The next day was 100 floors on the stair climber and a half mile slow jog. Again, no pain. I cooked a big meal today for about an hour standing on the hard kitchen floor without slippers. I am normally limping by the end of cooking or washing dishes but I had no pain. Crazy, but I think these are actually FIXING my injury. I read a review saying it seems to be healing. It really seems to be! I've tried 3 kinds of Dr. Scholl's insoles, countless reputable shoes, ice, therapy. Nothing has helped except these.

I'm on here to order 4 more pairs to cut for my favorite shoes. I'm a shoe size 6 to 6.5. Due to the underneath pads on the front, they probably can't be cut smaller than a shoe size 4 or 5. I took the shoes' original insoles out and replaced it with these insoles. Too bad they are too thick and obvious for high heels, but you'll appreciate the provided cradling. I am grateful for something that works AND seems to be healing me after 8 months of sharp, stabbing, constant pain in my heels with every step. I was close to agreeing to a steroid injection or surgery. I'm so glad to have read countless testimonies about these first. This is worth a try before you try everything else.

title: Relieves foot pain
text: I read a lot of reviews on these and other foot pads before purchasing them. I am always interested in reviews because there is such a large difference of opinion from "fantastic to a waste of money. Because there was no clear-cut review, I decided that the best way to know if they work was to try them myself. It amazed me that some of the reasons users gave these pads a negative review seemed a little ridiculous to me.  Turns black when placed in water, made in China (I guess that they could not find bamboo and ginger in Ohio), ingredient packet wasn't attached to the adhesive (you have to place it there yourself) , no scientific evidence that says they work (also none that says they don't ). I have spent a lot of time in the Far East and am somewhat familiar with Far Eastern medicine and most of that medicine that has been curing people for thousands of years is not scientifically tested. So, I tried these pads. First, let me say that I suffer from arthritis in my feet, ankles and shoulder. On first getting up in the morning, it is difficult to walk without holding on to something for support because of the pain. I tried these pads and received immediate relief from that pain, I kind of wondered if the pain was actually relieved or if it was all just in my mind? I used them for 5 nights. No problems with the pads but I did notice that the color was not changing. I decided to stop using them to see what would happen. The next morning the pain was back again.  I again put them on and again was pain free the next morning. I really don't care what other people say about these or if they are not scientifically approved. All I know is that my pain is gone. And if it is that this is all psychological, who cares! I don' hurt!

Cassava is much much cheaper produced, and poisonous if processed into flour incorrectly.
When vendors sell Cassava/Tapioca as if it's Arrowroot -which is more expensive- they profit from unaware customers.

title: Must try!
text: If you, like me, have been on the hunt for a zero waste deodorant, you must give this a try! Everyone’s body chemistry is different, so everyone will have different reactions to new products. That’s a given. I personally love this brand, what it stands for, its environmentally responsible rigor in their creation and distribution of products, etc! The bar itself may seem smaller, but it will last you months and months. It glides on incredibly smooth and smells lovely without being overbearing. The bar may sweat, that’s normal! It’s an all natural product, so it’s just the oils. Do transfer it to an airtight container (soap tin or glass food container is fine). I’ve tried some others on the market (Lush’s Aramaco-couldn’t stand the smell, but also irritated me personally, a couple of the push up ones, which always ended up smearing off and I’d have to physically rub it in, etc) and this by far has been my favorite. It feels the most like regular deodorant but even better. Of course, there’s no applicator, so you have to get comfortable with touching it or store it with a piece of paper to grab it with. It’s an adjustment, but if you’re willing to commit, so much better for your body and the environment!

title: Don't let the price fool you!
text:
I have to admit that I wasn't expecting much due to the low cost of this iron, but as with other reviewers, I was pleasantly surprised! It's initial presentation makes it appear as if it was one of the top of the line (and very expensive) flat irons. It comes with two different options to store it, one being a black sturdy box with magnet closures and the other being a case that is perfect for travel. The inside of the case has a lining that I believe is specifically for "hot tools" but I am not sure and unfortunately, the product brochure didn't elaborate as to if this is the case. Another bonus found inside this case was a set of alligator clips, which also appear sturdy and well made. Having had many flat irons, most of which were on the more expensive side, I was really surprised at the weight of this one. Compared to my well known brand / high end flat irons, this one is light weight, which is a big bonus. I found it much easier to maneuver. With that being said, it is smaller than my flat iron in regards to overall size. This iron is suitable for traveling, for it is small, light weight & comes with it's own bag which has room for additional supplies/accessories. Perhaps it's due to my personality, but I am bothered by little things such as typos. Therefore I was slightly disappointed as to the instructions provided for they had several grammatical issues such as missing words. I know this can be looked at as a very minor and perhaps an insignificant detail, but something that I wanted to mention since it is an overall impression of the company. Perhaps this was overlooked due to their exceptional detail and desire to focus their energy on the presentation of this flat iron, for they did a fantastic job. I gave the iron 4 stars, for I really do like it and will use it for travel. It is missing a few features that I like, such as auto shut off, notification when the iron is at ideal temperature and I wish it were just a tad bigger, but all in all it is a great iron for a fantastic price!

title: Best Mineral Sunscreen: Not Greasy and No Bad White Cast!
text:
I never write reviews but felt like I was obligated to tell you how great this sunscreen is.

Definitely one of the best mineral sunscreens I've ever tried. It's NOT GREASY and the white cast is offset by a very light tint so it blends very well (may not pair well with darker skin tones, but for fair/medium, it works well). I don't like those mineral sunscreens that act as a tinted moisturizer with heavy coverage, so this sits very well with me. No one will be able to tell it's there.

The only reason I can't give it 5 stars is because the packaging is cheap, especially the cap. Be careful. I was kneading the bottle while getting ready and the closure came loose, but I didn't realize until it was too late... needless to say I lost about 1/3 of the product.

It smells so, so. I like my skincare to be fragrance-free, especially for my face, but I can understand since it's marketed for kids. The scent is very similar to Palmer's Cocoa Butter Formula. It goes away after about 15-30 minutes.

Also, for the people who are complaining about the price, I'm not sure if there's a similar product on the market for much cheaper... It's 3.3 oz with 20% zinc oxide and a lot of antioxidants.

title: recommended this lotion to help with cramping & spasmed muscles
text:
My doctor, a Fibromyalgia specialist, recommended this lotion to help with cramping & spasmed muscles. I just started using it, so I can not speak to the long term effects, but so far the lotion is as described. It is unscented and does dry a little sticky. Also, if you have dry or sensitive skin on your hands, I would suggest putting gloves on to apply the lotion to your body. Magnesium is a salt and while this lotion is marketed for sensitive skin, it burns if you have any tiny cracks in your skin. It also seemed to further dry out the skin on my hands after only a couple of uses.
I am glad that I purchased this regular lotion and not the Ultra with OptiMSM lotion. Turns out that this regular lotion has more magnesium per pump - 40mg elemental magnesium per 1ml pump vs the Ultra lotion with OptiMSM which has only 20mg elemental magnesium, but has an added 20mg elemental sulphur.

text:
I had high hopes when I got the Fitbit Aria -- for one thing just about everyone I know has it. I've been working out lately and wanted something to continuously monitor my weight, along with the other activity monitors I currently use. I also wanted something the whole family can use.

Setup was easy enough.

Inviting the rest of the family to use the scale was a nightmare. This thing was NOT designed with family in mind (which is very confusing since they clearly spent a lot of time in the "invite others" part of their software stack, and unless I missing something, people that would possibly consider using the scale together do live together. And if they live together, couldn't fitbit have used that fact to make the process a little easier). Inviting others to use the scale REQUIRES the invitee create an account w/ them -- and fitibt will NOT allow kids to create account. Anyway, that part annoyed the jesus out of me.

Once everyone was on board with fake birth years, etc., the scale is working fine. The app and site have some great features but there is just too much other junk there that creates more confusion than helps.

Version 2.0 of both hardware and software is much needed ... for now, I would still use it and recommend it.

title: Adapter missing. Took 9 days to get it.
text:
The product clearly states that it comes with a 2.5mm to 3.5mm adapter. When mine arrived on August 8th, it did not. I could not test the product since I do not have any devices that use the rare 2.5mm plug. I contacted the seller via Amazon and they responded that they would send me one at no charge. It finally arrived today (8/17). Took 9 days but now I can test the product.

Not sure why this product uses a rare 2.5mm headphone plug. As far as i know, the only devices that use this are very old flip phones (10+ years ago models). A family member has a Alcatel flip phone they bought last year and it has a typical 3.5mm headphone jack. The only other product that I know has 2.5mm are some cordless home phones.

The reason for the 2 star rating is that the product works (I have only tested it for about 15 minutes) but the fact you have to always use an adapter with any modern product is going to be very inconvenient. An adapter is easy to loose and this type of adapter is not very easy to find if you need one right away as you will basically need to order it online to replace it. I hope that the manufacturer will update this product with a modern 3.5mm plug.

The coiled cord is also annoying. Its coiled length is too short to be useful and it takes a bit of force to stretch it which can cause the hooks to move away from the hearing aids. It needs a 6 foot straight cord like any typical stereo headphone uses, since these are really just headphones for hearing aid users.

This product feels like it was designed by engineers who do not wear hearing aids or do not have access to people who do. It is ultimately a good idea with a poor design. If my hearing aids had bluetooth, I would not have needed these.

title: Functional, but has issues.
text:
As a portable noise generator for taking on vacation or to put pretty much anywhere, this is a great little device. But it's not perfect. First, some background:

So, I use a noise generator to sleep every night. Right now, I have an older gen 4 iPad running a noise gen app (in the background with a full screen clock app in the foreground, since it's useful). This iPad is then plugged into a small sound system via the headphone jack so it sounds better then coming out the tiny iPad speakers.

I was eager to give the Renpho Noise Machine a go, since I know my current solution's days are numbered (the apps are starting to crash regularly and can't update anymore due to how old the device is, etc).

Hence the Renpho device. And it works fine. Up to a point.

The first thing I noticed is that while you can have a single color and adjust the brightness to whatever level you like which is good, if you turn on color cycling it jumps back to full brightness and you can't adjust the brightness in that mode. If you try to, it switches back to single color mode. So, that's a bummer as I like to have my glowy things always cycling through their colors, but don't want to have this thing searing my retinas every night.

The next issue I found is when trying to plug in my sound system to the headphone jack of the Renpho. The sound level coming out of the device is maybe 30-40% the volume of the iPad's headphone output. Even with the Renpho noise gen at max volume and the stereo at max volume (25 according to the stereo's display), it's not even half as loud as my iPad's headphone output at 100% and stereo at med volume (15 on the stereo's display, for reference). That's a non-trivial difference, and kinda makes it unusable for that specific use case. Granted it's a very specific use case most people won't care about, but still...

I could always use the built in speaker, but like all tiny speakers the sound is tinny and lacks the depth of a proper sound system. I really like to hear the boom of those thunderstorms, ya know?

I'm hopeful that at least the lighting issue can be fixed via a firmware update, but ideally both could, depending on how they implemented the headphone interface. So, if things change, I'll update the review to reflect it.

Note:

Updated to 4 stars since I was contacted by the makers saying they would take my critiques under advisement. So, that's a star just for response time. And if they actually release some kind of firmware update to fix any of my issues, that's star number 5...

Cheers,

J^2

You can use it on chapped skin, baby’s face, dry elbows, to smooth your unruly brows, or for a quick swipe of moisture to give your cheeks a healthy dewy look. Sure, plenty of organic brands have balms in these tiny containers for like twenty bucks, but this does an equal ( if not better) job. Dr. Bronners does have a metal twist top container with a similar formulation intended for babies ( I think?) but the stick version is a bit more tidy. Both are amazing though.

Lifetime buyer. Please never change the formula.

title: Exceeded All Expectations!
text: Yes, it is embarrassing (and gross!) that I've never properly cleaned my yoga mat after three years of use. I've used it outdoors quite a bit, and I thought that the dirt ground into the groves of the mat would never come out. The sad condition of my mat finally got to me, and I put it in the tub and scrubbed it with soap--not a lot of improvement. Next I used a homemade concoction I read about on the net which was a total fail. Finally, after much research, I ordered the peaceful lavender Asutra mat cleaner. I got an email from the owner of the company before I received the cleaner with very helpful tips on how best to use the cleaner. Honestly, I thought the best results I could obtain was that I could clean the surface dirt off the mat. Boy was I wrong! The Asutra mat cleaner has removed years of grime from my mat. The deep cleaning method as explained in the very helpful email removed the stains that I thought were embedded in the mat and would never come out. This, in my opinion, is the best mat cleaner on the market. A little bit goes a long way, and the free microfiber towel is the perfect cleaning tool--just the right size, lint free, and dries quickly. The customer service is excellent! In addition to the first email, I also received another email checking to see if I was satisfied with the cleaner. Oh, yes, yes I certainly am! I'm a customer for life! If, like me, you need a product that easily deep cleans your mat and smells wonderful to boot, then take the plunge and order Asutra. You won't be sorry.

text:
Please note that my review is for the SMALL size ear plugs, users of the STANDARD size may not have the same experience as I did.

I have pretty small ear canals, which according to my wife explains my "selective" hearing! I was happy to find Earpeace Moto ear plugs to use on my motorcycle for hearing protection, as they are available in a small size. I find these very comfortable even after using them for an entire day.

Based on this, I purchased a set of the Earpeace Sleep ear plugs. Unfortunately, these prove to be very uncomfortable and even somewhat painful to use. This is due to the permanent filter that is MUCH larger than the filters on the Moto ear plugs and also not completely embedded (see picture). The end result is if you lay on your side, the filter cuts into your ear canal which is enough to wake me. This is unfortunate, as the the sound reduction works great on these and they don't cause the weird "I can hear my own breathing and heart beat" like the foam ear plugs, which sadly I'm back to wearing.

title: Bumgenius diapers are the BEST!
text:
I cloth diapered my older daughter (now 8 years old) in Bumgenius diapers, and now with baby #2 (born January 2016), I'm doing the same. I've tried a number of different brands with both girls, and Bumgenius are hands down the best. They're very easy to use, versatile (you can add extra absorbency when needed, such as at night), they are the trimmest cloth diapers that I've ever used, and come in some very cute prints! The Audrey print in particular is one of the most adorable that I've seen. I used all hook-and-loop ("velcro") diapers with my older daughter, so I was a bit disappointed to see that Bumgenius is no longer offering hook-and-loop (except in the neworn size), but I've gotten used to the snaps. For me, it's not that I find snaps particularly "difficult," but it's more about sizing it perfectly; though that may be more about my Type A personality than anything! I'm very particular about symmetry, so I like to use the same snap setting on the right as on the left, so if the diaper needs to be adjusted up or down just enough so that I only need to go the the next snap setting on ONE side, it bugs me that they're not symmetrical! Again, more a personal problem than a functional one! If I had one suggestion, it would be to place the snaps a little closer together so that the diaper can be adjusted in smaller increments (and that complaint really isn't a big deal, and not enough to warrant losing a star!) I highly recommend Bumgenius pocket diapers to anyone.
Pros:
•Easy to use
•Trim
•Adjustable Absorbency
•Cute Prints
•Superb construction

Cons:
•Company no longer offers hook-and-loop option
•Snaps could be positioned closer together so that size could be adjusted in smaller increments

text:
As an IBS-C (C for constipation) sufferer, this product has been fantastic!! I was first diagnosed with IBS back in 2004. A gastrointerologist recommended that I take Psyllium fiber tablets which I have taken for the last 12 years & still do today. title: I tried for cushions, and this one's the winner!
text:
Guys. My butt is so happy. I'm not joking, I legitimately bought four different cushions to try to make sitting at my desk for hours on end less uncomfortable. I tried the Comfilife cushion that has awesome reviews, plus a wedge-shaped cushion and a cushion/back support combo. The Comfi-Life came close, but for me it still wasn't quite right. While it was made of memory foam, it was extremely firm. The tailbone support idea is nice in theory, and I can see how the cutout in the back would work well for someone with significant pain issues. At 5'1 and about 115 lbs, the Comfi-life wasn't right. It elevated me too much, and the cushion was so firm that the cutout in the back was very obvious. While it was a step up from no cushion at all, I did have to reposition myself frequently to stay comfortable, even after just a few minutes.

The Royal cushion by Purple was a totally different feel. While it has enough structure to support you, the rubber itself is soft. Unlike the Comfi-life, it doesn't matter how you sit on it. It's comfortable in any position, not too soft, not too hard, and very supportive. Mine came in perfect condition, and the cover fits perfectly. I do wish they had replacement covers in different materials and colors so you could match it with your decor. If you're in an office with a typical black desk chair, it probably doesn't matter. My mini home office is in my bedroom, so I try to make it look as nice as I can.

I paired the cushion with the Coop lumbar support pillow and a foam foot rest, and for me that was the perfect combination. While the other seat cushions weren't bad products, I think their comfort level depended on your height and weight. I would guess that the Purple cushion would work well for almost any body type. Before you buy it, do measure the chair you're going to use it in and compare it with the dimensions of different models. I can't attest to their customer service, but I love Purple's product.

title: I expected a little better - Royal not really helpful for sciatica
text: I've heard all of this raving about the Purple mattresses and thought this would be something kind of revolutionary for my sciatica. I have the Royal. Does it remove some pressure when you sit? yeah. Does it stay fairly cool, yes. But the shape of it and the edges do not really help the situation. It did not really cover the seat of the desk chair I have, so I have to kind of move it around into position any time I change position for it to not cut in to various pressure points at the back of my legs or at my tail bone from time to time (or sometimes I turn it lengthwise, but then it's just a tad narrow). It is too thick and wide to be helpful in the car also. Where I do expect I will use it is in the bleachers at my daughter's volleyball tournaments, but do note it is a little heavier than you might expect so it's not like you haul it everywhere you go. It's not terrible, and maybe not outrageously priced, but it's far from revolutionary. It seems the "Ultimate" has been added since then, which maybe has better coverage and I notice has a dip for the tail bone. I'd try it but I don't want to lose that kind of coin since I waited too long to return this one. Should have listened to my gut in the first few days that it didn't really do a lot. woopsie.

title: This is a keeper!
text:
Bought for my wife who has L4/L5 problems. The cushion is very substantial and surprisingly heavy. Appears to be a high quality product. Don't understand why the mattress has a 10 year warranty and other of Purple's products haev a 1 year warranty.

The cushion has helped my wife on kitchen (hard) and dining room (soft) chairs. And in the passenger seat of the car. I have tried it while driving - it's comfortable but my head touches the car ceiling. I have used it as a pillow and slept very well. I suspect others may find it a little hard for sleeping, but it's fine for me.

It is still off-gasing a chemical smell after about a week. The off-gasing is a major reason to deter us from buying the mattress.

title: Not wide enough
text: I'd give it a five, since it is comfortable and does help with pressure points -- but it needs to be wider.  Not everyone in this world is skinny as a stick; some of us were born with a wide chassis, and it doesn't do the job if you can't fit both butt bones onto the pad (I'm a 5'10" woman with the bone structure of a medium sized man -- thanks, Dad).  The comfort is compromised when you need to sit in a way that isn't relaxed, just to try to keep yourself perched on the cushion.  At this price, I should think making it at least a full 20 inches wide would not be asking too much, and it would make the pad much more useful for a wider range of body types.  It makes a good back cushion, but not so good for where I need it the most.

It's really a good hookah over all, especially for the price. Easy to store and pack away with the case. Although, if you want to pack charcoal and tobacco in the case, you may not have enough room. Each hose having its own ball valve is a great feature - people don't have to cap their hose while others are pulling. The glass base is very nice quality and the main stem and gasket that fit into it create a good seal. I've enjoyed this one enough and trust it enough that I gave away my old hookah.

If you're a hookah enthusiast who collects high-quality pieces, this may be a bit below you. However, if you're like me and just want a good two-hose that looks nice for a good price - this is your one.

title: Real Deal
text:
[[VIDEOID:a20495c25ebe5211efb8537f50ed5a93]] Packaging: It was packaged nicely (like typical sea moss pakages are) with a see-through window in the front as pictured.

Initial Inspection: It was not overly salty or sandy and there was definitely an ocean-like/sea-like smell upon opening the bag, but it was not overwhelming. It did not smell like bleach, chlorine or any chemicals whatsoever and it was amber in color, which is indicative of it being wildcrafted. It was not crunchy but very dry and no moisture was present. So far so good!

Soaking: I DID NOT BOIL MINE! I let it soak overnight, approximately two to three ounces. When I tell you it more than doubled in size, please believe me! I had to tranfer it to a larger soaking bowl. Though it did not "melt" when I squeezed the strands, it was very soft and jelly-like after soaking.

Blending: Before blending, (tip) I used kitchen scissors to cut the moss into smaller strands to prevent them being caught in the blender and causing it to overwork. I added the cut up sea moss to the blender and then added the water in which it soaked. It blended smoothly into a consistent paste with no absolutely no lumps.

Storage: From the two to three ounces, I was able to fill two 16oz mason jars and one 8oz container! Talk about bang for your buck! I stored them in the refrigerator and they formed a perfect gel.

Quality: I waited to give the review because although the preparation was easy, I wanted to be sure I FELT the true benefits based on CONSUMPTION since this is my first time trying this seller. I absolutely do. I hope the product never changes because I am sold on this one! Sea moss for life.

text:
I had a very scary reaction the the Clear Care with HydraGlyde.I've been using the original formula of Clear Care since 2011. I originally switched to this formula because I having issues and sensitivity to another brands solution. Recently I tired the new version with HydraGlyde because the store I went to was not carrying the original formula. I had and extreme reaction the first (and subsequent times) I used the product.

The first day I wore my lenses they were fine. After storing them for the recommended time in the HydraGlyde formula I experienced a cloud like film. Initially I just thought my vision was a little blurry but within a half hour my visibility was the equivalent of being in a smoke filled room. In addition to that when I was driving at night there were extreme rainbow halos around any light source or reflective surface. Unfortunately I was not able to take them out right away and had to wait several hours. When I did finally remove the contacts stored in HydraGlyde the haziness persisted. I was scared that I would wake up the next morning and my eyesight would still be affected. Thankfully it was not. I did give the solution a couple more trys just to run a little self experiment. Each time was just as bad even when trying it with ta different set of lenses.

When I returned to the original formula and had absolutely no issues. BE EXTREMELY CAREFUL with the product. My eye doctor mentioned that the push is to start storing all their contacts in an equivalent HydraGlyde solution when packaged for consumers. I also worry that the original formula will be phased out of stores and only HydraGlyde will be offered. Alcon Laboratories, please, please do not do this. Many of us use your product specifically because additives have caused us issues in the past.

DO NOT BUY, stick with the original Clear Care.

We purchased a Kelvin for my father-in-law who went blind when he was 80. It was fairly easy to install; directions are thorough and clear. It took me a while to get the hang of programming it for various periods of the day, but once we got it programmed, we hardly ever touched it again for the rest of the 6 months he used it.

My only complaint is that the voice which announces time/temp/thermostat setting was not loud enough for him to hear as he sat in his chair in the living room 12-15 feet from the thermostat. He was somewhat hard of hearing and just couldn't make out what it was saying even when the house was quiet.

I'm just sorry I didn't buy it several years ago when he was still mobile. He would have been SO grateful to finally know what temperature his house was and what temp he was adjusting the thermostat to. I would probably still have had to do all the programming, but the everyday adjustments he would have handled well.

title: My Experience With Tangy Tangerine
text:
I don't usually write reviews, but I was surprised to see negative reviews for this product when I have used it for almost 2 months now, and have noticed significant positive benefits! My Dad gave me some of this, I took it at around 5pm, went to bed at 10pm and I literally had trouble sleeping because I was so alert and awake!

I continued to take this drink in the morning, and yes, in water it doesn't taste the greatest. But I mix it with juice or koolaid or even ice tea, and it tastes great! I actually enjoy it in juice or koolaid, as I think it actually tastes better.

I am more focused at work, have more energy in the morning, and just feel more focused while thinking clearly. It's hard to describe, but it feels like a natural energy and alertness that I haven't felt for a long time. The only time I felt close to this good, was when I was juicing fresh fruits and vegatables every day and drinking 3 glasses of juice. This is quick and easy. I read some people complained that it can clump up in your drink, but you just have to mix it with a spoon really good before you drink it (or add it to a bottle of juice/ice tea and shake it up). Then it pretty much all dissolves, and goes down easy.

I didn't take this to lose weight, but I did notice I did not have as much of an appetite for garbage foods, and I could definately see how this would benefit someone trying to lose weight.

Overall with continued use, I feel better, think more clearly, am more focused and generally feel healthier all around.

NOTE: I take less than the recommended dosage, as just one or two scoops work for me all day. So this makes it last a lot longer for me, since it is pricey, I try to make it last as long as possible. So maybe start with only a scoop or two a day, and go from there until you see how much you really need.

title: Not miraculous, but one of the better supplements I've tried.
text:
I heard about this supplement on the Alex Jones show as a UK listener. I'm sceptical of American infomercials in general (sorry, US readers -- I just find them overly enthused) but have been supplementing for years for chronic fatigue and concentration issues, so I tried out a couple of trial packs of this. I'm now ordering a canister of it.

There is something in this that helps my symptoms somewhat, but I don't know what it is. I have tried most supplements out there, and prefer liquids, as capsules and powders don't tend to work for me. I have paid more in the past for superfood green powders. BTT is expensive, so if you don't like the sound of it, Source of Life Gold by Nature's Plus would be my recommendation -- it gave me a short-term energy boost and gave my skin a nice glow. I'm just throwing that out there, as SOLG and BTT are the only supplements I've tried that have given me an effect.

BTT comes in a granulated form that dissolves in water (sometimes it can clump slightly though when mixing, and bits will need a good stir). It is sweet enough to drink in water, but it also tastes good in orange juice.

In terms of the ingredients, I don't see a lot in BTT that you can't get from other supplements, but I do know the effect I get from it isn't placebo, as most multivitamins do nothing for me. I also know of the criticisms made of BTT in terms of trace metals -- I am not a doctor or a nutritionist, so I don't know enough to comment. I am very sceptical of claims made that trace amounts of substances such as arsenic are good or even necessary for health. I think that the manufacturer should back up claims of necessity with peer-reviewed evidence. Some of the feedback online does seem to be distributor hyperbole -- treat this as a good multivitamin/multimineral, and try to eliminate gluten from your diet if you're sensitive, but don't expect miracles.

For me personally, this is a multivitamin that has a pretty strong effect. I'll update my review in another month once I've gone through a full canister. In short, it's not miraculous, but it is pretty good. If you can try a trial pack or two (five sachets apiece) before splurging on a canister, I would try that beforehand.

title: Great elbow brace for many purposes!
text:
I love this compression band! After typing and using my mouse all day, most of my evenings are either filled with tennis or softball so I get really bad tennis elbow/tendonitis/carpal tunnel from time to time. I've used other elbow wraps and sleeves but they either make my skin feel raw after a while or it just traps the sweat inside.
When I tried this elbow brace, it felt really comfortable and stayed dry. The pad on the inside lining is both soft and strong and it provides the perfect amount of compression on the muscles that hurt. The material seems very high quality, the stitching is strong, and I really like the design. It's got two velcro straps so it's easy to adjust. I wear it while I play sports, lift weights, use my computer, ride my bike, and even while I drive.
The set comes with TWO elbow braces, TWO wristbands which are also great quality, a drawstring bag, and a headband. No better deal out there. All I need is one brace for my right arm, so I gave the second one to my mom to use. She uses it while she plays badminton and even around the house while doing housework!
