title: It's an overengineered scale.
text:
Let's face it, at the end of the day the most important thing a scale should do is show you an accurate number representing your body weight. The additional features that this scale provides are mostly unimportant if you don't get that basic thing right.

Unfortunately, this scale will refuse to do this until you go through the steps necessary to connect it to their online service. This should all be clear from reading the product's description, but I feel it's important to reiterate this: if you're not plunging head-first into the whole fitbit ecosystem, willing to give them your personal information and sign up for their web services, this scale will be a brick.

What makes me the most uncomfortable is that It lacks a fallback mode to just "be a scale" if you haven't set it up yet. The lack of this fallback mode wouldn't be such a big deal though, if it wasn't such a huge pain to get set up:

If you're lucky enough to have a computer on your network that has WiFi, it *should* be a simple matter. But first of all, if you use an ethernet connection, you're out of luck. You *must* be able to use wifi, even if the scale and your machine connect to the same router.

This is because the setup guide relies on being able to switch to the scale's factory-default ad-hoc network, configure the scale, then switch back again. That means your entire OS, and any applications that are running and maybe using the internet, have to be disconnected and reconnected again to set up your scale.

Even that would be fine, if it *worked*. Unfortunately for me, on OSX 10.9 Mavericks on a circa-2013 iMac, it did not. I retried 5-6 times, watching as it tried to switch my wifi network to the Aria, switching to my neighbor's WiFi instead (maybe it thought their wireless router was the scale?) timing out, failing, and prompting me to retry. I tried various methods like manually selecting the Aria from my list of wireless networks, nothing really did it.

And this is especially bad when the panic starts to set in... when you realize you just spent upwards of $130 on a scale that *won't even tell you your weight* until you get their little wifi utility working.

Eventually I gave up and rebooted into my Windows partition on my same machine, and I had better luck there. But that experience really put a bad taste in my mouth.

Now that it's working, it's logging my weight and sending it wirelessly to fitbit's website. Cool, I guess. Don't know what use I'll really have for that.

I bought the scale to integrate with the "Lose It!" app I've been using tirelessly on my iPhone for years. I really wish the scale would just send my weight directly to my phone, but alas, it sends it to fitbit's servers instead, and Lose It syncs with their service indirectly. This means fitbit could pull the plug on this integration at any time, which makes me nervous.

Seeing as how this product is bad at both being a scale (which is really priority number one), and it only indirectly and flimsily supports the only other use case I have (integrating it with "Lose It!"), I'm very close to shipping this back to Fitbit and buying a bluetooth scale instead.

title: BEWARE--INGREDIENTS HAVE CHANGED, CONTAINS PHENOXYETHANOL
text:
I have used Thayer's witch hazel for many years, but not after today. They now have added the ingredient Phenoxyethanol, also called Ethylene Glycol Monophenyl Ether. It is a preservative with antibacterial properties. According to the Material Safety Data Sheet on phenoxyethanol, it is known to cause irritation to both the skin and lungs. It is considered a "paraben alternative". Personally, I do not want this in my Thayer's witch hazel. I am truly heart broken. So now I must find a new witch hazel and I will be returning the two bottles purchased. I just called Thayer’s customer care center and was told by a very sweet woman that they have recently added it as a preservative. I urge all people that love this product to call and voice your concern. Thayer's, you have lost my business and loyalty.
Update 2/22/19 — Amazon refunded me the amount for the two bottles. Excellent customer service.
Meanwhile, I found another brand of witch hazel. It has the same ingredients that Thayer’s used to have. So if you want something without toxic ingredients, the name is “Quinn’s”. I recommend it. It’s wonderful.

title: Okay
text:
This is branded as either Eveready or Energizer. It's body is sturdy, but not as well-built as comparable Streamlight or Coast Cutlery products. AAA batteries are common--which is good since you'll probably need to change them relatively frequently (incandescent bulb). Push button activation is convenient--it feels just like a push button pen. Pretty good light output.

It's nothing fancy, but it gets the job done. For a little extra money you can get an LED-based light that will last much longer (both bulb and batteries) and will probably be more sturdy. The only reason I can think of for getting this is if you don't like the light output from the LED's (I think incandescents have a reassuring warmth to them, while LED's seem a bit sterile). Otherwise, I would recommend looking at the LED's from Streamlight or Coast Cutlery (in particular, the Streamlight 65018 Stylus is pretty impressive).

title: Weight stayed off despite sedentary lifestyle
text:
I took this product before and liked it, so I got it again.
I know the instructions say that you should use adequate amounts of exercise and drink plenty of water, but this time my goal was different and I decided to handle it creatively.
I have voracious appetite and cannot control it at times (hormone cycles), so when I feel i'm getting uncomfortably heavier, I do a cleanse with either complete water fast or an intermittent fast with a timed once a day meal, and it'd helped me to lose a lot of weight but I usually gain it back as soon as the fast is gone. This time I didn't have a chance to exercise as recommended, had to take a very difficult exam and sit for studies day in and day out so it should have been hard not to gain this weight back considering I'm 46 and my metabolism is much slower than it used to be, but surprisingly the weight stayed off and I was able not to feel hungry at all, even through the hormonal cycle. Out of 20lbs that I lost, I only gained 2lbs back, and that i attribute to higher water content from salt and to intestinal filling.
As for the high caffeine warning, I completely stopped my daily coffee intake so it's kind of a replacement of a morning cup, and not an issue.

title: High hopes despite criticism but failed to deliver
text:
I've owned a Fitbit Charge HR for about a year and have loved it. I wanted to take my Fitbit experience to the next level and start tracking my weight daily (plus having the body fat %). I've read the reviews about how inaccurate the body fat percentage numbers can be and how much of a nightmare the Aria setup is but I thought, I'll roll with the punches and give it a shot. Bottom line: all of the other reviews outlining the shortcomings of the Aria are true.

My biggest gripe is the connectivity. I used the mobile setup method. Through the Fitbit app, there's a link to connect your Aria to your account and the process itself isn't that bad but my Aria would never stay connected to my network. It wasn't that the Aria forgot my SSID, because when I went through the reset procedure, my network was still saved, it just stopped communicating and wouldn't recognize me anymore (just as "guest"). I tried putting the Aria closer to the router but that never resolved the issue, it would just stop working.

It is actually quite astounding that the Aria has been out so long, yet Fitbit hasn't responded to the connectivity criticisms. Utilizing Bluetooth would rectify all of the Aria's connectivity problems, but they stick with Wifi (band b, no less which is antiquated). I shouldn't have to worry about these things when using a scale, especially at this price point.

Second, the body fat percentage numbers are really, really bad. I'm talking +/- 5% or even more, so it's hard to even get a gauge at your average, making it a useless feature. Yes, it is known that BIA is objectively inaccurate but it's really all over the board with the Aria and negates any selling value that it is included in the scale.

While I had really high hopes the Aria would work for me, it followed through on delivering the common criticisms that everyone else has outlined. My advice: buy a standard, low-cost digital scale and manually enter. You'll save time, money and stress.

title: Good Visual Reminder, Awkward With Mugs
text:
Headline says it all, pretty much. It's been a very good way of getting my ADHD brain to remember that I need to actually drink and my water bottle and mug are not just desk decor. The only thing is, hydration doesn't just come from water. I like to have a mug of tea most days, and since the band is one solid piece it doesn't do well with drinking vessels that have a handle. Since the unit itself does separate from the band and can be clipped onto other things, I've been able to rig a solution with velcro cable ties. But it doesn't look very nice, doesn't fit my mug as precisely as a stretchy band would, etc. It would be great if there were a band that buckles or snaps or something so that it can be threaded through handles.

Glancing through the comments above, I also agree that an (optional?) audible alert might be a good idea too. After all, if the Ulla isn't in your line of sight or if your sight is impaired then a purely-visual alert isn't much use. At the same time, I recognize that adding that feature would dramatically increase the complexity of the device and drive the price up. Accessibility vs price is never a fun equation to solve. :(

title: Frustrating to Use
text:
I use iProven’s bbt thermometer which I really like, so I figured I’d give their strips a try. I’m kicking myself for not getting the strips I used for my previous cycle because they worked A LOT better than these!

When the five minute window is up, there’s not even a clearly visible result. The control line is still really faint and you can see the dye hasn’t even settled yet. If you wait 7-10 minutes, the lines are a lot easier to see but then you have the problem of wondering if it’s even accurate since you had to wait until outside the five minute window. This isn’t even the only problem with these tests.

With the same urine sample, I used three different strips and they all ended up with different darknesses and didn’t finish developing at the same rate. After 5 minutes, only one of them had readable results, the other two took more like 10 minutes. So I guess it’s safe to say these tests aren’t accurate quantitative-wise.

If you want an easier time tracking ovulation, I’ve found that Choicemmed ovulation strips have been the most reliable and are also really affordable. I’ve also heard from a lot of people that easy@home strips work great too. Just don’t use these, you’ll be ripping your hair out.

title: Unreliable. It's at most a toy, a Tamagotchi.
text:
This item is much more of a toy or Tamagotchi than a "fitness scale". Accuracy was non-existent, UX sucks, and support was poor. If you want quality you'll probably need to wait a couple years for Fitbit to get its act together. Sadly it took several hours to discover my Aria was a lemon ( http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemon_law ), and we had to discover this fact the hard way since Fitbit's support is slow and 20th-century. More on what went wrong:

* Body Fat feature is purely a toy: The scale's body fat measurement suddenly dropped from 30% to 15% without me changing anything on the scale or in the app. Moreover, day-to-day measurements appeared *inconsistent* with my food intake-- my body fat has trended /down/ over a week of eating /more/ fatty foods (and carefully maintaining constant water intake). And what the hell is Normal vs Lean mode? Is clicking Lean supposed to make me feel better about myself?

* The scale's measured weight was more than 5% inconsistent between weighings (even after 5 weighings). After drinking a bunch of water, a Shaper Image scale confirmed I gained 2-3 pounds and yet Aria registered no change.

* The wifi setup is A MAJOR PAIN, especially when the device FAILS TO CONNECT to your wifi. I lost over an hour trying to get this thing to connect to my standard 802.11 WEP-protected network. Laptops, phones, iPads, and lots of other devices have no trouble connecting. There are SO MANY THINGS wrong with Aria's UX, from requiring you to enter your Fitbit login and scale name on EACH SETUP ATTEMPT, to using (on mobile) an out-of-app web flow, to the web app not reporting the same errors as the scale itself. Fitbit's Product Managers need to take a hard look at how Chromecast does buttonless wifi setup, which is orders of magnitude easier and ACTUALLY WORKS. They could also spend a couple dollars to put a Bluetooth chip in the scale for not just setup but sync.

* Fitbit wouldn't issue me a straight-up refund. In comparison, Amazon gave me a refund for an unopened Fitbit charge that I returned to them *without a receipt*. Furthermore, Hoka One One (a new shoe company) gave me a FULL REFUND for a WORN pair of shoes that failed while I was running.

* While I guess I should be happy Fitbit even answers email, their email support isn't much more than somebody walking you through a bunch of troubleshooting wizard questions. I asked to actually converse with an expert several times and was denied. While the people answering emails appear to be doing their job well, the managers who set up this whole process have done a pretty sloppy job and let down their own staff.

Unless you're a gadget freak and really want a toy regardless of its reliability, get yourself one of the other scales on Amazon for a fraction of the price.

title: I'm glad that I have now found the worst product ever ...
text:
I just burned my left eyeball with this rubbish. Why the absolute hell would you put bleach in an contact lens solution product? As a product designer, I'm glad that I have now found the worst product ever designed - but I'm not sure the ongoing pain in my eye was worth it. Binned it right away and would love to sue the makers for intentionally maiming their market.

"Oh, lets shape the bottle exactly like all other eye solutions". "Lets give it a red lid, because EVERYONE knows that a red lid means 'don't put directly into eye'". "Lets bury the warnings in the small print in case actually warning people they may scar their eyeballs with incorrect use may make some people think twice about handing over their cash". "Lets stock this crap next to all other contact lens solutions that have completely different methods and parameters of use".

I'm pretty neutral about companies in general, but this has made me hate this company because I know they are aware of the product use cycle, consumer perceptions and behaviours and the fact a lot of people will assume it's okay to do the same thing they do with all other contact lens solutions with this product such as swap up containers, rinse their lenses with the solution bottle or occasionally need to reuse their lenses with less than 6 hours between sessions. They know this, but they clearly did a simple sum that made them conclude it was far cheaper to keep hawking this cheaply manufactured eyeball melting bleach and ignore the injuries it's dishing out to their customers (google it).

I'm seeing my optician this week to make sure it hasn't damaged my eye. The worst, most horrible thing I can wish upon the contemptuous suits at "Alcon" is that they use their own bloody product.

I can only assume (I've not checked) they also have a line of cookies flavored with broken glass ("but EVERYONE knows that if the packet's purple, it means that you aren't actually supposed to eat the cookies, just look at them").

I will check everything I buy to make sure it's not made by this company.

title: The cork equivalent of particle board
text:
I bought this expecting a roller that was actually a chunk of cork wood (it's advertised as "natural", after all).

You know how particle board is basically sawdust mixed with glue and pressed into shape? That's what this is - complete with the strong chemical smell. The fact that all the reviews talk about how heavy it is should have been a clue (cork is extremely light).

I was still thinking of keeping it just to save the hassle of a return, when I noticed that its edges were leaving beige marks on my yoga mat - meaning this unsealed roller was actually shedding cork dust (and god knows what other chemical glues or plastics are holding it together) into my home and, presumably, lungs.

The fact that the surface is unsealed means it's porous - which, for something that's meant to be in frequent contact with the floor and a sweaty human body, is pretty offputting. This thing is going to start looking and feeling gross pretty quick.

If you have eco-guilt, you're better off looking for a used plastic roller on craigslist than getting some faux-greenwashed product like this shipped to you from halfway across the country.

title: Great training robot
text:
Background:
- Previously purchased a [[ASIN:B016A7UMV8 iPong V300 Table Tennis Trainer Robot]] but decided an upgrade was necessary
- I've only used the V300 and the S9.
- I'm an average "garage" ping-pong player but hope to enter a competition for fun at some point.
- I use this as a training aid and for a workout
- I've been using the machine for 2 months.

Additional points to consider:
- It's difficult to tell, but the control panel is actually detachable (it's a separate unit and comes with a mounting bracket). The cord attaching the controller to the machine is long enough to allow you to mount the controller to the opposite (player) side of the table. This is really a necessary and nice feature.

Good:
- Fast (check out youtube videos, I don't anticipate ever "out-growing" this robot
- Consistent. You can set up multi-ball practice really easily and can expect consistent results
- Control/Customization. You can set up the machine in a number of custom ways (the user interface is a bit confusing though [more below])
- Reliable. I've put 500+ balls through each session and haven't had a single jam yet.

Could be better:
- The user interface could be improved. If you want to program the machine to produce a certain pattern it's probably possible but figuring out how to do it will take some time. I don't feel this reduces the start count as it doesn't affect performance, it just requires some time to get used to.

Final Comments: I really enjoy using this machine and find it to be an extremely useful training aid. Though I wouldn't have previously considered solo-ping pong a workout, I have been using the random mode and have been surprised at how serious a workout training with this machine can produce. There is a an option for limiting the number of balls or minutes for each session and I will occasionally use this to get a surprisingly intense workout in.

*(I purchased this robot from oukeiusa's web page and not directly from Amazon).

title: Abstract art gets its due in this sensational DVD
text:
Rarely does one have the opportunity to hear from abstract artists about the meaning of their lines, swaths, materials, and colors. Dr. Teck opens this marvelous tour through Jewish art of the high holidays with works by Peachy Levy, Barnett Newman, and Judy Chicago. Each work is explained in terms that impart the spiritual meaning of the artwork as it is shown on the screen. The narration is concise and understandable as example after example held my attention.

Suddenly there is a work about Genesis from the early 14th century. I felt the centuries melt away as the simplicity of the early work reflected the same effort as that of the abstract expressionists to depict the spiritual aspect of their lives. Dr. Teck continues to juxtapose Jewish art from different ages and styles in ways that provide deeper meaning to an impressive line-up of paintings and artifacts.

This hour-long DVD would be excellent for teaching children, adults, artists, art lovers, campers, senior citizens, anyone who is open to learning more about art. I especially hope it is presented to some adults who think they "don't like" abstract art. They may be surprised at what Barnett Newman has to say!

title: Wake up to the sun even on winter mornings!
text: I have owned other sunrise alarms, the last one made a buzzing sound when the light came on that was less than soothing and defeated the purpose of waking to the sunrise.  The Good Morning Sunrise clock makes a much smoother transition to waking up and all you hear is the alarm sound you choose.  I like the halogen bulb which definitely brightens my large bedroom on dark winter mornings when I am routinely up before the sun.  There is a nice variety of audible alarm sounds that increase in volume along with the increasing light.  I do wish the snooze button worked on both the light and the sound, instead of just the sound.  On other lamps I have owned, you could snooze both light and sound.  If the light/clock had more weight to it, the buttons would be easier to use.  The overall look of the clock is attractive and unobtrusive.  All in all, a good value and a much better way to start the day than a traditional buzzer style alarm clock or even one set to a radio station.

Cost, I feel like I should get a discount after buying a bottle or two

title: Worked good for me.
text:
Saw and read a few reviews. Wasn’t expecting much but decide to try it. I live in an area that is really dusty and hot (90-107) on average in the summer.
Typically a dark colored vehicle left outside will be visibly dusty the next day after washing it. I applied one coat to my dark grey truck and gave it a week.
Dust did not really become noticeable until the 4th or 5th day which may not sound like much, but that is a huge improvement.
Day 7 I simply rinsed the truck with water and dried it with a shammy. Looks as good as the day I washed it!!
The bugs easily came off the grill. I was happy with the results and applied a second coat. It really helps on the plastic trim. Makes it look like new and works better than Armorall, no greasy feeling or residue.

**Note: I applied this in the sun on a hot day. I noticed if it dries before I can buff it out it can leave streaks. I simply went over the area with the damp side of the towel and then buffed it out with the dry side. Worked every time. **

Not sure why it didn’t work for others, but worked great for me and replaced a lot of my other products saving me time.

title: so far, so good...
text:
I first learned about the Bodybugg while looking at the Costco website. I wondered what in the world it was and after I read a few reviews, I knew I wanted it! I read several reviews on the Costco website and tried to compare best as I could to the other GoWear Fit System by reading different internet reviews.

I think each item has as many positive as it does "doesn't work" reviews so I was confused which item to purchase so I decided to buy both.

Costco sent the Bodybugg in 2 days. I'm still waiting on Amazon's GoWearFit product so I can only review this Bodybugg. That said,the packaging was very simple to remove the device and the start up directions very straight-forward. It took about 10 minutes for me to find the usb port, hint! the black body snaps out of the arm band! And once I found the usb port, it took another hour or so to set up my profile. The website was easy enough to navigate for set up and my Bodybugg worked fine.

It takes 3 hours to fully charge. I love popping over to the computer and doing a quick synch to see where I am at the moment. This whole process takes about 3 minutes. I am able to record my food intake. The caloric intake is limited in that it is divided into a 6 meals, so if I have had my 6 meals, but decide to have a glass of milk before bed, I have to go back in and edit my 6th meal to add that milk. This is a slight extra step beyond the weightwatcher's website, but not a dealbreaker.

I have only done one workout while wearing this and it was spinning. I have read that the BB does not do a great job of tracking burned calories for cyclists, but I can't comment on that just yet.

There is a coaching session that comes with this item and my "coach" has been very diligent in trying to contact me to set up a time for us to have our 45 minute phone chat. I think I'd like to wear this for another few days before I chat with her so as to get to figure it out best I can on my own and then ask questions about things I don't understand.

I have not had any skin irritations and it is not a bother at all under long-sleeved shirts.

I have only used this for two days so it's silly to comment on my 2 pound weight loss, but I am optimistic that this is going to be a wonderful tool to take away that emotional aspect to eating. It really reduces weight-loss to a more clinical level of calories in vs. calories burned and I am hoping that will help me fight different cravings and binges!
Hope this helps!

title: Getting amazing results!
text:
I knew Dr. Turchin from when I lived in CA, and I have the utmost respect for him and his work. I had not seen him since 1996, but when I saw this affiliated with him, I figured it would be really good.
A nagging knee injury that would not heal was the impetus to order. I had suffered for months with it, only to have it flare up again when I tried to lift weights. I had trouble going upstairs, and could not lift weights. After only two treatments the knee pain was gone! It returned once, and with a couple more days of treatment, it disappeared and has not returned. I also used it on various old injuries, from years of martial arts and rock climbing, all with similar results. Some were gone overnight, and a couple of them took about 3 weeks to resolve. A few of the old injuries and pains were thirty years old, and all resolved. I've let numerous friends use it, and they've had similar results. Some issues seem to be permanently gone, and others take an occasional tune-up to keep me pain-free. The effects seem to be cumulative overall. My physical activity has increased as a result of the effects, and I'm back enjoying some of my favorite sports again!
One more thing, I had occasion to email Dr. Turchin and work with him on a customer relations issue. The customer service is top notch, and he responds quickly to any clinical questions. It's an excellent product and great service! Highly recommended.

title: Does what I need it to do.
text:
Most people will tell you that consistency is the most important part of any routine. Included in my "routine" are quarterly measurements of the areas on my body that concern me.

First and foremost, this device is not going to be precise to the 1/100th of an inch. It does, however, provide consistent measurements each and every time.

The best part : the self-tensioning mechanism. It always, without fail, puts the same amount of tension on the tape giving me accurate, repeatable results.

My advice is to formulate a plan to measure those body parts (quads, arms, chest, waist, hips, etc) that matter to you and find a way to measure them the SAME way the next time you use the device. Sure, you may have +/- a few pounds the next time, but if your tape placement strategy is sound, then you'll get consistent results that you can track over time.

I've used this device for approximately four years and logged my measurements through the years. It does what I need it to do. I am not a competitive body builder nor do I need to publish my measurements to any publication, so the measurements are good enough for me to track MY progress. I recommend it, its inexpensive and easy to use.

text:
This stuff smells good, cleans well, is a good size bottle, has wonderful list of organic ingredients, pretty label, and came with a towel. I love the mat I got from them in 2010 dearly and we have been through so much together -including a 200hr teacher training, daily yoga at studio for years (in addition to lots of hot yoga classes), and a move across the country from Colorado to the Midwest over a year ago. Being a native of dry air, I have no idea how to clean my yoga mat in this funky humid environment! In Denver I could soak and clean my mat and hang it up dry, and it would be good by the next day --- not here.. and it was developing a weird mold funk smell. I quit using it and thought I was going to have to through it out (and haven't found a new mat I like yet!)- but this stuff has saved the day. title: Accurate reviews for a good product
text:
I read a lot of reviews before purchasing this and I'm happy to write that the positive reviews were accurate.

I accidently ordered the 580A instead of the 980A, but decided not to return after reading that the low speed on the 980A was not very useful and few ever used it. The 580A gives off a mixed sound of static and fan sound and does an excellent job of blocking and minimizing the noise from the TV when my partner is in her office. I'm only about 20 feet away from her and with the door closed I can crank the TV up to over 17 on the volume meter. Way louder than I usually turn it up (12 or 13 is normal for me).

The only things it doesn't block well are distinctive noises, like talking on the phone, although I do have a rather loud and projecting voice.

I would definitely recommend this and will probably buy another one for the bedroom when one of us goes to bed while the TV is still on.

title: Buyer, use caution
text:
I recently purchased ReMag and have been using it for about a week. I was eager to buy it based off the reviews and what I read in The Magnesium Miracle. I did notice a difference in how I slept (I don't suffer from any sleep issues, but I noticed deeper sleep while taking it). I also feel a general sense of calm (I have had anxiety off and on, and I seem.to feel a bit better).

However, upon reading further reviews, someone mentioned that it may contain lead, to which I grew concerned. I don't remember the name of the reviewer, but it was one of the 1 star reviews on Amazon. Thry did not indicate what lab did the resting or how they came across the information, so I looked deeper into it.

I was able to find information on ConsumerLab.com, in which they independently tested multiple magnesium supplement brands. The information is copyright protected, so I won't share the details here, but you can pay for an account and receive the full report (and others).

Their findings did indicate there was lead contamination. I would recommend viewing the report so that you can judge for yourself as to whether or not you wish to continue taking the supplement.

I personally will not continue taking it as I would prefer to have a pure product with no contaminants (especially no lead).

I have found another that I will purchase instead – Nutricology Magnesium Chloride.

It sucks because I spent quite a lot of money on it, but there is no value on my health.

I give it 2 stars because it actually did seem to help, but I cannot give a full recommendation given the information I know now.

Follow the directions on the box unless you want maximum results then leave the tea bag in there! After I did my buisness it felt like there was nothing in my stomach I felt completely emptied. text:
It really is the height of poor customer service that a bathroom scale should result in such frustration. I have much more complex electronics that connect to my network with ease, yet I had to call my wifi service provider to change a setting because the requirements of this scale make it impossible to connect on your average settings. Finally, I was able to get it work connect back in July...for a few months. Today I went to use it, it weighed me, and then attempted to sync that data. I kept getting an x instead of a check mark. Their online help forums are a collection of frustrated customers (they don't appear to have a FAQ section with quick explanations about common issues) all explaining the same issues and with the occasional service rep providing links to another forum to a solution that may or may not work. After a couple hours going round and round, I called them only to have them offer to send me another one because it's clear the troubleshooting wasn't going to work. I don't want another scale to go through the same headache. This is supposed to be a benefit to my health, not add stress to my life.

title: and intelligent testing at ages 3 to 5
text:
For months I have been doing research on the benefits of Omega 3 fish oil and finally I had the opportunity to try it out. I have only been taking it for a few days but knowing the benefits is enough for me. The package arrived quickly and there was no damage at all. The bottle was completely sealed and safe. In the even that you weren't aware, I took the time to list the benefits of taking Omega 3.

1.Omega-3 benefits your heart health. An Italian study (GISSI)7 of 11,324 heart attack survivors found that patients supplementing with fish oils markedly reduced their risk of another heart attack, stroke, or death. In a separate study, 8 American medical researchers reported that men who consumed fish once or more every week had a 50 percent lower risk of dying from a sudden cardiac event than do men who eat fish less than once a month.
2.Omega-3 normalizes and regulates your cholesterol triglyceride levels. Compared to a statin, both fish oil and krill oil are more efficient in doing this. According to a study comparing the efficiency of krill and fish oils in reducing triglyceride levels,9 both oils notably reduced the enzyme activity that causes the liver to metabolize fat, but krill had a more pronounced effects, reducing liver triglycerides significantly more.
Fasting triglyceride levels are a powerful indication of your ability to have healthy lipid profiles, which can be indicative of your heart health.
Studies have also shown that omega-3 fats are anti-arrhythmic (preventing or counteracting cardiac arrhythmia), anti-thrombotic (prevents thrombosis or a blood clot within a blood vessel), anti-atherosclerotic (preventing fatty deposits and fibrosis of the inner layer of your arteries), and anti-inflammatory (counteracting inflammation – the heat, pain, swelling, etc).
3.DHA affects your child's learning and behavior. Do you want to maximize your child's intellectual potential? A study published in Plos One in June 201310 linked low levels of DHA with poorer reading, and memory and behavioral problems in healthy school-age children. In another study published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in August 2013,11 children who consumed an omega-3 fat supplement as infants scored higher on rule learning, vocabulary, and intelligent testing at ages 3 to 5.
Previous research also found that children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and related behavior or learning disabilities are more likely to have low omega-3 fat levels.
Omega-3 has such great impact on your brain health – EPA and DHA keep the dopamine levels in your brain high, increase neuronal growth in the frontal cortex of your brain, and increase cerebral circulation.
“Omega-3 has been found to save the lives of children going through short bowel syndrome (SBS)”4.Omega-3 has been found to save the lives of children going through short bowel syndrome (SBS), which is uncommon but impacts thousands of people in the United States. SBS can occur from birth (when a portion of the intestine fails to develop) or due to an infectious inflammatory disease striking premature newborns. In adults, it can be caused by surgery for Crohn's disease or injury.
Alarmed by the situation, Dr. Mark Puder, surgeon at Children's Hospital Boston,12 said that they knew most of the children with SBS were going to die. Then the physicians noted that when the kids were given the nutritional supplement Omegaven (made of fish oil), they began to improve drastically.
The fish oil treatment was given to 112 children at the hospital, where more than 90 percent of the children with SBS are still alive. There has been striking results that the fish oil supplement is also made available at 70 hospitals worldwide.

I received this product at a discounted rate for my honest review.

title: Cheap, no support. Do not use for sports!
text: I take exception to them mentioning athlete in their title. I bought this because it was the highest rated & cheap - you get what you pay for. The velcro straps are similar to the Ace Bandage Brand knee brace I bought (black with 3 straps)....there is no fuzzy complement for the velcro. It relies solely on the fabric of the brace. What occurs over time is the brace material wears down and soon, there is nothing for the velcro to grab. So down the road, the 3 straps break free or don't stick at all. Also, it's not a snug fit. The picture illustrates bubbling on the lower strap, which it what happens to me. The middle and top are fine; but, the bottom could use some tapering so that the brace is completely snug. I bought this for support of a torn meniscus, while I recover. These days, they sell ACE bandage type wraps, without the securing clips, relying solely on the tackiness. I wanted something that would last longer. This brace, while more substantial, doesn't offer the same support an ACE bandage would. Also, I would not use this solely for support while playing sports. This may do fine for walking; but anything above that, you could be in trouble. I've worn it all day at work (sit & walk) and it loosens. There is no lateral support and would not rely on this for knee support in any cutting sport (tennis, basketball, base/softball, etc.). This is a borderline Knee Brace/Wrap. I don't know what protection it offers. Like I said...cheap and you get what you pay for.

text: I had Lifestation for 4 years and did not need it.  One day I fell and hit the button, I lay on the floor bleeding and had to listen to the device tell me to push the button again if this was in error.  Then I got a machine telling me to hold for a representative.  I held and held.  Then I dialed 911 on my phone and just before the paramedics arrived someone answered.  They were impossible to understand, as the reception was poor.  A day or two later I called to express my concern for the service.  I talked to two people that were nice and very understanding, however they were not a supervisor.  The supervisor called me and had not sympathy or understanding at all.  She spent the time telling me that I could change the device and upgrade.  No way I was going to upgrade.  I told her that it was impossible for me to understand the rep because of interference.  She then then said that in my area the reception was poor.  I live in an area where everything else works just fine.  I would like to know why after 4 years they didn't tell me that the reception was poor.  I was paying them for good service and reception.  If you value your life and limb, do not under any circumstances use Lifestation

title: Good product, make sure it is right for you
text: Firts, this is a good product.  I don't want to say they are a poor product, but I want to caution people depending on their needs.  My masks were not being held tight enough to my face, so I got these to hopefully tighten them.  They work as advertised in terms of how they function, and I'm sure that there are a lot of people who it would work for.  The mechanism for attaching them to the ear loops is much better than I thought.  The little "button" that slides into the loop is attached to fabric, not a rigid material.  The result is that there is no problem attaching them to most any thickness of ear loop material.  However,for me, it was too long.  I adapted them to work by looping it around on ear loop and attaching it to the other ear loop, essentially cutting it in half.  It is adjustable, but the shortest length is still 5 1/2 inches long, which I may have missed in the description.  That is way too long for my purposes.  I think part of the reason is that my ear loops are elastic, and when stretched far enough, the distance between them is much shorter.  My advice, measure the distance between the loops when you pull them back far enough for you.  Elastic loops may give more than you think.

text:
I took the plunge and bought a Fitbit and decided to get the Aria scale as well. I was a little skeptical at first, I had never bought a scale that was so expensive but all of my cheap scales before this had broken and they were not digital. I loved the idea of this scale and for me has been wonderful.

First, I love not having to remember to track/write down what my results are because my free Fitbit profile will aromatically update. I don't weight myself often but I appreciate that I can track my weight since I have had this scale just by looking at my profile. I also love that it gives you a fat percent.

Second, this is an pretty scale, aesthetically pleasing with a minimalist look. It runs on batteries and surprisingly enough, I have hardly had to change them, but I do think that this scale might be a little better if the battery was rechargeable rather than batteries but the batteries don't bother me especially since the have lasted so long.

If you have a Fitbit, this could be a great tool for you to get to a weight loss goal, it is not necessary, but it is nice to have. So far I have had this scale for over 2 years and it has been great and I would totally recommend this to a friend.

title: First impressions of Vitargo S2
text:
So, this is my first use of Vitargo so I am not giving it 5 stars yet. I use it as a post-workout recovery supplement. Decided to give it a try after investigating the product from various sources such as Bodybuilding.com. The premise behind this product is that it is suppose to help rapidly restore the body's skeletal muscle glycogen levels that were depleted during vigorous exercise. Per the advertisement, it can also be used pre and intra workout but I find with a proper diet I can push hard in the weight room without it. I would rather use something like C4 or Jacked3D as a pre-workout. So what did I think?

I was a little concerned at first about bloating. After mixing it per the instructions and adding a scoop of BSN Clean Whey, this was a lot of liquid to consume (somewhere around 28 oz.) I am happy to report that my fear was unfounded and the claim of no bloating is true. I can also report that I did not experience any gas as reported by a few others. However, as with any other product, your results will most likely vary from mine. My body sucked it right in and my stomach fullness was gone in minutes. Almost all of it was pulled directly into my muscles and I experienced less post-workout fatigue immediately and the following day. So far I give it a thumbs up.

I found the product mixes well with water (I use a shaker cup). It does froth up which gives the appearance of there being more liquid than there actually is. If you follow the instructions, mixing should not be an issue. I use the tropical fruit flavor. The taste is tolerable which is a nice way of saying I would not drink it by choice but it is worth it for the benefits. This is of course personal preference and you might love or completely hate the flavor, texture, etc.. Stay Strong and Fight On.

Update 1: So...after about a month I can say I am sold on Vitargo and use it religiously three times a week post workout. All else being equal in my diet and workouts, I am seeing a noticeable improvement in my physique. They do recommend that you take a second serving after intense exercise of over 1.5 hours. I have not tried that yet but might as my recovery time has slowed down slightly. In the end, I think if you are serious into weight training and gaining muscularity you should consider adding this to your stack. If your goal is just to stay fit you could probably find better places to spend your money.

title: WORKS GREAT IN AIRBNB AND HOME HVAC - I now have THREE
text:
I purchased one of these as a test to see if I could brighten up the room smell in an Airbnb I operate in my home, which is popular and gets daily use. I always try to leave a pleasant scent via cleaning, but wanted something a bit more sophisticated. I saw a NYTimes article on scent marketing and started searching on Amazon for choices in an entry-level machine. My Airbnb suite is just 300 square feet, but has its own HVAC system. I purchased a tea/citrus scent from Aromatech after trying out their various samples (available for order on Amazon).

I've had the Kevinleo machine (sturdy and beautiful quality) set up and operating for about a month, and started with the lowest amount of scent spraying into the HVAC air return (which I installed by poking a hole in the HVAC return and setting up the machine in a bookcase in my my office, which is adjacent to the HVAC crawl space and Airbnb. Learning the buttons on the keypad is not a big deal to figure out. If you can the time on an alarm clock, you can set this scent machine operating times/hours/days. Lowest scent is 5 seconds on and 300 seconds off, which means it sprays scent for 5 seconds every 5 minutes. I set it to spray only during daytime hours when guests would be awake, figuring no one wants to be subjected to a scent while they're sleeping. This setting has been PERFECT and is just right, so every once in a while, you get a pleasant whiff of the tea/citrus scent. It isn't enough to really take notice that the place has a scent machine -- it's just a pleasant overall essence that's occasionally noticeable. As it should be, I think. Too much of a good thing is just that. I liked this machine so much that I bought another one for the bedroom level of my own house. After trying it out and setting it to scent for 24 hours a day, I can tell you that you DO NOT want to be smelling scent when you're sleeping. Also, for the Airbnb I bought the somewhat expensive Aromatech scent ($149 for 500ml or 16 oz= $9.31/oz). I'm trying out the White Tea reed diffuser scented oil in the rest of the house, which is $13.99 for 8 oz = $1.75oz. The less expensive oil works just as well and smells the same for less than a fifth of the cost of the other. Back to the Airbnb scent machine == it's been operating from 7 am to 10 pm since June 15, and scenting for 10 seconds on/300 seconds off, and when i check the oil bottle in the machine, it still looks nearly full. It appears I'll be able to go many months without having to refill. On a note to those who say "the machine doesn't work after a while," I HAVE occasionally set the scent output to a higher number of seconds -- like 20 on, 300 off -- just to make sure the machine occasionally is working long enough to ensure the tube from machine to hvac has some air pushed through it and avoids possible accumulation. Just a thought. I'm liking this all so much, I just bought a THIRD machine for the living room level of my home, and will stick to the less expensive white tea reed diffuser scent oil refill tea (the Westin Hotel-ish smell) as my scent. I hope this helps someone make their own decisions. Eric in LA

title: Amazing--best i have used
text:
I just moved into an apartment with a heavy traffic trail on a sand-colored, cut pile carpet. I did everything--baking soda and vinegar, a steam cleaning machine, and various brand-name carpet cleaning solutions. I got it looking better, but still not great. Carbona with a brush was on sale at Safeway so I bought it as a last resort. It's astounding. I started using it on spots/drips. They disappeared instantly. I couldn't believe it. Then I wondered if it would work on the carpet trail. So I did a two sq. ft area--massive improvement. I then went back and bought two more bottles of Carbona to do the rest. It took a while, not very long, and now the carpet really does look like new. Fresh and spotless. I am here to see if I can buy it in bulk on Amazon--apparently not.
PS, the secret is to let the solution sink in, fluff it up with a brush until it foams. 15 minutes later, go back and blot up all the excess solution with paper kitchen towels. The blotting is important. The stains will be gone, the carpet will look good – and it will look even better tomorrow when it's dry. The cost of Carbona + kitchen towels is much cheaper and more effective than a carpet cleaning machine. However, it is primarily intended for spots, not entire rooms.

title: Poor Quality Cost Me A Pair Of Riding Glasses. Don’t Waste Your Money.
text:
Pros:
2 cases for the typical cost of 1.
Semi-Rigid shell for better protection.
Fits larger sunglass frames.

Cons:
Products smelled HEAVILY of smoke when unpackaged.
Belt-clip fob stitching of VERY poor quality.

I bought these to replace a softshell case of similar design (different manufacturer), used to hold my off-pair of motorcycle riding glasses. I ride to work before sun up so, I ride in wearing a pair of yellow lensed glasses in the morning and carry a pair of glasses with smoked lenses for the ride home in the afternoon. I don’t have bags of any kind on my motorcycle and I don’t ride with a backpack so, I rely on using the clip of the sunglass case to attach the case to a D ring on the beltline of my work pants.

My initial impression of these cases was overall positive, except for the extremely pungent odor of smoke that permeated both cases and was immediately revealed upon opening of the zip-lock type baggy they come packaged in. Unfortunately, my initial assessment was quickly proven inaccurate when after only 3 days of use (riding to and from work), the first cases carry clip nearly tore completely off (see picture). Wanting to give these cases a fair shake and understanding that once in a while, flaws creep into a products manufacture, I wrote the first cases near immediate failure off to bad luck.

Unfortunately, my optimism was repaid with disastrous consequences when the second cases belt clip failed completely on the next day’s ride into work, costing me not just the case but, my other pair of riding glasses that were in the case when the fabric securing the case to the clip failed and the case was lost somewhere on the highway during that mornings ride to work. Please, save yourself the financial loss and frustration of losing your own glasses. DO NOT BUY THESE CASES.

title: Unequivocal Results
text:
I have been reading a lot of articles about betulinic acid. There is some very strong research that indicates that it can cause cancer cells to self initiate apoptosis, cell death. Betulinic acid is the active component of Chaga extract. That research prompted me to purchase this extract. Another thing that prompted me to try it was a mole like growth that popped up on my face about a year ago. It seemed to be getting bigger and my general sense of paranoia concerning cancer got me to thinking if the Chaga Extract would have any effect.

I think that I can say unequivocally that since I started taking the extract, the mole has almost disappeared. It started out about the size of a pencil eraser and is now just two small lumpy dots. That happened in just over a week. I wish that I had taken some before and afters because the result seems to dramatic.

I was pretty amazed. Everything that I can find about betulinic acid indicates that it is low in toxicity and works about as well as doxorubicin, especially in cancers that have a certain gene that confers resistance to doxorubicin. Doxorubicin is some pretty nasty stuff that is nicknamed red devil and red death because of it's high toxicity. It can permanently damage heart muscle. Based on what I read about the toxicity of betulinic acid, I have been taking 2 tsps per day at night. That's about 16 times the dosage on the bottle. I did that because in my judgement, it is better to take a higher dose over a short period of time than a lower dose over a longer period.

title: What a Sight
text:
I've used natural spectrum lights for several years, and I prefer them to other types of simple, inexpensive floor lamps. I like both the lighting and the flexibility they provide.

My purchase this time came after the fourth such lamp failed, in each case after a few years of use. I'm satisfied with their longevity, but I can't compare with Verilux because this will be my first time using it.

I chose Verilux because of what other reviewers said, but I also liked the images shown. All four of my other lamps were from the same, different company. The Verilux lamps cost a little more than the others, but not much more.

Both lamps are easy to assemble, and they look almost identical. However, although they both weigh about the same and the bases are similar, Verilux seems to have a more solid feel and its sections seem to snap together more securely. The light cast by Verilux seems a little brighter, but at the same time it seems diffused a light differently so there's less glare. (The others didn't really have a lot of glare either.)

If the measure of a purchase is that it meets expectations, then these Verilux lamps fully measure up. I'm very satisfied with them. They do what they're supposed to do and what they claim to do; they're unobtrusive but nice looking; they're simple and inexpensive; the lights last a long time and are easy to replace. (Replacement lights cost about $30 +/-). Should the need arise I would buy the same type, and even the same brand, again.

Now the FYI part...I genuinely never considered the fact that you could have an allergic reaction to a supplement...until I had one. That being said, I have notoriously horrible allergies and I've had severe reactions to random things before; a supplement was just not something I considered as a thing we could be allergic to.

The manufacturer and amazon were fantastic about doing a return because of my reaction and I honestly tried them again after my first reaction because of how much I wanted them to work. I think it's a great product, just be aware that allergic reactions to supplements (in general) are possible.

title: Horrible watch
text:
Bought this thing a few years back and it didn't last long at all. It worked for about 6 months, just a handful of regattas on a 30' sailboat. One race it randomly was resetting and I couldn't understand why. Come to find out, if I lightly bumped it--happens often while sailing--it caused it to reset. By the time this happened, it was out of warranty period (of course).

Having a watch dedicated to sailing which reset itself during the intense period of a regatta start was unacceptable, so I carefully sat it on a shelf and resigned myself to buying a different watch. When I came back to this watch a year later deciding I should finally throw it in the garbage where it belonged, I touched the buttons. When I did this, it froze. None of the buttons would do anything. Banging it on something wouldn't reset it... Instead, it would lightly beep about every 1 minute. This was annoying as all hell, so that hastened my speed with chucking it in the trash.

No more Ronstan for me. I now have had my Garmin watch with a Sailing IQ App (developed by a user) that works great. Good thing is my Garmin can be used for other sports in addition to sailing. Been going strong for 3 years now.

title: Much better than without, but . . .
text:
I've owned three Canon G series cameras. G11, G12 and G15. Every one of them has ended up with a badly scratched front element. It's a design flaw that is just a fact of life on these otherwise excellent cameras. I recently had the G15 repaired and decided to put this adapter kit on to protect the front element from stray dust, etc that those lens "doors" eventually drag across the face of the front lens element.
Problem numero uno.
Installation was straightforward but there are two minor (and not totally unexpected) downsides to this adapter. WIthin a few days of installation the adhesive for the adapter let loose. If you look at the Lensmate site they sell extra precut adhesive replacement for $1 plus shipping. I can see why. Why not just include an extra one with the original purchase?
Problem two. If you use the onboard flash at all at the 28mm setting the adapter and attached 52mm filter block part of the flash output and the result is a shadow at the bottom right hand side of the exposure. Most people don't shoot full frame so it probably wouldn't be much of an issue and can easily be cropped. But for pros that use this camera as a backup to their heavy DSLRs and expect to have a fill flash that covers the entire full wide angle frame this is an issue (see attached photo).
Overall, this is a very good resolution to a Canon design flaw with the G series cameras, but you might as well order a couple extra adhesives because you're gonna need them.

title: I Love Clear Flow
text:
I had been using another water purifier in my kitchen, but was having trouble changing the filters every 2-3 months. I have arthritis in my hands and almost always had to ask someone to do it for me. Plus the cost of the replacement filter was almost as much as the unit itself.

When I found Clear Flow I decided to try it. The ad says it should last a year before the unit needs to be replaced. I've only had it a month, so don't know about that yet. But I do know I will never use a different purifier again.

It was so easy to install I could do it myself. The knurled ring that attaches to the faucet is easy to grip and only needs to be turned finger-tight. The unit is small and doesn't interfere with using the sink. The water tastes delicious, like real water. And I have water so bad you can smell it when it comes out of the faucet unpurified.

It is disposable, but there is only one unit to throw away each year instead of the four or five filters from my previous unit.

I strongly recommend Clear Flow, expecially for someone like me -- older and with not much mechanical skill. And if you have arthritis, like I do, you can do it yourself.

title: Love this creamer!!
text:
I LOVE this Collagen Creamer. I have tried all three flavors, and I prefer the Vanilla and Coconut. The Gingerbread has a little too much spice flavor for me. The Vanilla and Gingerbread do have a bit of a grainy texture to them, which isn’t a big deal to me. You just need to swirl or stir your coffee up as you near the bottom of the cup.
The Coconut has the smoothest texture and since I use coconut milk in my coffee too, it pairs really well.
I read some reviews where people don’t like the “clumps”. This is really easy to fix. I have a handheld milk frother ($15 on Amazon) and I’ll put the scoop of collagen creamer into my cup, then pour a little hot coffee over it and use the frother to mix it well, then pour in the rest of the cup. I do add a little coconut milk in addition to the collagen creamer. I look forward to it every morning.
I also read reviews that the regular Collagen Peptide powder is, “basically the same thing”. I do not agree at all. I have the regular Collagen Peptides as well and there is a very distinct flavor to it that I can taste in my coffee and I don’t like it. I use the Collagen Peptides in my smoothies or protein shakes and it’s great. The creamer is specifically made for coffee and it’s delicious that way. I’ve seen a huge difference in my hair, skin, and nails since using these products! They can be a bit pricey, but for the amazing quality and the results that I’ve felt and seen, I will continue to use them!

title: Its great, but be careful
text:
The device works, and I have seen things flashing in my dreams because of it, which I hope to realize as a dreamsign so that I become lucid. It does what It is supposed to do.

Here is my problem with it. The second or third day of having it, the lcd screen became too dark to read until I push a button that changes what is being displayed upon the release of the button. I kind of know my way around it, so it is still useable. I think this may have been caused by me rolling on it in my sleep, or maybe something snagged while I put it in the dream mask.

Now another problem I have with it is that the circuit board has no protective case. This could be the cause of how the lcd screen now looks the way it does. But it could possibly be a low battery life. Either way, that circuit board is just exposed, and it needs to be taken in and out of the mask. The mask can catch one of the components attatched to the board. I may not be gentle with it in my sleep, I have broken things in my sleep in the past. $209 is a lot to spend on something to wear in my sleep.

In an effort to make sure I do not remove the mask in my sleep, I tied my hands to my pants. When I woke up, the mask was off and my hands were free. Of coarse, I knew how to free my hands since I am the one that tied them, I just figured I would have to wake up to do something that required some mental work.

The strap also hurts between the top of my ears and my skull. I figure I will naturally get used to that though.

Any way, the device itself works great. I would give it 5 stars if it had even a cheap plastic or metal case to help keep from damaging it during sleep and while pulling it in and out of the mask to adjust settings/change batteries. I understand that the price is high because the demand for lucid dream devices is not for a very large market, and this brand seems to be the most reliable because of the eye tracking sensor.

Don't let the negative feedback I gave stop you from getting it. It still looks like the best available as far as I have been able to find. But if you move around in your sleep, or want to be sure not to damage it from pulling it in/out of the mask, you should look into making a small case for it either out of cardboard, or 3d print one, or find someone that will 3d prind one for you, or maybe even hot glue some popsicle sticks together and drill some holes in for the buttons and screen, along with lining the inside with that same type of fabric as the insert of the mask to keep the wood from scratching the device.

It is a great device for what it is. 4 stars because I have to craft a protective case for it, and because the lcd screen MAY be messed up.

I decided to upgrade my old razor last month and landed here. I searched and sorted my options, the money didn’t matter as long as it had the stars(and more than a handful of reviews). I was surprised to see this had a low price and so many good reviews.

It has a small assortment of attachments besides the shaver. A precision clipper attachment to shave long hair, nose hair trimmer, and a rubber facial exfoliating attachment. It charges via usb cable, which is included, but you need to provide your own wall plug.

It gave a very comfortable, smooth shave with no irritation to my head and neck, and minor irritation to my throat. Mind you, I did not use any creams or gels before I used it. title: I have hashi's and I like what it's doing for me so far
text:
I have been diagnosed with hashimotos thyroidism since I was 15 years old. I have been on synthroid for most of that time and when I hit my upper 20's I started really noticing that my thyroid was slowing down. I felt sluggish most of the time, I gained weight even though I wasn't eating any differently, my period was really heavy, water retention, brain fog mood swings, and all that great stuff that comes a long with having a thyroid condition. I talked my dr into switching my to Armor which did do a little better but I was still experiencing some difficulties with tiredness and water retention. I was losing weight at a very slow pace.
Well, I was given the chance to try this natural product and I have been using it almost 2 weeks now. It has no taste when I mix it with water. What I do is a get an empty 2 quart jug and fill it almost halfway full of water and put 10 drops into it. I drink most of it at once and then the rest later throughout the day. I do notice a difference in it once it gets built up in your system after a few days. I notice I have more energy and I do not retain nearly as much water and my stomach finally is starting to look flat again. The brain fog is a lot less frequent too. I cannot wait till I have been taking this for more time, and I will update the results. I do think that this will last you a while and is worth it. I have actually not been taking my thyroid medicine for about a week to see if I could just switch to an alternative medicine. I am really considering it if it keeps giving me these results. I have also been taking a vitamin pill geared toward thyroid patients. I have just been really frustrated these past few years about what my body is doing, and it seems the synthroid absolutely doesn't help and the armor just helps some. So far this solution is winning for me. I received this at a discount for my honest and unbiased review.

title: Easy and fast to make. Easy and fast to clean.
text:
Reading about Soylent online, you hear a lot of people describe the taste, but you'll never be truly prepared until you try it yourself. This is one of the most neutral tastes I've had in my life, and I see that as a good things. If I've been working long hours and I'm too tired to cook, this is the perfect solution, because it's so easy to drink regardless of whether or not you have an appetite.

In my opinion, this tastes a bit like a bowl of milk after you've had Cheerios or Kix. It's a very slight taste, and it tastes exactly the same as it smells. I make mine by mixing the powder with water and shaking it up in my shaker bottle. It only starts to stick to the sides of the bottles if you've let it sit for too long, but even then, it isn't hard to clean off.

The label on the jug recommends that you drink this cold, but I prefer it at room temperature. Sometimes I'll throw in some instant coffee or peanut butter powder just to shake things up. A lot of people choose to buy the prepackaged bottles for convenience, but this is almost as fast and much cheaper. I would say get the powder rather than the bottles unless you're extremely pressed for time.

title: Don't Be Discouraged
text:
I'll start with my actual review and then get into the real purpose of me writing this review afterward. This is high quality real deal sea moss, straight from the ocean. This is my first time purchasing/trying sea moss and can tell how good it is already, based on what I've learned through others. I received my product in a nice resealable package that burst with the essence of the ocean when I opened it. I rinsed it in the sink and then proceeded to soak it in purified water with a squeezed lemon (didn't have any lime around). The next day, I checked on it and it certainly grew in size. I was at first discouraged by what one guide to making the gel said: that the moss should be soft and gelatin-like and break apart in your hand. Mine was still pretty sturdy, but was certainly soft to the touch, like you'd expect a soaked vegetable to feel. I proceeded to push forward regardless as I realized beforehand that there is some level of almost "elitism" it feels like, in terms of what sea moss should and shouldn't be. I threw it in the blender and poured in the water I had it soaking in til I felt it was at a similar level to the guide I was following and got ta' blendin'. After a couple minutes, I turned it off and checked it out. The consistency was all wrong, like water but with a bunch of ramen noodles floating around. So I kept on blending and it thickened up to a grainy texture relatively quickly. I noticed it was only blending the bottom portion of the moss, the top half was sitting there like a still lake and all the reviews questioning the quality of the product started to flash before my eyes as I started to agree with them. But then I put on my thinking cap and added more water, shook it up a bit to get the water down there, and started the blender again. It all started flowing like a whirlpool once again and after a minute or so, I saw that creamy yellow consistency I was looking for. I added a tad more water and blended further after that to try and get rid of the tiny bits of grain left in my otherwise perfectly smooth gel, which I was successful at. Now I'm left with some beautifully smooth and nutritious sea moss gel. When they say a little goes a long way, they weren't kidding. I took maybe an ounce or so of my 8 ounce bag and it made 3 cups of sea moss gel. This makes me much more comfortable shelling out more money for multicolored/strained sea moss so I can explore how those benefit me in contrast to this classic golden moss.

I wrote this review because so many other reviews made me doubt my purchase and question whether I made the right choice, but in the end I was left extremely happy with my purchase. Ignore the reviews that question the authenticity and/or quality of this product. "It looks like noodles" it's supposed to. No two plants grow exactly alike. There are many many different strains of sea moss. "It's grainy, this is plastic!" Try adding more water and blending more and watch how quickly that "plastic" melts away. Any further doubts, you should direct yourself to their YouTube channel and you can see the source itself. This is a great company with great product at a great price. Nothing but greatness here.

title: Simple "To the point" Review - Pro's & Con's
text:
I really like this pill holder and I plan to keep it. I will try to make this as simple as possible.

Pros:
1. Stainless steel - Strong & resistant to staining from contact to water. In my opinion, stainless steel stain's "less" but it is not 100% resistant to staining.
2. Well made - This container seems impossible to break.
3. It has been designed so that you cannot over tighten and crush the gasket. *Well thought out.

Cons:
1. Lower chamber is hard to open. This is not an issue for me but it may be for an elderly person or I suppose anyone, depending on their hand strength. This is not a quality issue; it simply tightens so well because of precise machining and the surface is smooth so your fingers tend to slide along the curve. Upper chamber opens more easily because you can grab onto the hoop.
2. The hoop (ring) has a bit of a gap in-between the ringed layers.
3. Heavy & Bulky - It is a bit bulky but this is the size that I needed so it is what it is. There are smaller sizes available. It is also a little heavy but let's face it, this thing is very small; if weight is an issue for you, I would go for the titanium which weighs roughly half and it is just as strong, if not stronger, depending on what grade of metal is being used. Titanium is more costly. You can also get titanium in different colors; they can get titanium to change to certain colors through a heating process.

text:
Holy hell, these things suck. I get that the needles (given their unique construction) may need slightly different steel, but the steel they used has the consistency of licorice. The thread they include in the set is like something out of George Orwell's 1984 in its inferior quality, they throw in a pair of cheap scissors that redefine cheap, and then package it inside a blister pack that adeptly ignores the one question that the inventor should have asked himself. (Yes, it has to be a him, no woman could have allowed these things to go to market without the misery of the product haunting her dreams.)

What he should have asked himself ... "do they work"?

No. They do not work. They're miserable. I bought a few of them thinking they could possibly have value for older people, but it seems the only value these things have is demonstrate, finally, that products need not work to sell, they only need a convincing image.

I have cheapened my own life by writing this review and by using them. There is nothing redeeming about these needles. They are miserable.

I have had life-threatening food allergies for my entire life, and have always needed to carry antihistamines with me at all times (plus an EpiPen). I did have one issue that was brilliantly resolved by the company: a diphenhydramine tablet broke in the top chamber of my holder, and that chamber then developed some rust inside. After contacting the company, they sent me a brand new titanium top chamber and lid that that they said would be more corrosion-resistant – along with an entire new top AND bottom holder (with lid) in stainless steel. They even shipped it overseas for free, as I'd moved out if the US since the original purchase!

Now that I have three chambers, I think the product is even better. I carry three different medications with me at all times, and don't even know they are there (until I need them, that is).

I wholeheartedly recommend this product, and the company that produces it.

title: Easy To Use, Very Detailed Results
text:
I had been looking for a water test kit for quite some time, and was so happy to find such a comprehensive test.

--> Pros:

- Dead simple, in fact I had this sitting on the kitchen counter for weeks because I thought it would be difficult -- it was nothing more than pouring wanted into a couple of containers, sealing them up and shipping them off with a pre-paid label

- Tests for everything under the sun!

- Also has a bacteria test that you perform yourself

- They email you a comprehensive report once the results are processed where you can look up all the ingredients or contaminants to learn more about what is in your water that might be harmful

--> Cons:

- Cost -- obviously this is not a cheap test, but if you care about your water, you owe it to yourself

- The PDF file that they sent and the website are a little hard to follow. Especially when clicking on the PDF to get more info on the website leads to sometimes ambiguous or hard to understand terminology or descriptions, and their user interface is not good, so it took me a while to figure out how to get a deeper understanding of the potential contaminant level of something or what it even meant.

They could use a UI/UX refresh on their website

--> Overall: A great value for the money, comprehensive, easy to implement test that tells you all the potentially harmful things that can be in your water. Aside from a glitchy website, all the information you need is right there.

title: A Decent Addition
text:
I've read a number of studies on the efficacy of Inositol in treating mental health disorders, such as GAD and OCD.

The dosages used in those studies ranged from between 12 and 18 grams per day, and so I began to take 16 grams daily divided into two 8 gram administrations - one in the morning and one in the early afternoon.

I used to take gabapentin (Neurontin) off-label for Mood Disorder NOS. Essentially, I used Neurontin as a 'mood stabilizer.' And this effect, in fact, was strikingly similar to that produced by my a Inositol regimen. I must say that I was both surprised and pleased!

Treatment with Inositol takes patience to feel palpable results, and yet when they *are* felt, the weeks endured suddenly appear to be fleeting fancies.

To qualify myself, I definitely am feeling less.... Let's say, 'antsy' inside. I do not feel the urge to move about constantly to engage in meaningless tasks that later leave me tired and unmotivated. I have also noticed that I don't get as wrapped up in social exchanges as I used to. I am far more relaxed when I speak to others, which I feel has improved my communication skills.

Inositol's effects appear, in my experience, to synergize well with those of Taurine, and I recommend their co-administration whole-heartedly.

I am always impressed with LiftMode products' utility, portion, presentation, purity, shipping and communication, and Inositol did not part from this paradigm.

I highly recommend it.

title: Kitchen gadgets anonymous.
text:
It happens every few months that I cave in to the little merry maid on my back and buy something touted as being 'revolutionary' for storage. I believe it has to do with the happy-dancing-singing-frolicking-"I can't believe how much better my life is now that I have a place for all of my crab dip"-type advertisements that inundate my subconscious when I fall asleep in front of the tv in the "paid presentation" hours of the morning. But I digress.

Colors are good. The idea has merit. The execution, however, could use some massaging.

My first issue: The carousel system is chintzy. In particular, the container supports. I almost sheered a couple off in my methodical scramble to assemble it and have a better life.

My second issue: The container caps don't really fit into the alotted slot. Perhaps I was misinterpreting the diagram that showed them fitting into their container stall. Maybe they just sent me a rowdy bunch of non-conformists. I'm not sure. But they just don't seem to be happy fitting in where they should.

My third issue: I almost poked an eye out when the "flip-out" function deployed unexpectedly and caught me by surprise. While I was putting it in my cabinet and anticipating all of the happiness my impending purchase would bring to me, the containers shifted and attacked me. Be wary. They're wiley.

All-in-all, the idea is pretty good. Maybe it just takes more than colored, spinnning, plastic containers to bring true bliss to my life.

My display stopped timing after the first day, and the difficulty gauge doesn't seem to do anything.

So why did I keep it instead of returning it? Because with my attach-it-to-the-chair-you're-sitting-in trick, and pedaling fast, I got my heart rate up to about 135 beats a minute for half an hour - that's in my target heart zone. We have a small house, it's tough for me to leave my very high-maintenance family for long enough to go to a gym, and the weather in Chicago often prevents me from regular bike rides. At least I get a legitimate aerobic half-hour in with this thing.

title: Some sizing information
text:
Nice and low cut for those who can pull it off. I ordered 2 sizes to see which would fit better. I am normally a size Medium/32 inch waist in American pants/jeans/underwear. The thing to keep in mind is that the waist measurement is really more like a hip measurement since these trunks sit a few inches lower than the waist. The following are measurements taken with a ruler, straight out of the package and laid flat on a table.
L: Waist=28.5 inches, and the side stripe height=5.50 inches.
XL: Waist=31 inches, and the side stripe height=5.75 inches.
When worn, these will stretch to larger sizes due to the elastic waist band of course. And even though the side heights are similar, when worn, the dip below the belly button in the front is about 1/2inch shorter in the L, compared to the XL. As another person said, both fit fine for a someone who is normally a Medium. But the elastic waistband in the L will be tighter and maybe a tiny bit uncomfortable over time, leading to imprints in your skin. The XL will feel nicer during longer wear, but will look a little less skimpy.
