title: Upgrade and support issues
text:
I've purchased all the basic programs from The Wild Divine Project, and I've found them to be very helpful in developing useful biofeedback skills. Unfortunately, this company that creates expensive "enlightenment" software often disappoints me with their unenlightened business practices and unenlightened product support.

For example, they don't exactly make it obvious that there are no new biofeedback scenarios in the repackaged set sold as Relaxing Rhythms (formerly Healing Rhythms). It's all old graphics, albeit with an attractive new navigational interface, interspersed with some thoughtful discussion from well-known gurus. I'll bet many buyers were as disappointed as I was, to find out they'd been sold the same graphics twice. It's an old trick but I didn't see it coming from this company.

As another example, Wild Divine is currently (October 2010) selling only the XP/Vista version of their software for PCs, even on their Web site, though they have upgrades for Windows 7. Those upgrades will cost you an extra 20 bucks (each), but Wild Divine doesn't tell you that up front. (Why charge once when you can charge twice?) Again, an old trick, but I didn't expect it from this company.

I've also been disappointed with their product support. Their online information seems poorly organized, poorly communicated and incomplete. Some of their software still has annoying bugs that should have been patched out years ago. If you attempt to contact their tech support, don't hold your breath waiting for a reply. You may or may not get a response.

So yes, I still recommend this software, but it's ironic that the business practices of the maker are so out of sync with the intentions of their product. Be prepared for some frustration.

title: I LOVE this product!!!!!!!!!!
text:
This is my new favorite raw food ingredient. It has a very neutral flavor and ROCKS when it's used for thickening raw ingredients. So far I have added it to almond milk to make vanilla mousse with strawberries, to mangos to make a pudding and to coconut milk to make whipped topping.

It comes dry and sandy, so I rinsed it WELL and soaked it over night. Then I chopped it and add the moss and the soaking water to the blender. I let blended moss set over night in the frig, it makes about 4-5 times what I started with. The resulting product was VERY firm and dense. I used this mixture in the recipes I created. A little goes a LONG way. One of the things I was concerned about was if citric fruits would cause the gel to break down as citruses soften and tenderize. I've left it mixed with the mango and strawberries up to 48 hours with no issues, nothing has lasted longer than this w/o being eaten :) It has opened a new and exciting way to create goodies! These are the reasons I love it my recipes.

Irish it is one of the super foods as well. Irish moss is now thought to contain 15 of the 18 essential elements that make up the human body. I have not had enough time to tell you if I can see the health benefits listed for Irish Moss, but I already eat sea vegetable, algae, and wheat grass. title: Button or Mushroom-shaped nosepads that don't fall off as easily
text:
For years, I've tried different replacement nose pads for a favorite pair of lightweight, semi-rimless eyeglasses because the replacement pads have all fallen off so easily.

The ones I first got from Hermes / GroupMedicalSupply (GMS) were considerably less flimsy, more solid (almost plush in feel), with no hard angles and they actually fit well, so the first pair I took out were still secure in the frame's pad slots for a long time and I was not constantly trying to find out where one fell, as I had been doing with the others I'd bought through the years..

Well made, they're reasonably priced too.

HOWEVER, the last batch I got has, unfortunately, a smaller insert piece now, so these don't stay in as securely as the ones from the first batch I bought. They're still better than the ones I'd tried before. So I lowered the rating by only one star.

CAUTION - While these are called *"push-in"* via this maker/vendor on the PRODUCT page, many vendors (and even this vendor) refer to this type as *"slide-in"* pads on the package's labels. If buying from Goup Medical Supply LLC Shop aka GroupMedicalShop, you need to write them on their shop page to make sure they send GMS 22309 "9mm/Slide-in/Round" -- otherwise they send the rectangular-slot-in's despite the photo on this page (which has round ones).

The terms don't seem uniformly used by the various distributors of nose pads. "Button mushroom" best describes the shape though. I clicked on Push-in type when viewing the options because the picture matched what my eyeglasses need, but the little packages I received are labeled "Slide-in."

Even living in an urban area, I found that most stores (even very large ones) selling eyeglasses don't keep this type in stock.

While not designated 'Prime' with the colorful Amazon Prime icon, the text for the product states that 2-day shipping is free for "Prime members" and that's what I got.

(Edited Feb 5, 2016 to add more label information on the packages matching this photo.)

The mouth hole is pretty big, I have a hard time making a seal, I don't have a very big mouth.

The area between the mouth hole and the filter is 1.25" with a diameter of 2.5" - it's a pretty large area, so when you exhale through it, once you get to the end of the exhale and sit it down, the volume of that area is still full of unfiltered smoke that sort of drifts out and is still enough to smell. I have tried to take hits where I inhale the smoke and then remember to inhale regular air afterward, so that when I blow through it, the last of my exhale is just air, but it doesn't seem to work that way, it all blends together inside your lungs.

I didn't have these issues with the Smokebuddy Junior. The empty area outside the filter was much smaller and so was the mouth hole.

So I spent more on this one but use it less. Should have stuck to the smaller one.

text: I bought this to wake me up in the morning, so I can't talk to how it works as a desk lamp. It's a nice bright light, so I don't see that there would be any problems. As a morning alarm, it is a very bright light and it can be positioned so it is right over your face, which are both good thing. The one downside that I have found is that the light will turn itself off after a certain amount of time. If you have the alarm set for 6, for example, at 5:30 the light will come on, gradually getting brighter and brighter until it hits full strength at 6. Then at 6:30, it will go out completely. This might not be a problem if you are a lighter sleeper, but I sleep very heavily and half an hour is not long enough to wake me. I have been using this in conjunction with my existing alarm, rather than instead of as I was hoping. That works quite well, and I wake up less groggy and dragging with the light than I ever did without. Overall, it isn't perfect, but I'm still very satisfied with this product.

These leg irons are solid, heavy, and come with instructions on how to lock and unlock them. They're packed in a plastic bag in a small cardboard box, and they are already oiled/lubricated so they go on and off smoothly. The instructions explain how to engage/disengage this feature.
I ordered these leg irons as part of a gift for a friend. He's getting a metal case to keep his collectable cards in and these so he can handcuff himself to said case (the Blues Brothers carried their microphone around like this, which is what gave me the idea). Kind of a joke gift, but he still needed some way to carry and secure the cards, so this is a functional gift in a sense too. These leg irons were a better buy than most handcuffs I looked at for this purpose, because they give you more chain between the cuffs, which makes it more comfortable to handcuff oneself to a metal briefcase. title: A low budget DIY Holter Monitor
text:
I bought this because I was recently diagnosed with ventricular tachycardia with exercise. I got an ICD implant and am on beta blockers. The BB should keep the VT arrhythmias down, but there is no real good way to know they are working in the wild, especially with months between stress test check-ups.

I am happy to report that this cheap Chinese ECG is working well for me and is giving me the readings I want. I bought new 3M electrode pads (recommendation below) and electrode gel. I don't think this product is for quick casual use, although it can be. I set it up with the electrodes on my chest, do light exercise for 45 minutes, and then looks at the results for anomalies. I use the "lead I" measurement with three leads on my chest (see manual appendix 1 #3). This is giving me a reliable Lead 1 reading. The software is not going to win any awards and it only works in Windows, but it is surprisingly better than I expected. I have hill walks that have lasted hours and it finds all the anomalies for me after importing the data into the computer. I can zoom in to the anomalies and print out ECG strips for my cardiologist. As others have said, read the manual and practice importing to the software. It does work well with patience. I got mine for $165 from another source, but I got the electrodes and gel from amazon. That seems to be the going price.

title: Works wonderfully well.
text:
We had a bathroom remodel back in 2020. And after about 6 months, a couple of tiles started shifting and breaking out the grout. This resulted in the tile coming a bit loose. I pulled the time and replaces the mastic, reseated it, allowed to dry and then re-grouted… about 8 months later the same issue with the tile flexing and popping upstarted. I decided to try Fix a Tile instead of going through the entire process again. While the recommendation is to drill a couple pilot holes in the grout, I decided to dremel out all of the grout to ensure the best fill possibilities for the Fix a Tile. I also purchased a syringe kit for this.

The description is exact. The product is the consistency of Elmer’s glue. I used the syringe to inject the product into the grout lines and it wicked under the tiles in the problem areas. I used a bout an1”x3” syringe full for the areas. I then weighted the tiles. 24 hours later the floor felt more solid than when it was installed in 2020. I re-grouted the floor and it had been wonderful ever since.

I wish I would have gone with Fix a Tile the first time I repaired the floor.

I have to say this is the best double electric breast pump out there in the market.
Let me explain why.

My wife had tried various breast pump from different brands and types. She tried double electric pump from Medela, the famous one, single manual pump from Philips Avent as well as the double electric one. Every time the pump arrive, our excitement that we fought finally there is a good pump to express milk ended in disappointment because after 2-3 times use, my wife always feels pain. Until she found Dr. Brown's Double Electric Breast Pump, which we took a bet to purchase it because it is quite expensive and more over, there's no support available in Singapore.

And it paid off. Yes, the pump is slower to express milk compared to others she had tried before. But this one doesn't cause any pain. It's so smooth. Yes, the parts to assemble the pump is quite tedious and it contains 6 different parts to assemble 1 pump, but those many parts are for the smoothness that the pump is meant for.

The only down side is that the top part of the bottle which is used to connect to the "pipe" to the electric pump is very tough to be assembled. One morning, I pushed to hard and it caused a small part broken. As I said, there's no support in Singapore where we live. So I contacted the customer service via online contact page and that night someone replied and she immediately arranged a replacement parts. The best part is that the replacement are free and they even ship to Singapore, all for free, no charge at all. And furthermore, they didn't just ship the broken part, but instead they shipped the whole parts that assemble the bottle complete 2 sets. So it's like receiving the entire new set except the electric part. What a great after sales service.

This book features recipes from the central region of Umbria, a land known for its magnificent art, charming hill towns, gentle landscape, and fantastic food. Letizia's recipes are mostly simple, non-pretentious, authentic, and delicious. They are organized by season, which reflects a culinary tradition that is based on seasonal, local ingredients. The book is greatly enhanced by the inclusion of short essays on Italian food culture and spectacular photos.

This is a "must-have" book for anyone wanting to experience authentic central Italian food! It also makes a wonderful gift for anyone interested in cooking and Italian culture.

-Setup was a challenging at first, but after submitting a ticket to Customer Support, I was able to sync the device to my phone/app quickly. My ticket was answered quickly (within a couple of hours, at most).
-The app itself is pretty basic, feature-wise, but easy to navigate and keeps a log of your sessions; hopefully more will be added over time and the device can connect to other apps like Apple Health, etc.
-The fit of the device is a little awkward, but not a non-starter.

title: A stoner essential
text:
Anyone who uses cannabis for medical (like me) or recreational purposes knows how gross glassware gets and how difficult to clean. RezBlock simplifies this greatly. Just 8 or so drops in the water of my medium-sized bong keeps all parts in contact with the water resin free. All you do is rinse with hot water and the glass is clean! No need for brushes or pipe cleaners that are impossible to bend to reach all surfaces, no need for abrasives and shaking with breakage risk. I sometimes finish by swishing around an ounce or so of isopropyl alcohol to sanitize, but nowhere near the volume needed for the traditional soak & scrub.

RezBlock is nontoxic and organic, but the latter means that, to avoid microbial growth, you should change the water fairly often (which you should do anyway if you appreciate good weed). It colors the water a pale orange. I have not noticed any impacts on taste or aroma.

Do note that you still have to clean the bowl and the part of the downstem above the waterline the old fashioned way: isopropyl & pipe cleaners.

RezBlock was a game-changer for me. It significantly made bong cleaning less odious and has thus induced me to clean it more often for a healthier, tastier experience.

title: Gluten Ease greatly reduces discomfort from eating wheat products
text:
I first found out about Gluten Ease when I encountered it in a natural foods store back in 2006. I immediately bought a bottle to try, and was pleasantly surprised that it works.

I have never been diagnosed with celiac disease or gluten intolerance but I am pretty sure that I don't tolerate wheat products well. In my food journals and on elimination diets, I observed that I felt horribly tired after eating pasta, bread and any wheat product. Furthermore, whole wheat products that I thought would be better for me would give me severe indigestion and sharp stabbing pains in my stomach, colon and bowels.

I take one Gluten Ease capsule right before consuming a small portion of wheat product (eg one serving of pasta is 1/2 cup). Since the capsule contains enzymes that digest gluten and lactose, it makes sense to take another pill if I eat more servings or if I stretch the meal out over a longer period.

I rarely feel the need to eat wheat products nowadays but it's nice to be sociable and eat food at family dinners. Gluten Ease is a great 'antidote' that I can take and it only costs 50 cents per capsule.

Highly recommended.

title: Life changing
text:
This supplement has quite literally saved my life. I was suffering from unexplained symptoms for 5-6 years. Went through hundreds of medical tests, CAT scans, allergy tests and what not. Chronic fatigue, chronic dizziness, tinnitus, breathlessness, anxiety, itching, you name it, I had it.

Long story short, in addition to Daosin, two supplements that have helped me immensely are Methyl B12 and Magnesium Citramate.

If you have unexplained reactions to food, this could really help you. For years doctors kept telling me its all in my head! But I knew it wasn't. Thank god I stumbled upon this supplement.

UPDATE (6/22/14): DAOSin is still working great for me!! It has really saved my life and I am on the road to complete recovery. I am now able to enjoy my occasional beer and scotch, and ALL other high-histamine foods (b'bye CFS). I usually take two caps when I know I am going to indulge too much. title: Review based on 6 months of use, not opinions
text:
From [...]
"1900 - 1910 Invented and perfected the steel alkaline storage battery and made it a commercial success."

I wonder if the other reviewer even owed one of these rechargers. I have owned and used one for 6 months and I am buying another. Yes, some cells leak on recharging. As other writers have mentioned, the batteries that leaked were Rayovacs. I also had new, never regenerated, Rayovacs leak in my equipment so I don't use them anymore. I have had no trouble with others so far. I also drastically cut down on my battery bill.

Originally, I did measure the battery voltage before and after regenerating. I have had batteries as low as 0.81 volts regenerate to 1.6 volts. Yes, that is higher than the 1.5 volts they measure when they are new but that is what my voltmeters read, They work fine. I use them in LED flashlights, portable CD players, and my grandson regenerates the same battery for his cheap MP3 player. He has been using the same battery for over a month. I have one set of three in an LED flashlight that I left on for a week. I regenerated them and they are back in the flashlight and still working after several weeks. NOTE: LED flashlights will not drain the batteries to zero as an standard bulb will. A standard flashlight bulb might kill the batteries. I don't know. I don't use standard bulbs any more.

Actually, any application that takes the battery voltage to almost zero such as an R/C car, a toy, or a standard flashlight bulb, may kill a battery permanently. My electronics and LED lights all shut down before the battery is fully drained so the batteries have a better chance of recovering.

If you are concerned about Alkaline battery leakage (read the Wikipedia entry on them to see what it looks like), cut a small piece of plastic wrap and line the regenerator chamber leaving just the contacts exposed. If a battery leaks, you can contain it and throw it out before it damages your unit.

Considering that the reviewer's first "Fact Check" was wrong, and that my experiences have been completely different than the reviewer's opinions, you might want to be skeptical.

Remember, a completely depleted (0.8 volts or less) battery may take 3 days to regenerate but my grandson has found that he can "top" his off overnight if it has had light use. Also, batteries, even new ones, can leak, it is wise to take precautions.

title: Tool doesnt fit Nespresso D290, but with considerable effort, can make it work.
text:
I agree with the "Works fine" reviewer on the details, but not the score: as others have pointed out, this wrench is microscopically too small for the screw heads it's supposed to engage. But since the screws are aluminum, it's possible--with considerable effort--to make it work. As "Works fine" and others said, you need to press down very hard on the screw--in fact, so hard that you deform the aluminum screw head to (almost) fit inside the wrench. At first, this process was taking me about 10 minutes per screw; I had to grip the wrench with vice-grip pliers to be able to push down hard enough. Finally, I got the idea to tap the wrench firmly onto the screw head with a hammer (after finding the right orientation of the wrench on the screw head by feel). It's tricky--tap firmly enough to force the screw head into the wrench, but not so hard that you destroy anything inside. In fact, once I got it opened, the mechanisms inside are quite robust and were impervious to my hammering. With this hammering technique--maybe 5-10 firm taps per screw, enough so that the wrench holds by itself on the screw head--I got it down to 1 min per screw. So yes, you can make it work, but no, the tool is *not* sized properly for my Nespresso--a D290.
ADDED: they gave me a speedy refund, including shipping and handling

title: It's the new trend in K-Beauty
text:
So this is the new THING in K-Beauty where the collagen film gets absorbed directly into your face.

I tried 2 different brand before this one and like this the best.
One company's product left a thick film on the face and within hours it was peeling off from my face.
The other company's product, I had to spray and massage into my face and within hours it was still peeling off from my face. They Both were kinda hard to apply on my face.

But this one didn't peel off and there was no massaging in needed.

So the application process is a bit tricky so i hope my review helps.
If you're using this at the end of your skin care routine i dont think it's necessary to spray on the mist prior to applying the film patch but here it goes

Spray the mist over your face evenly please don't over spray your face where it's dripping down your chin.
Just a slight mist would do.

Apply the film onto your face the pink is out side and there's a slight white cast that side is for your face.
Please please try not to touch the film (inside of the patch cause it is super fragile)
Make sure your hand is not wet either cause the collagen patch will melt.

Apply slight pressure and press onto your face and the pink fabric will kinda automatically come off.
If your face is too wet you wont be able to see too much of the film's whiteness and if your face is too dry, the film wont stick to your face. So delicate this thing~!! So just the right amount of moisture to start off.

After you peel off the pink fabric spray the collagen mist over the film and while you're at it spray all over your face and neck avoid spraying your eyes it kinda stings.

I noticed that right after the mist dried, the face felt a bit tight they say this is the collagen working in your skin. I slept on it and noticed that the next day my face felt more moisturized and had less dryness from the sunscreen that i use to have.

I used it every other day for the past 2 weeks and noticed that my skin started to have this glow and less fine lines. I sprayed my face with the mist occasionally even when i wasn't using the patch. Hey it's collagen what have i got to lose?

It is now Monday as I write this (and no this is not covid or anything else): one hour after having this candy, big headache at the back of skull.  Bloodshot eyes.  Painful bulging eye feeling.  I could not sleep at all from the headache.  It took a tylenol to allow me to sleep but as soon as that wore off the headache was back.  Same thing for Saturday.  Same for Sunday.  Monday...same.  My left eye is constantly watering and is painful and very very bloodshot.  This didn't do anything except make me sick and I'm still here.  Clogged my nose.  Friday evening I had an asthma attack and I haven't had one in years.  I could hear congestion in the lungs but there wasn't anything to cough up.  This should be illegal - especially the "proprietary" ingredient.  This is to be ingested in the body.  WTF is it?  If I wasn't a healthy man in my prime - this might have killed me.  My eyes still are in pain and I seriously am thinking about legal recourse.  DO NOT BUY THIS.  See your doctor for recommendations.

title: Expensive, but nice for protein powder variety
text:
I follow a special diet for a chronic health condition, and I'm always interested in unsweetened, additive-free protein powders that meet my needs. I originally tried this brand of sunflower protein a few years ago, when it came in a (larger, less expensive) package. I've reordered it several times, including once recently in this new package. Now that there are more protein powders on the market that meet my needs, it's no longer among my top favorites, but I still like it and suspect I’lll order it again occasionally in the future for variety.

Taste: to me this tastes mild and pleasant, a little like untoasted sunseeds. It goes well with lots of different flavors, and unlike certain other types of unflavored protein powder (e.g. pea), I don't really find the taste is a limiting factor in how much can be added to food. I would not recommend it if you don’t like the flavor of untoasted sunflower seeds, though.

Versatility: I use this mostly in smoothies and homemade no-bake protein bars/bites. I also like it in small amounts stirred into drippy nut/seed butter, added my homemade grain-free protein granola recipe (which I then dehydrate rather than baking), and in grain-free porridge. I wouldn't use it for “protein fluff” or in unflavored nondairy milk, except maybe as a small portion of a blend of different protein powders. I haven't baked with it a lot, but it works great when I used it in chickpea flour crackers (for less than half the dry ingredients). I find it less versatile than most other types of single-ingredient plant-based protein powder due to its weird culinary properties (see below).

Color: this is a pale neutral gray when dry, and turns darker gray when mixed with water... and then sometimes gives other light-colored foods an unappetizing grayish-greenish tinge, presumably due to it being a sunflower-based product (like sunbutter). A couple of times when I put it in winter squash porridge, it looked so disgusting I almost couldn't eat it despite the taste being fine—I suspect this had to do with the natural color of the particular squash plus the pH of the other ingredients. This powder also makes green smoothies kind of swamp-colored if I add more than a very small amount. In berry smoothies or chocolate recipes, though, the grayish color makes little difference.

Texture: this is a super, super fine powder—finer than the other brand of 100% sunflower protein I've seen and tried, more like a very fine pea protein. It works great in smoothies. But in other foods, it can turn into a gummy lump when adding liquid to try to make a dough, batter, granola mixture, etc. For baking and granola, I find the weird textural properties to be the limiting factor in how much I can use. Definitely mix with other dry ingredients before adding to wet! Smallish amounts aren't usually a problem, and it's good blended with other protein powders. I wouldn't generally drink this in plain nondairy milk without adding other smoothie ingredients, as I don't like how it separates or sinks to the bottom of a thin beverage. I also don't think it would mix well in a beverage without using a blender, at least not to my preference.

Usability of package: I find this style of bag unusable for protein powder—it's fussy to reseal, and because the powder is so fine, it flies all over. I cut the entire zipper off the bag and slowly, carefully transferred it into a good food storage jar. I'm not deducing any stars for this only because the annoyance is a one-time thing for me.

Overall experience: I've found Lekithos to have really good customer service when I've called or emailed with product questions or special order requests, including helping me figure out how to get free shipping on a large order. I do find it annoying that the prices seem to have gone up and there aren’t the type of constant promotional deals that reduce the cost of other high-priced brands of protein powder. But I like the Lekithos products enough to order them occasionally when they're in my budget, although I don't think I'll order this sunflower one as often now that another brand has started making a lower-priced 100% sunflower protein.

Note: I review foods and supplements based ONLY on my liking of their taste and culinary properties, and whether they work for me. Not being an expert in nutrition or food safety, I have NO IDEA whether the health, nutrition, and safety claims made on the package are accurate so that doesn't come into my rating!

title: Failed after a month, poor internal soldering
text: This seat warmer worked wonderfully in gentle use for about a month, then failed.  The temperature control unit failed, displaying "99" instead of the set temperature.  Now, whenever it is turned on it turns off after exactly one minute.  So, I just can't keep it turned on except by pressing the ON button every minute.  Frustrating!  UPDATE: I was able to repair the control unit.  Fortunately the unit was not glued together but its plastic housing just snaps together.  Inside, the wires going to heating mat were soldered to a small PCB, but one of the connections for the temperature sensor had come undone -- it had been a cold solder joint.  I resoldered it, and reflowed the other connections too because they looked poor.  It now works again.  I'm keeping the one star rating because the unit failed, and most users would not have been able to repair it.

title: Good training device
text: I have had mine for over 4.5 years and it is still working well. I also still have the original Novadreamer. in my personal experience, these devices will not give you a guaranteed lucid dream, I wish it was that easy! What they are useful for is in training the mind to look for specific and consistent cues in your dreams which if recognised, can help you realise that you are dreaming. You still need to use prospective memory training during the day and program your mind to pay attention to bright lights and bright objects in your waking life, and have a strong intention to recognise these also in your dreams. The good thing about this mask is that you can set the light flashes to last up to 30 seconds when they detect REM. When I use the mask and set the right brightness level it will help me to wake up after each dream period during the night and I manage to remember 3-4 dreams fairly easily. This is normally quite difficult to do without waking up during the night as when we sleep through all the way, the brain struggles to remember. So this tool is not only useful for training the mind to recognise dream signals (things that typically happen in one's dreams) but also for dream recall. Considering the reliability, build quality, and results, I think it is worth the price. All of my lucid dreams have happened without the REM mask by using well known LD techniques but the mask has definitely helped on this journey and I am still using it.

title: Interested in Inositol? Price and Quality make this Brand Ideal.
text:
Chemically, inositol is a sugar alcohol with a cyclic backbone. Some other sugar alcohols are sorbitol (used in ice cream) and xylitol (famously prevalent in chewing gum). Like the two aforementioned chemicals, inositol is sweet and very safe.

There's some interesting, though limited, research about the potential benefits of inositol but I'll leave that to you.

Here was my experience with inositol. Swanson was having a sale on the stuff and I bought a tub (much smaller than liftmode's). Inositol, unlike most powdered supplements, tastes great and I diligently took it every day until it was empty. The very last bit of inositol I used to sweeten jello pudding.

Unfortunately, I did not experience effects noteworthy enough for me to remember any years later (not a memory enhancer, I guess? ;-). Perhaps there was an improvement in mood and ability at some cognitive tasks. However, the fact that I never purchased more is telling.

Sounds like a neutral experience... So why the positive review?

Liftmode's inositol is much cheaper than their competition, but they provide lab purity tests. My experience with their products is that their quality is as good if not better than that of any competition.

Maybe I didn't consume enough years ago because I didn't buy enough from Swanson. Liftmode's 400 gram product is generous enough that under-dosing won't be an issue.

Also, a less noticeable vitamin-like effect may also take place- B vitamins may not make you feel any different but proper supplementation may nonetheless improve your health.

Inositol may not work for everyone but its cheap and probably very safe (the worst side effect is diarrhea, as far as I know). Try it. If I start reading reviews from people raving about the amazing nootropic effects of inositol, I'm definitely going to try it again!

text:
I will be buying a back up of the Facial Toner (120 mL) and am giving this a BEE Shopping recommendation. I used this both morning and evening right after cleansing. I just squirted some onto a cotton round for the face, neck, and also behind my ears. Doing this treatment twice a day, I believe, helped keep the psoriasis from getting out of control. It’s didn’t get rid of it, but did lessen the thickening.

Have I ever told you how much I love trying new beauty products? In July I was fortunate enough to be sent the Pure Mauve Line of Products Made in Canada by Carapex Inc. of Chambly, Quebec to test out for 30 days and give my opinion. One of the reasons they thought I could benefit from this specific range is because I have written previously about the scalp psoriasis I’ve had for the past 18 months. The Tea Tree Oil is thought to help clear up the plaque that grows quickly over the scalp and sometimes other areas. This plaque appears very dry and can flake, crack, and if scratched can bleed and be very sore. Here’s a quote from the Carapex website about the Pure Mauve line “Due to our passion in the benefits of Tea Tree Oil, we developed this line of clean, natural, invigorating products. Only the purest, highest quality of Australian Tea Tree Oil has been utilized to work wonders on skin inflammation, breakouts and other conditions.”

So I don’t have to type it out every time, each Pure Mauve product I was sent has the name “Invigorating” and “with Tea Tree Oil”. I like the dark purple bottles because they’re different from anything else I have in the bathroom so stand out. I wear contacts so can barely see without them or my glasses and each bottle cap (except the Body Lotion) has a large silver letter on it so you know what it is you’re grabbing for. “S” for Shampoo, “C” for Conditioner, “T” for Toner, “M” for Moisturizer and “C” again for Cleanser. The Hair products are double the size of the facial ones, so you wouldn’t ever mix up the two “C”s.

I’ve been using everything exclusively for 30 days now and have 2/3 left still of the Lotion, Shampoo and Conditioner and 1/2 of the facial toner, cleanser, and moisturizer. I estimate the face items would last 2 months, the hair products for 3, and the body lotion would depend on whether you use it all over or just in certain areas. If you do not enjoy the smell of Tea Tree Oil, then these products are NOT for you. I joke that I smell like a health food store when I’m done my routine! Luckily the smell doesn’t last all day and you can still wear body mists or perfumes without the fragrance changing.

Final Result: To BEE (shopping that is).

title: Hey Sister I hear yah
text:
Since I was 17, I’ve been prone to getting frequent UTI’s. And yes, trust me, the doctors have given me the pamphlets on how they’re caused and how to prevent. Before you dismiss this review—
I wasn’t sexually active at the time, I’m a very hygienic person, and so help me Allah, if one more 65+ year old male doctor whispers all-knowingly “you have to wipe front to back”— the depths of Mordor will hear my screams of frustration.

My story took a turn for the better with a doctor at a minute clinic where I worked. Lovely Linda- told me a story about her mother who had chronic UTIs up until the end of her life— where they had gotten so bad, the medical field had run out of effective/strong enough antibiotics for how intense these bacteria had gotten. She told me about taking a supplement called D-mannose- a simple sugar that helps coat the walls of the bladder to inhibit bacteria from sticking... and it was from that point on, where I started my once naive journey of exploring what would keep me healthy and away from unnecessary antibiotics that would over time leave me only with the gladiator bacteria I was ever so afraid of as the cause of my eventual demise.

I tried many different types of D-mannose supplements but ultimately found that this one has helped the most. I went from having at least 6-7 UTI’s a year- some so excruciating where I wouldn’t be able to make it the 20 minute drive to work without stopping multiple times, or one that was so bad in college where never since my Elmo-on-the-potty days had I lost control of my bladder as such in the dressing room right before a dance recital. I was 21.

And now? Nothing. No I’m serious.
I don’t take them everyday. Only 2-3 times a month, or sure I’ll make a point of taking them before/after I do end up having “relations with that woman” or even having a weekend to Vegas with my ladies guiltily knowing my rum-water ratio will be skewed (maybe someday I’ll learn).

Anyway, point is. These helped me get my life back. I have enough anxiety without having to worry if even the slightest mishap in my regimen will ruin my next few days or worse- the inability to cure my body when modern medicine can’t keep up with our increasingly longer life expectancies.

Best wishes,
Mai Thai in one hand, coffee in the other.

title: Cut my styling time in half!
text:
Wow - it gets HOT! I have a flat iron hair straightener that I have to set to its highest setting to get the results I want. I'm so used to it, that when I started up this brush for the first time, I set the temperature to 390 degrees and figured I would go up from there as needed. Little did I know, for my hair, 390 was more than enough heat! I have naturally wavy hair that frizzes like crazy. I use hair straighteners to get a straight look and to control the frizz. This brush might be too powerful for me! And I mean that in a good way. If you have actual curly hair (unlike my slightly wavy hair) I don't see this brush having any problem at all straightening your hair! I also have a lot of very thick hair and usually have to straighten it in sections. But with the brush being able to brush through and grab a lot of hair with each brush, I don't have to do sections at all! That's my favorite part about this product! Also, I have to rave about the glove. It works very very very well! I have a heat glove from another product and it helps shield some of the heat to help prevent burns, but definitely still can get burned. This glove, I could touch the brush and never even felt heat! I was able to hold my hair in the brush as I brushed so I could get a pretty curved look. That was very cool. And now the only reason I gave it 4 stars was because the brush gives off a funky smell when it's hot. At first I was afraid it was from burned hair, but it wasn't. It was the brush itself. It's not horrible or even that noticeable. I hope it's more of a new-product smell and will go away over time. But it definitely doesn't deter me from using the brush! Oh and one more thing I want to point out is you can press the brush prongs against your scalp - the tips of the brush aren't hot! I included some before and after pictures.

I am so glad that I took a chance on this product.

title: Not the same quality!
text:
Beware! I have four pair of PowerStep ProTech orthopedic inserts and love them. They are great for my problems with plantar fasciitis, high arches, and over pronation. I ordered two new pair from a different seller and noticed some major differences immediately. The new inserts (1) have a rounded bottom instead of the molded heel; (2) have a shallower heel cup; and (3) have a smaller arch support.

Seeing these major differences, I then found a number of minor differences including: (4) the U.S. Patent number is missing; (5) the labeling is faded; and (6) a ridge line is detectable under the arch.

I looked at the packaging and a small label has been applied to the box that states; "New, Improved PowerStep." I can say, with no hesitation, these new inserts are NOT IMPROVED over the originals. They appear much more cheaply made and do not provide the deep cup and high arch that the original inserts have. Either these are cheap knockoffs or PowerStep has changed their design. I'm not sure which but I am sending these two new pair back. I will try attaching photos but since this is my first time to post a review, I'm not sure if I'll be successful.

title: Unfortunately not reliable or long-lasting
text:
I managed quality control for an electronic manufacturer for years, I know often customers perceive a product as flawed because the one they buy fails - but they only have one, so their sample size is too small to see that their one failure was an exception rather than the rule.

In my case, I bought four of these, one for each of my family, in February 2020. One failed within a month and was replaced. Another failed after about two months and I received a refund. The third failed a short bit ago, I emailed the seller and have gotten no response.

The failure was similar - they just stopped working. Acting as if they were not charged. Of course since I have others I know the charger and cord are working fine.

I'd love to have a copy of the warranty - these were bought with a credit card that would refund me for them if I can give them a copy of the warranty (they double that warranty) but there appears to be no such thing available anywhere.

Unfortunately I can't recommend this product as a result. I've replaced the last failure with a much more expensive Water-Pik model, so far so good....!

title: Product doesn't match description
text:
As a couple other reviewers have said, this product doesn't match up with the photos and description. The worst difference being the rubber cane tip. The product photo shows a fairly durable looking piece of rubber. What you really get is essentially a hollowed out pencil eraser (I'm attaching 2 photos) screwed into the bottom. It showed signs of wear after ten minutes of use in my apartment. It would disintegrate in under an hour of regular use out on a sidewalk or street, I'm sure.

The other main difference is that the cane is one solid piece, and it doesn't unscrew to become two separate pieces. That's fine for me, but I'm sure that's important to some people. The quality of the cane seems ok and is what I expected in this price range.

The handle is nice. It has a nice heft to it and feels good in your hand. This part of the cane is properly represented in the pics and description.

It seems like a perfectly suitable cane except for the rubber tip. Other reviewers said they got replacement tips, but I don't believe purchasers should have unexpected additional costs on this item just to make it what they were expecting to see when they opened the box. I hope this helps out future shoppers from being mislead.

title: Overwhelming Stevia Flavor
text:
The list of ingredients are excellent. No doubt about it. An extremely healthy product. However, I despise the taste of STEVIA. I looked at the list of *other* ingredients, which is where I usually find natural flavors and stevia listed. Since I didn't see stevia on the label, I got excited and purchased the product thinking there would be no putrid taste of stevia to spoil my smoothie or shake recipes. Wrong. The first gulp had me sprinting for the sink. Gross, gross, GROSS!

If you like the taste of stevia, you'll like this product. If stevia freaks you out, like me, then a couple scoops of this horrid-tasting stuff will be hard to swallow.

I gave three stars because it really is an excellent product IMO. My dislike for stevia is a personal issue. Many folks like stevia. I'm not one of them, and never will be. However, I wish manufacturers would BOLDLY list the addition of stevia in a more prominent way -- make this horrid ingredient easier to spot on their product labels. I'm really getting tired of tossing out expensive nutritional drink powders with stevia. Had I spotted stevia in the ingredient list, I would NEVER have purchased this formula, knowing my strong revulsion to the bitter taste of this sweet leaf herb. Manufacturers use waay more than necessary. Why not just keep the flavors of nutritional powders neutral and appeal to ALL health-conscience taste buds???

I also tasted no "natural" vanilla and chai flavor -- whatever that means.

I absolutely HATED the disgusting stevia taste. But I LOVED the nutritional profile. A serving size of 65g (2 large scoops) provides 240 cal, 6g fat, 22g carbs, 15g fiber, 26g protein. Plant based protein blend: organic hemp, yellow pea, organic brown rice, flax. Maca Rt (2,500mg). Chlorella. Omega 3 & 6 EFA's. Digestive Enzyme Blend. Mixed Berry Complex. Dairy-free Probiotic Blend. *Other* ingredients: natural vanilla and chai flavor. Xanthan gum (does not list source: corn, wheat, or soy).

Also listed in the mineral lineup is *iron* (as citrate) 18mg (100%) and a WARNING to keep the product out of reach of CHILDREN under 6 in case of accidental poisoning/overdose of iron-containing products.

Net weight 16.3 oz. (461g). Servings per container 7 (total 14 scoops).

I feel like one of the other reviewers... I REALLY WANTED to like this whole food dietary supplement product. I'm being very generous with three stars.

Made in Canada. Brendan Brazier is the product's formulator, a professional ironman triathlete and author of "THRIVE, The Vegan Nutrition Guide...shows you how plant-based whole foods can improve health, performance, and vitality." Check him out and his yummy and *famous* homemade *raw food* energy bars.

title: Not a Scam, but be careful
text:
This teeth whitening system works quick, and extremely well. I used 1 tube and my teeth were noticeably whiter. There was little to no sensitivity using the product, and it was very easy to use.
People think that it is a scam because they don't read the terms and conditions before buying it. As soon as you purchase the product, they will automatically enroll you in a preferred customer program (which means they will send you 3 tubes of teeth whitener every 3 months at a charge of 69.00 or something near that). If you only want the initial tube or tubes you ordered, you need to visit the website shortly after ordering to cancel your preferred membership (you must do this to avoid unwanted charges to your acct.) As far as the mail in rebate goes, it is not a scam either. Unfortunately though the customer (you) has to do a lot of leg-work to get the rebate. You have to call the company offering the rebate (Wellness Watchers was the 3rd party company I had to go through). The third party company I went through also had a preferred customer program, that I was automatically enrolled in when I agreed to buy the teeth whitening system. Be sure to cancel this membership also to avoid the 39.00/month fee they will charge your acct. The rebate was not sent until I called them and requested it. Luckily I had kept the original packing slip that came with my teeth whitening package. You need this in order to get your rebate.
Product = A+
Scam = No
Satisfied Customer = A+
Cons to ordering = too much leg-work to prevent extra charges.

Purchasing this was a HUGE mistake - I poured 1 teaspoon (the bottle calls for up to 2) of the bitters in a glass of cranberry juice. At first I felt great... somewhat numb - then within 15-20 minutes I had diarrhea, cold sweats, my heart racing like crazy. My body was shivering and eventually I threw up everything in my stomach. It was horrible - to the point where my husband almost took me to the emergency room. It felt like I'd been poisoned. After reading the ingredients, my husband realized it contained Camphor - which is toxic to humans if ingested - look it up online and read about it.  For 2 weeks I had Colitis resulting from the effects of Swedish Bitters. I went to my Dr. and they said this product contained Senna - which is a laxitive! title: Does the job, but why no variable speed?!
text:
My girlfriend and I moved into a great new apartment recently. The only downside is a loud neighbor, a night owl who crashes around in her apartment at midnight, leaves for work at 1am, comes home at 4am, then takes the garbage out.

The noise machine creates a soothing blanket of whooshing air that covers up our neighbour. However, why oh why doesn't Marpac make it with a dial to adjust the speed of the fan? Honestly, it is just a little too loud - we'd love to be able to dial it down a bit. If we wanted something this loud that we could just leave the bathroom extractor fan on all night.

Marpac does make a more expensive model with two speed settings, but why not just make one model with several settings (like every desk fan on the market, for instance). The people who buy this product are most likely sensitive to noise already, so why not give them the ability to adjust the noise generator to their own specifications?

I guess Marpac are the only people out there making these things, so they have no competition and thus no reason the improve the product. One model, with multi-speed setting (more than just two!), would seem to be an obvious next-step for them.

Still, if noise is a problem where you live, this will do the trick.

title: Exactly The Same As Excedrin Extra Strength!
text:
I managed a woodworking shop in the '80s, and this stuff simply vanished each time the medicine box was refilled -- so much so that one of the other managers began locking it up in his desk and doling it out by request. As good as it is, it isn't a unique formulation -- Excedrin Extra Strength, Excedrin Migraine and Excedrin Menstrual Complete all have the same exact ingredients: 250 mg acetaminophen, 250 mg aspirin and 65 mg caffeine.

This three drug combination was the subject of a double-blind study comparing it to ibuprofen (and a placebo) -- it was found to be more effective for the relief of migraines:

http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16618262

title: This movie is lots of fun!
text: This movie is terrific. I watched it with my 8 year old son (he is in French immersion) and we both enjoyed it. I am sure he did not understand every word, but the movie is quite funny even if you don't catch every word. If you have read any Petit Nicolas stories you will enjoy how they managed to weave so many individual episodes into one coherent and hilarious story. The movie is appropriate for a high school or college classroom, but while not offensive in any way, may not be appropriate in an elementary immersion classroom. There is one scene where the humor is based on Nicolas' mother getting drunk because she is nervous and trying to impress her husband's boss. I did not mind my son seeing this (since he does not know what drunk is, he thought she was just being silly). But I would not show it to his immersion class at elementary school. On the other hand, my French 1 college class thoroughly enjoyed the movie. If your students are reading Petit Nicolas they will really get a kick out of this movie.

title: 1-st impression of Sleeptracker Pro
text:
I've bought a Sleeptracker Pro from Amazon in Oct. '08. I've tested it for ca. 3 weeks in both US and EU, including the few jet-lagged days in between. Bgnd info on the tester: I buy and test sundry bio-feedback devices that may help me to improve, or document, my sleeping patterns.

My 1-st take on Sleeptracker Pro: A good & simple idea with a flawed --alpha-- implementation. Good enough for a prototype, useful for geeks and novices, yet a let-down for folks expecting hassle-free results, or for advanced users.

The idea is simple: Use a motion sensor to inferr the wearer's current sleep stage. While it can't tell the diff between deep sleep and resting (not moving), or, a longer meditation session, the concept is a practical approximation. The execution, though, is unnecessarily limited. Rarely i've actually stumbled upon a potentially useful device so unfinished as this...

Items that can be improved.

1. Please consider adding a "Free Sleep One-touch" record function, w/o having to set both the "to bed" and the "alarm" time. This type of acquisition window reduces the consumer benefit (to simplify the development effort?). I'd like to press once to start the sampling, and once more to terminate it. Man people would like to analyze their sleep w/o actually using the alarm.

2. Extend the user memory (e.g., by 100-1000x), enough to store a few weeks of sampled data. Currently --unless one doesn't download daily to a PC-- each night will over-write the previous' session data. While FLASH memory costs cents/MB, the S.Pro stores merely a few 'user' bytes, forcing one to either daily download or loose data. When a 4GB USB stick costs a few $, one would expect an $180 device to squeeze more than 0.1KB of user data.

3. Relocate the "Mode" button to make it accessible while the USB clip (the 3-prong gotic device with USB cable) is attached. BTW, it's quite an irony to have the *only* button needed for USB transfers being blocked by the USB clip... Or just use a mini-USB port (water may become a problem, but it should actually matter for this device).

4. Software: Reminiscent of the 80s + GUI. While the GUI is relatively clean, it's mostly an empty shell devoid of the needed functionality. Please enhance the s/w beyond its still alpha version where it's stuck since '07. At least pls. allow the data to be deleted, added/inserted, shifted and displayed in more useful ways.

5. Pls. allow the user to set the "eagerness" of the alarm, which currently starts always on the FIRST motion during the window. Explain clearly with examples or a picture how the alarm window works. E.g., the 20min interval is NOT centered on the alarm time, but it's ahead of it. With larger windows, this means that the user must accept to sleep less; a few times the alarm woke me up nearly an hour earlier. Perhaps I could've slept 1-2 more deep episodes before the final alarm...

6. Allow once per month downloads (repeat) w/o over-writing the data.

7. Provide more suitable statistics. The average can be misleading when placing 5 billionaires (Gates, Buffet etc.) i the same room w/ 95 homeless and concluding that this must be super-rich's assembly. Median and variability could better describe a sleep made of 3-4 long segments (90min. each) plus a dozen 8-12 min. tracks.

Net: A good idea w/ a coarse 1-st implementation (actually this is the 2nd or 3rd generation), slow in technically improvements. Marketing seems to trump technology thus far, because with a tad more thought the hardware and the software could be greatly improved - to reach new markets.

Does it actually work? Yes, with limitations. The commercials have fuelled some false expectations, of more than the actual device can do. This is a basic alarm watch with a built-in motion sensor (like those used in most 2.5" hard-disks to avoid crashing the heads) that will go on at the 1-st move detected during the alarm window. The trade-offs are obvious...

Is it worth your money? Yes, if you have some moderate sleep problems and enough discipline in your daily schedule to work on them. No, if you expect an true sleep monitor (headband sensors) or a reliable, thoughtful and straightforward tool.

IMHO it's a thoughtless raw design that could do much better. I rarely had to resort to adjectives such as 'thoughtless' until now, yet there's little engineering attention paid to this product. A shame. I gave it 3 stars to reward the idea, which by now is common in many other products.

gusat"atsign"ieee.org

Update Febr.'09: The Glow button no longer works w/o pushing really hard - but it's still functional. A few s/w bugs have caused the watch to display wrong Data A, and to repeat the same readings for 2 nights.

text: I don't usually leave reviews for things, but feel compelled to do so in this case. I was really excited to get these--they seemed like a great selection of scents for the cost, but there must be problems with the company's packaging process. Even as I opened the box, I could tell it was all spotted in oil everywhere, and I was concerned one of them had leaked, but it doesn't smell like any one scent--like a combination of a lot of them. I checked every lid, none of them had been opened, nor were any of the bottles cracked. And it wasn't just one bottle--almost every single one is so covered in oil that the stickers are bubbling up, and their little individual foam cubbies are slick with oil. Needless to say, this is not good. Some of these oils are phototoxic and skin irritants, but now you have to touch them with your fingers to even open the bottles. I had also assumed I would be able to keep them in the box they came in, as other brands have sturdy cardboard boxes, but this is like cereal box cardboard, and also covered in oil stains. Given that so many of my bottles seem effected, I don't think it's just a defective product--I think it's a problem with the company's packaging process. I would not recommend, not unless you're willing to spend a lot of time cleaning up the mess and buying a different storage container to keep them in

title: Stinky at First, but Very Good!
text:
I've had an Awful desk chair for years now that I've only been able to sit in by placing a big plush on the chair and letting that act as the cushion. But over the years, that plush has definitely lost its fluff and volume, so it was time to find an alternative.
The Purple cushion came in a nice over box with the cushion and its case, along with best use and cleaning instructions. It was easy to fit the cushion in the case- less than 10 second set up. It had a very strong, plastic-y smell, but it seems to have dissipated after a few days of airing out, and you go nose-blind to it pretty quickly. (If you're planning to use this in the office or in a car, have it air out a few days at home first).
I've seen a few complaints of people saying the cushion slides forward in use, but I personally have not encountered that issue with my vinyl/leather-esque chair.
As for the actual use, it's Absurdly comfortable. I am a heavy person, frequently in my desk chair all day but for bathroom and eating breaks. My tailbone and other sitting parts used to ache after too long in the chair, but I have never felt more comfortable or less aching after a long desk day.
Even sitting in strange positions (criss cross, foot in the crook of the knee, etc) is more comfortable now, which means the world to me when I constantly sit in weird positions.
My only concerns for people would be the smell (solvable by a few days airing out) the thickness (it's very thick and could limit armrest access in chairs without adjustable armrest heights) and the size (it's very big- I use it in a standard size gamer chair, which fits it nicely, but it weighs a little bit and is the size of like a big sack of rice). But for a heavy person with a proper sized chair, it'll work great! So far, it's worth the price.

text:
[[VIDEOID:9799f269badc43fdae4a36d4912990ea]] On the second replacement. These things are proving to be overpriced trash. The initial setup is clumbsy having to switch back and forth between WiFi networks while navigating the Fitbit app: if you are lucky enough to get it to setup after the second or third full try, it will only stay in communication with your devices for a limited time. At some point, it will stop syncing and you will have to run through a reset protocol, which basically means starting all over as if it were new. This time, however, the WiFi setup refuses to complete and the scale no longer syncs and I must manually enter my data points. I could have picked up a basic digital scale for a fraction of the cost of this thing for the basic functionality which it provides. I am very disappointed.

Edit: after trolling through Fitbit’s community support forums, it seems this is a common problem which many users experience and the ONLY support Fitbit’s employees offer is to direct you to the basic reset directions.

It will take a miracle for me to consider another Fitbit product. I may as well have just thrown a stack of $20 bills out of my bedroom window.

title: My go to Italian cookbook for "real" Italian cooking.
text: I purchased Letizia's book, and 9 more to give to family and friends, because it includes recipes that you would find on most any Italian family's table. My wife and I love small village Italy, and this collection of recipes represents these treasures in a very real and simple fashion. The recipes in this book will open your eyes to true Italian cooking, and is very representative of the slow food movement. Good quality ingredients, simple tastes, and how to use whatever is on hand, Letizia can blend these lessons into some of the most masterful, and simply artistic dishes you have ever tasted. She was careful to write this cookbook for both Italians, and non-Italians alike. Ingredients can be found locally, even in small town, mid-western America.  Our family makes home made pizza regularly now, because Letizia's slow dough foccacia recipe makes the best pizza crust ever.  I am happy to say that this book, is my go to book for real Italian cooking.

title: Ineffective warning
text:
I have a warm mist humidifier (the Vicks UV with 2 water containers, similar to my previous Slant Fin humidifier), and this cleaner is extremely effective. Rather than filling the heating compartment five or six times with vinegar when I clean it once a week (after removing the mineral absorption pad), I can fill the compartment once for a matter of a few minutes and all the hard water residue is gone. My water may be harder than yours.
Unfortunately, the instructions on the bottle say that the product should not be discarded in the sink; it should only be discarded in the toilet. This turns out to be virtually impossible to do. The sink in my bathroom is too small to rinse out the humidifier, so I have to rinse it in the kitchen sink. The warning is not specific enough to tell me what the danger is for putting it down the sink. Does it harm the tadpoles in the sewer, or what? My solution is to run the water in the sink for three or four minutes to minimize whatever the potential is. So I am left to wonder if I'm doing damage to my plumbing. I'm giving only five stars for effectiveness minus one star for uncertainty.

title: Great product, let down badly by the wireless
text:
I've had my Aria now for about 3 months and have very mixed feelings about it. It looks really nice in my bathroom, it's easy to use (step on, step off) and from a weighing point of view, it's great. None of those reasons were why I bought it however. I got it to integrate to my Fitbit account, and save me from manually entering my weight into the website. On that point, the scale falls well below expectations due to what appears to be a very poorly designed and implemented wireless radio.

First up, I should say I'm in IT, so know a lot about wireless networks (often the bane of an IT persons existence). I have about 20 wireless devices in my house currently, all of which quite happily talk to my wireless router regardless of device size or physical location.

The Aria however is a different matter. Firstly the wireless range of the scale is dire. It sits no more than 30 ft from my router with an almost clear line of site, yet consistently fails to get a signal. This despite the fact I can quite happily get a signal from other devices even when outside in my garden.

Secondly, setting up an configuring it with anything other than the minimal security policy causes it to refuse to connect to the network. It doesn't like hidden SSID's, WPA2 encryption, MAC address locking, or any protocol above wireless B.

Unfortunately, given that the sole purpose of the scale is to communicate via wireless to the internet, these are pretty severe issues. The Fitbit help is contradictory, with some sections saying the Aria will work with certain settings, whilst others say it won't. Even the support people aren't sure, expressing surprise when I pointed them to the Fitbit tech specs which contradicted their advice.

In the end, I did get the Aria to work, but now sits 10 ft from the wireless router in a second bathroom, and I've had to buy another router just for the scale to work (so I can keep all my other wireless devices secure). Not an ideal solution by any means.

One other issue I've noticed is that the scale has no way of determining who is who (no "tap once for person A, twice for person B" setting). In other words if you've more than one person of similar weight, the scale has no idea who it's measuring and can potentially upload the wrong info. Your only recourse is to then manually correct the entry on the Fitbit website, which kind of negates the reason for using it in the first place.

Pro's
Looks great
Accurate weighing mechanism
BMI measurement is reasonable (close enough for home use)
Easy to use

Con's
Struggles to differentiate between people of similar weights
Wireless reception is woeful

Conclusion
If you want is a fancy looking set of scales, that are easy to use, and don't want to upload the data then the Aria is fine. If you've more than one person in the house of a similar size, want to use the Fitbit integration, or have anything other than a perfect environment for wireless you may find you're out of luck.

title: Defective product; short warranty
text:
Like some other posters have mentioned this scale has a serious manufacturing defect that many users have reported. You can read about this by doing a quick search for "Aria randomly turning on".

This happened to my unit. It would randomly turn on and drain the battery until it ran out. So, in effect, I now own a door stop.

I contacted support and they said that since my unit is outside of warranty (only 1 year), they won't replace it and there's nowhere that will repair it.

title: Simply Awesome
text:
The FitBit Tracker is good, and the FitBit Aria scale integrates with it beautifully, giving you an accurate (sometimes too accurate, IMHO) picture of your fitness level. It's easy to set up, dead simple to use, and it wirelessly transmits your measurements to the FitBit site. What could be better? I'm done manually entering weight into a spreadsheet or into a diary. It's right there on the FitBit site.

I've also found it very easy to track food on the FitBit site. I am very impressed with the FitBit products.

title: Works without a hitch
text:
Contrary to the experiences of some others, I found the setup procedure very straight forward. I used the web browser on an iPad, and therefore did not have to download any software. The Aria was connected to my network and ready to use less than five minutes after opening the box. As long as you know your network password, have the scales in front of you, and follow the instructions step-by-step, there is very little scope for misfortune as far as I can see. I already had an account set up with FitBit, since I have been using the FitBit Ultra for several months. The weight measurements from the Aria appeared on the website without any further fiddling on my part.

The range of the Wi-Fi transmitter is impressive. I tested the scales on both levels of the house (each level has its own access point) - and in various rooms - and it sync'd each and every time, even through several walls.

As far as accuracy goes, I found that the recorded weight was identical on every occasion, whereas the body fat percentage crept up gradually from 17.0% to 18.1%. It never recorded a lower figure, always a higher one, so I have no idea what is going on there.

Build quality is very good. The scales have an impressive weight to them, and the materials seem to be of a high standard. However, I agree with others that the spring terminals in the battery compartment look and feel very cheap. As long as you take care when replacing the batteries, this should not be an issue, but it is nevertheless disappointing to see corners being cut. The LCD screen is very easy to read, with high contrast and a good, strong backlight.

Overall, the Aria scale is an impressive first generation product and I recommend it highly, especially if you already use or intend to use a FitBit.

title: Aria - great concept, but implementation still lacking in accuracy...
text:
This product has a great concept -- measure your weight & body fat % & send it wirelessly to view in your fitbit app or website, making it easy to track trends. The uploads work well. Many people have reported it's hard to sync with wifi but I didn't have that problem. Replacing batteries also easy for me. It does need to be on a hard surface. It's worked "reliably" for me for about 3 yrs now (that's reliable for weight & wifi uploading, but not body fat% measurements).

My problem with the Aria has been with accuracy. It has always given a higher body fat % reading than with other scales, like the Eatsmart. That's tolerable when you're just tracking trends. However, one time after a measurement, I stepped right back on, & to my surprise my body fat % went up by .1 %. So I did it again & it went up by another .1 %. This is troubling. I checked the fitbit forums & several people report variances in weight or body fat %. The solution proposed by fitbit is to remove the batteries, reseat them, then weigh yourself 5 times so the scale can re-calibrate. For me this worked okay for weight, but does not work for body fat %. For others, it does not fix the weight issue either. Fitbit support has not given me any explanation body fat % would increase with repeated measurements within a few minutes.

I would not by this scale again until there is some progress on the accuracy issues.

title: Potentially great product with an inherent flaw.
text:
Went on Fitbit's website after receiving a "Charge" for my birthday. Decided that the "Aria" scale would be the perfect companion to track all of my progress. Through Fitbit's website there was a 6-8 week back order. Decided to shop Amazon.com and I was pleasantly surprised to see several sellers with the item I wanted in stock and about $25 cheaper than what Fitbit had it for. It was a no brainer.

The item arrived neatly and professionally packaged. Relatively easy to set up and I had it working and synced within 10 minutes or so of opening the package. I was really pleased and the product appeared to be well put together. After using the product for 3 days I went out of town for 5 days on business and came back, got on the scale and got a repeated error message. I spent 2 days trying to trouble shoot the issue using Fitbit's online forums and contacting customer support. Based on what I can see on the forums/community help page at Fitbit.com this is a fairly common error and there are many frustrated users. It seems that many, too many in my opinion, were experiencing this malfunction for a scale of this price.

After none of the online recommendations seemed to help, I contacted Fitbit's customer service folks who are located in Guatemala. While both representatives were extremely nice and very helpful in the end, English was a secondary language, and the delay in the phone lines did make it somewhat difficult to understand. The Fitbit representative stood by the product though. They told me it must be an internal hardware error and that if for any reason the seller through Amazon.com would not take it back (I don't know why they wouldn't) they would take the product back and ship me a new one, albeit, with a 6-8 week back order as mentioned previously.

I have requested a replacement and not a refund. I really want to use the Charge and the Aria together for maximum effectiveness, but after my own experiences and reading all the others with similar issues, I fear that this is not an anomaly and may be an inherent problem. I'm willing to give it one more try. Kudos to Fitbit for standing by their product regardless. Quality appearance and feel, but ultimately it was defective and I'm not alone. Two stars for now. Will update when new scale is received. I would say buyer beware at this time.

I wish I had been told this the first time I called and explained the exact situation because I wanted to avoid spending time and energy trying to set it up and then having to go out of my way to return it. However, it may all be for the best because I found a Bluetooth scale by Weight Gurus that does the same things, automatically SYNCS WITH THE FITBIT app and is half the price (not to mention better reviews, but I can't judge on the functions of the scale).

title: Convenient, except for setup
text:
We use this in a very simple way: To keep a log of our weight. Since the Aria does the logging for us now, it's just a matter of stepping onto the scales each morning before dressing, so we do it more consistently.

As others have noted, the initial network setup is a bit of a mess. I gave up trying to do it with my desktop computer (and I have a Ph.D. in computer science and have a pretty easy time with most network configuration stuff). Doing it with a mobile phone worked, and that was a one-time process, so now it's ok.

If you're curious, the reason the setup process is so fidgety is that the scale is trying to discover which wireless network to connect to (yours or your neighbor's). It does this through a bit of a trick: the scale temporarily acts as a wi-fi base station, and the configuration program on your desktop machine attempts to drop the connection to your regular wi-fi, connect to the scale instead, communicate your usual wi-fi connection information to the scale, and then switch both your desktop computer and the scale to use your regular wi-fi again. Neat trick if it works, but there are lots of chances for things to go wrong, and not much you can do to trouble-shoot. Since switching from one wireless network to another is something that smart phones do pretty regularly, the trick works a little better there.

title: Just got it, Love it
text:
I was anticipating a ton of trouble setting this up after reading the reviews. Thankfully, it set up fairly fast and I didn't encounter any of the problems a lot of others have reported. I did set it up on a Mac, and I think most people have trouble setting up on a Windows computer. That said, my recommendations are as follows - 1) Make sure to disconnect your host computer's ethernet cables. This makes sure that the computer is using the wi-fi network that it will share with the Aria. 2) Pull the tab out of the battery compartment (without removing compartment cover, as instructions say) BEFORE running the set-up. 3) Download the software and get started. I think where people might be getting tripped up is by not disconnecting their ethernet cable on their host computer.

Anyway, the set-up did pretty much everything itself on a Mac. I didn't even need the network password as my mac shared it from the keychain after asking me if it was ok. The scale and the way it uploads and that information immediately synced to my fitbit app on the iPhone the next time I turned it on is pretty remarkable.

I'll follow up in a few weeks after daily use (what it's really designed for), but if it's anything like my fitbit flex, I think I'll be a happy camper. You have to be pretty committed to logging everything you eat and staying on top of it, but I think doing that has made me MUCH more aware of how many calories are in the foods that I'm eating (and drinks), and also I'm aware of days that I'm more sedentary. The other upside is that if you do work out, you'll be surprised how much you can eat since you'll be logging that and then eating back the exercise calories. It's just a healthier way to diet since I just eat normal foods but know when to cut back if I'm logging and tracking my activity level/calories burned. I'm hoping the scale makes this even better with the granularity of always knowing exactly where I stand in terms of weight loss.

title: Love this scale!
text:
This is the best scale I've ever owned.

* It measures to the 1/10th of a pound, which I find very helpful given that I'm only trying to lose about a pound a week, so less precise scales don't show me progress as often.

* The scale wirelessly uploads to the fitbit web site, so I don't have to do any work--I just step on the scale then I check charts of my progress on the web.

* The scale measures body fat percentage, which has been very motivating because I started doing basic weight training, so often I've seen my weight hold steady while body fat percentage has dropped (as my body replaces fat with muscle). A normal scale would show that I've made no progress.

I will say that about 1 in 10 times my body fat percentage reading is inaccurate (too much change from the prior reading), but I just delete those readings from the web site and all is good.

Overall, this scale has been my #1 tool in my effort to lose weight. I also bought a fitbit pedometer and if I could only buy one of them, I would buy the scale.

title: Product Setup
text:
Like many other reviewers, have to say that the ease of wifi setup leaves a lot to be desired. Have a Mac and am pretty tech savvy. Downloaded the setup software as instructed. Bottom line. After several attempts, could not get it to work. Even the "remove one battery" instruction did not activate the scale setup. Had to remove them all, and then finally got scale to activate. Then, downloaded software did not work after at least four or five attempts to configure system (maybe five minutes of futzing).

Then went directly to the website alternative. That worked like a charm and synching was completed quickly on the first try. Tested scale weight against my previous alternative, and weights were very close (about a .2 lb difference).

Liked the overall scale design from the outset, and out of the box, appears to be a high quality manufactured product. Will see.

In short, spent 10-15 minutes trying to get the scale to activate and sync with my wifi. Agree with other reviewers that there is no excuse for this inconvenience. And can easily understand why buyers would give up in frustration. Even in my case, don't know why the website worked and the downloaded app did not.

So am hoping all goes well from here, and if it does,my 4 star rating is probably justified, given the apparent product quality and functionality. But in some important respects, jury is still out. Could be I've been way too generous.

This simple battery-powered light, while somewhat dim, is a real blessing. I can continue reading at night in peace, without eye strain associated with traditional types of artificial light.
