And what is more, if you have rechargeable batteries, the device can even charge them (though this feature is somewhat crude, it never fully charges the batteries). I actually have two of these now, for reading hardcover technical books, I clamp one to the back cover, and another to the front cover. It works great, and does not disturb anyone.

The light is especially handy for College students, as if you have your laptop with you, even if it's not turned on, you can plug this light into one of your laptops USB ports and the light will use a very minuscule amount of your laptop's battery.

The only reason I would not give this a 5 is that the USB cable that comes with it is constructed very cheaply. I have a suspicion that the cable will be the first thing to fail, but I really cannot guess how long it will last.

title: there is no competition between administered bacteria and a lower daily dosage of 5 billion per dose is recommended. The bacteri
text:
The video done by the CEO, Kiril Petkov, I believe, is very interesting and quite convincing, especially for a lay audience. To summarize, a probiotic, L. bulgaricus GLB44, has been isolated from the snowdrop flower in Bulgaria. It was originally planned for use in unpasteurized vegetable juice to eliminate pathogenic bacteria. When it was found to be very active versus pathogenic bacteria while preserving normal bacteria flora (good bacteria), it was decided to manufacture it as a probiotic. In vitro studies done by Professor Onderdonk, director of clinical microbiology at Harvard's Brigham and Womens Hospital, are very supportive. One clinical trial in 20 subjects with H. pylori indicated elimination of H pylori without using any antibiotics in 18 of the 20 subjects. To date, I have not found a publication on this study. Anecdotal evidence indicates that it can be used by travelers (in Africa) to prevent adverse gi symptoms.

The probiotic is grown in a vegetable matrix and has no additives.It is sugar free, gluten free, yeast free, and allergen free. It is not a gas forming bacteria, so should cause no bloating or gas formation. It is reportable shelf stable and needs no refrigeration.

It has been contrasted with multi-strain probiotics. As there is only one strain in ProViotic, there is no competition between administered bacteria and a lower daily dosage of 5 billion per dose is recommended. The bacteria are reported to be much larger than those in other probiotics and more small peptide bacteriocins which are responsible for killing pathogenic bacteria, therefore, are produced.

While there is a need for clinical studies, ProViotic appears potentially to be a great product and I would be interested in trying some. It would be valuable to have studies in subjects with IBS as well as in SIBO (small intestinal bacterial overgrowth). I'd be interested to find out more details, such as the viability of the bacteria over time without refrigeration, the long term effect on stool flora, and plans for clinical research.

title: Not for the faint of heart...
text:
I bought one of these off of a co-worker this morning after he posted a picture of a can on social media last night. Something about the words "very strong stimulants" got my immediate and undivided attention. To be perfectly fair, my first experience with this was not exactly a fair one as I had drunk a Monster before coming into work. Something about ingesting 480mg of caffeine seemed like a great idea at the time. I'll try to do a timeline as best I can remember.

T-00:00 - I open Spike Shooter and take a sip. It actually tastes pretty good. I can't remember what it tastes like now because that feels like a lifetime ago but I remember it being pleasant.

T+00:30 - I definitely feel some jitters and the urge to talk more. Usually I'm a pretty succinct person but at this point I feel the need to pack conversation with additional words I usually deem unnecessary. I start using a manual surface grinder and notice that my rhythm and reflexes are much improved.

T+01:00 HOLY COW I'M TOTALLY GOING SO FAST I CAN GET ALL THE GRINDING DONE FOR TODAY AND THEN I CAN DO EVERYONE ELSE'S TOO. My left bicep is starting to crank up because of working the handle so fast but I ignore it. I get a notification I'm doing a tour for a bunch of high school students in half an hour.

T+01:30 Okay I'm here in the meeting room, ready to give a tour. There are twenty people in this room, the average number of hairs on their head is 3,562. Why is everyone else taking so long? I'm pretty sure if I stop moving I'm going to die. I'm gonna teach the SHIT out of these kids about everything.

T+01:40-05:00 - Who knows? I'm sure I acted perfectly normal and and in a calm and professional manner.

T+05:30 - Definitely crashing. Not sure if I'm going to throw up or shit my pants, maybe both. I've been sweating so much over the past few hours it smells like I took a swim in malt vinegar.

By using the Sacro Wedgy about 20 - 25 minutes per day the tightness that has inhibited my activity is virtually eliminated.  As the manufacturers state, this product is not an immediate cure-all for lower back and hip pain.  Along with regular usage of this product, I will be practicing yoga, Pilates and light weight training to improve both my strength and flexibility in order to get back to full activity and a fuller range of motion/flexibility.  The specific value of this product is that it provides an extended period of relaxation (the traction effect) to the pelvic girdle and the muscles in that region in a way that stretching/yoga don't accomplish.

title: Good concept. Needs refining.
text:
As a quadriplegic with fair hand function, I was looking for a tool like this to avoid relying on someone else to cut my food for me. I was very excited to try this concept! I believe with some tweaks, you would be on to something:
1.) The utensil is quite heavy. The handle is a pretty good size but the fork and blade are too heavy making it difficult for weak ha d function to hold.
2.) The blades go up the side so when taking a bite, they touch the lips. Someone with a shaky hand could cut themselves. Also, the side blades are unnecessary. As they don’t really cut the food but trap it onto the fork instead. If you made the back blade sharper, the side blades wouldn’t be needed.
3.) I tried the fork with a salad and a steak. The lettuce got stuck in the back of the blade against the fork making it difficult to pick out. I was unable to cut the steak even pressing down a few times.

Again, it’s a great concept but it’s not quite there yet.

text:
I am not an expert on applying makeup at all.
I have always been very interested in skincare. I have spent ( and continue to do so ) hours and hours researching skincare products.
My skincare products are clean, non toxic, beneficial and effective.
Over the last year I started researching makeup that were equally healthy. I wear a minimum amount but it seemed ridiculous after cleansing and hydrating my skin to then apply makeup filled with toxic ingredients.
Two months ago, my daughter bought me a beauty blender sponge to use to apply my makeup instead of all the brushes. It was indeed much easier for me to use and simplified my makeup application.
But in my research I came across the silicone makeup sponge.
I ordered it and have been using it for a week now.
As described far less makeup is absorbed and wasted as compared to the beauty blender sponge.
I like the texture and it feels so much cleaner as well.
I gave it 4 stars, because of its shape. That is where the beauty blender is superior. I would love it if it had a round bottom to make application of makeup easier to use on my cheeks, chin and forehead.
But the pros definitely outweigh this con and I will continue to use the silicone makeup sponge.
Hope to see a new version with some reshaping in the near future.

title: 85 year old Dad loves it!
text: I bought this for my 85 year old Dad to soak in the bath tub with! He loves it! The bubbles are great for his circulation. He is using a bath tub "Lift chair" so I put that on top of this matt and have no issues with keeping it in place. I don't think it is extra loud at all like some people are saying? It certainly does a good job and makes my Dad smile!

title: To sum it up
text:
Ok so as other commented, the suction cups did not stick. Plain and simple, suction cups generally never work on anything correctly. That was a given, I expected that. Don't get me wrong, if the suction cups worked it would probably be even better.
But, I was amazed at how powerful that pump was. Someone mentioned that if they put the connector part down by their feet the bubbles did not reach their back, or vise versa. So I tried it first coming from my feet. Yes the mat floats all over. But, the issue with the bubbles not reaching all the way through is the positioning of the connector, if the tube is pointed one way the bubbles will only go so far, but if moved a different way it will shoot bubbles all through the mat. It's all about the positioning. I then switched the mat to have the connector by my head. Same thing, if positioned differently the results are different. Although some people may not like that, I found it relaxing. I was able to manipulate the mat with me feet or back or knees to have the bubbles shoot out in one local area, or flowing perfectly through the entire mat. I have bad knees and bad back, and if I let the mat float up against my knees most the bubbles came full force out where my knees were. That felt great on them. I did the same to my back. This mat is all about positioning it correctly for what you want out of it.
As some said, the pump is loud. But, what pump isn't? If your in a hot tub, is that not loud? If your in a jet bathtub, is that not loud? I have a tiny bathroom, so of course it was decently loud. If it bothers you, put in some ear plugs or maybe some noise canceling head phones. Either way it was relaxing.
Now it's supposed to heat your water to help maintain the temperature. I can't say it did that. But it could have, I really don't know. My baths are already hot, and not to mention I have the window open (and it's 30 degrees out), so that could affect that part, I can't really say.
I did read someone say it smelled funny when it arrived. It's plastic, most every new thing that is plastic smells at first. But goes away.
When I bought the mat, I knew it wouldn't stick to the bottom, I knew that it had a pump which is going to make noise. But honestly, it was well worth it. It was relaxing, kind of fun just to manipulate it to bubble more in one spot than another. Made me feel great and relaxed. I would recommend it. Can't wait to take another bath and use it.

He had tried a bunch of different socks to try to cushion it, but it caused the casting to not fit right. He didn't want me to spend money on anything, but I thought, hey, if this works, it's money well spent! They worked great! They don't interfere with the fitment of the new casting (apologies, I don't know the proper term for this part of the prosthetic) or the socks at all, as they are super thin, and they help ease the friction of the bone in the stump rubbing against the inner wall of the casting. He told me he was actually able to run for 30 minutes, which he hasn't been able to do since the incident. Now he carries them with him everywhere. Overall, a great product, easy to use, durable material, machine washable, and made in the good ol' US of A. Highly recommended!

title: Wish I Spoke Japanese
text:
I wish I would have reviewed Godzilla Returns way back when I recieved that one. Now I have a chance to talk about both, sort of.
This is a direct to Japan version of this movie, with no English track or titles. Fortunately there is an option for English subtitles. And for me, that's really enough. This is a well done movie and now that I look at it, one of the best from the Heisei Godzilla series. It has great elements of classic sci-fi as well as a very sincere feel, similar to the origional 1954 Gojira. The scientist father character is compelling with his duel wreckless and wise natures. He's a character who learns from his mistakes, and actually lives long enough to pass this wisdom to others. His is a great, tragic character arc. This is the first movie to use Godzilla's standard Heisei look, and I think it's pulled off quite well here. He's a slow, lumbering character, but the point is, it doesn't matter how slow he is or if you can spot him. Because you can't stop him! Te close ups of his face are fantastic. I really like the detail on the fleshy tongue. And Biolante is one of the great classic, tragic monsters. She's dangerious, deadly, devious, but has the trapped soul of a lovely girl.
As for the DVD itelf, it's pretty basic. There are vew special fetures or options, but as this is the only official DVD release for this film, that automatically makes it the best. The video quality is somewhat lacking too, but nothing you're not used to if you grew up watching these movies on TV as a kid. But I can see this being somewhat of a dissapointment for many, as there is no English dub. Again, that's fine by me, but it is a little harder trying to watch this with friends who refuse to watch a movie with subtitles. But to be honest, the 80s/90s series had some pretty weak English voice talent, and hearing the origional actors is kind of nice. Also there's a bonus special feature at the end, after credits. It's about a 40 minute behind the scenes spot, that shows quite a bit of detail on making the film. This is a rare thing for 80s films in general, so it's kind of nice. Again, it's a little tough going with no English to stand on, but the behind the scenes visuals themselves are nice! I still with whatever studio holds the American distribution rights would hurry up and for this thing over already! Or better yt, give it to Classic Media so they can do what they did with the Godzilla movies they release!

title: Excellent replacement Qlink!
text:
Bought this about 3 months ago to replace my acrylic version. I wore the acrylic version for nearly 10 years and finally managed to put a crack in it, I finally caved in and bought this as a replacement. I really wanted the titanium version of this pendant but couldn't find it through Amazon. It's actually a little nicer than the titanium version, smoother edges and no raised edges anywhere, nice weight that keeps the pendant hanging right where I want it - which was a problem with the acrylic version; it would creep up the string or the chain that I had it hanging on and end up in my armpit or hung up on the chain link or the knot. Beautiful quality. I can see this one lasting me at least another 10 years or more.

Caveat: it comes with a string rather than a chain. I would suggest picking up a chain made of the SAME metal - stainless steel. I put mine on a cheapo aluminum ball chain and the stainless steel pendant would dig into the softer metal of the aluminum chain. There are tons of options for chains out there, just be sure that the chain material is stronger than the pendant or you'll end up with a broken chain!

title: We were using Gerber soothe drops and they made a very noticeable difference but the design of the bottle is absolutely terrible, so I wanted to try a different probiotic ...
text:
I really wanted this to work. Little man has trouble passing gas and stool on his own. We were using Gerber soothe drops and they made a very noticeable difference but the design of the bottle is absolutely terrible, so I wanted to try a different probiotic with dropper. The liquid is in this like a very runny oil. My 6 month old choked a little almost every time he was given these drops which wasn’t really a big deal, but almost the same day we switched to Upspring drops we noticed him go right back to struggling to poop. I thought, maybe it’s just a change to his system. I’ll give it a week and see. A week turned into two weeks, and even though he got the same dose, the same time every day, he was straining all the time and often waking up at night uncomfortable because he needed to pass gas.

Again, I REALLY wanted to love this product so I kept waiting but finally switched back to Gerber. Could be a coincidence, but he’s already going poo regularly again and he’s slept great at night ever since we went back.

I believe this product may be able to help some babies. It just didn’t work for mine. Disappointed in the time and money spent on it.

title: High-Quality, Precise Images, Variety for all Occasions
text:
It's spring, so I don't know what that means for you, but for me that means the season of Thank You notes has arrived. Mother's Day, Graduation, End-of-the-Year Teacher Gifts, Bridal Showers, Baby Showers, Weddings, Births, Birthdays. . . . it's all jam-packed into spring/summer. This box of 100 sweet thank you cards is just the thing to get you through the season.

You get ten cards of each design, which means that for each occasion, I can send one style. This cuts down on the "did I send her the daisies or the daffodils last time?" moment of confusion. (Yes, I like to make sure I send different cards to people. I don't want to send the same card over and over to my Mom -- let's face it -- she already bought me all those different presents for all of those different occasions. .. she deserves variety from me. :) )

The card stock is high quality -- this was something I was a bit concerned about when I ordered. I thought because the images were of flowers and signs that on the actual cards the images would be less precise and the cardstock would be on the lower end. (I rarely find floral designs that are crisp and high quality, so I was skeptical.) When I pulled each of the images out of the (cute) box, I was ecstatic. Each one was precise and the quality of cardstock used was incredibly high. The envelopes are also a substantial weight and are self-sealable. Yes, no more licking! Yay!

Truly, the fact that I get ten cards of ten different precise/high quality designs, means I won't be sending duplicates to anyone. Selecting one style for each occasion will keep me organized and happy. These sweet cards will make their recipients as happy as they make me.

text:
We purchased two other brands of reishi from a retail store in capsules (each around $25-30) but was too anxious to wait. Both brands of opened capsules tasted like a very dark chocolate = full of fillers. Continuing my search I found this Real Mushrooms brand who has ALL the information I was looking for including where it's sourced from/grown, polysaccharide content, all ingredients, how it was extracted and that it's bitter! All the reviews backing this up are true. It's more expensive, however I've already learned you get what you pay for with reishi.

It's only been about 4 days taking it daily so I can't say if I notice anything yet. I read vitamin C helps break down the polysaccharides leading to higher absorption, so I mix 1,000mg of real vitamin C from HealthSource with water (do not take abscorbic acid as it's linked with arterial plaque, gallstones, who knows what else), take a big sip of the C water, then dump 1/4 tsp reishi directly onto my tongue, then gulp down the rest of the C water to flush the bitterness out of my mouth. Also found some info that taking it on an empty stomach first thing in the morning (if you can handle it) , plus extra water "helps flush poisons from your system." Today I started doing that and my stomach handled it fine and I've felt remarkably calm despite being a normal workday, so there may be something to it!

Luckily we were able to return the originally purchased bottles for full refunds and now have an actual source!

text:
I am a side sleeper and I have a chronic problem with tingling in my hands due to the weight of my head against my arm even though my arm is under the pillow. I was searching for a side sleeper pillow when I came across this SlumberSleeve. I figured it was worth the chance to try for $25 but I really had almost no expectation at all that it would work. However, I am simply stunned how effective this product is. It immediately alleviated my numbness problem and as a huge extra benefit, I am sleeping much better and waking up much more rested.

I think the key to this product is to be sure to follow the directions and after fitting it to your arm, set it 2 notches wider. This allows the sleeve to flatten out in an oval which gives it a bit of a bounce and flexibility so it is more comfortable for your head. The key is for it to flex but not so much that the product itself is resting on your arm.

title: So-So Design
text:
Did the cleanse. Whatever. This review is about this bottle specifically.

Biggest issue, is that the shape of the bottle at the top makes it impossible to finish your drink. The 90-degree angle that joins the bottle to the lip always will hold and retain some beverage. Once your liquid does make it over this ill-conceived geometric obstacle, the opening is wide and uncomfortable.

The bottle itself is of good, strong, durable plastic. I actually wish more reusable plastic bottles were made with this material integrity. Can't say so much for the black cap. It's kind of cheap, and the only carrying method is by the cap strap thing.

I like the measuring lines on the back, and the lemon dude makes me smile. Post-cleanse, I only use this bottle on rare occasions. Actually can't remember the last time I pulled it down from the top of my fridge.

Bottom Line: Get it if you want a cool lemon dude to remind you that you're doing the cleanse every time you reach for your cayenne maple lemonade. Don't get it if you want a great water bottle post-cleanse.

title: Crunchy people unite! Unlimited uses and stored in GLASS!
text:
You CAN'T get any better than organic, extra virgin coconut oil.
Seriously, the applications here are ENDLESS.
I frequently call myself crunchy. I am a big organic choosing person, I like natural remedies, I don't vaccinate my kids, I love homeopathic remedies. I may be a controversy and you may not agree with me. Hell, you may hate me.
But we can all agree that a high quality coconut oil has so many applications. I have seen articles listing 101 uses for coconut oil, and guess what? They're not wrong.
There are a lot of reasons why I will choose this brand of oil over the pre-packaged Costco mix. For starters. this oil is shipped safely and is in GLASS. I am so anti-plastic it's unreal and this oil is stored in glass. In the past, when my oil would come, I would transfer it to glass to avoid the plastic exposure. But with this brand, I don't have to do that!
I love that it's organic and virgin. Before the natural movement, nothing was organic.
I have a few applications I want to share and I hope, besides cooking, you use these.
For one, if you love Thai or Asian food, that you take the time to make fried chicken for curry or stir fry with this oil. It doesn't handle high heat (it isn't meant to) but it certainly fries up small pieces of chicken deliciously and it's a healthy, beautiful MCT fat strand oil to use for this purpose. Everything you've heard about deep fried goes out the window when you use this oil. Heat the pan. heat the oil. and cook delicious chicken. I promise you won't regret it.
The next thing I want to talk about is a hair mask. Go get your essential oils if you're like me for this one because that's going to help.
If you have dry hair, this is the best thing ever. I have colour treated hair (it's a vegan dye, but my hair is naturally dark brown, so yes -- I have to unnaturally lift it to white blonde to get the colour I want)-- without coconut oil I am positive my hair would be fried and dry.
Once a week, I take a high quality oil such as this, and I mix in 2 drops lavender, 2 drops sweet basil, 2 drops rosemary, 2 drops cedarwood, and 2 drops thyme. Mix thoroughly. I generally have 6-8 tbsp of oil for my hair, although I have long hair (to my bust line). Stir vigorously until combined.
Apply to your hair, from root to tip (mostly tip) until saturated and then braid or clip your hair up for the afternoon. I love to put on a hankerchief and do my thing for the day. Rinse with a great shampoo until it doesn't feel greasy anymore. This is such a great hair treatment and while you rinse, at least spend 1-2 minutes massaging your scalp. This encourages hair growth. As a woman having had 3 kids, this is great for my hormonal imbalance that doesn't want my hair to grow. Add biotin and garlic and watch your hair grow like crazy!
Got dry nail beds? Massage nightly into nails and watch your nails grow like crazy. Biotin, again, is a great addition here. Push back your cuticles gently while you massage the oil into your nail beds.
Got body aches? Add a few drops of lavender oil and massage onto areas of the body that need an analgesic affect and soothe sore muscles.
Need a lubricant that doesn't quit? Plain coconut oil will be the greatest sexual lubricant you'll ever use. I actually smell coconut oil and get turned on now. My husband LOVES it. Real talk.
Dry skin on your baby? Cradle cap? Coconut oil.
Dry hands and feet in the winter? Coconut oil.
Tanning in the summer? Coconut oil.
Like, staphhhh. The greatest essential oil carrier alive.
I can't say enough good things.
I got this oil at a discount in exchange for my review and I couldn't be happier.
Buy this oil. It's value is worth it (undiscounted!) and it's stored in glass. Keeps my crunchy counterparts from taking an extra worthwhile step.

title: FANTASTIC for what it's worth
text: These bars are fantastic! I have been on a strict anti-sugar, anti-dairy and anti-gluten diet for over a year now for medical reasons and these fit the bill providing something that soothes my appetite and is tasty to boot. I also really appreciate that the ingredients are completely understandable and straightforward--no added fluff. Does it really taste like a salted caramel cube? Absolutely not. Is it really cake-like? Only if it's left in the hot sun.  It's a little softer than the consistency of one of the original power bars. But if you have truly eliminated sugar and gluten and dairy and truly want a Paleo experience, then these are absolutely heaven. Full of protein and fiber and with a little sweetness and caramel flavor-they are about as good as I have found (and believe me, I've both shopped and made them myself) for a true Paleo bar. It's all about the expectations, folks. If you want to try and truly compare this to something it's not, then this is not the bar for you. These travel well and make great meal substitutes when I am very busy.

text:
Does it really mix up lump free? Well, not without an immersion blender. The problem is the immersion blender creates a froth with an amazingly amoxicillin aftertaste. The scent is definitely reminiscent of amoxicillin as well. The warmer the water, the easier it dissolves, but the more pronounced the aftertaste becomes.

My personal solution has been to mix with hot tap water and an immersion blender, followed by addition of some ice mixed to a slushy consistency; then gently stir in enough lukewarm water to bring it to a temperature you can comfortably just chug-down-and-get-it-over-with. The alternative, for an additional 150 calories or so is to dump in a container of Chobani greek yogurt with fruit and blend to the consistency of a "smoothy"; the pomegranate and blueberry flavors mask the amoxicillin aftertaste best.

Realistically, this is a flavor that can be lived with day in, day out, without retching.

UPDATE: 8/26/2012

So I decided to give this product another try after my favorite toner ran out (I hate to waste), and I would have to say there are a some good and bad points to it. I have been using it for about a little over a month now and here are some of my observations.

---------------------------------
-I'm certain that it helps to push out new skin cells because I had a few acne scar spots that dried up (they were scabs at the time) and healed up after a few days of using the toner. Beware: It stings horribly on open skin!

-Keeps any sort of acne congestion from developing (I have that issue around my jawline) which is always a good thing.

-Still makes my skin itch when I apply the toner, but overall it's not as bad as it used to be. I try to only use it at night and sometimes take a break for a day or two to give my face a breather if I notice my skin is looking a bit over-worked.

-Prepare to see all the gunk underneath your skin surface! I had to endure a bit of a breakout that emerged as my skin cells were turning over due to the prep refresher. I found myself at the mirror every other day doing extractions, but it has gotten better after a few weeks since I've found less and less to extract. I've also avoided wearing foundation on a daily basis as to not stir up any other acne.
---------------------------------

From my initial review, I gave this toner another star because it's done pretty much everything it says (minus the healthy looking complexion, I'm still waiting on that) but have not decided to give it 4 stars since I believe there are other products out there that are less harsh and can accomplish the same things. Despite that, I would still recommend anyone considering purchasing the prep refresher to give this product a try.

title: Good for two in the tub at once
text:
This is not my first kid - and therein was my dillema. How to fit a baby and a toddler in the same bathtub? For kid #1, we got the inflatable duckie tub (munchkin, I think) and it was fantastic for a baby learning how to sit. It got moldy right around the time that he was ready for the big tub all himself, so we tossed it and were fine. And then we had another one. :) Duckie tub was going to be my go-to item, but it's too big to fit in the tub along with another kid. We really wanted both kids to have fun in the tub together, but this is a tall order at these ages.

I found this and it looked like the best option. For our purposes, it works great. It's like having a third hand in the bathtub for your kid. It will not save your kid from disaster, for sure, you need to be right there. But my 7 month old has figured it out, tried to plop face forward, and still has been able to prop herself back up, no issue. It all depends on your baby's development and personality, and how you use it.

It does weigh a ton after bathtime, but we've been drying it out per instructions and have had no issue (we're one month in).

If we were just bathing one kid at a time, I'd probably go for the duckie tub again. But since we have two, it really has helped. It's let me wash them both at the same time, the older one gets to help a little more, and I don't have the slippery soapy baby issue anymore. She's gotten more time to splash and play in the tub too since I don't have to wisk her out of the tub as soon as she's clean. Glad I got this. :)

text:

I pulled out the box (just a white discreet box, but the label says "dildo" on it, so beware) and was nervous about the immense size of it. I pulled it out of the box and was amazed at its length and girth and knew I'd have to prep myself.

After some getting used to, it's amazing! Definitely fun to play with, mixing up the play style. You can insert at your own pace, and twisting it around would be a knew experience you wouldn't feel from other basic toys. The toy itself is flexible (there is a video in the Q&A section to show), and it takes some effort but if you squeeze it, it has a firm softness. However, I would disagree with some of the other reviews - I don't think it is for beginners. You will need a lot of working up to it, but it is worth it. Because of its unique features and shapes (many grooves and ridges), it is definitely a different and unique experience.

There is a line down the middle where I supposed the two halves were put together which takes away from the overall look, but you may not even notice it if you don't look close enough. As for cleaning, it is obviously going to be a bit tougher to get clean since there are so many ridges, so make sure you give it a good clean and wiping down before putting it away!

Overall, if you are a bit more experienced or adventurous, I would give it a recommend just for fun!

title: Finally figured out that Crest Pro Health is causing my slime!
text:
No drama here, this toothpaste does literally peel off a thin layer on all gum surfaces, and it peels off in a slime. I spend a half hour in the morning, after brushing, getting the slime out of my mouth or it gums up into yucky little blobs. Two months ago I had 4 impacted wisdom teeth removed and at the same time I happened to buy Crest Pro Health. I had been attributing my problems to my surgery, but eventually I realized that my surgery was completely healed and through a process of elimination, it was the Crest Pro Health. My husband is always complaining that my breath smells like chemicals and he was concerned that my surgeon had left something "medical" in my gums! But that is not the case.

I have always liked Crest products, but it seems that this one in particular has some problems. I don't even want to know what kind of ingredient/chemical is causing the skin to peel off. It seems iffy enough, to probably avoid this product, until it has been around for a few more years and more problems are noticed.

I have not noticed any staining, but I also do not have any plaque on my teeth at this time.

And my mouth and breath never tastes fresh and clean with this toothpaste. I feel self concious about it even right after brushing, as if I hadn't brushed at all!

text:
I have had the chair for one week. Am returning. The shape in appearance is nice, will fit in small places. The chair is not a light color nor a dark color but far darker than the photos. It is like a desert sand color. It does have a warehouse smell to it. The wood is much darker in color, like a dark cherry wood.
The real problems are that the chair screws nor the tension knobs, "grip" The ottoman screws would not screw all the way down, which leaves it either wobbly or I suppose, the screws could be forced down and then what? ... Because the arm rail screws will not grip, after one week, both arm rests are loose and creaky when you sit down and especially if the vibration is on. I weigh 120lbs. The tension rods have no grib whatsoever and are just sitting in place where they should screw in and out for tension. The tension rods are a mystery to me, they just do not fit (maybe a manufacturing flaw) since I purchased the chair new. IF you have muscle spasms at all, RUN from this chair. It does not recline smoothly at all and brings on instant spasms, at least for me! The chair could be oiled? The screws corrected? BUT, I do not want to pull maintenance on this chair every other week or so. And eventually......, well, you get the picture.
I don't usually write reviews, but thought this might help someone. Also, please note: I read the previous reviews before I purchased the chair. Alot of the above had been mentioned, but I thought maybe the assembly had not been done correctly - however, it appears that other purchasers are experiencing the same issues.

title: Sloppy.
text:
1. Not easy to put together.
Poor instructions and screws that are not the size they are supposed to be and do not fit in the holes they were designated to fit in. To be more specific, there are 4 screws labeled "K" to make it easier to identify them for the step in which the arm cushions are attached to the chair. 2 of those screws are different than the other 2. And only 2 of the screws fit into the arm cushion attachment.

Now I have to go to Lowes or Home Depot and find 2 more screws that will fit. Doesn't seem worth it to return the entire chair for 2 screws.

Plus, some of the other instructions need just a little more detail. For example, the instructions state that you should attach the seat to the back. But they don't tell you that the back attachments should fit on the outside of the seat attachments. It is VERY difficult to get the two to line up so once I had the first attachment location lined up, I put the screw in (back on inside, seat on outside). Now to the other side. Ooops! Doesn't come close to fitting. Not hard to fix. But annoying that they couldn't tell me that simple but necessary detail in the instructions.

And the color does not match the picture of the product. You can see by the picture of the product it looks like a sandy brown. The chair that I received is a chocolatey brown. Luckily, that color still works in our room. But come on! Again, sloppy.

I may update later when the chair is actually together and I can determine if the trouble was worth it. But for now, 1 star because I cannot give it 0.

title: Did not do what is says it will do
text: The city where I live in New Mexico has some pretty brutal tap water. I tested it with a calibrated water tester and it read 737 ppm on the tester. on the back of this tester it states that 500ppm is the maximum allowable by current standards. I mixed the Adya clarity per the directions on the bottle to 2.5 gallons of tap water and let it sit for 24 hours. Took another test reading and it dropped to 608ppm. The directions on the bottle state that you may have to add more adya clarity to obtain the desired results. So I added four more teaspoons to my 2.5 gallons of tap water. Again I let it sit for 24 hours. This time the test results indicated that the ppm level went from 608ppm up to 686ppm. So it didn't decrease the toxic ppm levels, it actually increased them. So I poured out all 2.5 gallons of water, and that's when I noticed that the adya clarity had left a very noticeable yellowish residue in the bottom of the water container. So I then took purified drinking water from the store, poured it in a clear drinking glass and tested it, and the reading was 19ppm. I wanted to see if the adya clarity would reduce the ppm level from 19ppm down to around 0ppm. Again I added the adya clarity to it in a clear drinking glass and let it sit for a little over 24 hours. I tested it again, but once again instead of reducing the ppm level it increased it. The test reading after adding the adya clarity came in at 86ppm, and once again it caused the purified water in the clear drinking glass to have a yellowish tint to it. I am writing this review on June 18, 2019. I tried to contact Adya Water to speak with them about this very morning but have not yet heard back from them. At the time of writing this review, I would not suggest getting this product.

text:
I bought this for my wife, who just have birth and was suffering from terribly swollen feet.

As soon as the package arrived I was anxious to get it running asap. Unfortunately I found that the bubbles did not work at all. After looking online I found that this has happened to others - one review found a kink in the air hose between the blower moter and the water jets.

In our case I found that the one-way valve between the motor and the air hose seemed to have been installed the wrong way around. After correcting that and putting it back together - all is good now. My wife loves it and thinks it's an 8/10 (she gets pedicures every once in a while so she knows what her feet need to feel good).

I would love to give it five stars for the way my wife enjoys it, but having to dismantle it to get it working would be an issue for anyone not willing to do some DIY surgery.

title: Top notch Beard trimmer
text:
I put the Breadscape Pro head to head against the Andis Slimline Pro GTX. It was honestly a very difficult decision between the two. I ultimately went with the Andis Slimline, because it fit my needs better. It is no slight to the Breadscape. In many ways the Beardscape was the superior unit. However, in a few key areas the Andis slimline design was the deciding factor.

Build Quality: Both seem to be solid units. I did hear some reports of issues with the Andis on/off switch and I will admit, it doesn't feel very solid. I could see this being an issue for a heavy use/barber. However it feels solid enough for a home user. The Beardscape on the other hand feels very solid. It has weight and just looks and feels like a solid unit. Winner: Bearscape

Unit Size and Design: This is one of those key factors that I think hold more weight than some of the other categories. Both have a good design. However the Andis slim feel gives it the edge. The Beardscape is no slouch. It is a beautiful device. Looks and feels really well made. The blade design to remove is easy to use. The beards cape is a larger unit. It size compared to the Andis Slimline is the only knock. The Andis feels wonderful in your hand. Yes it does feel a bit less quality do to being lighter, but the size is pure perfection. The Beardscape is just a little too big. At times it can be more difficult to see around. Making edge work and highly detailed trimming easier to do with the Andis. Winner: Andis Slimline

Blade: The Beardscape came with an adjustable blade. On it's lowest setting it was near zero. Very close to the Andis Slimline GTX blade. The GTX blade is as close to a zero blade as I think you can get. Very close. The GTX is metal on top and bottom. The Beardscape standard blade is Metal on the bottom and plastic up top. Makes me wonder about the longevity of the standard blade, however in my limited time with the unit, the standard blade it cut well. However if you get Beardscape pro it also comes with a zero blade and it is a true zero blade. Metal top and bottom and zero gap. The one major advantage of the Andis GTX blade it is a T blade, versus the Beardscape's straight blade. For detail work, the T blade is again easier to see around and do that fine work. Also the GTX is a more narrow blade, again making it easier for detail work. The GTX is the perfect blade width and design. Overall declaring a winner, I have to call it a draw. If you get the standard Beardscape, the winner is the Andis GTX blade. Cuts a little closer, more narrow and easier to see around. If you throw in the Beardscape Pro's zero blade it becomes much tougher to declare a winner. Depends on what you are after. If you want that true zero blade closeness, then the Bearscape zero blade is the winner. If you want a detail trimmer, the Andis GTX is the winner. Winner: Draw

Power: The Andis Slimline has a single speed. it is lighter and I'm betting houses less battery power. The Beardscape has 5 speed settings which alter your batter life and speed of the blade. The Bearscape on it's lowest setting sounded to be about the same speed as the Andis. Ultimately they both cut really well, so while I will declare the bears cape the clear winner, both seemed to have plenty of power to get the job done and never had a problem. Winner: Beardscape

Battery Life: The Andis Slimline has a single speed. it is lighter and I'm betting houses less battery power. The Beardscape has 5 speed settings which alter your batter life. I ran both units for a little under a month, shaving like every other day. Both had enough battery life that they didn't need a charge. The Beardscape has an LED screen and clearly tells you where it is battery life is. It's weight also just feels like it's loaded with plenty of battery power. At the rate I was using it, it felt like it could have gone 6 month between charging on the lowest speed setting. Winner: Beardscape

Features, Extras & Kit: Both units came with a charging base and some clipper guards. The Andis came with 4 guards and no case. Opening the Beardscape reminded me of opening an Apple device. Just the design and presentation were next level. Beautiful box, beautiful case that had a felt liner and a spot for everything, including the addition of the Pro zero blade. It had 4 dual sided guards which again have their own spot in the case. The case is not small, so if travel size is an issue this might be overkill. However the case is ready to take your clipper and all it's extras with you on the go. Winner: Beardscape

Charging Base: Both have an optional charging base. They can travel with just the cord and not require the base. however the charging base was a requirement for me that drew me to these two units and they both do the job. The Andis base is smaller so it takes up less real estate on your counter. But Beardscape's base is not much larger. The Beardscape's base also has a specific direction, where as the Andis was a circular plug, thus not unidirectional. Not a big deal either way. Winner: Draw

Final Verdict: Both solid units and I think anyone would be happy with either. The Beardscape is the better all around unit. It's a leatherman's tool. Does it all and does it well. The Andis is also a great al around clipper, but it's more of a scalpel. It's smaller design and more narrow T blade make detail work easier than the beard scape. It's near zero blade gives a shave that, to me, is almost indistinguishable from the Beardscape's Zero blade. I got this unit to keep my cheeks and neck clean, and knock down the hairs that spring out for the beard base. The Andis is the superior tool for this specific job. Now if you want to use the guards to trim down your beard, the Beardscape has a lot more lengths and options. Note the guards do not fit over the zero blade. You have to put the Beardscape's standard blade to use the guards. Another thing to note in my case. I also have a really nice Wahl Elite corder clippers that has a bunch of high quality guards and different lengths. Thus I already have a unit that can use guards to trim my beard. So this was a bit of overlap with the Beardscape. If you are looking for one unit that does everything, the beards cape is a fantastic unit. If trimming those precision areas is your primary goal, the Andis Slimline Pro GTX is your best bet. I went wit the GTX for this reason. Hope this helps any guys weighing a similar decision.

title: Best thing for red bottoms!
text: I am not one to typically post reviews, but I had to share in this case. My new husband bought me these as wedding shoes, and I wanted something to keep them in as best condition as possible. I read the reviews here and was apprehensive due to the ones that said removing these peeled off the red lacquer. That would defeat the purpose. However, if these are applied properly and removed properly, they are AMAZING! Read the directions carefully, apply with water and let sit for at least 24 hours. I did this and then wore them for my dress rehearsal and wedding ceremony (couldn’t wear them much longer, the prettier the shoe the more painful and let me tell ya, these are the prettiest shoes I have ever worn).  But those times included walking on concrete and you can see in the pics with the seal still on, it definitely got scuffed off. It has been a month since the wedding and I finally got the courage to try and remove them, as long as you heat with a hair dryer and peel slowly, you will have no problem! You can see there are some indentions on the bottom, but no scuffing! I have these on other pairs of red bottoms I own as well, and I can see how they may only last you one or 2 wears and then you need to apply a new set, but definitely worth it in my opinion! I highly recommend for those trying to extend the life you you Louboutins!

title: White, Bright and Ultimately Impressed with Fast Results
text: Dreows Teeth Whitening Kit works so good I decided to space my applications out. I experienced visible results after just a one time use. I started boiling water while I re-read over the instructions just to make sure I didn't miss anything. Then I put two trays in a mug with the boiled water and let soak between 5 and 10 minutes. Immediately insert one on upper teeth and lower teeth and bite down to mold till teeth feel firm in place. You may have to resubmerge in water again to get a good fit. Then apply one half of a syringe of whitening gel to each tray. I suggest setting a timer for 10 or 20 minutes. I did 20 minutes for my initial application. If you have sensitive teeth or develop sensitivity than you may want to try 10 minutes. The whitening gel has a pleasant minty taste and no gritty texture but try not to swallow any gel.Take the batteries out of the handheld LED light, remove the plastic piece on bottom, reinsert the batteries and turn on the light holding it against the trays with teeth clenched but keeps lips tucked up to expose the teeth to the light. Expect to drool, it is only human nature, but keep a washcloth nearby! Once your 10 - 20 minutes is up remove the trays, thoroughly rinse both your mouth and the trays out. I was immediately trilled with the results. Yellowing was so light, areas that were not as stained prior to application were impressively white. I could not be more satisfied the results of this product and after only a one time. I did notice my teeth were slightly more sensitive but not painful to cold or hot and gentle on my gums. I received Dreow Teeth Whitening Kit at a discount to give my honest and unbiased review and I stand by this product. As does the company with their 100% hassle free money back guarantee. No more hiding your smile, at an extremely affordable price you can have the smile you deserve and will want to show off!

title: Helps lazy people like me - reduce the amount of deep scrubbing you need to do!
text:
I am super addicted to this stuff.. My wife and I spray it religiously after each use of the shower and it has minimized the amount of deep cleaning we have to do.

As new homeowners we were not aware that you need to maintain your shower not only with regular cleaning but also ideally with the occasional deep scrub, and -wait for it- grout sealing. We didn't learn this until a few years in but better late than never! The first deep scrub took a lot of elbow grease and some foul smelling chemicals, so we vowed to stay on top of routine cleaning to never have to do that again (or at least keep it to a minimum).

In comes this miracle product to save the day! I'm sure other similar daily shower sprays work just as well, but we just really like the scent of this one (thanks to a reviewer on a different grout/tile product for the tip). All you have to do is spray the walls, tub, and curtain after you shower and just walk away. You probably don't need to EVERY time but why not? Just leave it next to the tub and unleash a couple of blasts on your way out.

It has made a huge difference. I'm sure the grout sealing helped, but there hasn't been any noticeable pink staining on our tiled shower walls ever since. We used to buy this at the local big box stores but the ones nearest to us stopped selling this particular one. Luckily Amazon still sells this stuff and will hopefully continue!

title: Packaging is misleading
text:
We use the Bumgenius 4.0 hook and loop pocket diapers and up until last week were using the ImseVimse diaper liners. I decided to try your brand of liners because they were a little cheaper on Amazon. At first glance I was impressed with their softness (the ImseVimse have more of a dryer sheet texture to them). They are slightly bigger than the ImseVimse, so I feel they do a little better job catching poo. However, the packaging is very misleading. On the packaging there is a little icon that says "wash and reuse" near the graphic showing how to use the liners. I was excited to see this because with the ImseVimse ones, we wash them with the diapers and get about 5-6 uses out of them if they have only been in pee diapers. So, based upon the Real Nappies packaging I assumed these could be washed as well. Boy was I wrong. Last night we washed our diapers with only one Real Nappies liner in the wash and it managed to clog up every single hook and loop tab on all the diapers. Needless to say after an hour of picking liner pieces out of the velcro, we were far from impressed. I now wish I would have payed closer attention to the reviews on Amazon where the owner of Real Nappies responded to comments of the liners not being washable saying they were for single use only. Given this, the slightly more expensive ImseVimse are a better value for us since we can reuse them.

If we were not reusing the liners, I think they are a great product. We will use up what we have, but do not intend to purchase them again.

title: Not useful for heavy sleepers
text:
When you look at the watch descriptions, it sounds like it is a high tech devise that detects your sleep cycles, but it actually has nothing to do with the 5 stages of sleep cycle. It basically detects when the watch is moved, you know, just like the Nintendo Wii knows when you swing the remove control. It beeps when you move your arm or turn over, and their idea is that you tend to move when you are in the lighter stage of sleep.

The problem I have with this that when it beeps, I wake up for a second but fall back to sleep right away. It does not snooze like a normal alarm, so once you missed the time you set, the watch does not go off again. So the watch does not help me getting up and is basically useless for me.

There is also a glitch in the time calculation. When it records your sleep for more than 8 hours, it shows a totally incorrect time. I asked the manufacturer about this, and they confirmed the problem and told me that they would send me a software patch to fix the problem. Unfortunately, a month passed, three months passed, and 8 months passed now, they keep giving excuses and they still haven't come up with a fix yet. I am disappointed with this matter.

After evaluating this watch, I think this watch is overpriced for what it does. If you are a heavy sleeper like me, it probably won't help you getting up in the morning, and if you are a light sleeper, you probably won't need this watch in the first place.

title: Tangles long hair terribly.
text:
You can absolutely make beautiful buns with this product. The problem is that in order to do so, you need to pull your rolled up hair down the sides of the bun in order to cover the hook bits. When trying to get your hair out of this contraption, you need to unhook the hooks and unroll. The problem is that your hair is tangled in the little teeth that run along the sides because you pulled it down to cover the hooks. As soon as you try to unhook the hooks it will also be instantly tangled in them as well. What results is a minimum of 20 min of careful untangling with pain and hair breakage. There IS no easy unrolling your hair out of this thing.

My hair grows down to my rear. If you have short hair (shoulder blade length or shorter), this probably won't happen to you.
I recommend the magic hair bun thing I've linked below. There are no teeth or hooks for your hair to get tangled and broken in AND the foam adds some extra thickness to your bun. It's also less expensive:

However, if you keep rolling despite the imperfections, you'll have a great "starter bun."  After that, you can take bobby pins and hide the strays. title: This worked for my 12 mile run!
text: I have been a runner for over 20 yrs. Blisters have always been a problem for longer distances (18 miles plus). Recently the blisters were becoming a problem around 6 miles. Mainly on my toes but also on the ball/arch. I actually had one on the ball of the foot before the run and it didn't get worse. I tried about 5 different types of socks, even the toe ones. I never thought a product like this would work but finally decided to try it. While running there were times where my toes felt a little irritated but I was able to finish the 12 miles without blisters. I still have some blisters healing so I think the irritation has to do with that. Once you put your socks on the product does feel a little weird at first. When you are finished and take the socks off, the product is all soaked in and your feet feel soft. Also, two days later one of my blisters I have had for a while has healed. It seems the product also helps in healing. These were the types of blisters that were also like a callous forming and sometimes blood blisters. I just bought the tube and will use that just on my toes for the shorter runs.

title: Durability and lots of room
text: Under the category of "welcome to old", due to all the various pills my wife and I now have to take, we have gone through several sets of these types of pill containers over the years. Both this size (2" x 1.5") as well as the smaller size. Usually after a little use (and occasional drops on hard floors) they begin to chip off at the top edges and can no longer be attached to one another. Not so here! These are great containers! Much more heavy duty than what we have previously used. In spite of their larger size, they will indeed fit pretty easily in a travel (carry on) bag. We both recently began taking calcium (2 per day) in the form of "gummies" (see pic), which can take up a lot room in a pill container. No problem here. They easily fit along with all my other pills with extra room to spare. The extra lid is a great option for being able to carry only a single (daily) pill dosage when necessary. Great product! Highly recommended!

title: If protein powder and Laffy Taffy had a baby, this would be it
text:
What I liked the MOST about these bars is that the ingredients are clean, and since I cannot have dairy, the egg white protein is PERFECT. I feel good after I eat them, whereas many other protein bars leave me feeling inflamed. I also like that the net carb count is low.

I do hope they continue to develop the texture, though. The texture of these is exactly like if I mixed my egg white protein powder into a vat of Laffy Taffy. I have to allow several minutes to chew these bars. They are like taffy or caramel. Now, I am willing to deal with the texture issue because I am not looking for a replacement for cookies, cakes, and brownies. Cookies, cakes, and brownies are the reason I’m in the position of needing a protein bar to begin with. I’m needing a quick protein source that I can grab and go, and this fits the bill. If you are a person with texture issues, though, just take into consideration - these do not have the texture of bakery treats.

title: Nice, but beware of the silicone nubs...
text:
I saw an add for this on Facebook, and thought I'd give it a try. I have thick, frizzy, coarse hair that's wavy/curly. My normal hair routine is to wash, then blow dry, and then straighten. I've gotten pretty fast at this, and I was intrigued by this product since it claimed to straighten faster than a normal flat iron. I washed my hair, and decided not to blow dry, so I could really test this product out. I set it to the highest heat setting, after my hair was completely dry and brushed through. I started using the Moxie Brush, and was pleasantly surprised with how quickly it straightened my hair. Normally, straightening with a flat iron if I haven't blow dried my hair is horrible and takes forever, but I was done with my hair in about 15 minutes with the Moxie Brush (straightening normally takes about a half hour, and if I blow dry, my whole routine takes about an hour).

I knocked the rating by one star because the blue silicone nubs on the brush were falling out as I combed the brush through my hair. The nubs don't really heat up, but the bristle they are attached to do. So when I slid the brush through my hair, I accidentally touched one of the bristles (the nub had fallen off, exposing the part that heats up). The burn isn't that bad, but it's uncomfortable. I would recommend using a heat glove so that you can protect your hands. Also, the nubs don't seem to be anchored in well (two of the nubs fell off while I was doing my fair). I pushed them back in after the brush had cooled down, but I'm sure they'll fall out again. That's not a deal breaker though, since with the glove I'm sure my hands will be fine, even if the nubs fall off, and it shouldn't affect the way it straightens.

Overall, I'm fairly happy with the Moxie Brush. I'm glad I was able to take a chance on it. It'll definitely be my go to product for straightening my hair.

text:

Definitely recommend this product, it's stylish, light weight, and super comfortable!

title: The most comfortable ear plugs I've worn!
text: I've been going to concerts regularly for around 15 years and in the past, I've either gone without ear protection (don't do that) or worn single-use foam ear plugs.  I knew I was going to be attending 4 or 5 concerts within the span of a couple of months, so I purchased a pair of Loop ear plugs and I'm happy to report they worked great!  They do a really excellent job of reducing the intensity of amplified sound in such a way that you can still hear it but it doesn't hurt or leave a ringing in your ears.  The foam ear tips fit really well and the loops stay in my ears even while bouncing around (the first time I wore them there was some slight discomfort but the next concert I could barely even feel that they were in).  My one complaint is that it almost completely shuts out non-amplified audio, so the crowds singing along at the concerts are barely audible, leaving me with the weird feeling like I'm the only one singing along... but it's so much better than disposable foam ear plugs, it's worth the slight drawback.  Bonus: the little carrying pouch is a nice feature, and I like that there are several color options so my wife and I could pick different ones and not get them mixed up.

text:
My fiancee cannot sleep at night without some sort of noise in the background. Usually at night before we go to bed, we will turn on our air purifier which has a nice soft fan noise. We also love that it is rechargeable since it's usually a struggle when traveling to find adequate plugs for all of our devices. With the unit having a rechargeable battery, we are able to charge it during the day, and then unplug it at night while our phones charge. The timer feature is nice as well and we usually set it for 90 minutes which is more than enough time for us to fall asleep and stay asleep.

Would definitely recommend this product for it's noise selection as well as portability.

title: Game Changer!
text: I usually don't write reviews, but this stuff has been a total game changer for me!  I keep thinking it can't be making a huge difference, but then I'm reminded just how essential it is for me.  I tried a different brand about a month ago and this last week I must have gotten a bad batch because the taste was a little off.  Both times, I immediately felt the difference.  I started breaking out, I was getting irritable, having intense cravings, feeling exhausted, and gaining weight.  As soon as I ordered a new bottle and started taking it again, within a few hours, I was back to feeling better.  I've always had hormones from hell!  This last year, I had a total hysterectomy, which was a huge blessing!  The dr put me on an estrogen patch, which made a significant difference... sometimes, but I would always get major swings between the days I had to change my patch, and I had to keep upping my dose, which was dangerous with my clotting problems.  So, I started searching for other options.  I've known about maca for a while, but it never really stood out to me.  I came across a study that talked about how it actually works on the pituitary gland, which is basically the part of your brain that controls all your hormones.  This caught my interest, because I felt like I just kept swinging myself up and down trying to figure out how much estrogen I needed, since I'm super sensitive.  The maca works by balancing everything out and prevents the guessing game.  When I first started taking it back in February, I had to take it about every 4 hours, otherwise, I would feel the symptoms creeping back.  It usually takes a couple of weeks to build up in your system and notice the difference, but after a while, you don't have to take as much.  Now, I only take it 2 to 3 times a day, depending on how I feel.  My mom also had a hysterectomy and didn't want to get off of her patches, but she finally did and is doing great on the maca too.  It gets rid of her hot flashes.  She doesn't seem to notice a difference in brands, but for me, it made a huge difference.  There are also different types of maca.  The red maca is the best for hormones but isn't just for female hormones since it works on the pituitary gland.  The black is better for energy, but the red seems to give me a good amount of energy too.  This stuff has made it possible for me to lose almost 50 pounds now.  My hormones have been a major trigger for my autoimmune reaction.  I would gain 5 pounds in a single day and would get so swollen, painful, exhausted, and depressed that it was a struggle just to get out of bed.  On top of that, they would trigger severe sugar cravings.  It felt like I was thirsty all the time, but the only thing that quenched the thirst were carbs.  Hormones affect your neurotransmitters, and your neurotransmitters are made up of building blocks that you get from foods.  Sugar increases both your serotonin and dopamine, which make you feel better.  My poor family always knew that when I was hormonal, I NEEDED sugar or I would literally lose my mind.  Since being on the maca, I rarely get any sugar cravings.  Unfortunately, for me, losing weight hasn't been as simple as fixing my hormones and staying away from sugar due to the many foods that trigger my immune system.  However, I keep being reminded that the maca has been essential in my journey to better health, and I literally can't function well without it.  So, I wanted to share in case my experience could possibly help someone else too.

title: Illegally Represented as USDA Certified Organic
text: I can't even give it 1 star. I purchased this product and it had NO USDA Organic seal.  This product is FALSLY and ILLEGALLY represented as USDA Certified Organic.  I work for a USDA accredited Organic Certification Agency and deal in organic regulations. In order for any product to be represented as USDA Certified Organic, the USDA's National Organic Program (NOP) regulations and requirements state that in order for a product to be represented as and sold as USDA Certified Organic, it must be certified by an accredited certifier and have the USDA Organic seal and the name of the certifier listed on the product.  This product has neither. Misrepresenting a product as USDA Certified Organic is illegal and punishable by law; subject to heafty fines and penalties. You can verify this your sellf by looking up the USDA National Organic Program and asking them for the name of the certification agency that certifies any product. If there it is not listed and they cannot find the company; THAT COMPANY IS NOT CERTIFIED. The official USDA Organic seal is either completely black in color (circle, letters and lines within), or it has a dark green circle and brown letters with green lines within the circle. Any other colors are illegal and not representative of the USDA in any way. I have reported this product and company to the NOP. I hope this information helps ANYONE safely purchase USDA Certified Organic products in the future.

title: Didn't work for me
text:
I would say I like the watch design, but other than that it was useless (at least for me), and on top of that you can not return it because it is considered a "dangerous good".
If anybody is seriously considering buying it, I would suggest borrowing somebody else's.
I read a lot of the reviews and I really was excited to receive it, because every day I wake up very tired, unfortunately it didn't work for me.
1. It is too bulky and sometimes during the night I woke up because the watch is so uncomfortable
2. The watch works based on your movement, if you almost don't move at night, it will detect very few almost awake moments
3. According to the manual if it doesn't detect an ideal almost awake moment, it will sound at the moment you set the alarm, but only ONCE, that means if you are in a very deep stage of your sleep you will have only ONE chance to wake up.
4. Based on my above point you will require a backup alarm, and it is a very expensive alarm ($175) that requires a backup alarm
5. The alarm has to be set on a daily basis; it doesn't have any option to set it from Monday to Friday, weekends, etc.
I read a lot of people love it, which was the reason because I bought it, but it didn't work for me and I cannot recommend it at all.

title: Recalled for Radon radioactive poison!
text:
Just so everyone knows these were recalled by Costco in Korea for containing 9x the limit of Radon. I’m pretty worried what I was exposed to after using these for 2 years. Costco had imported the pillow from Sinomax between December 2017 and April 2018. The World Health Organization categorizes radon as a Group 1 carcinogen, because the radioactive material may cause lung cancer. The retailer denied the consumer's claim at that time, citing a private institution's measurement.

The institution's data includes the radon content of the pillow, but lacks thoron content.

Thoron is a radon-220 isotope, a natural decay product of the most stable thorium isotope.

Local broadcaster SBS claimed the pillow contains 1,406 becquerels per kilogram of radon, nine times higher than the permissible level.

Costco said it has been aware of possibility of the pillow containing excessive amount of radon, after it carried out in-house testing on the product after complaints from several customers.

"We reported our findings to the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission on Oct. 29, and decided to conduct a voluntary recall, regardless of the commission's investigation," the company said.

However, it declined to disclose the specific radon content and the reason why the pillow contains the radioactive substance.

It also refused to mention the amount of sales and imports of the product.

Although the warehouse club has 1 million members in Korea, it has yet to notify each customer of the recall.

It has not come up with a compensation plan either.

title: Worth replacing - once!
text:
Mine lasted 4 months before succumbing to the design flaw mentioned by several others, which is that the device is not well anchored to the elastic band and can fall off and get lost during relatively normal handling of a water bottle. I had silly aesthetic worries about sticking a piece of black velcro tape under the translucent clip to prevent this & tried to improvise further with a lightly adhesive clear product, but evidently not adhesive enough.

While I had this little device, it actually did exactly what it said it would do and I found it very helpful. It won't take you by the hand & pour the water in your mouth, it's still a tool you have to make the choice to use rather than ignore or leave on a shelf. But if a significant part of your water-drinking problem is that you get too engrossed in your tasks or lose track of time and just forget to drink, this may be the reminder you need.

Really at this price point the manufacturer should just add a little snap or anchor or bit of velcro themselves, and I wavered on the affordability & value of replacing it. But decided I will one time since it remains the only such product I've found that I can move around to different bottles, glasses, and cups depending on what I'm drinking and what dishes/bottles are dirty, rather than having only one reminder-equipped water bottle. If the second one goes AWOL, I'll just have to hope the time I did have it gave me better hydration habits and do my best sans technology from there.

title: Good hookah for the price
text:
You could say that, as with many things in life, you get what you pay for in a hookah. Having seen a bunch of negative reviews on hookahs which seem to be from the same company as this, I was aware of potential quality control issues. As such I ordered from a site other than Amazon, which I've had good dealings with in the past and which I knew would handle any issues I had, but as it turns out it was unnecessary. Either I got lucky or this hookah company suffers from a lot of bad press, because while it's not something you'd find in the Louvre (visible seams, uneven frosting on the glass base, tool-marks on the lathe-cut metal stem, industry-standard ugly finish on the wooden hose grips, cosmetic marks on the tray, so on and so forth), it is reasonably air-tight (minor problem with a tiny leak where the hose ports connect to the stem; I sealed it, or tried to, with epoxy), and quite pretty glasswork despite it not being executed perfectly. Basically, it's a good hookah for what you're paying for. Don't expect perfection, but if you want it to smoke and look good to the average joe, this is a great hookah for you. Oh, and one final note, the other hookahs that come with cases on this site are basically from the same manufacturer from what I can tell (they send a small flier with the purchase showing pictures of them). The people who leave reviews saying they can't get these back into the case are morons, because it packs up nicely if you have any spatial awareness at all. Does need to be dismantled a bit (hoses removed, stem removed, downstem separated, bowl removed) but it's not like it'll take you more than thirty seconds to put it back together again. They actually pack it into the case for shipping, along with some air bags to keep things from moving around, so there's plenty of room in there to get it all back in.

tl;dr You're paying forty bucks, fifty with shipping. That's definitely a fair price for this, just don't compare it to a hookah that costs a hundred plus. Moderately handy people can fix most issues with it. Play a little Tetris and putting it away is a snap.

text:
This is exactly what I needed. I had a seizure (but I believe it was a stroke) that left me unable to move my right side properly. I can still walk, but my right side doesn't move quick enough to be able to drive. So, I looked up whether it was legal to drive with your left foot, and I found that it wasn't.

So I got on here and looked for one and all they had was the one that you had to have installed. I ordered it, because I am 33 yrs old and I have a long life to live, and I wasn't going to let this disability stop me. So when it got here, I didn't even open it and w/in two weeks I sent it back because who has time to got it installed and still be limited to only 1 car. So, I got back on here and I was about to order it again, when I came across this.

Let me tell you it is what I needed to gain my independence back. I no longer have to depend on my mom and dad to give me rides, not that it was a problem, I just wanted to get up and go as I saw fit. So to say that this has truly been a blessing, is an understatement. This has given me the ability to be independent again. 5 stars and if I could do more, I would. The only thing is, it weighs 15lbs to ensure that while your driving, it won't go anywhere.

title: Burns hot, burns great
text:
I subtracted a star because these are brittle and can crumble, and because their big strength is also a potential hazard--they burn real hot, and the flame will flare up at least four inches above the lit tablet.

I got that stainless steel pot (the one made to cook over a campfire) that had the little plastic clips to hold the lid on. I used it over the folding commando stove for the "boil water" test. I set a small steel grill on top of the commando stove because the pot was too small. The heat melted the plastic clips like taffy within the first couple of minutes. (No great loss, I was planning on removing them anyway.)

On the other hand, this passed the "boils water" test with flying colors.

I recommend lighting them at a corner with a candle or long-style lighter. I also recommend saving broken tablets and using them to adjust burn time if needed. Absolutely have water nearby when using these. Thoroughly dousing them puts them out, but the remnant of the tab will crack and break or crumble outright.

Also, I had the folding stove set on an old wooden table outside. The table started to smolder underneath the stove! Make sure you set your stove on packed dirt, rock, brick, steel, or cement. Do not set it up on an aluminum, wood, or plastic table--it burns too hot and will damage them.

On a recent group camping trip, these saved the day when it rained and drenched the wood for the bonfire. One of these burned hot enough to get past the surface moisture on the wood and start the bonfire, no muss, no fuss. I would carry these camping even without the stove just for that.

Good product. Does the job. Just be aware that it does work as advertised, have a cup of water to dump on it in case something goes wrong, and keep in mind that there is no way to get low heat out of these.

title: Gospel-Centered or Me-Centered?
text:
Simple, brief devotionals that build on the concept of God as the center of the gospel message and how that mind-shift can make our jobs as moms more peaceful and far less myopic. Our identity does not come from our own skills, talents, abilities, or lack of the above. Our identity is found wholly in Christ Jesus and our job as moms is to continually point our children to Christ. Failings, successes, and all the in between mundane stuff are part of our testimony and the solid bedrock is Christ. If we do not point our children to Christ, we are doing them the greatest disservice. We could focus our time and energy and opinions on a million different things, but if those "things" are not bringing Christ into the picture, then we will find ourselves hitting our heads against a brick-wall in our parenting.

This is a great devotional for the mom who is harried and in the midst of those crazy, chaotic phases of life, where just ONE breath of fresh air would be enough to get us moving again.

title: Great set of stamping polishes! Worked well!
text:
My review is for the stamping polish set #2, and as soon as I received them, I was impressed. They came packaged in a 'BMC' printed box with a specially made foam insert that perfectly held and protected the polishes for shipping. The caps are smooth, but also pull-off revealing a textured extra-grip cap underneath, which comes in handy. The bottles are not labeled with color names, but instead numbers (corresponding names can be found on the Bundle Monster website). The colors are all beautiful and on-trend, with no odd or unpleasant odor.

As for their performance, I was very pleased! The lighter colors in the set (#15-Sunshine Yellow, #12-Orange Peel, and #21-Electric Pink) are lovely and vibrant, but not completely opaque when stamped over black/very dark polish. However, they looked perfect over all other polishes. The darker colors in the set (#20-Sky Blue and #8-Lucky Green) were impressive when stamped over light and dark polishes alike! And as for #10-Amethyst, it's obviously too dark to show up when stamped on black/very dark polish, but still opaque and looks amazing over every thing else. The formula on ALL the polishes was fantastic: great consistency, creamy but not too thick, and there was no separation. The images you get when stamping with this polish are always crisp. Dry time was great as well, allowing just enough "work time" to get your images aligned and stamped on the nail properly. Finally, I used a variety of different topcoats and had no smearing of the stamping at all, which was really impressive!

Over all, I would definitely recommend these stamping polishes to anyone wanting to add to their stamping polish collection. And at this price point, you need them all! ;)
