title: Good design, horrible price
text:
The design is simple and straight-forward, typically adding about two inches of additional clearance to doorway openings. Things to be aware of:

1) You need about three inches between the wall and the door jamb (where the hinge mounts) to get the full benefit of these hinges
2) The hinges utilize the existing holes AND screws from your current door hinges. Existing hinges, especially in older homes, may utilize four screws. If so, drilling of new pilot holes will be required. You may wish to install longer screws as well, depending on the condition of the door jamb and the existing holes.
3) These are best purchased elsewhere. As is the case with almost every product designed to increase accessibility or to make daily living easier for those with disabilities, the price is ridiculous. You should have no problem locating similar hinges online for $12-$13/pair.

title: Great bundle!
text:
Grave Before Shave products are some of my favorite beard products. You simply cannot go wrong with them. I love the Cigar blend, although beware, it is strong!

I have a wild beard, so I typically use both oil, as well as balm at the same time. I'm probably over moisturizing, but it seems to work well. This oil is truly high quality. I do suggest you use it sparingly though, because it smells strong. The aroma is a strong vanilla and maybe even a little bit cinnamon-y. I would say it's actually very light on the tobacco smell, with the dominant scents being very sweet.

If you're in doubt, I suggest buying the 2oz. can of the balm first, and then go the whole way with the oil and the wash.

I should let you know that I actually do not use the wash any longer. While I do like it very much, and it has a wonderful scent, my hair is extremely dry and I can only use a beard soap. I am an exception here and still love the smell and the wash that the wash provides. Give it a try, but just know that your mileage may vary.

title: The "mood" putty only turns purple all the way through if you cool it in the fridge or something similar for a ...
text:
First off, this putty hasn't gotten stuck on any surface or clothes yet.

But... I'm not a fan of misleading descriptions.

The "mood" putty only turns purple all the way through if you cool it in the fridge or something similar for a while. The putty will turn from purple to blue in under five minutes and stay that way until you cool it again. If you only cool it briefly, it will immediately turn from purple to blue again. Pretty disappointed in that.

The metallic putty does *not* sparkle or do anything special when you play with it. It does have the appearance of metal, even when stretched. That is neat, but it is not what I understood from the descriptions.

The product itself does its job, and doesn't make a mess, which is why it doesn't get a 1 star.
The descriptions of the products come close to outright lies though.

title: Don't Listen to the False - Bad Reviews. Excellent Nutrition Bar.
text:
I'm always amazed at how people can throw out statements without any facts to back them up. Please don't listen to these people who are stating their 'opinions' that this has the same nutrition info as a snickers bar! It does not! Being a scientist and a bariatric patient I have to be very careful what I eat and the means to monitor intake properly. So when my surgeon told me I needed to increase my protein I immediately thought of the Tiger Milk Protein Rich Bars that I grew up with. I too was taken back by the claims that these are just candy bars, but don't be fooled by false statements. After doing the research I found that the reviewers who claimed this couldn't be further from the truth.

Snickers Bar: 2oz size: 271 Calories; 14g Fat; 5g Sat. Fat; 7mg Cholesterol; 140mg Sodium; 0mg Potassium; 35g Total Carbs; 1g Fiber; 29g Sugars; 4g Protein; 2% Vit. A; 0% Vit. C; 5% Calcium; 2% Iron

Where as a comparible King Size Tiger Milk Bar; approx. 2oz size: 220 Calories; 8g Fat; 3g Sat. Fat; 0mg Cholesterol; 95mg Sodium; 230mg Potassium; 28g Total Carbs; 2g Fiber; 21g Sugars; 9g Protein; 25% Vit. A; 15% Vit. C; 25% Calcium; 30% Iron.

True that the sugar for these bars is a bit high. However, it is still less than a candy bar and has almost half the fat, twice the fiber, and over twice the protein of the snikers bar. Not to mention it is considerably higher in potassium, vitamins A & C, Calcium, and Iron. HENCE IT IS A NUTRITION BAR. Also please take into account that the King Size version is more than I could or should eat. The actual 1.23oz original size is better formulated for nutrition (140 calories; 5g fat; 2g sat. fat; 60mg sodium; 140mg potassium; 18g carbs; 1g fiber; 14g sugars; 6g protein)which just further proves the point (not to mention that is the actual product we are reviewing here) that it is no where near the sugar and fat intake of a candy bar.

I hope my ranting has better informed those who are looking for a good tasting nutrition bar. Personally, I would recommend this to anyone who needs to get more protein in their diet ... and actually do.

title: Wonderful for decent support on the knees
text:
This is a wonderful compression support sleeve. I used to use another knee support sleeve that irritated the skin around my knee and gave me a bad rash. To be specific, this was the McDavid knee support that had neoprene material. The Li-Ning sleeve is much more breathable and I don't have any issues with sweat building up around my knee or any issues with the rash. However, I must say that the compression isn't as much as the McDavid knee support sleeve. If you are looking for something that provides much more support I suggest you look into other products that provide better support.

Currently, I own two pairs of these knee sleeves as I use them for when I am playing badminton. I find that compression sleeves in general do help with any high impact, high movement, sudden movement sports, and a fast change of direction. For example, badminton, tennis, basketball, squash, etc. I would personally buy this product again as it is very durable, lightweight, and provides a decent amount of support.

As for the care and maintence, I typically just throw it into the washing machine. I will try to avoid putting this in the dryer as the material is part nylon, rubber, and spandex.

text:
My initial review was very cautious and conservative for obvious reasons... I had just used the shaver on one occasion. Having used it now for 3 months I can provide a full-throated, honest review, which luckily for the manufacturer is all positive.
First everything I said initially still stands. Add to that, the unit holds well in my big hands.
Secondly, the shaver holds the charge for several uses. Excellent.
Thirdly, it is super easy to clean. Just use a credit card or similar thin plastic to prize each head up from the base of the black section. If you do not flip it securely from the bottom of the black section, you run the risk of hitting the foil, which cannot be a good thing.
Fourth, I can speak only for the basic use of the shaver, I have not tried any of the attachments, although I am going to experiment with the face brush.
Fifth, Shaver does a great job covering my head-top and face, including my mustache.
Sixth, the change in sound tells you when you are covering areas where there is still hair.
UNFORTUNATELY, in anticipation of having to eventually replace the head which must get dull at some point, the seller advised me that they do not sell the replacement heads. I believe that the documentation required that only the head built for this unit be used. Hope I am wrong.
I would be very happy to hear that they now sell an eight-head shaver.

Of all plastic wraps, even the high priced name branded Glad Cling Wrap, Great Value 300 was the best for sticking and staying stuck to whatever you wanted it to. Now, sadly, it seems Walmart has discontinued the 300ft roll with slide cutter, leaving only the 200ft roll with basic razor edge available. You would think the product in both packages was the same…think again!! The product in the 300ft package was smooth and completely clear; the product in the 200ft package has vertical stripes in it, parallel with the outer edges of the film as you dispense it. O.K., so it looks a little different…but wait, it doesn’t hardly stick to itself anymore let alone other objects.

To be fair, this is my first roll of the 200. I will peek at the next box on the shelf before buying it. If it has the same stripes in the wrap I will switch to Sam’s Club (Member’s Mark) wrap. I like Sam’s equally, but their wrap only comes in a 3000ft countertop dispenser…a bit of a waste of countertop space for my kitchen; countertop space is limited.

I’ve searched all Wally Worlds in my region, but sadly none have the 300ft available, and it isn’t available to order on Walmart’s website or app either. A sad day for my kitchen. 😢

title: I felt like such a fool to have been duped
text:
I normally weigh between 222-224, and my brand new 'high accuracy' scale put me at around 292. I thought my girlfriend was at about 135, but on the scale, she weighed in at around 200. After I fat shamed her, which led to a screaming argument, our relationship ended and--as a result of the fight--we got kicked out of our apartment and fired from my job (there was a lot of throwing and breaking things and crying on both our parts, as well as incriminating video of the altercation that led to my termination).

After a few days of living on the streets, now without a job, girlfriend, or home, I came to a startling realization: what if the scale had just been off? Impossible, I thought. It said it right there...high accuracy digital bathroom scale. I definitely weigh almost 300 pounds, and I was dating a girl who had been lying to me all along by around 70 pounds! I felt like such a fool to have been duped. Yet, the doubt still kept creeping in...what if it was wrong? There was only one way to know.

I went to a drugstore where they had a scale where you could test your height, weight, blood pressure, and all that stuff. I got on the scale and waited....for what seemed like an eternity. When the digital display finally stopped moving, it read: 223. TWO TWENTY-THREE! No, that can't be right. After all, the scale I purchased said 'high accuracy.' I mean, if it had just been called 'Ballpark Digital Bathroom Scale' or 'Drunk Guesstimate Digital Bathroom Scale,' I wouldn't have let it get to me. It said High Accuracy. Not just moderate accuracy. HIGH Accuracy.

I went to another store....223. Another: 224. ANOTHER:.........223! Holy Jesus, I've made a terrible mistake!

My girlfriend of 4 years still won't speak to me--too much damage had been done, and too many hurtful things were said that fateful day. My landlord won't let me explain the situation to him. My work heard all about the outburst and won't offer any sympathy.

If you want to lose everything you hold dear to you....go ahead. Buy the scale.

....For real though, I got the scale and it was like 70 pounds off. Doesn't matter what surface I set it on, batteries out and back in, etc.

title: Staying hydrated and loving it!!
text:
I absolutely LOVE this product!! It’s simple but impactful and it has absolutely helped me drink more water throughout the day than I have in the past several years. I have tried pop-up reminders on my work computer (Outlook), apps on my phone, reminders from my FitBit and posted signs near my desk but nothing helps like this blinking* light. I already had several reusable water bottles so I sought an accessory; this item is much cheaper than “smart bottles” and doesn’t need washed. :D

It fits on water bottles of various sizes. The reusable bottle I have pictured (I have 3 of them) has a diameter of almost 3 1/2” (nearly 9cm) but the band also fits on a standard 16.9 oz. bottle and bottles larger than the one I typically use.

The light blinks every 30-45 minutes to remind you to drink. After you drink it will light up slowly and turn off slowly so that means it has recorded you drinking and reset the clock. It does not blink all night while you sleep; the instructions explain it will go through about 2 blinking cycles and as long as it doesn’t sense movement, it will stop blinking until it senses movement again.

The only caveat is that you need to have the bottle in front of you in order to see it - it doesn’t make any noise (like yell at you, which I would also likely respond to). So make sure you take the bottle from your work station to other rooms where you spend time outside of work. I work from home so I grab my bottle and move it at the end of the day.

This item is currently unavailable, but the last time that happened they had some available a few weeks later; I hope there are more available soon!!

*This product may not be ideal for those with light sensitivity or conditions like epilepsy because the light flashes quickly. If flashes about 10 times, then stops, and repeats that series twice more.*

Happy drinking!!

[[My additional tips for drinking more water from my research, if you’re interested, since I have been dehydrated to the point of being off sick from work 4 times in the last year:
-Using a wide-mouth bottle may help you drink more during each session.
-Aim to drink somewhere around 80 ounces per day; some sources suggest at least 80 oz. or up to half of your body weight in ounces, so if you weigh 200 pounds, you should drink 100 ounces of water…that’s a lot.
-Water helps every function of your body, improves your skin texture, and can even impact your mood.
-Drink between meals on this schedule:
—8-16 oz. shortly after you wake up (helps rehydrate after your sleeping “fast” and activate digestion).
—Drink 8 oz. before you get a shower (if you shower shortly after waking up, don’t drink extra water; this helps keep blood pressure stable).
—Drink BETWEEN, not with meals, so a half hour before and 30-45 minutes after you eat (a few sips is fine but otherwise you’re filling up with unnecessary liquid and watering down your food; this is an “Eastern medicine” technique). I will pick up my water bottle and pretend to drink so that the clock resets and I can drink again after I eat to aid digestion.
—Drink water at the temperature you prefer; I like room temperature water because I have sensitive teeth. If you like ice water, use an insulated cup.
—Drink 8 oz. of water 30 minutes prior to starting physical activities and then occasionally during activity, if you’re able. You don’t need really need an electrolyte drink/anything more than water unless you’re working out very hard for an hour or more.
—Drink 8 oz. right before you go to sleep; it shouldn’t be enough to wake you up to urinate overnight.
—Coffee does count towards your daily water goal, however, it is a diuretic, so make sure this is not your MAIN water source. Coconut water is very good, however, juice, soda, alcohol, etc. don’t count. Drink some electrolyte water before you go to bed after drinking alcohol and also the next morning when you wake up.
—I swear by electrolyte additives for water. Some have added B vitamins for energy (like “Liquid IV”) and others do not (like “Nuun” tablets, which I love). They really help no matter how much water you drink per day and provide a little natural flavor to plain water; I typically don’t use more than 1-2 per day.
-If you’re starting a new diet, make sure to drink a lot of electrolyte-enhanced water when you start. This is due to losing water weight first and that’s where your body holds salt and electrolytes. This is part of the “Keto flu” that occurs when you start that diet.]]

I had a dry itchy scalp over the last 5 months.

I cut out all possible triggers from my diet and that helped greatly. Then I saw this YouTube video where the girl mentioned psoriasis being related to gut issues and to try l-glutamine.... I bought it right away.

title: Most effective and comfortable eye mask ever, with multiple bonus features
text:
Am amazed at how well this works for falling, and staying, asleep! I bought it for me, frankly not expecting to like it nearly as much as I do. I was really only looking for an eye mask that would stay put overnight, through tossing and turning, without shifting or feeling tight. I was a bit worried about the pillow aspect of this product, but, desperate for a good night's sleep ( am in a certain amount of pain whenever I am lying down or sitting, the after-effect of multiple spinal fractures from a nasty car wreck years ago) I decided to order one.

What a great decision: this mask/pillow blocks out all light completely, and is so soft and gentle that it's immediately soothing. I am now getting to sleep more quickly than I have in years, and wake with no neck pains or headache. I was a bit worried that the wrap-around-the-head styling would make it uncomfortable for use in bed with a pillow, thinking that it would probably tilt my neck too much by lifting my head off the pillow, but not a bit so.

This is simply a terrific product! I've used many different brands and styles of eye masks over the last 5 years, but they either slide down on my face, baring my eyes, or slide up and off my head, when I turn over in bed. The only way to keep the others on is to make the band(s) so tight that they are uncomfortable--but even then, they still shift around and some have even gotten caught in my hair. This one stays put without any noticeable pressure on either my face, eyelids, or back of the skull. Don't know how it works so well, but it works. And talk about soft and cuddly!

Unexpected bonus: I live in the countryside, in a very quiet location, but if ambient noise in an issue for anyone, this design covers the ears so softly and totally that any such noise would fade away. I had company in the guest rooms on the same floor as my mine over Christmas, and I didn't hear anything! (Last year I heard various noises from these couples in the same guestrooms: low-volume TV chatter, one of their dogs coming and going, at least 2 people snoring, and various dressing/bathing sounds early in the morning.)
I am immediately ordering 2 more Wrap-a-Naps, to send to my husband and my brother, as gifts. They both travel worldwide, almost continually, and have the usual hotel-based issues with getting to sleep: too much light, too many strange pillows and varied mattresses, and noise of all sorts. They will love these! (I am going to be quite popular. Thank you, Wrap-a-Nap!)

title: Most doctors will recommend OTC antihistamines which will only treat the runny nose
text:
As a pharmacist, I am very passionate about the science behind over the counter (OTC) and prescription drugs. I have suffered from histamine intolerance from childhood and I only came to know more about it while in pharmacy school. I have a very high control over the foods i eat now, but that comes with a social stigma. You have to be empowered to avoid the foods. You need a certain level of histamine in your blood to help with your sleep wake cycle and other effects. The symptoms of high histamine can vary depending on which of the 4 sites of action (Called receptor) it binds. Most doctors will recommend OTC antihistamines which will only treat the runny nose, eye, or itchiness symptoms that are triggered through one of the pathways (H1 receptor). You might not be properly diagnosed if you have the other symptoms that are triggered through H2, H3, or H4. These other symptoms can affect your nerves and lead to back pain and anxiety.

The idea of supplementing the enzyme is one step towards the right direction. However, let me clarify some things. Diamine oxidase is a protein just like insulin and heparin. Insulin and heparin are not taken orally because every protein that you take orally is broken down by our enzymes to smaller units called amino acids. With that scientific concept, there is no way that you can get this enzyme into your blood. Our body's natural Diamine oxidase exists in our blood stream not in the gut. The only way that this product can help is that when it is broken down in our gut, the smaller units are taken into our blood and they will serve as raw material for our body to manufacture its own diamine oxidase. The subunits can also help boost our own natural diamine oxidase. This can work for people who only need the booster. It might not work for some people who have a genetic or family defect called a mutation on the part of the DNA that directs the production of the protein.

This product might work best if they can one day give it as an injection so it doesn't have to pass through the gut where our natural protein enzymes will break it down.

It might also be wrong to claim that it breaks down the histamine in out gut before it is absorbed because the product is dried and deactivated. Live and active protein is refrigerated just like insulin and heparin for it to work.

The only scientific fact that I can accept with this product is that it will be broken down in the gut to supply your body with the raw material required to build its own diamine oxidase. I do like the effort by Swanson to extract the protein from pork. Maybe one day the human form of the drug can be engineered like other FDA approved biologics.
I love to be criticized and challenged with evidence and logical thinking so I can learn more.

I've worn it a bunch of times outside and people thought it was my actual hair!! One girl was even surprised when she saw me again! title: Great product! Just as great (if not better) than my straightener!
text:
So, before you buy this just know that it doesn't magically give you straight hair! If you have curly ringlets, this isn't going to make your hair pin straight. However, in my experience it works just as well as a straightener does. I have medium to thick hair that reaches down to nipple length, and this brush works great!

I like it better than my straightener for two main reasons:
1. It is super easy to use. Obviously, you aren't squeezing your hair between two plates, so its less effort on your part.
2. Temperature control. You control what temperature setting you want which I think is super convenient.

If you're going to buy an Apalus striaghtening brush, I would recommend this one over the "original' brush. I believe this one costs about $10 more than the original, but in my opinion it is completely worth it. This one has a locking feature so you don't accidentally change temperature or turn off the brush while you're using it. It also does NOT have the rubber tips that the original one has, so it pulls out virtually no hair.

One thing to keep in mind when using it (especially if you have thick hair) is that it works much better if you portion your hair into sections. I usually section my hair into bottom, middle, and top layers. This ensures that every section of your hair is straight and gives you a better result.

Also, I see that some people when reviewing products get discounts or whatnot... As cool as that would be, I'm just a normal person who really loves their new straightening brush. Sadly, I paid full price for mine.

title: WILL NOT WORK AS IT IS!
text: First of all, I'm a strong proponent of "grounding".  But the fact is, this product has multiple issues.  The most important of which is that the product will not (can not) work as it is.  They REALLY should have consulted someone who knows ANYTHING about electricity before releasing this.  The problem (as stated in another review here), is that there is no electrical connection between the grounding wire and the actual sheet.  The wire snaps to a connection on the sheet, but that's it.  The snap is not connected to the conductive threads in the sheet.  This is sort of like laying the plug of an appliance next to an outlet without actually plugging it in, and expecting the appliance to operate.  Doesn't work that way, there needs to be an actual electrical connection!  One solution to this, although I'm still not content with it, is to put a clamp on the snap to hold it against the threads in the sheet.  This works, but still a cheesy solution.  Secondly, the grounding wire that it comes with is of such small gauge that there is a lot of resistance (Ohms) in just the wire itself.  Not a good start to reach a ground especially with all of the added distance of house wiring until there's a true ground.  My solution to this one was to splice in better wire to the snap connection.  This got me down to about 1/40th of the resistance even with a longer run out to an actual grounding stake in the ground.  This brings me to a third problem.  Using the ground of house wiring is inherently noisy electrically speaking.  I won't go into the details of all of the possible causes of this, but if you were to look at this ground with an oscilloscope probe you would see what I'm talking about.  This probably explains some of the other reviews of people not even being able to sleep with the sheet.  If someone is especially sensitive to this sort of noise, which many are, it will certainly disturb sleep.  This is why I opted for an actual Earth ground using a copper grounding rod in the ground outside of the bedroom window.  Anyway, with all of that said, there are work arounds, but DON'T EXPECT THIS PRODUCT TO WORK AS IS!

title: 5-Star Product w/ Falsely Advertised Quantity: 79.53 (not 90) Days Total Supply = 10.47-Day shortage
text: I received my Amazon.com order of three containers of Gundry MD Vital Reds.  The manufacture date (not to be confused with a "sell-by date") of all three containers indicated that the product was 196-days-old upon arrival.  This is more than half the 365-day shelf life of a typical consumable product.  Since I already planned to fully consume all of this product within less than 169 days (365 days of assumed freshness - 196 already aged upon arrival = 169 days of assumed freshness remaining), this excessive age upon arrival was not actually a problem for me.  I am mentioning it only as an objective observation.  The false advertising about product volume is mildly concerning.  Each container contains 3.984 ounces (not 4.0) = 112.95 grams of product.  The complementary "scoop" included inside each container measures 5.0 cubic centimeters (cc) dry = 5.0 milliliters (ml) dry = 1.0 teaspoon (tsp) dry = 4.26 grams (g) dry.  One "scoop" is falsely advertised as 3.765 grams, which would neatly equal 30 days of supply, if it were actually true (112.95 grams/container ÷ 3.765 grams/day = 30 days/container, as FALSELY advertised).  Assuming I use exactly one level "scoop" per day, I will truly get 26.51 (not 30) "scoops" (i.e., days) per container.  This is 3.49 "scoops" (i.e., days) less than the 30 "scoops" falsely advertised, but it is close enough for my needs.  With 26.51 days of product in each container • 3 containers, I will have enough product for 79.53 (not 90) days total.  90 days falsely advertised - 79.53 days of actual product = 10.47 days short of the falsely advertised amount.  Again, this 10.47-day shortage is acceptable by my very forgiving and tolerant standards.  Although the blatant fakery of product measurements is not necessarily a deal-breaker for me, it would be helpful if the product measurements advertised were to actually be congruent with reality.  At this very high (but well worth every penny) price-point, many other consumers might not be as forgiving as I am.  The product itself is worthy of five stars!  The obvious lack of truth-in-advertising regarding product measurements is worth removing one star.  Thus, I gave four stars overall.

title: be careful when you buy this chair
text:
The chair that I have got doesn't recline to 180 degree as the product description says. I think it reclines to 150 at most.
The middle portion of the back is just a piece of fabric which means when you sit on it your back(or your spine) won't get much support so it is not a very comfortable chair to sit.
The back warming doesn't cover the middle section of the back so unless you are big person that can cover the whole seat otherwise the back warming function is useless which is what I feel.
The roller is buried deep in the back padding so I don't feel much of the massage.
The worst part is that you only have 7 days if you want to return it. When I got the chair I called them right a way to report the problem. They told me to send them pictures. I did that in about 2 weeks because I was pretty busy and was not sure if I should return it or exchange for another type. But by the time I sent out picture to them and got feed back from them it is already later than 7 days and I was notified by them that I can't return it any more.
On the other hand even if I can return it I would not do it any way because it is too much trouble to pack it back and pay for the shipping fee.
To make long story short, I am selling it for only $1000 after less than one month use. I would be very happy if I can get rid of it and get paid $1000. I paid about $2000 including about $200 shipping. But I am afraid no one is going to buy it at $1000 because it is really a piece of junk.

I don't write reviews often but, I know how helpful it is for other people when they're deliberating on a purchase so I'm going to try to start doing it more often with products that fail or excel.

I purchased the Cigar Oasis Ultra 2.0 which works pretty well, and bought their smart Wi-Fi attachment to go with it. Unfortunately, the smart Wi-Fi attachment is a product that has failed for me. The set up has a couple of extra hurdles but nothing too complex, and it worked for me initially for roughly a week but then it stopped communicating with the app, rendering its functionality useless. I've tried several different ways of re-establishing the communication between the unit in the app – but nothings worked so far.

At this point I wish I'd gone another direction for remotely monitoring the humidity in my cigar humidor, so my advice would be to avoid making the same mistake I did and save yourself the money, and the frustration.

title: Bye Bye ScotchBrite Sponge!
text: I've been using ScotchBrite's scrubber sponge (the blue non-scratch one) for years because I just assumed there wasn't anything better out there. WRONG! I bought the Dish Fish on a whim because it claimed to resist bacteria and I HATE touching a stinky sponge.  I've had it for several weeks and it doesn't smell at all--unlike my old sponge.  But, what really surprised me is that it cleans way better than my old scrubber sponge.  It makes short work of greasy pans and then doesn't transfer that grease to wine glasses.  I wasn't sure about the shape at first.  Why is it a fish? Seemed kind of silly.  But then, as I used it I started thinking "why are other sponges rectangular?"  Almost nothing in my kitchen is shaped like that.  The curved fish shape reaches all the way to the bottom of wine glasses and follows the round shape of dishes, pots and pans much better than the old square sponge did.  And, I love how standing it on its tail dries it fast so it doesn't grow bacteria. I guess the fish shape isn't just a gimmick.  It makes sense.  Not sure yet how durable it is--I've only had it for three weeks, but that's longer than my sponge usually lasts, so, so far so good.

title: Going strong after 3 years of use!
text:
I bought this back in 2020. After 3 years of consistent use and machine-washing, it's still intact and remains soft!

I have used both sides of the pad. I use the soft velvety side to apply toner and its softness keeps my face from getting red and irritated. The rougher bamboo terry side - I have used to remove makeup. It feels slightly rough to the touch (by hand), but on the face it feels gentle while also being effective in removing cosmetics that I don't have problems using it on my eyelids. One, and only one of my pads did stain though, but that's probably due to the formula of the eyeliner I used. Other than that, the others have remained spotless.

The absorbancy of these pads are not too much, meaning you will be using less products than you normally would if you had used a cotton ball/pad. This is a big bonus for me because I do like getting the most of my buck. I now go through a bottle of toner at least twice as long as I did before.

The laundry bag has been very useful as well. I wanted to hand wash them but having little to no time, I find it convenient that I can just toss them in the machine. Pro-tip, and I don't know if this is an already known tip: do not use fabric softener on these so it doesn't lose its absorbancy.

Lastly, I have read some complaints about the fabric separating from each other when wiped on the face. I haven't had this problem so far but that's probably due to how I hold my pads. I included a photo for reference but of course, do what is most comfortable to you :)

I don’t have complaints about this product at all. There's enough pads to last a whole week, a laundry bag for efficient washing, and two sides for different purposes all — for $7-$8? That sounds like a great deal to me.

title: Doesn't Mix Well (Need a Blender), Foams Excessively (Fixable Issue), Great Neutral Taste
text:
UPDATE (after going through a 5lb bag): I decided to upgrade my review to 5 stars despite mixing issues, which only exist because there are no additives (mainly no lecithin of any kind, for which I'm grateful), because the protein tastes so neutral both on its own and in smoothies. It also has the best individual protein profile I've seen and has a nice thin consistency when mixed, which is probably what gives it a more neutral taste over other proteins. Lastly, the protein sits really well with me (other proteins will give me acid reflux/make me feel bloated). As long as you don't drink it while it's foamy (see mixing tips below), you shouldn't feel bloated. This is probably the least bloating protein I've tried since it's thin when mixed and the only ingredient is whey.

Mixing Tips: a large blender that allows you to drop the protein in from the top while you have the water moving is the best, but any will do.
I've found that pressing the stir/mix button on the blender gently while dumping an entire scoop of the protein into half a cup of water while the water is just moving is good enough to mix it (it takes a few seconds). There is still quite a bit of foam, but enough of it will settle in a few minutes to make it drinkable. I separate any remaining foam and put it in the fridge to settle so I can drink it later (it doesn't amount to much but probably still a few grams of protein). Alternatively, I'll mix the protein a few hours before I want it and let it sit in the fridge until the foam settles. SMOOTHIE TIP: to make a smoothie, I mix the protein, let it settle as I just mentioned, and set it aside. Then, I blend all the smoothie ingredients in the blender, pour the smoothie mix into the shaker with the protein, and stir with a spoon to combine. Stirring the rest of the smoothie into the mixed protein ensures that no foam is created. You end up with a smooth shake. I find that thick fruits, like a full banana, in the smoothie work the best to neutralize any remaining whey flavor over thinner fruits like watermelon.
______________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Previous Review (after a few days of trying the protein):

The reason why I gave this protein four stars instead of five is because it should really come with a warning that it requires a blender to mix. If you try to stir it, it will clump and stick to the side of your glass. If you try to shake it, it will foam like crazy but still be clumpy. Both of these methods of mixing make the protein undrinkable. You have to mix it in a blender ever so slowly to get it to mix well enough to drink. However, despite mixing it intermittently on the slowest speed, you will still end up with 50% foam. I use this blender method and reduce the foam by putting the mixture through a fine mesh strainer. I discard the strained foam.

I mix the protein with water. To make a fruit/vegetable shake, I would use the method I described above with water or milk, strain out the foam, then mix it in by hand to the rest of the shake (if you use a blender to mix the protein with the rest of your shake ingredients, it will foam too much to be drinkable. Although if you have a very small blending container, it may work as there wouldn't be as much air circulating within it to make it foam).

Other than the issue of mixing, the protein has a great neutral taste and the best amino acid profile I've seen. It's also nice that it's from grass fed cows and is not a byproduct of the cheese making process as most other proteins are. For these reasons, I think I can deal with the mixing issue.

title: Easy setup + Reliable measurements + Pleasing Aesthetics
text:
I am very happy with both the aesthetics and functionality of the scale.
While the design seems minimalist the device has some heft to it and seems well built.
Setup was a breeze and batteries included. (see details below)
Pairing with my iPhone​ was trivial once the app was downloaded.
We created multiple users to keep track of the whole family stats and can all be accessed through the same app.
The app interface is very pleasing and intuitive.
The different body measurements seem to have high repeatability, as we cycled through four different users a couple of times and each one attained consistent measurements each time.

Some details to keep in mind
- We had to press the factory reset button at the bottom of the scale prior to first use.
- The scale comes with a set of for "caps" to put on the bottom legs, which are intended for using the scale in carpeted areas. We found measurements to be unreliable on our carpet using said legs. Be sure NOT to leave said caps on when using the scale on hard surfaces (e.g. bathroom tile), as they are smooth plastic and may cause the scale to slide along the floor when dismounting.

Overall, the scale seems high quality and offers great ease of use.
Time will tell how reliable the measurement are over extended periods.

This product was provided at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review.

title: STOPPED WORKING AFTER SHORT TIME!
text:
Purchased this steamer for my Aesthetics business. From the beginning this machine was tricky to get up and running. Professionally, I was trained to only use distilled water during my facial treatments so naturally it is upsetting to learn that this machine requires "tap" water or the addition of salt to the water in order to work. Tap water can have heavy metals that can affect the integrity of the steam itself. Distilled water prevents bacteria build up in the device. Tap water contains minerals that can clog the machine's parts and leave mineral deposits on your face while steaming.
Secondly, within a couple months of purchasing this machine, it just stopped working all together during a treatment. Just "beeped" and then quit working. No dramatics, just stopped. The whole thing is upsetting, honestly. I felt very unprofessional during my clients treatment. I guess that's what I get for going for aeathetics (looks of machine) here instead of quality.

title: 3 minutes well spent
text:
I have a few heirloom rings that I've been too scared to take anywhere and risk damage or theft, so I started thinking of alternatives. I've been hearing a lot of buzz around this brand so when I came across this item I thought I'd try this out first.

It was honestly the best choice I've ever made. I was a bit skeptical at first, so I tried the first cleaning on the lowest setting. I could already see a major change around the band plus the water had a different color so I confirmed that it did in fact, clean it.

I then tried the 2nd timing setting, and that did it. The device comes with 2 different baskets, and little ring holders, which gave me peace of mind that my great-great-grandmothers rings weren't going to be thrown on this aggressive cycle, completely the opposite, the holders and baskets, allowed for the more delicate rings to get a proper cleaning without risking damage.

Between the gentle cycle and the ultrasonic light that comes on as the cycle begins, this is a truly incredible state-of-the-art device. Strongly considering getting my mother one as well so she can also clean through her jewelry box thoroughly.

CONS (even though I'm about to make a complaint, I didn't knock off any stars)
I believe the power cord needs to be redesigned & longer. The control unit is all the way at your feet & the cord is too short to reach the wall outlet (if your bed sits with the headboard against the wall). So if you jump into bed too quickly, you'll find yourself whipping the covers back to reach down and turn it on. I only mention it b/c I hope maybe the designers might take this into consideration in the future. Even though I feel this way about the power cord/control unit, I would still purchase this one again w/o hesitation. It is built w/ quality in mind & my wife loves it...so that's that.

title: Probably the best of its class!
text:
This little trimmer is as far as I can tell; the exact same or nearly the exact same design as the rest of these identical-looking trimmers: not the most well-built thing in the world but gets the job done as long as you don't abuse them. But one thing sets this one apart from the rest of them:

This company actually OFFERS replacement parts!! That is HUGE with these things. Most of the blades on these things will last maybe 3 months or so and then, because their parent company offers no parts, you need to throw the entire thing away and buy a new one. Such a waste!

Not in this case! The company allows you to purchase replacement blades for the trimmer and they even have a little maintenance guide that comes with it that recommends you oil it! I don't think I've ever seen any other company even mention maintenance with these things.

Sure you pay maybe $5 or $6 more buying one from this company; but it comes with replacement parts and it's fairly easy to take apart to maintain. So long as the electric motor and those plastic gears that drive the blade stay intact this device should last the longest out of any other company due to the support offered.

Highly recommended if you need a little trimmer like this!

My only gripe is that it's difficult (or impossible? I did not try very hard as I don't want to break it yet.) to get to the plastic gears that drive the blade from the electric motor. I did get some silicone lubricant (So it doesn't damage the plastic) down the neck of the device but I would've felt more confident it's lubricated properly if I could get to the gears.

title: Helping My Feline with Large-Cell Lymphoma
text:
My 13 year old kitty, David, has large-cell lymphoma. It is diffused and there are several masses. He was diagnosed May 26, 2019. The oncologist's prognosis, after the ultrasound and biospy, was a month to live without chemo and a few months with. I didn't want to go down the chemo or steroid route. So I started digging for other possibilities.

I purchased this infrared device after reading NIH studies showing that Infrared looks like a promising tool for mice with cancer.
Dr Turchin has been amazing in communicating with me as I navigate through all these unknown waters. He has been so helpful.

David is at 50 days post diagnosis and is continuing to do well without chemo, steroids, or any other drugs. According to the prognosis, he should have died 20 days ago, but here he is with good quality of life. He gets a weekly B12 shot, daily infrared, and daily acupressure, and fresh food without alot of carbs (which promote cancer in cats).

His vet did new bloodwork four days ago and the results just returned. His liver enzymes are almost in the normal range now and everything else looks good. This is a great improvement from May ... and there is no medicine to thank for this because we arent using any. Think about that ... it is exactly the opposite of what it "should be" happening. I'm so thrilled with this outcome.

I believe that this device is contributing to David's quality of life and am so grateful for it. I cannot fully replicate the NIH study on mice with David, but I would like to believe that it may be helping to kill his cancer cells slowly as well.

50 days in, Tams and David, Atlanta Ga,
July 17, 2019.

text:
THE GOOD: It does work well to open tight jar lids and it does work well as an oven mitt. I also LOVE the concept of germ-resistant dish-washing product.
THE BAD: I am VERY disappointed in its ability as an all-purpose dish-washing product. I had a large, Teflon-coated fry pan that I used to brown hamburger meat. Even doubling the normal amount of dish soap I would normally use, the mitts just smeared the meat fat around. Another time, I was washing out my slow cooker used for making chili. Even though the leftover scrapings were minimal, the silicon teeth of the BetterSponge would just float over the crusted food and would not scrub the food off. In both cases, I resorted to my very old, worn out, green scrubber and had instant success. I bought the BetterSponge with the plans of disposing of my dishrag and my scrubber. The BetterSponge would mean having THREE washing products at my kitchen sink which is ridiculous, so I sent it back.

As I said, it's a close shave; just gotta use small, slow circles as instructed and I get a super close shave every time.

Replacing batteries is simple and straightforward; nothing too fancy, but the water proof design does mean that you have to close up the battery compartment completely. If you use water to clean the electric razor, then make sure to follow up with the suggested machine oil on the foil. It makes a huge difference over time, if you don't.

The guard is so simple, yet effective, Plus, it works as a safety mechanism when in the upward position, so the razor won't turn on while you're trying to change the batteries, or just not using it. I've gotten pretty used to the feel of that guard part in my hand while I shave. Everything else feels weird to use now lol

All in all, a great electric razor, and even though I've dropped and wrecked a couple on tile floors, I always come back to it, because it's the best razor I've had in 20 years of shaving.

title: Saw improvements in infected fish in a few hours :)
text:
So I only got this today but I'm going to share some things I've already noticed about my infected fish.

I have a 5.5 gallon tank with 7 fish. 3 guppies, 1 adult swordtail, and 3 juvinile swordtails. They are going to be moved to a 15 gallon tank this weekend hopefully with their trapdoor snail friend.

Just 3 days ago I noticed camallanus worms from my smallest guppy. He had been skittish more then usual but I thought that may be due to the juvinile swordtails being about his size and more active then as fry. I noticed the worms later in the evening and acted quick to do a water change and gravel vaccum of the tank as well as changing the filter. The sick guppy hadn't eaten anything for 3 days nor has he had bowel movements. Pretty soon 2 of my other fish showed worms, a medium guppy, and a juvenile swordtail. Luckily they were both still eating even by today.

So by following another review I did 5ml per gallon of medicine after disolving it in 1/2 cup of water. So about 25ml for my tank. Before adding the medicine, I did to a water change of about 50% to also vaccum up old feces so I can monitor the water condition before and after putting the medicine in. The two more infected fish who hadn't had bowel movements FINALY had some a few hours after I put the medication in. The worms are still visible but I can see some in the droppings as well meaning that they are being pushed along through the fish. The small guppy also has his appetite returning and is returning to swimming around the tank with his guppy friends. My juvinile is having more active bowel movements like before for a fry and is acting energetic again. Before I put the medicine in, I did remove my snail and put him in a seperate containment away from the fish and medicine so that he would be safe.

Make sure to remove your carbon filter when administering the medication or it'll all get sucked up into the filter. And remove any shrimp, crabs, or snails from the tank. Don't overdose the tank but also don't underdose. Thank you to the kind fellows who figured out the ratio as it seems to be working out in my tank.

If anything goes drastically wrong I may update this but it looks super promising!

title: Worth the extra money!
text:
My grandparents were going on a cruise to the Caribbean and I decided to give my grandmother something she could enjoy during her trip. She has mobility issues and I wanted to give her a new walker. I was not very happy with the walkers that she has had, all of them very flimsy, and thought that a better quality walker could be a perfect gift.
I made an extensive research on Amazon and the Comodita Brava caught my attention. I was attracted by the modern design and the fact that it is so compact. There were no product reviews when I purchased and that was a concern, but I checked the reviews of other Comodita walkers and that made me feel confident to go ahead.
I just received the walker and gave it to my grandmother. She loved it and I loved it too! Beautiful color (champagne) and very stylish. Very easy to maneuver and grandmother says she feels very confident using it.
It takes a little while to assemble but no big deal. The travel bag that comes with it is SO convenient! Very nice touch!
It is more expensive than an average walker, but it is definitely worth the extra money. Very happy with my purchase.

title: Manufacturer claims this contains cat's claw: UNTRUE!!
text: Believing the manufacturer's claim that the product contains a species of Cat's Claw (they state on this site it is the species Uncaria rhynchophylla, Gou Teng), I purchased this only to discover that the fine print on the label states that it contains "cat's claw" from the source ranunculus ternatus, also known as catclaw (not cat's claw) buttercup. It is a 12" wild buttercup that grows in China and has no use in Lyme disease or other tick-born illness. The Cat's Claw used in Lyme disease (either Uncaria tomentosa or Uncaria rhynchophylla) is a 100 ft. woody vine that grows in the South American Jungle. I called Samsara twice leaving a message describing my concerns and asked for a call back to discuss this before writing a review. The hand trigger is easy to use and doesn't cause cramps in your fingers or hand. The parts are very easy to put together and stand up to a lot of washing. (also comes with spare parts!) Being able to pump straight into the storage bag is also a plus. With my second child I had to pump into a standard bottle then transfer into a disposable for feedings. You can use this pump with Avent traditional bottles too. The silicone petels are great for stimulating let down. I can empty both breast in no time. If you are in a real rush and need to double pump...buy two, it is still less expensive than an electric!

title: Too Much and Yet, Not Enough
text:
I purchased two (2) cutters, which were well packed with an informative invoice/flyer, and promptly delivered.

I hoped that these cutters would replace a similar simpler cutter. (Its blade became dull after years of use). Upon inspection of my two new cutters, I was disappointed to note that there is a pair of arms at each of their sides, which seem to be intended to stabilize the cutter, though after several uses, I can report with certainty that the arms more likely are a well-intended classic example of over-engeneering, which does a dandy job of making it impossible to retrieve my pill pieces with my fingers. Since the arms prevented me from picking my pill pieces out of the cutter, I had to fully open the device, and dump my pills out (ideally onto a piece of cloth to prevent the pieces from bouncing away).

The sad thing is, I have managed to cut about 5 or 6 out of 10 of my quarter inch pills with convex sides in half.

There must be a way for design wizzards to overcome this, and while they're at it, save some plastic by doing away with those bothersome arms! There's too much design intended to ensure an even cut, yet not enough design to accommodate rounded pill sides and easy retrieval of pill pieces. (Great seller, but a so-so product.)

I am a 6'2" 205# male. i ordered 3 styles of camp ben products. CAMP BEN (TM) LARGE Padded Posture Corrector was difficult and frustrating to get on and very hard to reach under my arms to adjust, i took off the padded shoulder portions and it was somewhat easier to get on.

The Figure 8 Clavicle was very uncomfortable under the arms, i think due to the extra thickness of the straps and it dug into my arms and chest much more than the padded unit. it's labor day weekend and am still expecting one more unit to test.

The 3rd unit worked best for me, it was the CAMP BEN Posture Corrector Clavicle Brace. The vertical strap on the back allows you to reposition the underarm straps depending on your size. For me I lowered it to the very bottom. I wore it all day yesterday and again today. Today I think I found an easier way to get it on and adjust it. I attached the hook end of the velcro strap end only about a 1/2" on the loop portion, then when I put it on I could reach under my arms and easily detach the straps and pull them tighter. it you attach all of the hook portion it is much more difficult to detach when reaching under your arms. this method would probably work with all 3 units.

title: Sadly Disappointed
text:
I never leave reviews, but instead rely on others' reviews to determine if I'd like to make a purchase. This scale got glowing reviews, for the most part. Hence why I bought it. I wish I had paid closer attention to the the not-so positive reviews. I received my scale and it's clean, sleek and gorgeous! The numbers are very visible, even in a brightly lit room, and it's great and convenient that batteries were included. I especially like that you're able to switch the weight reading between kilograms and pounds.

That's where it ends, unfortunately. The readings are sadly and bizarrely inaccurate. Only my first weight reading was close to being accurate. All subsequent readings show my weight as 20 lbs lighter. Even though that's my immediate weight goal, I just know from weighing on other scales (work, the gym, the hospital, the mirror😩) that I haven't lost 20 lbs. Another disappointment is that the reading is different EACH time I step on it, off of it, then on it again. I do it 3-4 times and the reading is 2-4 lbs different on each occasion, including the lighter 20 lbs.

It's annoying to see people give a product a low rating for what seems like a petty issue. However, this is just too much of an issue that now forces me to buy another scale. I have to lose a certain amount of weight for health reasons, and I need to be able to accurately assess my weight loss/gain. So sad...

title: Is that a banana in your pocket?
text:
George and I are on planes often enough that leg cramps are a real issue. So we like to keep a source of potassium handy--like a nice, ripe banana.

So ripe in fact that we need to use "protection." The Banana Bunker sounded like a great solution. The first time we passed through security at LAX, the TSA was doubtful. The Banana Bunker showed up in the X-ray, and we had to answer some pretty embarrassing questions.

So this last trip, I told George to keep the bunker on him going through security. It was was made of plastic, after all, and wouldn't set anything off. But naturally George forgot to remove his belt, which triggered the metal detector--and a pat down.

The TSA agent nearly jumped back when he felt the bunker. "What's this?" he said.

George didn't miss a beat. "This sounds like a punch line, but there's a banana in my pocket," he laughed.

"A banana?" the guard frowned.

"Or, maybe it was just a great pat down," I offered.

Even George was caught off-guard. "Oh myyy, Brad. That was sassy."

title: A Good and Affordable Heat Patch.
text: This is a good, affordable heat patch. The patches are very easy to use and do not get too hot. They are a warm, soothing temperature similar to an animal laying on you. The four belts included are a lightweight material with two pockets for patches and a thin velcro-like clasp making them easily adjustable. The product image implies that these are best used for your back but I have been using them anywhere that the belt fits around. I have MMAS which is a chronic joint disorder. I cannot walk or sit for long periods of time without severe pain in my joints. I have used an electric heat pad for years now but the problem with that was the lack of mobility. This belt helps to carry around the heat with me so I can still do things while treating my pain. It is great that the price is affordable because pain can strike anyone. The one improvement I would make to the belt would be to add a type of velcro to the top of the openings for each patch so that the patches don’t fall out when you lay down. Overall, if you need an affordable, heated, mobile form of pain relief, I think this is it.

title: Tasty soda with a little bonus
text:
I was on a kick checking different dietary supplements that don't make me feel like I'm taking medicine to unwind. Having already tried and enjoyed this brand's Brownzzz (relaxation brownies, that is), and my being a fan of soda, made this an easy purchase. This is indeed an antithesis to popular energy drinks, and I gave it a shot based on its promise. This is something you want to take your time with. Sippin' Syrup is not just a clever name.

The brand's unusual collection of flavors make it stand out from the norm, and it doesn't taste like medicine. It's fizzy and light, and it takes effect pretty quickly. The bottle says it's 2.5 servings per, and I certainly don't recommend drinking the entire thing unless you want to play Rip Van Winkle in a community theater production. Just a few sips, and I'm off to slumberland. Counterpoint: my friend drank, against my advice, a whole bottle of another flavor (blue) and he was totally fine the next day. The soda's tasty. The supplements work.

title: Great for musicians
text: I play guitar in a funk/blues/jazz band, and practices can get quite loud. To protect my hearing, I bought several brands of earplugs including Hearos, Etymotic, and NoNoise (music version). With standard foam earplugs, the high frequencies are disproportionately attenuated such that all you hear is the low (bass) frequencies. As a musician, this is a nightmare--all you can hear are the bass notes and the drummer's kick drum. Of the three brands I've tried, NoNoise does the best job maintaining the high frequencies while reducing the overall volume of the music. There is a tiny bit of roll-off at the highest frequencies, but I was able to play a live show while wearing them. With the other brands (Hearos and Etymotic), the reduction of high frequencies was too great to make them useful on stage. The NoNoise earplugs are the priciest of the bunch, but they are worth the extra cost.

title: It worked!
text:
My 5 year old had a chalazion for 5 months. It kept getting bigger. I was applying heat 2 to 3 times a day for over 2 months. She wouldn’t tolerate it for more than 10 minutes at a time. The eye looked so bad that it was the only thing people noticed about her.

I was ready to request that an ophthalmologist surgically remove it. I found this product when I was doing a Google search for an ophthalmologist.

So, I decided to give it a try. Why not? $26. My copay for a consult is $80 and I’d probably spend $1,000 and have a traumatized child if she had the surgery.

The oil doesn’t have a strong scent. It doesn’t burn, but my daughter did not appreciate me massaging it on her eyelid 3 times a day....especially when over a week went by and nothing changed. I assumed I’d be calling an ophthalmologist.

On the 10th day of using the oil, my daughter was laying in bed and felt something moist on her eye. The chalazion was draining from the outside. She wouldn’t allow me to press on it to drain it much. But, I kept rubbing the oil on it, 3 times a day and the eyelid kept looking better.

It’s been a month since we got the oil. She has a tiny scab on the eyelid and I’m still rubbing the oil on it once a day. The bump is gone. I don’t know exactly what is in this product. I don’t know if the ingredients are effective, or if the act of massaging the eyelid is what made the chalazion heal. But, it’s the best $26 I’ve ever spent.

title: E730 Model-Good Value for the $800 Spent
text:
For a little background on me, I used to be a manager at Brookstone and have sold several different models of massage chairs. I don't claim to be an expert, but I know a thing or two. Now for the review:

I've owned this chair (E730) for a little over 5 months now for $800 from the Cavalier Store.

Shipping process:
I don't remember exactly how long shipping took, but I remember it being right in the middle of the delivery window. The shipping company would not step foot on my property and would not come through the gate to the backyard. I'm in Chicago so they left it in the alley and I dragged it through the gate by myself. The company called me a day before and told me approximately when it would arrive so that I could be home to sign for it.

Getting it inside and assembly:
This thing is heavy and big. You definitely need two strong people to carry it. It comes two pieces: the main unit and the foot massager. It was a challenge to fit it through some of the door frames. I had to take two of the doors off so make sure it will fit through yours. Assembly was pretty easy, just follow the instructions and connect a few hoses together for the airbags.

The massages pros:
The massage is really nice. I think it's a little on the harder side so it may not be the best for people who are sensitive, but I love a good hard massage. The airbags feel really nice, especially on your calves. I really like some of the pre-programed massages. The zero gravity really take a load off your back. I used to get massages about once a month and I've stopped going completely since buying this chair. The chair looks nice and the faux leather is really nice too.

Cons: The machine definitely has some quirks to it. For instance, if the timer runs out or if you want to switch from one pre-programed massage to another and you are in zero gravity, the chair will go fully upright and then you can put it back into zero gravity again. The user interface is moderately featured, but is lacking in some areas. I wish there was more customization. For instance, there are a number of manual options, but no way to program a custom massage. There is not a way to designate which airbags to use, it's either all or none. The airbags on your feet can be a little too strong. I don't know if this is just my machine, but the body scanning has not worked at all since day one. It's stuck on the tallest height setting and I cannot change the settings to fit someone smaller. But I'm 5' 10" and it's perfect for me. I haven't reached out to any kind of support to try to resolve this issue. Other than that, I've had no mechanical issues with it. Lastly, there are bluetooth speakers on the outside of the chair, but they are absolute garbage. But who buys a massage chair for its speakers?

Overall rating 7.5/10. It was well worth the $800 I spent on it. I see that it's going for about $1300 now, I'm not sure it's worth it at that price, but it's a solid machine.

A word of advice for any massage chair shopper, BUY THE WARRANTY! I haven't had to use it yet, but many massage chairs, even from well known name brands breakdown and you don't want to spend all this money just for it to die in a few years.

title: Received the Correct Chair
text:
I titled my review as I did because several people commented that the chair they received is not the one shown in the photos. I can confirm that I did receive the correct chair - Model# DK-EC9006-Black-FDW. FDW is Factory Direct Wholesale - this company sold their chairs through Costco recently, and as of June 2019, they are sold at Sam's, so they are a known, trusted company.

First impressions - I ordered this chair on a Monday night, and I received it on Friday... much quicker than I expected. The chair arrived as scheduled on a large truck. I wasn't sure if the driver would only leave it at the curb, but he brought it into my garage. Upon request, he transferred the box from the pallet onto a dolly I had ready, and he took the pallet with him. The unit was packaged very well, with multiple layers of cardboard, wood, and dolphin skin wrap. It was very easy to attach the foot part, and this was accomplished in less than five minutes.

This chair has been in use now for two weeks, and has run multiple times per day. The rollers are very strong, and do run from the neck to glutes. The foot rollers are also very strong, and the air bags work very well. I had tried an Infinity chair (probably the most expensive chair on the market), and although this chair is not quite as good, it is also about 1/15th the cost. As far as value goes, I don't think you can do better. I did a lot of research, and this chair is the best value I found. The only question at this point is durability... I hope it holds up for at least a few years. I don't often leave product reviews, but I felt obligated to do so in order to counter the reviews that suggested you will receive a different chair. I can't speak to those claims, but I can confirm that I did receive the correct chair and so far it is fantastic!

Ring finger (Left): I never tested this finger, I decided to let my nail continue to grow. I have my reasons.

Feet:

Large Toe, Left foot: DO NOT USE THE CLIPPERS ON THIS TOE! I was halfway done before I realized. I was careless and failed to understand. Please make sure you do not.

text:
As a dental assistant, this earplug are as advertised! Blocking the high pitch noises of drills, cavitrons, low speed, rumbling noose biosonic, trays’ making machine: any and all noise of a bustling dental office!

I had a week or so to get used to wearing this. Tips: you may speak louder than normal when you first wear them, a couple days and you will adjust. Tell your Drs, managers and receptionists that you wear noise reduction earplugs so they know and repeat if you can’t hear them xD!

I wash them with cold water and soap after each day in the shower, then dry them, because if not, I can’t wear them! Actually, it got softer and adhesive more to my earlobes!

Oh, be prepared to have a sore earlobes for two weeks while wearing them, but after two months now, I’m adjusting well. Wish I had discovered this sooner. I assisted with a 2 hours crowns, this earplugs blocked the drilling on metal crowns so well, I could suction for 8 hours with ease~~~.

Talking with patients is clear when I adjusted well to wearing them. There are 3 layers of masks so I have to raise my voice!

Make sure you put the landyard including to the earplugs, it helps puttting them on and off a piece of cake~. I looped the cord around my high bun and most patients won’t even know I had an earplugs. I did tell some patients and asked them to speak louder in case I don’t react to their sayings. All our patients are very nice and understood completely.

A very valuable earplugs for dental staffs! High recommend to all! It is as advertised, dampening the high pitch noise, you can still hear the noise, but it is much like a rainfall layer covering it. Sometimes I thought they didn’t work and took one earplug out to hear, and oh yeah, they work perfectly. Don’t hesitate, it worths every penny!

title: I bought a pair for myself because I had to go back to him for another procedure and I absolutely HATE the sound of the drill and thought maybe it ...

I bought a pair for myself because I had to go back to him for another procedure and I absolutely HATE the sound of the drill and thought maybe it could help me with my anxiety. WOW!! I was astonished at how much the sound of the drills/suctions scared me. I popped these things in before he started working and I can honestly say that my fear/anxiety was cut in half! Since I was numb I couldn’t feel anything and since it blocked the sound of the drill, I couldn’t really hear anything either but I could still hear the dentist when he asked me questions, etc. Really cool technology!  It seems as though the earplugs removed the “sensory” overload factor. So I could truly say I felt pretty relaxed, unlike most times. I told my Doc that he should buy a bunch of these and sell them to his patients haha! I definitely recommend them if you’re a patient or even a dentist or dentist nurse.

title: Cute! Fits snug. I ordered a small and I have a medium boot
text:
I measured my surgical boot from the last time ( it was indeed 16 inches tall by 8 inches around) so I knew that the tall boot cover would fit. My surgical boot from my right foot was a small last time, so I ordered the small for my boot I was getting on my left.

I am out of surgery and got a medium boot, but this boot stretched out over it well. I did not even undo the Velcro because it fit like a glove. The only thing it doesn’t do is zip up all the way if you don’t pull it to the top and over your boot ending (the part closest to your knee). I did notice that if I did pull it over the boot and zip it up all the way, it would leave an indention on my leg.

However, all of that to say the small size fit snug but well enough on my medium boot. I would say they are true to size, but I am happy with how the small fits on the medium. It just means it won’t be going anywhere no matter how much I move around.

I am excited because my toes are covered and I feel much safer from whatever the weather outside wants to throw at my foot. Not to mention I’m not ruining the Velcro on my boot by it attaching to the dog hair on the couch. 😂😂

title: Nice unit and support but sunrise too bright and fast for me
text:
The idea is great but not satisfactorily implemented for my particular needs. This newer model seems to be built reasonably well for the price, although I can't comment on the longevity since I'm returning it after just a few uses. I found the following to be issues for me:
-- Too bright too quickly (the dealbreaker for me): This is very subjective but it gets too bright too quickly for me, even at the 60 min (highest) setting. The 30 setting was linear but too fast and the 60 setting *seemed* (as I did not follow up with later verification) to have a sudden uptick in brightness, as if the sun just came up over the horizon. My main complaint here is that there is not enough lower-intensity ramp up time. Again, this is subjective on my part, based on my specific needs which weren't being met in this case. I didn't verify this perception with a light intensity meter.
-- Low volume "warbling" sound in speaker: This could have been a defect in my particular unit. From a technical view, it sounded lime poor power supply filtering. This artifact manifested only when the alarm button was enabled. After about a 1-2 second delay, a low whirring sound could be heard from over 6 feet away with good hearing. If the clock is far enough away or your hearing around 200 Hz is not too good, it may not be objectionable. I called customer service on this and in all fairness they said they had not heard of this complaint before. The person did seem to be genuinely surprised so it may have been a genuine defect and not respective of other units. I am inclined to give them the benefit of the doubt on this issue.
-- Size of Clock Digits: The size of the digits is too small for my almost 60-year old eyes.
-- Clock dimming feature: The clock only dims when the alarm button has been activated. The brightness cannot be adjusted otherwise.
-- Sleep Sounds: I only tried the ocean surf sound. What I found is that it was too loud on the lowest setting. Over time I could have adapted to that. However the unique portion of the recording was so short that I found I was caught in a "brain loop", like anticipating when the scratched part of a record would come around again for the skip. Very subjective on my part and may not be an issue for others. If I had chosen to keep the unit, I would have just disabled the sleep sounds.

Otherwise, the unit seems well-built. The customer service person was very patient and congenial. If you like a faster, bright sunrise, this clock may be for you.

title: Poor quality, loses time.

title: A nice way to wake up
text:
I live in a ground floor apartment in Chicago, the largest city within the Arctic Circle (it dips down to cover this part of the Great Lakes area), so I bought this lamp to help me wake up in my bedroom, where the sun does not shine. For that purpose it's been pretty great. It's designed to simulate dawn over a thirty-minute period - so if you set your alarm at 7:15 it will switch on to a dim setting at 6:45 and gradually increase to full power.

The first few weeks this was maybe over-effective - I would wake up 10 to 15 minutes into the simulated dawn. But even though I didn't get those extra 20 minutes of sleep, I did find it easier to get out of bed. It's a much more natural way to rouse than an alarm clock, and that's what I was looking for. I do think my body has started adjusting from that honeymoon period, but it's still nice to feel like I'm easing out of sleep, not jolting.

Several reviewers have commented on the poor interface and complexity of programming the lamp, but I don't find it too bothersome. Yes, it is more complicated than it probably needs to be - and if that's going to frustrate you, you may want to go in another direction. (I'm flashing back now to the early 2000s, when I futilely wrote out instructions for my parents explaining why changing the channel on the TV set was not the same as changing the channel on the digital cable box.) More irksome have been the repeated emails soliciting a review of this product - but here I am, so I guess that (like the lamp) served its purpose.

In the end, I award 4 stars because this really is the best tool I've found for waking up in a city whose winter rivals Westeros in length and intensity. Oh, also the "night" setting makes for a nice, gentle reading lamp. It's not a perfect score because it's not perfect: as you can see it's not going to be the most attractive light fixture in your domicile. And the array of tiny LED bulbs can seem a bit institutional. But it is an incredibly useful tool, and sturdy enough that my roommate's undisciplined cats don't knock it off the window sill.
