title: Not that programmable.
text:
Just acquired a couple of these from another vendor and unboxed it a few minutes ago. It's... sort of pretty okay! Especially if you can't be bothered or don't have the space for a DIY solution. Definitely bright as a desk lamp at full. But not as configurable as you might expect.

The real features once you receive the lamp and the manual are:

-Dawn simulation, something like a 30 minute brightening at a set time.

-Noise alarm.

-Sunset simulation, something like a 30 minute dimming when you push the off button.

-3 user-settable color temperatures (daylight, mixed 'afternoon' light, warm white).

-Automatic color temperature shift (toggleable): Will adjust the color temperature at the designers' idea of what the appropriate times of day are. Actually an abrupt flipping between color modes at 1PM and 9PM... or you could think of it as selecting the 'right' mode for the time of day when you turn it on.

I guess you could skew the automatic adjustment by playing with the clock, but if you were hoping to automatically gradually dim the lights at _your_ bedtime without pressing a button, you're out of luck. I was _really_ hoping for that feature, but no dice. This makes me a sad wolverine (who stays up too late for lack of reminders).

[My wishlist would really be something like a 7-day timer with adjustable on/color-temp-and-brightness/off times... take a look at how programmable thermostats work, most let you start from setting for 'weekdays'/'weekends' and then you can override individual days from there or leave it alone. That's what's missing here.]

Various observations:

In some pictures the backlight looks like an obnoxious blue LED. I can report that it's a not-too-obnoxious white LED with a blue cast (somewhat resembles a white-blue EL backlight), which dims when you're not operating it and apparently goes out when the lamp is off.

The plastic/paint(?) is that rubbery matte finish that will probably show scuffs over time. Mine seems to have come with some whitish scuffing on the 'shoulder' of the front plate but I have yet to see if it will wipe off with water.

"You will instantly notice" quirks:

- Holding the -/+ buttons doesn't smoothly dim the lamp. You have a choice of something like 10 discrete settings when manually dimming. Which are only selected when you -remove- your finger from the button. Not exactly a dealbreaker but far more awkward than an "X10" remote control from two decades ago.

- Mode settings are indicated by blinking the status indicators. Which means that if blinking catches your eye, leaving the 'sunset mode' for the power switch activated will be catching your eye. Forever. At least it's nowhere near as bad as blinking LEDs; still from the '$1 digital wristwatch' school of design. The curious thing is that they've got the ability to toggle the box 'circling' the indicators as an element, so they're not short on I/O lines to the LCD... 'circling' or 'uncircling' would also be less annoying than a blink.

If this is an advance over the "Per3", I look forward to the "Per1" or "Per0" if they iron things out and make it affordable. Give me more programmability - especially the ability to make it pull a sunset to 'dim but not off' by both timer and demand - and a slightly fancier diffuser [the one on the dumb-and-timerless "MarsLG" lamp I recently reviewed is spoiling me, but that prismatic sheet stuff has got to be what they're using in LCD monitors and must be becoming readily available by now - in comparison, this little guy makes everything throw 6 sharp shadows of 2 colors when in 'afternoon' mode] and I will not eat your fingertips.

Edit: Still sitting with the lamp on the desk at 9PM, I just caught it flipping into "evening" mode, so I can note that the color temperature changes are instantaneous - there is no gradual transition, disappointingly, just a timer you can't tweak except by skewing the clock. The cool backlight becomes far more noticeable in a dark office with the lamp in warm mode and 50% dimmed, but only to 'digital clock' levels... so while I'd prefer a way to kill it, it's not too bad (it does shut off when the light's off and you're left in the dark.. so this is another lamp with a 'this light is on' indicator light of a mismatched color, great).

It also _seems_ like the lumen output goes down accordingly (where the afternoon mode uses all 6 emitters, but morning and evening modes only use the warm or cool 3), but I don't have a light meter around and I'm a bad judge of absolute brightness across different color temperatures. I sort of want to take this down to 3 stars for doing little better than I could do with individual warm/cool lamps and dimmers/timers, but I'll leave it at 4 for trying and convenience. What I really need are "go home already" / "go to bed already" signals for work and home, and the fixed timing and lack of a way to tell it, say, "Okay, gradually dim to 50% and warm by 8PM, then 10% and warm by 12:30AM and stay there until I turn you off" means it doesn't quite meet my needs. Still better than nothing - and far better than sitting under unchanging workplace lighting into the night.

To recap from the above, the color 'auto-shift' timings are:

5:00 AM: Morning (Cool white)
1:00 PM: Day (Mixed - both banks on)
9:00 PM: Evening (Warm white)

So if you leave the lamp on all night, at 5AM it'll pop from warm to cool; then at 1PM it'll pop from cool to mixed - and possibly increase apparent brightness for both banks of LEDs being on; then back to warm and maybe less bright at 9PM.

title: From a home health nurse
text:
I'm a pediatric home health nurse, and I use the thermometer available at the client's home to take temperatures. I'm used to using axillary thermometers, so when I saw this one at a new case, I had to read the directions. Push the button once, wait until you hear two beeps, then press it to the child's temple. Another beep about 10 seconds later, and you have the temperature.
It's fast and accurate, I use it on the baby I care for, and myself as well! I like it so much I'm getting one for my own son. That's the frustration I've had with regular over-the-counter axillary thermometers- they are not fast (even 60 seconds is a long time to hold a thermometer under a sick baby's arm), and they are not very accurate (if an axillary thermometer is slightly cool you can take a temperature over and over and keep getting a higher number).
Although most children don't mind having a thermometer under the arm, babies do. This is great, and a great price for the accuracy. And of course, I don't have to worry about germs anymore with this thermometer, because it won't be going in anyone's mouth.

title: IF GOOD HEALTH IS YOUR GOAL LOOK NO FURTHER!
text: It never ceases to amaze that people expect a gourmet experience when taking a whole foods supplement! This is freeze dried acerola cheery and it tastes like acerola cherry!  The acerola cherry is very tart, and the freeze dried version is very tart!  If you want sweet, and don't mind something straight out of a test tube, then seek out one of the many maltodextrin (corn sugar) enhanced powders out there.  If you want the BEST 100% natural product for your HEALTH, then look no further.  One serving is 1 teaspoon, but that gives a person 800% of the daily requirement.  I don't believe in mega-dosing anything, and so I take 1/4 teaspoon which still gives me 200%of what is needed.  I've never found an acerola powder that mixes well with water, so I just pop it straight into my mouth and chew it.  Yes, it is tart, but it only takes a moment to consume, and then I swish some water.  You could also take the advise of Mary Poppins and take with a spoon full of sugar (honey for instance) if you really must have something more palatable, and if you demand that all of your food be an entertainment experience.

title: usually bad. However after trying this and seeing no one ...
text:
I've never been one to leave reviews on Amazon and after probably several hundred orders I can count on one hand the times I've left a review, usually bad. However after trying this and seeing no one else saying anything I've been feeling a little compelled to share my experiences with it.

Now before we start I'm just going to say I grew up with John Meadows in a small town and tried out his Intra-MD peri workout drink for the last couple of years and continue to consider it the best on the market, I'm not a professional or even a heavy body builder, I just do these things in my spare time to keep in shape at 45.
Which brings me to this product, while I was doing research on weight loss and supliments every review I would read was an obvious marketing ploy by the company selling the product. I looked all over for a non-bias review and couldn't find any. So I had heard that John had started his own line of supplements, and knowing he was a good guy in high school I figured what the heck I'd try this.
It worked. Quite well in fact. The instructions say to take two pills 30 minutes before breakfast, but I broke that up into one in the morning and one six hours later and it worked fine. I make it through about 12 hours before I get hungry agian. I've lowered my calorie intake while maintaing my usual physical activities and am losing weight. This isn't, and there is no such thing, as liposuction in a pill. You have to expend more energy then you take in as calories, short and simple, and this supplement aids quiet well in managing your hunger and the negative side effects of a reduced calorie diet.
I don't know what else to tell you but it works. This aids you, greatly, but the hard work is still up to you.

title: Rock Doc you suck
text:
I really wanted to like this product and application was a breeze. I guess that doesn't matter for anything if the product simply doesn't work. Two cans (purchased at my local Lowes) and three very generous applications later, our granite still soaks up liquid.

Update:

Since posting my review I have learned that not all granites are created equal. After trying 2 other products without a proper seal, I gave up and called a professional. A local stone company rep came to my house to give me a bid on getting it sealed right. He was surprised how porous my granite was as he said that this is typically only seen in lower quality granite (which he assured me mine was not). He quoted $400 to seal it using 2 coats but could not guarantee that even that would totally seal it. He said "he would prefer not to inherit my problems" and told me how to do it myself with the products he uses.

Both products are from Modern Stone Technologies which was not sold locally but there are a few online retailers that will ship it. I purchased a quart of "Scorch" stripper to remove all the other sealants and start with a clean surface, and a quart of "Clear Guard" (solvent based) sealant. I am happy to say that after 2 coats my granite is sealed and I have my kitchen back! While Rock Doc didn't work for me, neither did allot of other consumer sealants so it really depends on how porous your granite is.

title: Worthy performer
text:
This walker was purchased a month ago to provide my elderly mother a better solution than two walking sticks. While she used to get by with the canes, she needed something with more stability, and this is most certainly a sturdy, well-built walker. The offset of the horizontal bar makes it easy to navigate stairs, as the front wheels can be placed on a lower stair while the rear wheels maintain contact with the upper stair. When the brakes are set, by pushing down on the brake handles, the rear wheels lock into place, so the walker won't roll away on an uneven surface. It is a little wider than the doors in the house, but by simply pulling on the webbing strap that's on the seat, it is possible to collapse the walker slightly to fit it through the door without compromising its stability. Once through, by pushing on the sides of the seat, the walker is effortlessly snapped back into place. Initial assembly is also a quick, straightforward process.

While this walker may be pricier than other options (and admittedly, none of the other ones have been tried to compare performance), I find it was worth it. The peace of mind alone, knowing this walker will reliably offer my mother the support she needs to get around, makes it a valuable addition to the household.

text:
I originally bought the Fruity Cereal flavor protein powder and it tasted exactly what was advertised - however, it was a bit too sweet for my taste, almost like a dessert, so I wanted to give the Cinnamon Swirl a try.

Like the Fruity Cereal powder, I was impressed with the nutritional facts and was particularly excited that BCAA's were included. I also had no issues with drinking it (I had it with milk in a shaker bottle) and didn't experience any digestive problems.

Unfortunately, I have to say I was disappointed with the flavor of the Cinnamon Swirl even more although it smelled pretty good. Although the initial swig of it isn't bad (it's still very sweet), the after-taste is awful and tastes just plain rancid somehow. If you're unlucky enough to sip on a small clump of the powder, then you'll know what I mean. I can't stomach the taste no matter how hard I try because of the after-taste so I'm going to have to pass on Innosupps from here on out.

text:
These filters are pieces of junks and they fail very quickly by creating super loud noise!!!

I bought these filters for my Philips CPAP machine. At first sight, I found them in different sizes and texture compared to my original ones, but I didn't take it seriously. While during the first two nights they worked just fine, both my wife and I were woken up around 3:00 am the third night by a very loud noise made by my CPAP. It was just like someone is snoring heavily right next to me! The next morning, I tested multiple times and found the noise was actually due to the failure of the so-called "ultrafine" filter. While it should be soft, but now felt just like a piece of very hard & rough paper!

I thought this was just a coincidence, so I replaced another new ultrafine filter. Guess what?! Three days later, it failed again by waking me up in the middle of the night!!! The CPAP was to help me improve my sleep condition, but with these poor-quality filters, it has made my sleep much worse!!!

This is completely ridiculous since my original ultrafine filters would last for a month. I am very annoyed by these filters and wouldn't reorder them again! I would recommend anyone AGAINST buying these junks!!!

title: Very affordable &for the price, it can't be beat!
text:
This deal is amazing for the amount of pads you get for the price.. Initially, I was less than impressed with the level of stick the long pads had..or didnt have for that matter. However, that was only an issue when the pads were used for the very first time.. They just weren't getting a strong stick despite me having thoroughly prepped my skin by first washing the area with warm soapy water..pat dry with paper towels followed by fully air drying and applying 91% isopropyl alcohol to the area where I wanted to place the pads (& of course allowing it to dry first which only takes mere milliseconds lol) and still they just wouldn't really stay on. I had to stand there and hold them in place which was super annoying. I was slightly disappointed to say the least but considering that I did not have any other pads and I had already paid for,opened, & began using these ones I didnt feel right returning them and just tried to be positive about it and I went ahead and used the pads again fully expecting to have to physically hold the pads for the entire duration of the treatment.. But,strangely, to my [pleasant]surprise...this wasn't the case. This time, they were plenty sticky..almost too sticky at times lol. I did put on some tight spandex clothing just as a reinforcement cuz I will say that despite them being sticky (the 2nd time around lol) if youre moving around a lot and they happen to be in an area where the skin is highly manipulated during movement (like the lower glutes/"under-butt" area where the glute meets the leg)and you start sweating..if you don't have something like spandex shorts to keep them in place they will def eventually drop off..and I'll tell you what, having the pad begin to lose contact with the skin during a muscle building treatment(deeper more intense &full muscle contractions that are held for longer lengths of time) is sooo not fun! Its actually rather painful.. The pins&needles sensation is extremely amplified into more of of a stabbing sensation coupled with a very real shocking sensation and in my experience having the pad lift up like that actually intensified the muscle contraction 10 fold so now you've got this feeling of being stabbed, shocked, &the most painful cramping charlie horse you can imagine..it was almost paralyzing lol I couldn't even move I had to wait for the contraction to stop before I could move to push the pause button to figure out what in the world was going on! I do have to admit it was pretty conical despite the pain..I'm glad it happened tho as it lent itself to the expansion of my knowledge...salt water (aka sweat) is the #1 substance to increase conduciveness AND I wasn't crazy in thinking that the pad lifting intensified the effect..cuz since the pads work by sendings signals back and forth between eachother passing thru&stimulating the muscles directly below that area.. When you slightly start to lift one of the pads of the skins surface it's still within range to successfully exchange signals,however the signal is now travelling a further distance which creates a stronger force on the muscles being stimulated. The example that helped clarify this for me was using your finger to move water. Create a set distance between point A& B and move your finger back and forth between those 2 points at a steady even rate/speed and note the reaction in the water ..now increase the distance between those 2 points(A&B) and repeat using the same rate/speed as before and you'll notice a significant increase in the intensity of the water movement even if the distance wasnt increased all that much..plus, the speed will naturally increase on its own due to the build up of momentum and the same is true for the signal being sent between the pads which you can really feel during those deep intense muscle building treatments.
Anyways, for this price, I totally think its worth it and have yet to find a better deal. I've found pads that were cheaper, but when the cost of shipping was factored in it was no longer a more feasible option.

title: The cover is basically quite well built and does well ...
text:
The cover is basically quite well built and does very well. It is made of heavy duty, water proof material. It fits my wife's portable mobility scooter very well. The tie-downs hold it firmly in place.

The corners are not reinforced. I suspect it was designed for use with racks with rounded corners, or to tie inside the corners of the rack. In such cases it should do well without reinforcement.

In my case, my rack has 90 degree corners and I wanted to completely cover the rack. It only took one 1000 mile trip to wear holes the two front corners, even though I attempted to pad the corners of the rack with rags, which did not stay in very well. Had the corners been reinforced, I would have given it 5 stars. I will get the corners reinforced, probably with a heavy vinyl material, then there should be no problem in the future.

Surprisingly, I thoroughly researched this product before I bought. I know its only 3 bucks, but I wanted it to be a $3 well spent. Pros: I personally like this watch because of its style. Its a really clean white and the Mirror LED is very fancy. Its not too big,like the other cheap watches from china and includes function for the date.

Cons: Shipping takes a month. The rubber is very flimsy and you have to poke through the holes on the band to get the metal piece through. The whole band is really quite weak. It isnt attached to the watch very well. No instructions on how to change the time, though youtube can provide that info. Also, this might be a deal breaker, but you need to press one of the buttons on the watch to see the time. It requires another hand.

All in all, fancy watch for super cheap that takes a long time to arrive. This is not a daily wear watch and should not be used in sporting activities. Treat it like you will treat a Skagen.

4. loss of focus and stamina, instead of having focus & stamina! I had to lie down to recover so I didn't feel my best going to work out.

I have no idea what BB did to the formula; but WHY! I have taken the TIME to return it for my money back. So disappointed at BB. I have now Purchased ION GLOW (GNC) tastes WAAYYYY better! and works with my skin and nails and DOES NOT give all the above feeling. I was always afraid of switching, but now having this experience has helped me to find a very healthy version of PRE-WORKOUT formula that tastes really good an give me the stamina and results I need to push through Bob Harper's Kettle Bell Ball Workout for 40 mins and even into the evening with just 2 scoops in 5 ounces of water. And I think I found out that BB added "Beta-Alanine 800mg, which a nutritionist stated might have caused that reaction. But anyway, it was horrible and NOT LIKE THE ORIGINAL E&E. Don't know who you're trying to compete with, BB, but you've lost a loyal customer. At least I don't have to Wait on an order now, I can go right to GNC and find the ION GLOW. And women, you just get that specific kind, b/c I think even ION products may have the Beta-Alanine, but the GLOW has very little, so you don't even notice it.

A truthful reviewer,

J, Matthews, Detroit

title: Chalazion Review
text:
Starting late August 2020, I had a chalazion that became a huge stye on my eye that I had to undergo surgery for in Sep. The surgery did help decrease the size. In early October 2020, my chalazion came back. In my attempt to save money, I tried Apple Cider Vinegar (ACV) along with warm compresses for several weeks. That helped decrease the size but it never went away. At the end of Oct. I purchased this oil. I’ve been washing my eyelids with “We Love Eyes” cleanser twice a day. After cleansing my eyelids, I use this oil. First I put half a drop in my eye and then I rub it on my eyelid and follow up with a warm compress for 15 minutes. I’ve been doing this twice a day for a week, it’s no longer red and raised. I think with continued use (maybe another week) it’ll be gone. I’m also considering using this nightly for preventative purposes, probably just putting half a drop in my eyes. It does not make my eye vision blurry afterwards, like some other ointments do.

My one complaint is that it’s super thick and kinda hard to get a small drop. It could also get a bit messy.

Don’t go into this thinking you’ll get miracle results after one use. Some reviews make it seem that way. My chalazion (by the end of Oct) was a lot smaller than what I started with and it’s going to take about two weeks to fully get rid of it.

TL:DR- after dealing with a chalazion for 3 months this oil has helped it heal better than initial surgery.

text: I rarely take the time to write a review, but this item certainly deserves one.  I developed a lump on my eyelid back in February which I assumed was a chalazion from what I had experienced in the past. It was not painful, just annoying.  I showed it to my ophthalmologist who agreed it was a blocked gland and referred me to another doctor whom she said could remove it.  I've had four major procedures done at this eye clinic and trust them completely, but I did not like the attitude of the doctor she referred me to so I left before he did the procedure which would have involved numbing my eyelid and cutting the clogged area open.  Back to square one.  Then I read about Goodbye Styes.  I am a believer in natural, herbal remedies, so I thought I would give this a try.  I did not use it as often as directed because it is obviously quite oily,  and I found that to be uncomfortable for daytime use.  I did use it twice a day and, within just a few weeks, I saw a noticeable shrinking of the lump.  It is now almost completely gone! I purchased the Princeton Model VF05 from Verilux about 2 years ago. At the manufacturers suggestion I also purchased an extra bulb. Last night the light went out and my husband, who is an electrician, took the bulb out and went to replace it with the new bulb only to see that the new bulb was defective. We tried the new bulb in another Verilux lamp we have and it did not work. My husband got out his multi-meter and trouble shot the whole lamp. Not working. Called Verilux and was told that it had to be the ballast. Electronic ballast. When I told Teresa that the new bulb was defective ( the white inside coating was missing in places) I was informed that the bulbs only have a 30 day warranty. I was told that I could buy a new lamp at a 25% discount but the bulb was already out of warranty and not covered.

This company pushes you to purchase a new bulb for $19.97 and then only warranties it for 30 days. These were supposed to be the best reading lamps on the market. They are not and I feel their practice of stearing the customer to an extra bulb at time of purchase knowing full well that the extra bulb will be defective within two years is just wrong.

I will never buy another Verilux product again and I strongly suggest that anyone considering it think twice and NEVER buy an extra bulb from this company. You can get this type of buld from any home improvement store at a much lower cost.

title: I love the feature for changing volume level
text: I received them 1 day after ordering (Amazon Prime).  Using the large silicone plugs I find them very comfortable. I play drums in a Progressive Rock band and after so many years I have noticed some problems with my ears. I should have started using something like this years ago, but I guess better late than never! Being able to change the level is quite a nice feature and is easy to do while wearing them after sliding the "switch" a few times to "break it in". I used them at band practice the night I got them.  Since we play fairly loud, I was still able to easily hear the music with them on the full setting (-24db). When things got a little quieter (rarely, lol) I could just switch to the lower setting. The magnetic feature is also very nice since it helps reduce the chances of losing them while they are not in your ears. All these things and the handy little carrying case make this a very nice product, even if a little pricey. I figure it's either get something of quality that's useful and adjustable like this now, or spend more money on hearing aids sooner!

The blue ones are the next softest, so I tried those for sleeping next. I have no idea what's up with them, but they hurt. They itched and burned so badly I had to take them out and again, return to foam plugs. I am certain that I inserted them properly.

title: Worth the money and some.
text: I received these earplugs a few days ago. I wanted to give them each a try for a couple necessary occasions so I could leave a completely honest and open review. First, no, they do not cancel out 100% of all noises. However, for those who need to wake up in the morning to an alarm it’s quite appreciated that a SLIGHT amount of noise can still get thru. I mean, who wants to have the inability to hear EVERYTHING? What if the fire alarm goes off(GOD FORBID) and you can’t hear it due to your earplugs being TOO sound proof. Lol idk maybe it’s just me. Anyway! Due to the extreme generosity that this package contains(6 sets of plugs/4 diff styles), I decided to share with my Mother who is an avid user of earplugs due to my Fathers inhumane storing. She normally uses the plain ol, regular ol, orange foam-like ones. She tried the blue pair as well as a pair of silicone ones. She found them both to be much more comfortable than her usuals. She said she could not hear my fathers wailing, I mean storing. Yet, she could perfectly hear her alarm when it was time for her to wake up. My 5yr old daughter HAS to be involved in anything I do. She’s my little mini-me/side kick. So when she begged to try a pair herself, I allowed her to use a pair of the silicone ones during a baby bath to test out how successfully the plugs are at keeping water out of your ears when submerged(she is a fish and MUST dunk her head as much as possible). She didn’t budge when I was placing them into her ears. I even pushed firmly to ensure a solid form and fit into her ear. It didn’t cause her a bit of discomfort while I was inserting them nor while they were in place and she was splashing in the tub. They stayed in place despite her wild bath time. The floor was drenched but her ear canals were indeed as dry as a whistle. These plugs seem to have a definite use for many different occasions. I feel if fitted into your ear 100% as properly as possible, perhaps they could indeed be 100% noise proof. I also feel that depends on each individual person and the sound they’re attempting to mute. Overall though, for the insanely good price and crazy amount of different ear plugs they provided within this ONE package, you really can’t go wrong. They’re 100% worth the money and I plan on continuing use of them as do my family members. :) sorry for the novel.

So when she begged to try a pair herself, I allowed her to use a pair of the silicone ones during a baby bath to test out how successfully the plugs are at keeping water out of your ears when submerged(she is a fish and MUST dunk her head as much as possible). She didn’t budge when I was placing them into her ears. I even pushed firmly to ensure a solid form and fit into her ear. It didn’t cause her a bit of discomfort while I was inserting them nor while they were in place and she was splashing in the tub. They stayed in place despite her wild bath time. The floor was drenched but her ear canals were indeed as dry as a whistle. These plugs seem to have a definite use for many different occasions. I feel if fitted into your ear 100% as properly as possible, perhaps they could indeed be 100% noise proof. I also feel that depends on each individual person and the sound they’re attempting to mute. Overall though, for the insanely good price and crazy amount of different ear plugs they provided within this ONE package, you really can’t go wrong. They’re 100% worth the money and I plan on continuing use of them as do my family members. :) sorry for the novel.

text:
I have fairly long, blonde eyelashes that sadly grow out stick straight, so they are barely noticeable if I have no curl or mascara on them. They do curl fairly easily with a normal eyelash curler, and I have even used eyelash perming kits in the past as well. I was tired of my lashes breaking off due to the wear and tear those cause, so I looked for an alternative.

I came across this heated eyelash curler and thought it would be a lot less damaging to my lashes, so I gave it a shot. The first time I used it I was pretty impressed with how quickly it heated up. On bare lashes, it takes about 20-30 swipes to even start to develop a noticeable curl. The curl itself is nowhere near comparable to a regular eyelash curler. The only way to get similar results to a traditional metal curler is to apply mascara before using the device and then brushing the eyelashes with it, but then the mascara becomes semi-liquid again against the heat and goes EVERYWHERE.

This curler is takes too much effort and is too costly to even compare it to a traditional curler or perming kit. Save your money, and go buy a $4 metal curler from Wal-Mart instead.

title: A Detailers Perspective||| 4.6 Stars
text: I bought this at a Walmart and one thing I see a ton of people saying is that it’s not working, it’s not removing stains, etc. This product works fantastic with good ol’ fashion elbow Grease. I recommend having a stiff plastic brush, preferably toothbrush styles, and a cheap shop vac or something to extract liquids. With that you just have to spray evenly over the spot let it sit for a minute and then scrub to your hearts content. Suck the liquids out with your shopvac and try a good 3-5 times and the stains really do come out quite a bit. If it still isn’t out there is a good possibility the stain has dyed the fabric or set too long. But as a stand alone product, it’s awesome. It’s the best bang for it’s affordable buck. I detail vehicles all the time and this with Voodoo green all purposes cleaner make a great match. So over all a 4.6 star review is what this would get. So please really put effort into the clean and you’ll see fabulous results.

title: More than expected
text:
I received my 16 Sanyo Eneloop batteries today in 4 4-packs, with 2 8-cell battery holders included as advertised. What I didn't expect is that these are the new model of Eneloops rated at 1500 recharge cycles instead of the previous 1000. The two free battery holders are mentioned in the "Technical Details" section of the webpage but nothing is said about the batteries being the new improved (and more expensive) version. The picture on the webpage shows the older type as well so when I ordered I was convinced I was ordering the older type. All my experience with Eneloops is with the 1000-cycle type. They are long-lasting and trouble free. They last really long in devices right out of their packaging without being charged. I deliberately buy the 1000-cycle type because they are lower priced than the newer version and because they are already super batteries so why pay a premium for new and improved? For all I know some other aspect of their performance might be compromised in boosting them to 1500-cycle so why take chances?

I'm very happy to have the new ones though. If price were no object I would have ordered 1500-cycle, truth be told. This isn't the first time I've gotten more than expected from Thomas Distributing "and Fulfilled by Amazon." A few months ago I ordered from Thomas, along with Eneloops (these did turn out to be the 1000-cyle type), a Maha Powerex MH-C9000 WizardOne battery charger. The charger came with a dedicated soft case with Powerex logo and in addition had by far the lowest price at Amazon for that charger on that day. These buying experiences leave me with a good feeling because it seems I can have the best batteries and the best charger while paying the lowest price and in both cases receive more than expected.

title: great oud power, slick/rich/easy, costly to run
text:
tremendously fragrant and extremely thick/rich/stable tallow-based croap. I consumed 3.05g of the soap in one session using a large 25mm Rein Dachs Silbespitz brush, for net cost 2.64% of net product for 1 lathering! If lather can get much more costly per use, I doubt I've met it, and I've got a hard milled Creed Vetiver soap. Hopefully less extravagant brushes do not burn through 3.05g/use and I'll try to curtail the burn rate...[UPDATE 02.05.2019; have used 4x w/ 'Reine Borste' (= small German 19.5mm boar brush) aiming for frugality. Consumed in 4 sessions 1.09 grams (= $0.23 based on price paid), 1.51g (= $0.32), 1.80g (= $0.38), & 2.50g (= $0.53)...over five uses 8.7% of the net product was used, or roughly 57 sessions in the tub...wow!]

The oud fragrance has depth and amplitude and is for my nose to the muskier side of the oud spectrum; there's some black pepper and patchouli with strong arriving tones of oud, sandalwood, and amber.

This soap makes it a cinch to get rich stable lather. Wetness is very good indeed; not world-beating, but still excellent. Volume's not on par with some old English creams (especially the Vulfix) but those are loaded with the 'bad stuff' to make them do that trick, this stuff eschews stabilizers/parabens. Also this WK does have lanolin, which usually sets me alight, and I could feel no signature lanolin tinge...poison's all about the dosage and all of that.

Slickness cannot compete Bourbonnaise but it is still quite slick indeed and slicker than pretty much any shaving cream with water. And of course it is easy to use, so that's a huge plus.

Cushioning is spectacular.

Soap's absolutely loaded in heavy fats to produce richness and post-shave euphoria, and it delivers. It does not make moisture that I feel 'within rather than upon me' as the Ziegen Bart, but the ease of use and high fragrance quotient will make up for that for many if not most. Due to all the heavy fats it is simply not possible to have a poor face feel unless you've an allergic issue (fragrance oils, donkey milk, etc).

A happy coda; over an hour later, the powerful oud scent of the shaving soap can still be detected by my nose!

title: How do you know this is effective?
text:
Bought unit to clean veggies and to make a disinfectant solution since the COVID pandemic. Other brand disinfectants are all gone. Also bought a Hanna Instruments test kit and the SenSafe test strips to measure the dissolved 03.

Ran a couple experiments at the 10min setting(#5) in1000ml and 400ml of tap water. Both showed low 0.4 to 0.0 PPM of 03. Ran the 1000ml twice so for 20mins and still not a trace of dissolved 03.

Contacted the manufacturer and no reply.

This is a big buyer beware. Especially if you think your solution is now killing bacteria and viruses. Just because this device bubbles in the water it is no guarantee you are getting a decent ppm of 03. The recommend levels for disinfection is any were from 2-4ppm. I got no were near this. Plus free 03 in the air in a hazard for breathing. We got asthmatics in the house so this purchase will go into the never again column.

text:
[[VIDEOID:4906b0eeb97740b6aa8918eb22f9e9d3]] This is my review on the FOMI Lumbar Support. Disclosure: I was offered this product at a reduced price in exchange for my honest and unbiased opinion. When I do a review I always get one or more people to put their opinion in on it, because people have different likes and dislikes and I feel the more perspectives I get on something the better I can review it.

So, my first impression of the FOMI Lumbar Support: Over all I would have to say it was fair. Sadly some of it's value was lost in my use of it has my chair has Lumbar support (and by my chair I mean my husbands that I steal all the time). So when you pile Lumber on Lumbar it gets a little un-comfy. Now if I laid back in his chair it kinda suspended my back similar to how a hammock would and that felt pretty nice and the massage beads were a very nice touch and were not too intrusive to the back. But all-in-all, not for me.

My moms assessment of the FOMI Lumbar Support: She put it in her van and drove around town with it for awhile then gave me her opinion of it. Overall she seemed happy with it but wasn't overly impressed by it. Though it's not necessarily uncomfortable, it could definitely take some getting used to.

I ALWAYS try to find at least one thing that could be improved upon or slight imperfection in every product I review because NO product is completely prefect for everyone.

So the main issues with this product is: 1) It could prove slightly awkward at first and may not use it long enough to get start feeling the long term effect it would have on their back. 2) It presents its self as having adjustable elastic straps, I feel this is slightly misleading. The straps themselves can not be adjusted. Now there are two straps going diagonally and one horizontally. This gives it a sense of flexibility to fit a variety of chairs, but I would not classify it as adjustable.

title: UPDATING MY REVIEW - Dissatisfied
text:
UPDATED 2 weeks out... Hate to report that my device won't hold a charge. I can charge it for several hours, but then only get 1-2 uses out of it for 2-3 minutes each, for a total of less than 10 minutes (combined over 1-2 days). I wouldn't even be able to use this on bangs over a weekend without needing to recharge. Intended to use camping and sailing for the wispy curly hair around my face when we have no power. Such a bummer because it's definitely hot enough and great size for travel if you only need to use it once and in a 5-10 minute job. I read that it only has a "life" of 45-50 minutes before needing to be recharged, so I assumed 3-5 minutes per day over a few days would be feasible.

***********I received my mini straightener yesterday. I charged it for several hours before use and tried it for the first time today. It's travel sized and not intended to straighten a full head of thick hair every day. The heated plate is pretty small but works for my needs. I purchased this for quick touch-ups on the frizzy hair around my face that goes crazy when we're camping or on the water for a couple nights. I have fairly thin, medium-length hair and I could probably straighten most of my hair with this handy little tool - but it would probably need to be re-charged if left on for more than 20-30 minutes (the label says charge for 150 minutes to get about 30 minutes of use). It gets plenty hot and since I am only using it for 5-6 minutes each time, it should get me through a few days without needing a charge. I am glad I purchased and would recommend to anyone who needs it for travel (shorter hair) - or - just touch ups like mine.

title: Extremely Poor Customer Service/Faulty Product
text:
As a pageant competitor, suit fastener is an essential for a polished look in the swimsuit competition. I was very excited to receive this product, but was sorely disappointed. First, the glue had leaked all over the outside of the bottle making it extremely sticky. I decided not to worry too much about it--nothing that a little wash under the sink can't fix right? However, upon opening the bottle, the product smelled absolutely AWFUL. Once again, being a pageant competitor, I have smelled my fair share of suit fastener and this smelled exactly the opposite, it smelled absolutely rancid. After having some pageant friends take a look at it, they advised I not put it on my skin. I then decided to email the manufacturer to see if I could get a new bottle and was treated horribly. I was told that I "didn't know what I was talking about, the glue always smells that way" and that "they inspect every bottle so it couldn't possibly have been faulty". Thinking it was useless, I left the bottle in my makeup case until my next competition. When I opened it again, the glue had leaked even more all over the bottom of my case, still smelling horribly, and it had turned an awful yellow color. I had to use a knife to scrape it out and then rip out the bottom of the case.

Needless to say, I am sure the bottle was simply faulty since I have had other friends use this product and it be fine, but the customer service and the way I was treated as a consumer was unacceptable so I would not advise purchasing from this company.

text:
I suffer from blepharitis and had two chalazions in a row before I started using this product. After more than a year, I haven’t had any flair ups and the chalazions are gone. The key to this product is consistency! I run about one drop on my eyelash line nightly after cleaning my eyes with Ocusoft.

Pros:
• Consistent cleaning and use reduces morning inflammation from blepharitis
• Helps prevent chalazions from reappearing
• If used at bedtime, you won’t wake up with a lot of eye crust
• My eyes feel more moisturized throughout the day

Cons:
• Packaging sucks. I’ve received this product where more than half the oil had spilled out and had to send for a replacement.. that was also spilled.
• Not an overnight cure-all.

If you’re currently suffering from a chalazion or big stye, I’d recommend this IN ADDITION TO warm compress and regular cleaning

title: This British Anthology Series RULES!
text: I knew Roald Dahl had written many stories for the Alfred Hitchcock Presents series and also some children's books and stories so I purchased his Tales of The Unexpected. Let me tell you, this is as good, if not better, than any suspense/horror anthology series I have ever seen. The acting is good, the picture quality is good, the audio is good but most importantly, the stories are GREAT! I watched 4 episodes within a week or so and was hooked right away. Every story has a twist ending and none of the twists are expected (hence the apt title). Some of the stories, particularly Lamb to the Slaughter, really blew me away. I also enjoy Dahl's introductions (in Set 1 and Set 2) in which he gives you a little bit of history of the story and/or its premise. I watch and collect almost every suspense/horror anthology series on dvd (Twilight Zone, Tales From the Darkside, Tales From the Crypt, Thriller, Night Gallery, Alfred Hitchcock Presents, Hitchhiker, etc., etc.) and Tales From the Unexpected is at the very top of that list (along with Night Gallery). I still have 3 more Sets to go and I can not wait to watch these episodes. I highly recommend it. It must be a British thing as I really love Brian Clemens' Thriller horror series from the 1970's as well. They really seem to treat their horror and suspense with class and respect and do it right.

I was super excited to use these milk straws as an incentive to drink more milk, but they absolutely did not live up to my expectations. I don't know if I got an old batch or something, but they didn't function the way I thought they would. There was only a very subtle amount of flavor, certainly not enough to notice. The little beads in the straw disintegrated down into flavorless crystals in under a minute. this wasn't just one straw, I tried this on two banana straws and one cinnamon straw and they all had the exact same result. I have no idea what happened but I am extremely let down. It's also worth noting that I got 20 banana straws, 10 cinnamon, 6 chocolate, 6 cookies and cream, and 6 strawberry. Overall absolutely unsatisfied.
Edit: I got a refund. Thank goodness. Doesn't change the product, but at least there's a safety net.

title: Not worth the money - but wait! - They got much better
text:
Update: I got a very nice call from the company and they spent 20 minutes walking me through my water report. I now know what I need to know about our water safety. During the call they informed me that they were going to modify their report to give more analysis to help understand the raw data. I really appreciate the good customer service and am updating my one star to a 3 on that alone. If the new reporting is as good as what I got on the phone call I would give it at 5. Hopefully they will show a sample report on their web site you can see before ordering. Caring about their customers is certainly a great quality and I have faith they will do what is necessary to earn the 5 star rating.

Original review - For such an expensive kit, the turn around time is unacceptable. It takes at least 3 weeks from the date you order until you get results. The 14 days they advertise begins when they get your sample and they take the entire 14. The results were disappointing as well. 200 lines of data with individual indicators of good, caution or too high. No cumulative analysis. Our purpose was to evaluate the safety of our elderly parent’s water, and although we have a good amount of data points, we have no idea if it is safe or not. Total waste of money.

Most powdered supplements have to be choked down, which is definitely where this sets itself apart.  Also, I tried Muscle Milk to compare. Phase III uses cellulose gel (also fourth ingredient) presumably as a thickener and stabilizer. text:
I've had it for about a week. I broke my wrist and just got the cast off and wanted something to wear for a little support every now and then. I don't know about the copper and all that, but I have noticed that the sleeve does stay cool for quite a while. I'm 5'9" and weigh about 165 and I got a medium. It feels to be the right about of tightness that you would expect from a compression sleeve.

Regarding some the complaints I read on here - there is a little gap between the sleeve and the palm. This is no big deal for me and don't get what the problem is. The reason I give it only 4 stars has to do with the seam between the thumb and index finger. It is quite annoying. I turned it inside out and that seems to help quite a bit, but I have had to wear it slightly pulled up so the seem doesn't rub on that skin too much, especially if I'm wearing it for a few hours.

But all in all, if you have something going on with your wrist and want a little extra support and compression for a few hours at a shot, this may be the only thing for you.

The basketball motif cover that came with it is very striking in a nice way, but I have never used it to prevent skin burns.  That is because the ribbing on the front and back is so deep that it prevents the bottle from getting as hot as I would like.  I can use the bottle directly on my skin without needing the cover. title: This stuff makes your clear coat blister up/off over time!!!
text: I used in a couple of years ago and the shine was just OK. Better, but not great. But that's not why I'm slamming this product. It took about 1 1/2 years and I noticed my clear coat was starting to blister! It started out with small points and then grew, taking off large section of clear coat. If one thinks "well, maybe this person's clear coat was not applied properly" {i.e. water in the clear or a moist surface when being painted}, well I can tell you that it was ONLY the sections that I applied this product is where it started to blister. I did the hood, the roof and the very top of the doors {not the hatch {{it had relatively fresh paint on it}} and applied not any other areas of the body}. I am currently having the ride repainted at GREAT expense. I live in South Florida where the sun load is strong. The car sits in the driveway and I use a cover about 50% of the time. I just wanted to warn anyone that you too may see your great paint job get ruined by using this product.{my paint, except for that trunk hatch} was 6 years old and looked perfect}. Beware- you are taking an expensive chance.

title: Most effective way to secure a Foley catheter tube, that I have found
text:
My dad needs these to help key his Foley catheter in place and not get tugged on when the Foley bag moves around a bit.

I've tried a lot of products like leg bands to hold the Foley leg bag firmly, but there is still quite a bit of movement if my dad walks, sits down, exercises, etc.

So using these is more secure. They last about 2 weeks. We dont undo the velcro, we have enough tube to just wiggle out the tube end and replace the bag.

The adhesive is pretty strong.
When we change the Cath Secure, we are using Cavilon barrier wipes on his skin before placing the cath-secure (adhesive side in contact with skin). Cavilon is a product meant to protect delicate skin from being irritated by adhesives from babdages needing to be changed often. I think it prevents skin from growing into the adhesive or bandage or it prevents the adhesive from truly bonding with the skin and the pulling some off (Ewww!). In any case its really effective. You can find in on Amazon.

title: Excellent for ME/CFS, mold illness, and many other chronic illnesses
text:
I have wanted my own detox foot bath for 10 yrs! I wasn't about to spend $2,000 to get a quality one like I have used in medical offices. I spent hours researching the different options and was thrilled to find this one. It has enough power and a 5 yr warranty to be comparable to the really expensive professional units. The unit is very bare bones, but it gets the job done and is very affordably priced.

I have been disabled for 4 years with ME/CFS after living in a moldy house that made me incredibly ill. I'm a member of an an online group (1,500 members) designed to help people with mold illness. I posted a link to this item after I bought mine in July 2015. I was very excited to find a product even those living on disability could afford and explained how I had benefited from detox foot baths over the years. Since I bought mine, dozens from our group have bought one too. We have been sharing our experiences over the past 6 months and have been absolutely astounded at how much this is helping everyone.

Once you have been exposed to toxic mold, it causes severe neuroimmune problems. We become incredibly sensitive to the tiniest of mold exposures, much like someone with a peanut allergy is sensitive to peanuts. We experience severe reactions that can include seizures, cognitive impairment, burning skin, difficulty breathing, vomiting, etc. We must follow strict mold avoidance practices to stay safe and if we accidentally have a mold exposure, the symptom spiral can knock us down for days or weeks. This machine seems to universally benefit those of us with mold illness by reducing the impact of an exposure significantly. Some people have reported that it has improved electromagnetic frequency sensitivity, amazing! So many people have had positive experiences and are seeing gradual reduced reactivity, cognitive improvement, and reduced symptoms overall with regular use of this machine that many more people are planning to order as soon as they can save up the money.

The focus historically on what these machines can do seems to be on heavy metal detox, but it seems clear from our group's collective experiences that it is very likely removing fat soluble toxins such as mold biotoxins.

We would love to continue emphatically recommending this unit as an affordable therapy to help people with mold illness. Unfortunately, we have had two people so far receive machines that were badly cross-contaminated with mold (returned machines that were resold) and made them very very ill. They have found out the hard way that the company charges a restocking fee and the item must be returned within 14 days. We have tried to talk to the owner and customer service to explain the seriousness of this problem. We cannot continue to recommend that people with mold illness purchase this product unless the company can guarantee we will not receive a returned product that could have been cross-contaminated in someone's moldy house. Like I explained, we are incredibly sensitive and this can cause a major health setback.

I would like to suggest that if you are going to charge a restocking fee you should then resell it minus the restocking fee as a discounted item labeled clearly as refurbished or previously returned. That way if people want to save money they can knowingly buy a used machine and the company would not have lost a penny since the reduced price plus restocking fee makes up the total cost.

The type of people interested in purchasing their own detox foot bath for home use are very likely to be chronically ill. There have been rave reviews in autism groups about the use of detox foot baths. People with fibromyalgia and many other illnesses are benefitting too. They may not yet realize that mold exposure is making them ill. My point is that reselling machines that have been cross-contaminated in toxic homes, could affect more than just us with identified mold illness. People who get a contaminated machine, may feel awful and not understand why if they aren't mold aware yet and blame it on your product. Your customers are sensitive. Please protect us by not reselling returned machines unless you discount them and make it clearly known they will be receiving a returned/refurbished machine. This is critically important. We are all very grateful you have offered such an excellent and affordable product that is helping us to heal. Please listen and respond to our concerns about this issue.

Update 7/21/16: I haven't heard of anyone getting contaminated machines in quite a few months. It looks like the company has fixed this issue. Many more people have purchased this machine and reported very good results. Thank you very much for addressing our concerns. This is a great product, changing to 5 stars.

title: Does not dissolve
text:
I ordered this as a cost effective alternative to the Liquid IV packets I've been getting at Costco, which run about a $1 per packet/serving when not on sale. I sometimes get so engrossed in my work that I forget to stop for normal things like food and water, and it'll be 2pm before I've even realized it. Flavor wise, it's not bad. And it seems to serve it's purpose in keeping me slightly better hydrated than water alone so I will finish the bottle I bought, but definitely not as good as the Liquid IV. Therefore, I won't be purchasing this product again.
I have 2 main issues, the first is with the product, the second is with the seller/company.
1 - it does not dissolve fully, even after hours of sitting and shaking, there is still visible powder floating in the water. I used less powder than was recommended for a full size bottle of water, and still, not all of the powder would dissolve in to the water. I shook the bottle as vigorously as I dared without hurting myself.
2 - When I received my order, it came with this little card inside saying "send us an email with your review for a free gift". I followed the instructions, to a t, thinking maybe the solubility issue was isolated to this one flavor and it would be worth trying other flavors. Well, I never got my free gift. I did get an email saying, well now that you've done this part, can you also write a review on amazon and send us proof that you've done so before we send you the free gift? It irks me when companies add additional conditions on an offer. So be advised, that "free gift" offer you get with your purchase, will not be as simple as the card makes it sound. (I did check both the front and back of the card they had enclosed with the free offer, there's no asterisks or fine text to indicate there would be additional requirements)
Personally, I'm sticking with the liquid IV.

text:
It's a very good water bottle. Now that I've had time to break it in and test it, it performs excellently. It seems to allow for more heat to pass through than my older rubber water bottle, and the thinner tartan cover (compared to my old bottle) seems to help with this as well. This is the main improvement for me compared to normal rubber models, and like other reviews have written there is no smell compared to rubber as well. I do think this kind of makes it loose heat slightly faster, but that's not too big of an issue. The thin plastic line which holds the twist stopper to the bottle body is nice but doesn't seem that solid, but could be easily replaced with something else. The hook which folds away around the neck (where the plastic line attaches) is really useful for hooking it somewhere when you are done emptying the bottle and want to hang it to dry out with the stopper out.

Overall excellent hot water bottle where you can tell they put a lot of thought into the design and materials. Only thing I suppose if I were being nit picky is that thin plastic line (think those things that hold tags on clothes in store) doesn't look durable, but that's just an opinion, time will tell if it lasts.

title: Planaria using panacur c (29g)
text:
Used panacur c for dogs (purchased online- box with 3 envelopes). The planaria infestation was incredible so I decided to desolve half a packet in tank water and warmer sink water mixture- much shaking to dissolve granules then dump in tank.
-Remove cartridges first so medication efficacy is not lost.
-Dumped milky substance in tank and left apple and rams horn snails in bc planaria can hide in their shell
-Waited 2 days and repeated dosage.
-No water changes in between nor feeding. (non- feeding was the most difficult)
- Waited a day 1/2 then did ~80-90% water change
-Added prime and stability
-Later that night added algae wafer and apple snail (Gus) and rams horn ate in peace
(This was for 29g tank)

title: is the best brand I've used
text:
My package arrived on time and and I'm finding that this particular brand of Reishi, along with the Mikei brand, is the best brand I've used. I appreciate how Real Mushrooms educates the consumer about the importance of knowing the precise amounts of beta glucans and triterpenoids in your mushroom, something many other mushroom sellers remain conveniently silent on. Polysaccharides themselves do not reveal much about the quality of the product; the numbers of beta-glucans and triterpenoinds, on the other hand, will tell you precisely how powerful the mushroom extract is.

Word of warning: When you first open the bag, be careful! Open it very slowly, or some of the powder will accidentally 'explode' out of the bag.
